### Printed p. 101

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वर्धचः परोक्षकृतः । य इंद्र ऋत्वात् ॥ यून् मनुष्यान्
> क्षणोति । क्षणोतेर्णादिको दप्रत्ययः ॥ तस्माद्रक्षसो जातादंहसः पापरूपादुपद्रवान्मुचत् मुंचति । राक्षस एनं न बाधते किं पुनस्तं हंतीत्यर्थः । अपि च य
> इंद्रः सप्त सिंधुषु गंगाद्यासु नदीषु । यद्वा । सप्त सर्पणशीलासु सिंधुषु ।
> तत्कूलेष्टित्यर्थः । गंगायां घोष इतिवत् । पा. १-४-४२ । तेषु वर्तमानानां
> स्तोतृणामार्यात् धनादिकं प्रेरयेत् ॥ ऋ गतिप्रापणयोः । आशीर्लिजि
> गुणोर्तिसंयोगाद्योः । पा. ७-४-२९ । इति गुणः । बहुलं छंदसीति
> लिज्यप्यादागमः ॥ अथ प्रत्यक्षः । हे तुविनृम्म बहुधनेंद्र दासस्योपक्षपयितुरसुरस्य
> वधर्हननसाधकमायुधं नीनमः । नमय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The first half of the Ṛk is in the third person (परोक्षकृतः (*parokṣakṛtaḥ*)). Indra is the one who frees from the affliction, the sin, born of the rākṣasa (the sense of यक्षात् (*yakṣāt*) is given as the harm-doer of men): the rākṣasa does not trouble him, much less does he kill him; this is the meaning. Further, Indra is the one who, in the seven rivers, the Gaṅgā and the rest, or else in the seven flowing rivers, that is, on their banks, sends wealth and the like to the praisers who dwell there. Then comes the direct address: O Tuvinṛmṇa, Indra of much wealth, bend, that is, hurl, the weapon, the instrument of killing, against the Dāsa, the asura who harms. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- यक्षात् (*yakṣāt*)—arisen from the rākṣasas who are the harmers of men
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from sin
- मुचत् (*mucat*)—frees the sacrificers
- यः वा (*yaḥ vā*)—who
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number
- सिंधुषु (*siṃdhuṣu*)—in the rivers, the Gaṅgā and the rest
- आर्यात् (*āryāt*)—sends many kinds of wealth (he is Indra indeed)
- तुविनृष्ण (*tuvinṛṣṇa*)—O Indra, possessor of many kinds of wealth
- दासस्य (*dāsasya*)—of the harming asura
- वधः (*vadhaḥ*)—the weapon, the instrument of killing
- नीनमः (*nīnamaḥ*)—apply

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

He who frees the sacrificers from the sin arisen from the rākṣasas who harm men, he who sends many kinds of wealth in the seven rivers, the Gaṅgā and the rest, is Indra indeed. O Indra, possessor of many kinds of wealth, apply against him the weapon, the instrument of killing, of the harming asura.

##### English translation
(He it is) who rescues men from the wickedness of evil beings, who enriches (the dwellers) on the seven rivers: now hurl, you who abound in wealth, your weapon at the Dasa.

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॑ वरो सु॒षाम्णे॑ स॒निभ्य॒ आ व॑हो र॒यिं ।  
> व्य॑श्वेभ्यः सुभगे वाजिनीवति ॥ २८ ॥

### Printed p. 102

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । वरो इति । सुसाम्ने । सनिभ्यः । आ । अवहः । रयिं ।  
> विअश्वेभ्यः । सुभगे । वाजिनीववति ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनेन तृचेन वरोर्दानं स्तूयते । हे वरो वरुनामक राजन् सुषाम्न्य
> सुसाम्मे सुषमाख्यं राजानं स्वपितरमुद्दिश्य तस्योत्तमलोकप्राप्त्यर्थं सनिभ्यो
> भिक्षमाणेभ्य आ कोशादाहृत्य रयिं धनं यथा पुरावहः प्रापितवानसि अत
> एवविदानीं व्यश्वेभ्यो व्यश्वपुत्रेभ्योऽस्मभ्यं धनमावह । वाजिनीवतीति पदलिंगादियमुषस्या । अयं तृचोप्युषस्य इति शौनकेनोक्तं । यथा वरो सुषाम्न्य
> इत्युत्तमसौषसस्त्र च इति । हे सुभगे शोभनधनयुक्ते वाजनीवत्यन्नवति ॥
> मतुबनुवादार्थः ॥ यद्वा । वाजो वाजनं गमनमस्यास्तीति वाजिन्यन्नं । तद्वति
> हे उषः त्वं चास्मभ्यं धनं प्रयच्छ । वरोर्बहुधनदानात्तस्य दानस्तुतिः । यद्वा ।
> विश्वमना ऋषिर्वरुं संबोध्याह । हे सुभगे शोभनधने वाजिनीवत्यन्नवति
> हे उषः यथा त्वं सुषाम्न्य सुषामनाम्मॆ मम पित्रे धनं दत्वा तेनैव सुषाम्न्य
> सनिभ्यो याचमानेभ्यो धनं यथा प्रापितवत्यसि तेन यथा दानमकारयः एवं
> मह्यमपि धनं दत्वा व्यश्वेभ्यः ॥ पूजायां बहुवचनं ॥ व्यश्वपुत्राय विश्वमनसे
> धनं प्रापयेति मयापि दानं करोषि । हे वरो उपसमेवं वदेत्यृषिराह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this group of three Ṛks the generosity of Varu is praised. O Varu, king so named: for Suṣāman, the king of that name, your own father, for the winning of the highest world for him, you formerly brought wealth taken from your treasury to the petitioners (सनिभ्यो (*sanibhyo*)). So now bring wealth to us, the sons of Vyaśva (व्यश्वेभ्यो (*vyaśvebhyo*)). From the word वाजिनीवति (*vājinīvati*), which has the feminine form, this Ṛk is addressed to Uṣas. Śaunaka also says that this group of three is addressed to Uṣas, and that the Ṛk "yathā varo suṣāmṇye" belongs to the Uttama Sauṣasa Sūkta. O Subhagā, you who possess goodly wealth, O Vājinīvatī, possessor of food: the suffix is restating what is already known. Or else: वाज (*vāja*) is going, and वाजिन्यन्नं (*vājinyannaṃ*) is food, so, O Uṣas, possessor of that, give us wealth as well. Because Varu gave much wealth, his generosity is praised. Or else: the seer Viśvamanas, addressing Varu, says: O Subhagā, Vājinīvatī, Uṣas, as you gave wealth to my father Suṣāman, and by that wealth had gifts made to the petitioners, so now give wealth to me also, to the Vyaśvas (the plural is one of respect), the son of Vyaśva, Viśvamanas, and so bring about gifts through me also. O Varu, speak thus to Uṣas, the seer says. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरो (*varo*)—O king named Varu
- सुषाम्णे (*suṣāmṇe*)—for your father named Suṣāman, for the attainment of the highest world
- स निभ्यः (*sa nibhyaḥ*)—to petitioners
- आ (*ā*)—taking from your treasury
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner (formerly)
- अवहः (*avahaḥ*)—you gave (so also)
- व्यश्वभ्यः (*vyaśvabhyaḥ*)—to us also, the sons of Vyaśva, now give
- सुभगे (*subhage*)—you who have goodly wealth
- वाजिनीवति (*vājinīvati*)—you who have food, O Uṣas (you also give wealth to us)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O king named Varu, as you formerly gave wealth, taken from your treasury, to petitioners for the attainment of the highest world for your father Suṣāman, so now give to us also, the son of Vyaśva. O Uṣas, possessed of goodly wealth and of food, you also give wealth to us.

### Printed p. 103

##### English translation
As you, Varu, have distributed vast wealth to those who have solicited triches) on behalf of Sushaman. (so do you now distribute) to the descendants of Vyshwa: (and so too you), auspicious food-bestowing (Ushas). **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Addressing वरो (*varo*) as a king named Varuṇa, the commentator says that another meaning is also possible: "O Varuṇa, you pray to Uṣas. As Uṣas formerly provided wealth to Suṣāman and through him had wealth given to all the petitioners, so now have it given to me also; pray thus on our behalf." **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ ना॒र्यस्य॒ दक्षि॑णा॒ व्य॑श्वा एतु सो॒मिनः॑ ।  
> स्थू॒रं च॒ राधः॑ श॒तव॑त्स॒हस्र॑वत् ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नार्यस्य । दक्षिणा । विआश्वान् । एतु । सोमिनः ।  
> स्थूरं । च । राधः । शतवत् । सहस्रवत् ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आनया धनमृषिरादत्तवानित्याह । नार्यस्य । नरहितो नर्यः । तस्यापत्यं
> नार्यः ॥ तस्मात्संबंधमात्रे तस्येदमित्यण् ॥ तस्य सोमिनः सोमवतो
> यजमानस्य । यद्वा । व्यश्वानां विशेषणं । तादृशस्य वरोर्दक्षिणा दानं
> सोमवतो व्यश्वान् व्यश्वपुत्रानस्मान्नैतु । आगच्छतु । किंच स्फूरं स्कूलं शतवत्सहस्रवच्छतसहस्रधनयुक्तं राधोऽन्नं चास्मानागच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this Ṛk the seer says that he has received the wealth. नार्यस्य (*nāryasya*): one who is good for men is नर्यः (*naryaḥ*), his descendant is नार्यः (*nāryaḥ*); the aṇ affix is used for a mere relationship. Of him, the possessor of soma, the sacrificer; or else, this is an epithet of the Vyaśvas. May the gift (दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)) of such a Varu come to us, the sons of Vyaśva, who are possessors of soma. Further, may abundant wealth (राधः (*rādhaḥ*)), that is food, endowed with hundreds and thousands, come to us as well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नार्यस्य (*nāryasya*)—of Varu, the son of Narya, who is good for men
- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—the gift
- सोमिनः (*sominaḥ*)—the sacrificers who offer soma
- व्यश्वान् (*vyaśvān*)—us, the son of Vyaśva
- अएतु (*aetu*)—may it come and join
- स्फूरं (*sphūraṃ*)—abundant
- शतवत् (*śatavat*)—numbering hundreds
- सहस्रवत् (*sahasravat*)—numbering thousands
- राधः चॆ (*rādhaḥ cè*)—food and wealth also, may they come and join us

### Printed p. 104

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the gift given by Varu, the son of Narya who is good for men, come and join us, the sacrificers who offer soma and the sons of Vyaśva. May food and wealth also, abundant, numbering hundreds and numbering thousands, come and join us.

##### English translation
May the gifts of a humane (prince), when offering the soma libation extend to the Vyshwas, and substantial wealth by hundreds and thousand.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सोमिनः (*sominaḥ*) may also be construed as an epithet of Varu, so that the sense is "the gift of Varu, who is himself the sacrificer".

#### Ṛk 30

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्त्वा॑ पृ॒च्छादी॑जा॒नः कु॑ह॒या कु॑हयाकृते ।  
> ए॒षो अप॑श्रितो व॒लो गो॑म॒तीमव॑ तिष्ठति ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । त्वा । पृच्छात् । ईजानः । कुहया । कुहयाकृते ।  
> एषः । अपश्रितः । वलः । गोऽमतीं । अव । शिष्ठति ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदानीमुषसं संबोध्याभिधीयते । हे कुहयाकृते स वरुः कुह
> कुत्र तिष्ठतीतेतदिच्छयाभिलक्षणप्रवृत्तैर्जिज्ञासुभिः पुरस्कृते ॥ कुहशब्दात्क्यच् ॥
> एतादृशे हे उषः त्वा त्वां यद्यदा कश्चित्पृच्छात् पृच्छति ईजान इष्टवान् वरुः
> कुहया क्व तिष्ठतीति यदा पृच्छति तदानीमपश्रितः सर्वैराश्रितः । यद्वा । विवृतद्वारः ।
> यदा याचमाना आगच्छंति तदा दौवारिका न प्रतिबध्नंतीत्यर्थः । तादृशो बलो
> वरः स्वबलेनावारकः शत्रूणां । यद्वा । भिक्षूणां धनादिप्रदानेनावरिता। एषो एष
> वरुर्गॊमतीमेतन्नामिकां नदीं ॥ कालाध्वनोरिति द्वितीया ॥ तस्तास्तीरेव
> तिष्यतीति तदानीं त्वं कथयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now Uṣas is addressed. O कुहयाकृते (*kuhayākṛte*), you who are put forward, that is, questioned, by inquirers who set out with the wish to know "Where does that Varu stay?" (the word is formed from कुह (*kuha*), "where"). O Uṣas, when anyone asks you where the sacrificer Varu stays, then you say as follows. He is resorted to by all (अपश्रितः (*apaśritaḥ*)); or else, he has open doors: when petitioners come, the doorkeepers do not obstruct them. Such a Varu averts enemies by his own strength; or else, he is one who keeps the beggars from want by giving wealth and the like. This Varu stays on the very banks of the river named Gomatī.

### Printed p. 105

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कुहयाकृते (*kuhayākṛte*)—O Uṣas, who are questioned about Varu as to where he is
- ईजानः (*ījānaḥ*)—Varu, the sacrificer
- कुहया (*kuhayā*)—where he is
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- पृच्छात् (*pṛcchāt*)—one asks, then
- अपश्रितः (*apaśritaḥ*)—the refuge of all
- वलः (*valaḥ*)—and one who faces enemies
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Varu
- गोमतीं (*gomatīṃ*)—on the bank of the river Gomatī
- अव तिष्ठति (*ava tiṣṭhati*)—is staying (say so)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, who are questioned about Varu as to where he is: if anyone asks you, "Where is Varu, the sacrificer?", then tell him, "Varu, the refuge of all, is on the bank of the river Gomatī."

##### English translation
If any ask of you, (Ushas), when anywhere present, where the sacrificer (Varu dwells), (reply) the powerfull (prince), the refuge of all, abides on (the banks of) the Gomathi river.

## Sūkta 25 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ता वामिति चतुर्विंशत्यृचं पंचमं सूक्तं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । ता
> वां चतुर्विंशतिर्मृत्रावरुणं दशम्याद्यास्तिस्रो वैश्वदेव्य उपांत्योष्टिग्र्भेति ।
> व्यश्वपुत्रो विश्वमना ऋषिः । उष्णिक् छंदः । उपांत्योष्टिग्र्भा षट्सप्तैकादशा उष्णिग्र्भा । अनु. ४-३ । इति तल्लक्षणोपेतत्वात् । दशम्येकादशीद्वादश्यो
> वैश्वदेव्योऽवशिष्टानां मित्रावरुणौ देवता ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning ता वां (*tā vāṃ*) has twenty-four Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta. On it he cites the Anukramaṇikā: the twenty-four Ṛks are addressed to Mitrāvaruṇa, the three beginning with the tenth are Vaiśvadevī, and the last but one is of the uṣṇig-garbhā metre. The seer is Viśvamanas, the son of Vyaśva; the metre is uṣṇik. The last-but-one Ṛk is uṣṇig-garbhā because it has the marks "six, seven, eleven" (Anu. 4-3). The tenth, eleventh and twelfth are Vaiśvadevī; Mitrāvaruṇa is the deity of the rest. The use of the sūkta is by indication (लैंगिकः (*laiṃgikaḥ*)). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, beginning ता वां (*tā vāṃ*), is the fifth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has twenty-four Ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā is quoted to the effect that the twenty-four Ṛks are addressed to Mitrāvaruṇa, with the three beginning with the tenth to the Viśvedevas, and that the last but one is of the uṣṇig-garbhā metre. The seer of this sūkta is Viśvamanas, the son of Vyaśva. The deity of the tenth, eleventh and twelfth Ṛks is the Viśvedevas; the deity of the remaining Ṛks is Mitrāvaruṇa; the metre is uṣṇik.

### Printed p. 106

The Ṛk before the last, that is, the twenty-third Ṛk, is of the metre called uṣṇig-garbhā. If a Ṛk has three pādas, with six syllables in the first pāda, seven in the second and eleven in the third, that Ṛk is of the metre called uṣṇig-garbhā. The use of the sūkta is by indication (laiṅgika).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 25. Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 25. Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 2, Vargas 21, 22, 23, 24, 25. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 24. Seer: Viśvamanas Vaiyaśva. Deity: 1-9 and 13-24 Mitrāvaruṇau; 10-12 Viśvedevāḥ. Metre: 1-22 and 24 Uṣṇik; 23 Uṣṇig-garbhā.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता वां॒ विश्व॑स्य गो॒पा दे॒वा दे॒वेषु॑ य॒ज्ञिया॑ ।  
> ऋ॒तावा॑ना यजसे पू॒तद॑क्षसा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । वां । विश्वस्य । गोपा । देवा । देवेषु । यज्जिया ।  
> ऋतऽवाना । यजसे । पूतदक्षसा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ विश्वस्य सर्वस्य लोकस्य गोपा गोपायितार् देवा देवौ
> द्योतनशीलौ देवेषु मध्यॆ यज्ञिया यज्ञार्हौ ता तौ तादृशौ वां युवां
> हविष्पदानार्थं यजमानं भजथः । आत एव हे विश्वमनः ऋतावानर्तावान्
> सत्यवंतौ यज्ञवंतौ वा पूतदक्षसौ शुद्धबलौ । आवां बलवंताविति वचनमात्रेण
> बलवंतौ न भवतः किंतु यथार्थत्वेन सामर्थ्यवंतौ । मित्रावरुणौ यजसे ।
> हविर्भिः पूजयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitrāvaruṇa, guardians of the whole world, shining ones, worthy of sacrifice among the gods: such as you are, you attend the sacrificer so that he may offer the oblation. Therefore, O Viśvamanas, address them: they are truthful or possessed of sacrifice, and of pure strength. They are not strong merely by the saying "we are strong", but able in truth. You worship Mitrāvaruṇa with oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवा (*devā*)—the shining ones
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- यज्ञिया (*yajñiyā*)—worthy of worship
- ता (*tā*)—O renowned Mitrāvaruṇa
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two alone
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of all the worlds

### Printed p. 107

- गोपा (*gopā*)—you are the protectors (O seer Viśvamanas)
- यतावाना (*yatāvānā*)—the truthful
- पूतदक्षसा (*pūtadakṣasā*)—those of pure strength, Mitrāvaruṇa, to them alone
- यजसे (*yajase*)—worship, addressing yourself

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitrāvaruṇa, shining, worthy of worship among the gods, and renowned, you two alone are the protectors of all the worlds. O seer Viśvamanas, worship, addressing yourself to them, Mitrāvaruṇa, who are truthful and of pure strength.

##### English translation
You two are the protectors of the universe, divine, and to be adored among the gods; therefore, (Vyshwamanas), you sacrifice to the pair who are observant of truth and endowed with real power.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मि॒त्रा तना॒ न र॒थ्या॒३॒॑ ३ वरु॑णो॒ यश्च॑ सु॒क्रतुः॑ ।  
> स॒नात्सु॑जा॒ता तन॑या धृ॒तव्र॑ता ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मित्रा । तना । न । रथ्या । वरुणः । यः । च । सुक्रतुः ।  
> सनात् । सुजाता । तनया । धृतव्रता ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुक्रतुः शोभनकर्मा यो वरुणः सुकर्मा मित्रा च मित्रावरुणौ ।
> कीदृशौ । तना । तन्नंति मुकुटकटकादिनेति तनानि धनानि । नश्चार्थे । धनानि च रथ्या
> रथ्यौ नेतारौ । यद्वा । धनानि कर्मणः कर्तृपेक्षत्वात् प्रयच्छंताविति संबध्यते ।
> तादृशौ रथ्यौ रथवंतौ सनाच्चिरादेव सुजाता सुजात् शोभनजन्मानौ । तदेवाह ।
> तनया तनयावदितेः पुत्रौ धृतव्रता धृतव्रतौ धृतकर्माणौ ता यजस इति
> पूर्वेण समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mitra, and Varuṇa who is of good action (सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)): the two Mitrāvaruṇa. Of what kind? तना (*tanā*): that which is stretched, such as crowns and bracelets, that is, riches; the word na here stands for "and". They are the leaders (रथ्या (*rathyā*)) of riches; or else, since an act depends on its doer, the construction is that they bestow riches. Such possessors of chariots are, from of old, of good birth (सुजाता (*sujātā*)). He states the same: they are the sons of Aditi, upholders of vows and rites. The construction is with the earlier "you worship them".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—one of excellent action
- मित्रा चॆ (*mitrā cè*)—and the Mitra who has the same quality; these two, Mitrāvaruṇa
- तना (*tanā*)—

### Printed p. 108

  givers of wealth
- रथ्या (*rathyā*)—leaders of rites
- सनात् (*sanāt*)—from the beginning
- सुजाता (*sujātā*)—of excellent birth
- तनया (*tanayā*)—sons of Aditi
- धृतव्रता (*dhṛtavratā*)—those who impel the keeping of the vow by rule (worship such Mitrāvaruṇa)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Varuṇa who is of excellent action and the Mitra who has the same quality, these two, Mitrāvaruṇa, are givers of wealth, leaders of rites, of excellent birth from the beginning, sons of Aditi, and those who govern the vow by rule. Worship such Mitrāvaruṇa.

##### English translation
Mitra and Varuna, doers of good deeds, (diffusers of) riches, who are the charioteers (of men), well born of old, the sons (of Aditi) observant of vows, (you are worshipped by me).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता मा॒ता वि॒श्ववे॑दसासु॒र्या॑य॒ प्रम॑हसा ।  
> म॒ही ज॑जा॒नादि॑तिर्ऋ॒ताव॑री ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता ! माता । विश्ववेदसा । आसुर्याय । प्रमहसा ।  
> मही । जजान । अदितिः । ऋतवरी ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अदितेस्तनयत्वमेव स्पुटयति । विश्ववेदसा विश्ववेदसौ सर्वधना । यद्वा ।
> विश्वानि स्थावरजंगमात्मकानि सर्वाणि विदतुर्जानीत इति विश्ववेदसौ । प्रमहसा
> प्रमहसौ प्रकृष्टतेजस्कौ ता तौ तादृशौ मित्रावरुणौ मही महत्यृतावरी सत्यवती
> माता देवमातादितिर्जजान । जनयामास । किमर्थं । असुर्यायासुराणां
> हंत्रे बलाय । असुरान् हंतुमुत्पादितवतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He makes clear that they are Aditi's sons. विश्ववेदसा (*viśvavedasā*): those who possess all wealth; or else, those who know all things, moving and unmoving. प्रमहसा (*pramahasā*): of surpassing splendour. Such Mitrāvaruṇa were borne by Aditi, the great and truthful mother of the gods. For what purpose? असुर्याय (*asuryāya*): for the strength that slays the asuras; the meaning is that she bore them in order to slay the asuras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववेदसा (*viśvavedasā*)—those who know the whole world of moving and unmoving things
- प्रमहसा (*pramahasā*)—those of the most excellent splendour
- शा (*śā*)—and renowned, those Mitrāvaruṇa

### Printed p. 109

- मही (*mahī*)—she of great nature
- ऋतावरी (*ṛtāvarī*)—she of the nature of truth
- माता (*mātā*)—and mother of the gods
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi
- असुराय (*asurāya*)—to destroy the asuras
- जजान (*jajāna*)—bore

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Aditi, of great nature, of the nature of truth and mother of the gods, bore Mitrāvaruṇa, who know the whole world of moving and unmoving things, who are of the most excellent splendour, and who are renowned, in order to destroy the asuras.

##### English translation
The great and veracious Aditi, the mother (of the gods), gave birth to those two who are possessed of all affluence, and shinnig with great splendour, for the (destruction of the) Asuras.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒हांता॑ मि॒त्रावरु॑णा स॒म्राजा॑ दे॒वावसु॑रा ।  
> ऋ॒तवा॑नावृ॒तमा घो॑षतो बृ॒हत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महांता । मित्रावरुणा । संराजा । देवा । असुरा ।  
> ऋतवान् । ऋतं । आ । घोषतः । बृहत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महांता गुणाधिक्येन महांतौ सम्राजा सम्राजौ सम्यग्दीप्यमानावसुरावसुरौ बलवंतौ । यद्वा । सर्वांतर्यामितया प्रेरकौ । ऋतानाना सत्यवंतौ
> मित्रावरुणौ देवौ बृहत् स्तोत्रशस्त्रादिना महांतमृतं यज्ञमा घोषतः ।
> स्वदीप्त्या प्रकाशयतः ॥ घुषेर्लट रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

महांता (*mahāṃtā*): great through the abundance of their qualities. सम्राजा (*samrājā*): shining well. असुरा (*asurā*): powerful; or else, impellers, as the inner controllers of all. Mitrāvaruṇa, the truthful gods, make the great ṛta, the sacrifice, resound and shine by their own brightness, through stotra, śastra and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महांता (*mahāṃtā*)—those of exceedingly great qualities
- सम्राजा (*samrājā*)—those who shine exceedingly
- असुरा (*asurā*)—the powerful
- देवौ (*devau*)—of divine nature
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—Mitrāvaruṇa

### Printed p. 110

- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—having acquired a great nature through stotra, śastra and the like
- यतं (*yataṃ*)—the sacrifice
- आ घोषतः (*ā ghoṣataḥ*)—they make shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitrāvaruṇa, who are of exceedingly great qualities, who shine exceedingly, who are powerful and of divine nature, make shine the sacrifice, which has acquired a great nature through stotra, śastra and the like.

##### English translation
The great Mitra and Varuna, the two sovereign and powerful deities, the observers of truth, illumne our solemn rite.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नपा॑ता॒ शव॑सो म॒हः सू॒नू दक्ष॑स्य सु॒क्रतू॑ ।  
> सृ॒प्रदा॑नू इ॒षो वास्त्वधि॑ क्षितः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नपाता । शवसः । महः । सूनू इति । दक्षस्य । सुक्रतू इति सुक्रतू ।  
> सृप्रदानू इति सृप्रदानू । इषः । वास्तु । अधि । क्षितः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महो महतः शवसो बलस्य नपाता नपात् पौत्रौ । बलत उत्पादिताविति
> बलस्य पौत्रौ । तादृशौ दक्षस्य । दक्ष वृद्धौ शीघ्रार्थे चेति दक्षो वेगः । तस्य सूनू
> पुत्रौ । बलाद्वेग इति तयोः पुत्रत्वं । ता सुक्रतू शोभनकर्माणौ सृप्रदानू
> प्रसृतधनादिदानौ मित्रावरुणाविषोऽन्नस्य वास्तु निवासस्थानेऽधि क्षितः । अधिवसतः ॥
> अधिशीजिति वास्तुनः कर्मसंज्ञा । क्षयतेर्लट छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mitrāvaruṇa are the grandsons (नपाता (*napātā*)) of great strength: since they are produced from strength, they are the grandsons of strength. Such as they are, they are the sons of दक्ष (*dakṣa*), which here means speed (the root means growth and also speed). Speed arises from strength, hence their sonship to it. They are of good action, and liberal in giving wealth and the like widely. Mitrāvaruṇa dwell in the dwelling-place of food (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- शवसः (*śavasaḥ*)—to strength
- नपाता (*napātā*)—grandsons
- दक्षस्य (*dakṣasya*)—to speed
- सूनू (*sūnū*)—sons
- सुक्रतू (*sukratū*)—those of excellent action
- सुप्रदानू (*supradānū*)—those who give widely, Mitrāvaruṇa
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—to food
- वास्तु (*vāstu*)—in the dwelling-place
- अधि क्षितः (*adhi kṣitaḥ*)—they dwell (they are the lords)

### Printed p. 111

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitrāvaruṇa, grandsons to great strength, sons to speed, of excellent action and liberal in giving, are lords of food and dwell in its dwelling-place.

##### English translation
Grandsons of mighty strength, sons of energy, doers of good deeds liberal benefactors, they preside over the habitation of food.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं या दानू॑नि ये॒मथु॑र्दि॒व्याः पार्थि॑वी॒रिषः॑ ।  
> नभ॑स्वती॒रा वां॑ चरंतु वृ॒ष्टयः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । या । दानूनि । येमथुः । दिव्याः । पार्थिवीः । इषः ।  
> नभस्वतीः । आ । वां । चरंतु । वृष्टयः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ यौ युवां दानूनि देयानि धनानि सं येमथुः अस्मासु
> संयच्छतं तथा दिव्या दिव्यानि दिवि भवानि पार्थिवीः पृथिव्यामुत्पन्नानीषोऽन्नानि
> संयच्छतं । वृष्ट्यभावे कथमन्नं लभ्यत इति चेत् तदुच्यते । नभस्वतीरुदकवत्यो
> वृष्टयस्तादृशौ वां युवामा चरंतु । उपतिष्ठंतु । यदा वृष्ट्यवेला तदा
> वर्षतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitrāvaruṇa, bestow upon us the gifts, the wealth that is to be given; likewise bestow heavenly foods, those that are in the sky, and earthly foods, those born on the earth. If it is asked how food is to be had when there is no rain, the answer is this: may the rains, which are full of water (नभस्वतीः (*nabhasvatīḥ*)), attend upon you both, that is, come to you; when it is time for rain, you rain. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Mitrāvaruṇa) या दानूनि (*yā dānūni*)—the wealth that is to be given to us
- सं येमथुः (*saṃ yemathuḥ*)—provide to us
- दिव्याः (*divyāḥ*)—those produced in the heavenly world
- पार्थिवीः (*pārthivīḥ*)—and those produced on earth
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—provide to us the foods also
- नभस्वतीः (*nabhasvatīḥ*)—full of water
- वृष्टयः (*vṛṣṭayaḥ*)—the rains
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- आ चरंतु (*ā caraṃtu*)—may they serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitrāvaruṇa, provide to us the wealth that is to be given to us. Provide to us also foods, both those produced in the heavenly world and those produced on earth. May the rains, full of water, serve you.

### Printed p. 112

##### English translation
Bestow (upon us) good gifts, viands, whether of heaven or earth : may the water-shedding rains atten upon you.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधि॒ या बृ॑ह॒तो दि॒वो॒३॒॑ ३ भि यू॒थेव॒ पश्य॑तः ।  
> ऋ॒तावा॑ना स॒म्राजा॒ नम॑से हि॒ता ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अधि । या । बृहतः । दिवः । अभि । यूथा इव । पश्यतः ।  
> ऋतवाना । संराजा । नमसे । हिता ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या यौ मित्रावरुणौ बृहतो दिवो द्योतमानान्देवानधि पश्यतः । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । यूथेव यथा वृषभो गोयूथानि रंतुमभ्यभिमुखं पश्यति
> तद्वदेत् स्ववीर्येणासुरान्हत्वा देवान्मोदयितुं पश्यत इत्यर्थः । कीदृशौ ।
> ऋतावाना सत्यवंतौ सम्राजा सम्राजौ सम्यग्दीप्यमानौ नमसे हविषे हिता हितौ
> प्रियौ पश्यत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two, Mitrāvaruṇa, who look upon the great shining gods. The example: as a bull looks towards herds of cows in front of him in order to take his pleasure, so they look, having slain the asuras by their own strength, in order to delight the gods; this is the meaning. Of what kind are they? Truthful, shining well, and dear to the oblation (नमसे (*namase*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतानाना (*ṛtānānā*)—the truthful
- सम्राजा (*samrājā*)—those who shine greatly
- नमसे (*namase*)—to the oblation
- हिता (*hitā*)—dear ones
- या (*yā*)—those Mitrāvaruṇa who are such
- यूथेव अधि (*yūtheva adhi*)—as a bull looks at a herd of cows

### Printed p. 113

- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—those of great nature
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—shining gods
- अधि पश्यतः (*adhi paśyataḥ*)—they are looking upon

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those Mitrāvaruṇa who are truthful, shine greatly and are dear to the oblation look upon the gods, who are of great nature and shining, as a bull looks at a herd of cows.

##### English translation
(These are they) who look upon the great deities as (a bull contemplates) the herd, sovereigns observant of truth and propitious to adoration.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तावा॑ना॒ नि षे॑दतुः॒ साम्रा॑ज्याय सु॒क्रतू॑ ।  
> धृ॒तव्र॑ता क्ष॒त्रिया॑ क्ष॒त्रमा॑शतुः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत्‌वाना । नि । सेदतुः । सांराज्याय । सुक्रतू इति सुक्रतू ।  
> धृतव्रता । क्षत्रिया । क्षत्रं । आशतुः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋतावानर्तावान् सत्यवंतौ सुक्रतू शोभनकर्माण् सुप्रज्ञा वा
> मित्रावरुण् साम्राज्याय साम्राज्यार्थं नि षेदतुः । न्यसीदतां । तथा मंत्रः ।
> नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्त्यास्वा साम्राज्याय सुक्रतुः । ऋ. १-२५-१० । इति ।
> धृतव्रता धृतव्रत् धृतकर्माण् क्षत्रिया क्षत्रियौ बलवंतौ क्षत्रं बलमाशतुः ।
> आनशाते । व्याप्नुत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mitrāvaruṇa are truthful and of good action or good understanding. For sovereignty they sat down. So the mantra says: नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्त्यास्वा साम्राज्याय सुक्रतुः । (*ni ṣasāda dhṛtavrato varuṇaḥ pastyāsvā sāmrājyāya sukratuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-10) **GLOSS**. They are upholders of vows, of rites; they are क्षत्रिया (*kṣatriyā*), mighty, and they have pervaded, attained, strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतावाना (*ṛtāvānā*)—the truthful
- सुक्रतू (*sukratū*)—those of excellent action, Mitrāvaruṇa
- साम्राज्याय (*sāmrājyāya*)—to proclaim their sovereignty
- नि षेदतुः (*ni ṣedatuḥ*)—they sit down
- धृतव्रता (*dhṛtavratā*)—upholders of rites in the form of vows (governors of rites)
- क्षत्रिया (*kṣatriyā*)—those endowed with power, they
- क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)—strength
- आशतुः (*āśatuḥ*)—attain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitrāvaruṇa, truthful and of excellent action, sit down to proclaim their sovereignty. Upholders of rites in the form of vows (governors of rites) and endowed with power, they attain strength also.

##### English translation
Observers of truth, doers of good deeds, they sit down for the office of sovereignty ; observant of obligations endowed with strength they acquire vigour.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒क्ष्णश्चि॑द्गातु॒वित्त॑रानुल्ब॒णेन॒ चक्ष॑सा ।  
> नि चि॑न्मि॒षंता॑ निचि॒रा नि चि॑क्कतुः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अक्ष्णः । चित् । गातुवित्करा । अनुल्बणेन । चक्षसा ।  
> नि । चित् । मिषंता । निचिरा । नि । चिक्कतुः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अक्षश्चिच्चक्षुषोऽपि पूर्वं गातुवित्तरा।गातुवित्तरावतिशयेन मार्गवेत्तारौ ।
> यद्वा । गातुवित्तरौ गातु गमनशीलं प्राणिजातं चक्षुषोऽपि पूर्वं वेत्तारौ
> मित्रावरुणौ । कीदृशौ । नि मिषंता निमिषंत् सर्वमुन्मेषयंतौ स्वस्वकर्मणि निचिरा
> नितरां चिरंतनौ तावनुल्बणेन । उल्पणमिति दुःसहमग्नेस्तेजः । तद्वदॆदुःसहेन
> चक्षसाहोरात्रयोर्वाप्नेन तेजसैव नि चिक्क्यतुः । पूजितौ बभूवतुः । चिदवधारणे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They are the best knowers of the path (गातुवित्तरा (*gātuvittarā*)), even before the eye; or else, they know the class of moving beings even before the eye can see. Of what kind are they? They cause all to open their eyes, each in its own work, and they are exceedingly ancient. By a brilliance that is not unbearable, like the unbearable brilliance of fire, a brilliance pervading day and night, they have become honoured. The word चित् (*cit*) is for emphasis. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अक्षश्चित् (*akṣaścit*)—even before the organ of sight
- गातुवित्तरा (*gātuvittarā*)—those who know the paths of movement
- नि मिषंता (*ni miṣaṃtā*)—those who make the eyes of all beings open
- निचिरा (*nicirā*)—exceedingly ancient, Mitrāvaruṇa
- अनुल्पणेन (*anulpaṇena*)—without excessive sharpness
- चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*)—together with radiance
- नि चिक्कतुः (*ni cikkatuḥ*)—they have been honoured

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitrāvaruṇa, who know the path of movement even before the organ of sight acts (before the blink of an eyelid), who make the eyes of all beings open, and who are exceedingly ancient, are honoured together with a radiance without excessive sharpness.

##### English translation
Thorough knowers of the path, even before the eye (can see), causing (all beings) to open their eyelids, existing from of old, and shining with a mild radiance, verily they have been worshipped.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For गातुवित्तरा (*gātuvittarā*) the meaning "those who know all the doings of beings that are given to movement" may also be given.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त नो॑ दे॒व्यदि॑तिरुरु॒ष्यतां॒ नास॑त्या ।  
> उ॒रु॒ष्यंतु॑ म॒रुतो॑ वृ॒द्धश॑वसः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । नः । देवी । अदितिः । उरुष्यतां । नासत्या ।  
> उरुष्यंतु । मरुतः । वृद्धशवसः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च देवी द्योतनशीलादितिर्मित्रावरुणयोर्माता नोऽस्मान्रक्षतु ।
> नासत्या नासत्यौ । असत्यमनयोर्नास्तीति नासत्यौ । अश्विन् चोरुष्यतां । रक्षतां ॥
> उरुष्यतिः कण्ण्वादिः ॥ वृद्धश्रवसो वृद्धवेगाः । अतिशयेन वेगवंत इत्यर्थः ।
> यॆद्वा वर्धनशीलहनिर्लक्षणान्नोपेता मरुत उरुष्यंतु । आस्मान्पालयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And may the shining Aditi, the mother of Mitrāvaruṇa, protect us. The Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, in whom there is no untruth, also protect us. The Maruts, वृद्धश्रवसः (*vṛddhaśravasaḥ*) of increased speed, that is, exceedingly swift, protect us; or else, the Maruts, endowed with food that is characterised by increasing oblation, protect us. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उशॆ (*uśè*)—and
- देवी (*devī*)—of divine radiance
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi
- नः (*naḥ*)—may she protect us
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—the Aśvin gods
- उरुष्यतां (*uruṣyatāṃ*)—may they protect
- वृद्धश्रवसः (*vṛddhaśravasaḥ*)—of exceedingly great speed
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- उरुष्यंतु (*uruṣyaṃtu*)—may they protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Aditi, of divine radiance, protect us. May the Aśvin gods protect us. May the Maruts, of exceedingly great speed, protect us.

##### English translation
May the divine Aditi, may the Nasatyas also protect us; may the rapid Maruts defend us.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते नो॑ ना॒वमु॑रुष्यत॒ दिवा॒ नक्तं॑ सुदानवः ।  
> अरि॑ष्यंतो॒ नि पा॒युभिः॑ सचेमहि ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । नः । नावं । उरुष्यत । दिवा । नक्तं । सुदानवः ।  
> अरिष्यंतः । नि । पायुभिः । सचेमहि ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुदानवः तोभनदाना मरुतोऽरिष्यंतः केनाप्यहिंसिताः ते तादृशा
> यूयं नोऽस्मदीयां नावं यज्ञियां नावं दिवा नक्तं चोरुष्यत । पालयत ।
> शतो वयं पायुभिर्युष्मदीयैः पालनैर्नि सचेमहि । नितरां समवेता भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, good givers, unharmed by anyone: such as you are, protect our sacrificial boat by day and by night. Then by your protections may we be closely united.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—O Maruts, excellent givers
- अरिष्यंतः (*ariṣyaṃtaḥ*)—you who are not caught by the harm of anyone
- ते (*te*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- नावं (*nāvaṃ*)—boat in the form of a sacrifice
- दिवा (*divā*)—by day
- नक्तं (*naktaṃ*)—and by night
- उरुष्यत (*uruṣyata*)—protect (afterwards)
- पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*)—with your protections
- नि सचेमहि (*ni sacemahi*)—may we be united

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, excellent givers, you who are not caught by the harm of anyone, protect our boat in the form of a sacrifice by day and by night. Afterwards may we be united with your protections.

##### English translation
Munificent and irresistible (Maruts), guard our vessel by day and night, so that we may be secure through your protection.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अघ्न॑ते॒ विष्ण॑वे व॒यमरि॑ष्यंतः सु॒दान॑वे ।  
> श्रु॒धि स्व॑यानि स्सिंधो पू॒र्वचि॑त्तये ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 117

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> v v v - v - n - l - - -  
> ॥ हसिवु ॥  
> अघ्नते । विष्णवे । वयं । अरिष्यंतः । सुदानने ।  
> श्रुधि । स्वयावन् । सिंधो इति । पूर्वचित्तये ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वोऽर्धर्चः परोक्षकृतः । अरिष्यंतः पालनवत्त्वात् केनाप्यबाधिता
> वयमघ्नते स्तोत्यणां यष्टणां चाहिंसकाय सुदानवे शोभनदानाय
> विष्णवे स्वमहत्त्वन सर्वव्यापकाय्कॆतन्नामकाय देवाय स्तुतिं कुर्मः । अथ
> प्रत्यक्षः । हे स्वयान् । स्वयमेवासहायः सन् दिवि संग्रामे वा यातीति
> स्वयावान् । सिंधो स्तोत्यन् प्रति धनानां स्यंदनशील विष्णो पूर्वचित्तये ।
> चित्तिः कर्म । मंत्रांतरेऽपि तथा श्रवणात् । सा चित्तिभिर्नि हि चकार मर्त्यं ।
> ऋ. १-१६४-२९ । इति । पूर्वं प्रारब्धकर्मणे यजमानाय तदर्थं श्रुधि । अस्माभिः
> क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं त्वं शृणु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The first half of the verse is spoken in the third person (indirect address). "We, who are unharmed because we have the protection of Viṣṇu, offer praise to Viṣṇu, who does not harm those who praise and those who sacrifice, who is a splendid giver, who pervades everything by his greatness and bears this name." Then the second half turns to direct address: "O Viṣṇu, who goes alone and unaided, in the sky or in battle; O Viṣṇu, who makes wealth flow like a river toward those who praise you: *citti* means sacrificial act, as is also heard in another mantra, सा चित्तिभिर्नि हि चकार मर्त्यं (*sā cittibhirni hi cakāra martyaṃ*) (Ṛ. 1-164-29) **NOTE**. For the sacrificer who has begun the rite, hear the praise that we are offering."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरिष्यंतः (*ariṣyaṃtaḥ*)—(because we are protected by Viṣṇu) not caught by anyone's harm
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- अघ्नते (*aghnate*)—who does not harm those who praise him
- सुदानवे (*sudānave*)—who is an excellent giver
- विष्णवे (*viṣṇave*)—to Viṣṇu we offer praise
- स्वयावन् (*svayāvan*)—who rushes into battle alone, without help
- सिंधो (*siṃdho*)—O Viṣṇu, who makes wealth flow like a river
- पूर्वचित्तये (*pūrvacittaye*)—for the sacrificer who has begun the rite
- श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)—hear our praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, unharmed because we are protected by Viṣṇu, offer praise to Viṣṇu, who does not harm those who praise him and is an excellent giver. O Viṣṇu, who rushes forward alone and without help in battle and makes wealth flow like a river, hear our praise on behalf of the sacrificer who has begun the rite.

##### English translation
We, uninjured (through his protection, offer praise) to the libera
Vishnu, who harms not (his adorers): do you who go by yourself alone
(to combat), and cause wealth to flow (to the worshipper), hear (our prayer)
in behalf of him who has commenced the sacrifice. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तद्वार्यं॑ वृणीमहे॒ वरि॑ष्ठं गोप॒यत्यं॑ ।  
> मि॒त्रो यत्पांति॒ वरु॑णो॒ यद॑र्य॒मा ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । वार्यं । वृणीमहे । वरिष्ठं । गोपयत्यं ।  
> मित्रः । यत् । पांति । वरुणः । यत् । अर्यमा ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वरिष्ठमुरुतरं गोपयत्यं सर्वॆषां रक्षकं यतैः पालनीयं वा वार्यं
> सर्वैर्वननीयं तद्धनं वृणीमहे । वयं संभजामहे । यद्धनं मित्रः सर्वॆषां
> मित्रभूतो वरुणः शत्रुवाणां वारयितार्यमा सर्वदा गच्छन् एतन्नामकास्त्रयो
> देवाः पांति पालयंति । तद्धनं वृणीमहे । अस्मदीयस्य धनस्य रक्षका
> भवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"We choose that wealth which is the best and widest and which protects all, or which is to be guarded by effort, and which is to be chosen by all: we share in it. The wealth which Mitra, who is the friend of all, Varuṇa, who keeps off enemies, and Aryaman, who always goes (about), these three deities, protect, that wealth we choose." The meaning is that they become the guardians of our wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—which wealth
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- पांति (*pāṃti*)—protect
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- वरिष्ठं (*variṣṭhaṃ*)—the most excellent
- गोपयत्यं (*gopayatyaṃ*)—the protector of all
- वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*)—and desired by all, such wealth
- वृणीमहे (*vṛṇīmahe*)—may we obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wealth which Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman protect: such most excellent wealth, which protects all and is desired by all, may we obtain.

##### English translation
We solicit that ample, all-desired, all-guarding (wealth) which
Mitra, Varuna, and Aryaman hold under their protection.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the explanation of the word वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*), Yāska has given an etymological explanation of the first half of this Ṛk:

### Printed p. 119
वार्यं । वार्य वृणोतेरथापि वरतमं । तद्वार्यं वृणीमहे वरिष्ठं गोपयत्यं (ऋ. सं. ८-२५-१३) तद्वार्यं वृणीमहे वर्षिष्टं गोपायितव्यं गोपायितारो यूयं स्थ युष्मभ्यमिति ना ॥ (*vāryaṃ | vārya vṛṇoterathāpi varatamaṃ | tadvāryaṃ vṛṇīmahe variṣṭhaṃ gopayatyaṃ (ṛ. saṃ. 8-25-13) tadvāryaṃ vṛṇīmahe varṣiṣṭaṃ gopāyitavyaṃ gopāyitāro yūyaṃ stha yuṣmabhyamiti nā ‖*) (Ni. 5-1)
The word वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*) is derived from the root *vṛ* (*vṛṇoti*), meaning "to choose"; वार्यं (*vāryaṃ*) means that which is desired by all, or that which is most excellent. In the present Ṛk the meaning is this: O Mitra and Varuṇa, in you there are many things desired by all. Among them we choose, or desire, protection from you. For protection is found only in you; it is possible only through you, that is, you are protectors. Therefore we desire the protection which is possible only through you, or the most excellent protection. This is the sense contained here.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Again he asks for the protection of wealth. "And may Parjanya, the flowing one among the waters, protect our wealth; and may the Maruts protect the same. May the two Aśvins protect that wealth. So too Indra and Viṣṇu; all these deities, who are showerers of desires, united, protect our wealth." The meaning is that these deities, having given wealth to us, protect it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—for the waters
- सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*)—Parjanya, who causes them to flow
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- तत् (*tat*)—may he protect that wealth
- तत् (*tat*)—that wealth also
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts also protect

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin deities also protect that wealth
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu
- मीढ्वांसः (*mīḍhvāṃsaḥ*)—all the deities who shower desires
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—gathered together, protect that wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Parjanya, who causes the waters to flow, protect our wealth. May the Maruts also protect that same wealth. May the Aśvin deities protect that wealth. May Indra, Viṣṇu and all the deities who shower desires, gathered together, protect that wealth.

##### English translation
May he who causes the waters to flow (Parjanya), the Maruts,
the Aswins, Indra, Vishnu, may all (these deities) together, the showerers,
(of benefits, protect) that wealth for us.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते हि ष्मा॑ व॒नुषो॒ नरो॒ऽभिमा॑तिं॒ कय॑स्य चित् ।  
> ति॒ग्मं न क्षोदः॑ प्रति॒घ्नंति॒ भूर्ण॑यः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । हि । स्म । वनुषः । नरः । अभिमातिं । कयस्य । चित् ।  
> तिग्मं । न । क्षोदः । प्रतिघ्नंति । भूर्णयः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वनुषो वननीयाः संभजनीया नरो नेतारस्ते हि ष्मा ते खलु देवा
> भूर्णयः क्षिप्रगमनाः संतः कयस्य चित्कस्यचिच्छत्रोरभिमातिमभिमानं प्रतिघ्नंति ।
> प्रतिकूलं यथा भवति कथा हिंसंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । तिग्मं न यथा तिग्मं तीक्ष्णं
> जवेन गच्छत्कॊपद उदकमग्रतः स्थितं वृक्षमुन्मूलयति तद्वत्तस्याभिमानं
> घ्नंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Those leaders, who are to be worshipped and shared in, are quick in movement and strike down the pride of any enemy whatever, so that it turns against him. The illustration: as swift, sharp water running with speed uproots a tree standing before it, so they destroy his pride." This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वनुषः (*vanuṣaḥ*)—the venerable
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—and leaders
- ते हि ष्मा (*te hi ṣmā*)—those same deities
- भूर्णयः (*bhūrṇayaḥ*)—having rapid movement
- कयस्य चित् (*kayasya cit*)—of whatever enemy it may be

### Printed p. 121
- अभिमातिं (*abhimātiṃ*)—the harmful haughtiness (pride)
- तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)—swiftly flowing
- क्षोदः न (*kṣodaḥ na*)—as a flow of water brings down trees and the like standing before it
- प्रतिघ्नंति (*pratighnaṃti*)—falling upon that enemy, they destroy him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those venerable leaders, the deities, having rapid movement, destroy the harmful haughtiness of any enemy, however powerful, by falling upon him as a swiftly flowing stream of water brings down the trees and the like standing before it.

##### English translation
Those desirable leaders (of men), rapid in movement, break down
the haughtiness of any (foe) whatever, as an impetuous current (sweeps
away all obstacles).

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तस्य॑ व्र॒तान्यनु॑ वश्चरामसि ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तस्य । व्रतानि । अनु । वः । चरामसि ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मित्रस्य कर्माण्याह । विश्वतिर्विशां पालयितानयोर्मित्रावरुणयोरेकोऽयं मित्रः पुरु पुरूणि बहूनि चोरूरूणि च द्रव्याणीत्थेत्थं वि चष्टे ।
> स्वतेजसा पश्यति । तस्य मित्रस्य व्रतानि कर्माणि वो युष्मदर्थमनु चरामसि ।
> अनुचरामः । कुर्म इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He speaks of the deeds of Mitra. Mitra, the protector of the people, is the one of the pair Mitra and Varuṇa; he looks upon many and vast things in this way, with his own radiance. "We follow the rites of that Mitra for you", that is, we perform them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वतिः (*viśvatiḥ*)—the protector of the people
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the unequalled
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Mitra
- पुरु (*puru*)—the many
- उरु (*uru*)—and extensive things, all of them
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in this manner
- वि चष्टे (*vi caṣṭe*)—he sees together with his gaze in the form of radiance
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that Mitra
- व्रतानि (*vratāni*)—the rites
- वः (*vaḥ*)—for you
- अनुचरामसि (*anucarāmasi*)—we shall perform (or let us bear)

### Printed p. 122

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Mitra, the protector of the people and unequalled, sees together, with his gaze in the form of radiance, all things, many and extensive. We shall perform the rites of that Mitra for you.

##### English translation
This one, the lord of men (Mitra), contemplates many vast things :
we fallow his rites for you. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अनु॒ पूर्वा॑ण्यो॒क्या॑ साम्रा॒ज्यस्य॑ सश्चिम ।  
> मि॒त्रस्य॑ व्र॒ता वरु॑णस्य दीर्घ॒श्रुत् ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनु । पूर्वाणि । ओक्या । सांराज्यस्य । सश्चिम ।  
> मित्रस्य । व्रता । वरुणस्य । दीर्घश्रुत् ॥ १७ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> साम्राज्यस्य । सम्राजो भावः साम्राज्यं । साम्राज्यमस्यास्तीति साम्राज्यः ॥
> अर्शआदिभ्य इत्यच् प्रत्ययः ॥ साम्राज्यवतो वरुणस्य पूर्वाणि पुराशनान्योक्या ।
> ओको गृहं । तस्मै हितानि कर्माणि वयं सश्चिम ॥ सश्चतिर्गतिकर्मा । लिट रूपं ।
> द्विर्वचनस्य छंदसि विकल्पितत्वादत्र द्विर्वचनाभावः ॥ तदेवाह । मित्रस्य व्रता व्रतानि
> कर्माणि च दीर्घश्रुत् ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति षष्ठ्या लुक् ॥ दीर्घश्रुतोऽतिशयेन
> प्रसिद्धस्य वरुणस्य व्रतानि च सश्चिमेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Of the one who has sovereignty (Varuṇa), we perform the ancient rites that are beneficial to the house (*oka* means house)." The root meaning movement; the verb is perfect in form, and the doubling is optional in the Veda, so it is absent here. He says the same thing: the rites of Mitra, and the rites of Varuṇa, who is widely renowned, we perform.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- साम्राज्यस्य (*sāmrājyasya*)—of Varuṇa, who has the rank of universal sovereign
- पूर्वाणि (*pūrvāṇi*)—ancient
- ओक्या (*okyā*)—and favourable to our houses, those rites
- अनु सश्चिम (*anu saścima*)—we shall perform
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of Mitra
- व्रता (*vratā*)—the rites
- दीर्घश्रुत् (*dīrghaśrut*)—renowned even at a great distance
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—let us perform also the rites of Varuṇa

### Printed p. 123

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We shall perform the ancient rites of Varuṇa, who holds the rank of universal sovereign, rites favourable to our houses. Let us perform also the rites of Mitra and the rites of Varuṇa, who is renowned even at a great distance.

##### English translation
We observe the ancient rites of the imperial Varuna and the renowned
Mitra, (rites) that are good for (our) dwelling.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ यो र॒श्मिना॑ दि॒वोऽन्ता॑न्म॒मे पृ॑थि॒व्याः ।  
> उ॒भे आ प॑प्रौ॒ रोद॑सी महि॒त्वा ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । यः । रश्मिना । दिवः । अंतान् । ममे । पृथिव्याः ।  
> उभे इति । आ । पप्रौ । रोदसी इति । महित्वा ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो मित्रो दिवः पृथिव्या द्यावापृथिव्योरंतान्रश्मिना स्वतेजसा परि ममे
> परिमिनोति । तयोः पर्यंतान् स्वरश्मिना भासयतीत्यर्थः । स एवोभे रोदसी
> द्यावापृथिव्यौ महित्वा स्वमहिम्ना पप्रौ । आसमंतात्पूरयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mitra, who has measured the ends of heaven and earth with his ray, that is, his own radiance, lights up their boundaries with his ray. The same Mitra fills both heaven and earth completely with his greatness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—(and) of the earth
- अंतान् (*aṃtān*)—all the end portions
- रश्मिना (*raśminā*)—with his ray
- परि ममे (*pari mame*)—has measured (has lit up all the worlds)
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—by his greatness (the same god Mitra)
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- आ पप्रौ (*ā paprau*)—has pervaded completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Mitra who has lit up, as if measuring them, all the border regions of the heavenly world and of the earth with his radiance, that same Mitra has pervaded both heaven and earth completely by his greatness.

### Printed p. 124

##### English translation
(Mitra is he) who has measured with his rays the limits of both heaven and earth ; who has filled both heaven and earth with his greatness.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदु॒ ष्य श॑र॒णे दि॒वो ज्योति॑रयंस्त॒ सूर्यः॑ ।  
> अ॒ग्निर्न शु॒क्रः स॑मिधा॒न आहु॑तः ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ऊं इति । स्यः । शरणे । दिवः । ज्योतिः । अयंस्त । सूर्यः ।  
> अग्निः । न । शुक्रः । संइधानः । आहुतः ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यः सुवीर्यः सुष्टु सर्वस्य प्रेरकः स्य स मित्रो वरुणश्च दिवो
> द्योतमानस्यादित्यस्य शरणे स्थाने नभसि ज्योतिरात्मीयं तेज उदयंस्त ।
> उद्यच्छति । ऊर्ध्व० गमयति । सर्वत्र विस्तारयतीत्यर्थः ॥ यमेर्लुज रूपं ॥
> ततः सोऽग्निर्न शुक्रोऽग्निरिव दीप्यमानः समिधानो हविर्भिः समिध्यमान आहुतः
> सर्वैराहूतस्तिष्ठति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The one who is Sūrya, the excellent mover who impels all, that Mitra (and Varuṇa) spread out his own light in the sky, the place of the shining sun, that is, he raises it up and extends it everywhere. Then he stands like a bright Agni, kindled with oblations, invoked by all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—well known in the form of Mitra
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun, the impeller of all (the same Mitra)
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the shining Āditya
- शरणे (*śaraṇe*)—in the atmosphere, his abode
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—his radiance
- उदयंस्त (*udayaṃsta*)—extends and spreads everywhere
- आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)—being worthy of the invocation and worship of all
- समिधानः (*samidhānaḥ*)—and blazing
- अग्निर्न (*agnirna*)—like Agni
- शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—he is full of brightness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The same Mitra, in the form of the sun, the impeller of all, spreads and extends his radiance everywhere in the atmosphere, the abode of the shining Āditya. Worthy of the invocation and worship of all, and blazing, he becomes full of brightness like Agni.

### Printed p. 125

##### English translation
He, Surya, has uplifted his radiance in the region of the heaven ; kindled and invoked with burnt-offerings, he is bright, like Agni.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वचो॑ दी॒र्घप्र॑सद्म॒नीशे॒ वाज॑स्य॒ गोम॑तः ।  
> ईशे॒ हि पि॒त्वो॑ऽवि॒षस्य॑ दा॒वने॑ ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वचः । दीर्घप्रसद्मनि । ईशे वाजस्य । गोऽमतः ।  
> ईशे । हि । पित्वः । अविषस्य । दावने ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतः दीर्घप्रसद्मनि दीर्घं प्रततं विस्त्रतं सद्म सदनं यस्मिन्यज्ञे
> वचः । मित्रं वरुणं च स्तुहि ॥ वक्तेर्लॆट्यडागमः ॥ स वरुणो गोमतः पशुमतो
> वाजस्यान्नस्येशे । ईष्टे । स्वामी भवति । केवलं स्वामी न भवति किंत्वविषस्य
> महतः प्रीतिकारिणः पित्वोऽन्नस्य दावने दानाय चेशे । समर्थो भवति । ये
> स्तोत्रं कुर्वंति तेभ्योऽन्नं ददातीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, in the sacrifice whose hall is long and extended, praise Mitra and Varuṇa. That Varuṇa is lord of food accompanied by cattle; he is not merely owner, but is also able to give the great, pleasing food, he gives food to those who offer praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O praiser) दीर्घप्रसद्मनि (*dīrghaprasadmani*)—in the very long sacrificial hall
- वचः (*vacaḥ*)—recite the words of praise that extol Varuṇa and Mitra
- (स्य (*sya*)—that same Varuṇa)
- गोमतः (*gomataḥ*)—accompanied by cows
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—of food
- ईशे (*īśe*)—is the master
- अविषस्य (*aviṣasya*)—pleasing
- पित्वः (*pitvaḥ*)—of food
- दावने (*dāvane*)—and also of giving
- ईशे हि (*īśe hi*)—he alone is the lord

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, in the very long sacrificial hall recite the words of praise that extol Varuṇa and Mitra. That same Varuṇa is the master of food accompanied by cows. He alone is also the lord of the giving of pleasing food.

### Printed p. 126

##### English translation
Raise your voice in the spacious hall of sacrifice (to him) who is lord over food derived from cattle, who is able to grant nutritious sustenance.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तत्स्यूर्यं॒ रोद॑सी उ॒भे दो॒षा वस्तो॒रुप॑ ब्रुवे ।  
> भो॒जेष्व॒स्मा अ॒भ्युच्च॑रा॒ सदा॑ ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । सूर्यं । रोदसी इति । उभे इति । दोषा । वस्तोः । उप । ब्रुवे ।  
> भोजेषु । अस्मान् । अभि । उत् । चर । सदा ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यं सुवीर्यं तद्वारुणं मैत्रं च तेज उभे रोदसी उभे
> द्यावापृथिव्यौ च दोषा ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति द्वितीयाया लुक् । कालाध्वनोरिति
> द्वितीया ॥ रात्र्य वस्तोरहनि चाहमुप ब्रुवे । उपसौमि । त्वं स्तूयॆमानो
> वरुणो भोजेषु दातृष्टस्मान् सदाभ्युच्चर । सर्वदाभिमुखं प्रेरय ।
> दातृष्टेतेषां दानेष्टस्मान् पुरोभाविनः कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That excellent radiance of Varuṇa and Mitra, and both heaven and earth, by night and by day I praise. You, O Varuṇa, being praised, send us always forward among the generous givers, that is, make us stand before them when they give.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—having excellent valour
- तत् (*tat*)—that same radiance belonging to Mitra and Varuṇa
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- दोषा (*doṣā*)—by night
- वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)—and by day
- उप ब्रुवे (*upa bruve*)—I praise (O Varuṇa)
- भोजेषु (*bhojeṣu*)—toward generous givers
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- अभ्युच्चर (*abhyuccara*)—send forth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise by night and by day that radiance of Mitra and Varuṇa, which has excellent valour, and heaven and earth. O Varuṇa, send us always forward toward generous givers.

### Printed p. 127

##### English translation
I glorify by night and day that sun (Mitra and Varuna), and both
the heaven and earth ; do you (Varuna) ever bring us to the presence of
the bountiful.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒ज्रमु॑क्क्ष॒ण्याय॑ने रज॒तं हर॑याणे ।  
> रथं॑ यु॒क्तम॑सनाम सु॒षाम॑णि ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युद्रं । उक्षण्यायने । रजतं । हरयाणे ।  
> रथं । युक्तं । असनाम । सुसामनि ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुषाम्मः पुत्रो वरुर्नाम राजा । स यद्दानं प्रादाद्विश्वमनसे तदसा
> विश्वमना ऋषिरनयाचष्टे । उक्षण्यायने । उक्षनामा कश्चिद्वरोः पूर्वजः ॥ तस्य
> गोत्रापत्य उक्षण्यबाण्ण्यः । तदंतात्पक्प्रत्ययः । एतौछांदसौ । वृद्धिभावोऽपि
> संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इति न भवति ॥ तस्य गोत्रापत्ये हरयाणे शत्रुजीवितैश्वर्यादिदरणशीलयान एतादृशे सुषामणि । बहुवत्पितृशब्देन पुत्रोऽभिधीयते !
> सुषाम्मः पुत्रे वरौ राजनि ददति सति किमभूत् । ऋज्रमृजुगामिनं रजतं
> रजतमयं रजतसदृशं वा युक्तमश्वाभ्यां युक्तं रथमसनाम । एतेषां
> मित्रादीनां प्रसादाद्वयं संभक्तवंतो लब्धवंतोऽभूम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

There is a king named Varu, son of Suṣāman. The gift which he gave to the seer Viśvamanas, the seer describes by this verse. Ukṣan was a forefather of Varu; a descendant of his line is Ukṣaṇyāyana, and the form is Vedic. The one who is inclined to take away the life, wealth and so on of his enemies; and Suṣāman's son is meant here, the son being denoted by the father's word. When king Varu, the son of Suṣāman, gives, what then happened? We obtained a chariot that goes straight, silver, or like silver, yoked with two horses. By the grace of Mitra and the others we have received it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उक्षण्यायने (*ukṣaṇyāyane*)—who is born of the family of Ukṣan
- हरयाणे (*harayāṇe*)—who takes away the life and wealth of enemies
- सुषामणि (*suṣāmaṇi*)—and is the son of Suṣāman, in Varu
- यज्रं (*yajraṃ*)—which goes straight **NOTE**
- रजतं (*rajataṃ*)—made of silver
- युक्तं (*yuktaṃ*)—yoked with horses
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the chariot
- असनाम (*asanāma*)—we have obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We have obtained the chariot belonging to Varu, who is born of the family of Ukṣan, who takes away the life and wealth of enemies, and who is the son of Suṣāman: a chariot that goes straight, is made of silver and is yoked with horses.

### Printed p. 128

##### English translation
We have received from the son of Sushaman, the descendant of Ukshan, the overcomer (of foes), a well-going chariot of silver, yoked (with a pair of horses).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हरयाणे (*harayāṇe*)—The commentator explains this word as "one inclined to take away the life, wealth and so on of enemies", that is, one who fights and carries off the lives, riches and so on of his enemies. But Yāska explains:
हरयाणः । हरयाणो हरमाणयानः । रजतं हरयाणे इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*harayāṇaḥ | harayāṇo haramāṇayānaḥ | rajataṃ harayāṇe ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 5-15)
Having explained it in this way, he gives the present Ṛk itself as an illustration. The meaning is one who is always travelling, one given to going. Here the word is an epithet of Suṣāmaṇi (the king named Varu, son of Suṣāman). Therefore it may be inferred that the seer used this word to indicate the victorious expeditions of the king Varu, who, out of desire for battle, always marches against enemies (the Dasyus), fights with them and conquers.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता मे॒ अश्वा॑नां॒ हरी॑णां नि॒तोश॑ना ।  
> उ॒तो नु कृत्वा॑नां नृ॒वाह॑सा ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । मे । अश्वानां । हरीणां । नितोशना ।  
> उतो इति । नु । कृत्वानां । नृवाहसा ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिः प्रतिगृहीतावश्वावाह । हरीणां हरितवर्णानामश्वानामश्वसंघानां
> मध्ये नितोशना नितोषनौ । तोशतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । शत्रूणामत्यंतं बाधकृतावुषो
> अपि च कृत्वानां युद्धकर्मणि कुशलानां च नु कुशलमिति बाधकौ नृवाहसा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer speaks of the two horses he has received. Among bay horses, groups of horses, these two are the destroyers of enemies, extreme obstructors of enemies, and among those skilled in the work of battle,
### Printed p. 129

> नृवाहसावायुधनेत्यणां मनुष्याणां वोढारौ ता तावश्व मे मह्यं नु क्षिप्रं
> सौषाम्लैन वरुणा दत्तौ भवेतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

they are the bearers of men, of armed men. May those two horses be quickly given to me by the son of Suṣāman, Varu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—to me
- नु (*nu*)—quickly (given by Varu, son of Suṣāman)
- ता (*tā*)—these two horses
- हरिणां (*hariṇāṃ*)—of the bay-coloured
- अश्वान्यानां (*aśvānyānāṃ*)—among all horses
- नितोशना (*nitośanā*)—they who strongly injure enemies
- उतो (*uto*)—and
- कुल्यानां (*kulyānāṃ*)—the best among horses engaged in the work of battle **NOTE**
- नृवाहसा (*nṛvāhasā*)—and the best in carrying men

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These two horses given to me by Varu, son of Suṣāman, are, among bay-coloured horses, the strong destroyers of enemies, the best among horses engaged in the work of battle, and the best in carrying men.

##### English translation
Among bay horses these two are pre-eminently the destroyers (of foes), and of those eager in combat; the two strong bearers men.

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्मद॑भीशू॒ कशा॑वंता॒ विप्रा॒ नवि॑ष्ठया म॒ती ।  
> म॒हो वा॒जिना॒वर्वं॑ता॒ सचा॑सनं ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)
