##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वे॒ हि ष्मा॒ मन॑वे वि॒श्ववे॑दसो॒ भुव॑न्वृ॒धे रि॒शाद॑सः ।  
> अरि॑ष्टेभिः पा॒युभि॑र्विश्ववेदसो॒ यंता॑ नोवृ॒कं छ॒र्दिः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वे । हि । स्म । मनवे । विश्ववेदसः । भुवन् । वृधे । रिशादसः ।  
> अरिष्टेभिः । पायुभिः । विश्ववेदसः । यंत । नः । अवृकं । छर्दिः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्ववेदसः सर्वशो व्याप्तधनाः । बहुधना इत्यर्थः । तादृशा रिशादसो
> रिशतां हिंसतां शत्रूणामसितार उपक्षपयितारो वा विश्वे हि ष्म सर्वॆ खलु देवा
> मनवे । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । मनोर्वृधे वर्धनाय भुवन् । भवंतु । स्तोत्रे
> मनुष्याय धनं दत्वा तं वधयंतित्याशास्त्रे । ततो हे विश्ववेदसः सर्वधनाः
> सर्वज्ञा वा देवाः अरिष्टेभिः परैरहिंसितैः पायुभिः पालनैः सहावृकं । व्यकः
> स्तेनः । तद्रहितं । बाधारहितमित्यर्थः । तादृशं छर्दिगृहं नोऽस्मभ्यं यंत ।
> प्रयच्छत । शत्रून्हत्वा गृहेष्टस्माभिः कर्माणि कारयतेश्यर्थः ॥ यंतेति यमेर्लोटि छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । तस्य तबादेशः । तेनानुनासिकलोपाभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viśvavedasaḥ are those whose wealth is spread on all sides, that is, those of much wealth. Such are the rishādasaḥ, the devourers or those who destroy the enemies who do harm. All the gods, for Manu (the dative has the sense of the genitive), be for the increase of Manu. Having given wealth to a man who praises them, they make him prosper, so the text says. **NOTE** Then, O gods, all-wealthy or all-knowing, together with unharmed protections, that is, guardians not injured by others, give us a chardis, a house, that is avṛka. A vṛka is a thief, so the word means free from him, free from hindrance. The meaning is: having slain the enemies, cause rites to be performed by us in our house.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*)—those who possess all wealth
- रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*)—destroyers of enemies
- विश्वे हि ष्म (*viśve hi ṣma*)—all the gods
- मनवे (*manave*)—of Manu
- वृधे (*vṛdhe*)—for the increase
- भुवन् (*bhuvan*)—may they be close beside him **NOTE**
- विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*)—O gods who know all things
- अरिष्टेभिः (*ariṣṭebhiḥ*)—not harmed by others
- पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*)—with protections
- अवृकं (*avṛkaṃ*)—free from harm
- छर्दिः (*chardiḥ*)—a house
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- यंत (*yaṃta*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods, who possess all wealth and destroy enemies, be close beside Manu for his increase. O gods who know all things, give us a house free from harm, together with protections that no one has harmed.

##### English translation
May the universal deities possessors of all opulence, destroyers of foes, be (nigh) to Manu for his prosperity : do you, who know all things,

### Printed p. 163
secure to us an abode safe from robbers through your unassailable protections.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॑ अ॒द्य सम॑नसो॒ गंता॒ विश्वे॑ स॒जोष॑सः ।  
> ऋ॒चा गि॒रा मरु॑तो॒ देव्यदि॑ते॒ सद॑ने॒ पस्यॆ॑ महि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । अद्य । समनसः । गंत । विश्वे । सजोषसः ।  
> ऋचा । गिरा । मरुतः । देवि । आदिते । सदने । पस्यॆ । महि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समनसः सर्वेषु स्तोत्रेषु समानमनस्का विश्वे सर्वॆ देवा यूयं
> सजोषसः परस्परं संगताः संतो गिरा । शुशूषुतया 'प्राप्तव्ययेत्यर्थः ।
> तयर्चा सहाद्यास्मिन्यागदिने नो यष्टनस्माना गंते । आगच्छत । अनंतरं हे
> मरुतो देवि द्योतमाने महि महति देवानां मातृत्वान्महत्त्वयुक्ते हे
> आदितेऽदीन एतन्नामिके देवि सदने स्थाने पस्यॆऽस्मदीये गृहे स्तोतव्यतयोपविशत ॥ मरुत इत्यादर्वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ! उत्तरत्र पूर्वस्यामंत्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन वाक्यादित्वादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O all gods, of one mind in all the stotras and united with one another, come to us today with the praise, that is, with the ṛc, to this sacrifice (the words explaining the praise are damaged). **NOTE** Then, O Maruts; O shining one, the great one, who are endowed with greatness because she is the mother of the gods; O Aditi, goddess so named: sit in the place, in our house, as those who are to be praised.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समनसः (*samanasaḥ*)—of one mind with regard to the praiser
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—O Viśve Devāḥ
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—you who have come together
- गिरा (*girā*)—in the form of praise
- ऋचा (*ṛcā*)—with the Ṛk
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ गंत (*ā gaṃta*)—be pleased to come
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- देवि (*devi*)—who are divine in nature
- महि (*mahi*)—who are of great nature
- अदिते (*adite*)—O goddess Aditi
- सदसे (*sadase*)—in the place of the sacrifice
- पस्यॆ (*pasyè*)—be seated in our house

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viśve Devāḥ, of one mind with regard to the praiser, come together to us at this time of the sacrifice with the Ṛk, which is in the form of praise. O Maruts, and O goddess Aditi, divine in nature and of great nature, be seated in our house, the place of the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 164

##### English translation
Universal deities, united together and of one mind, come this day to us, (attracted) by the sacred praise addressed to you ; and do you, Maruts, and the mighty goddess Aditi, (come) to the dwelling, (our) abode

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि प्रि॒या म॑रुतो॒ या वो॒ अश्वा॑ ह॒व्या मि॑त्र प्रया॒थन॑ ।  
> आ ब॒र्हिरिंद्रो॒ वरु॑णस्तु॒रा नर॑ आदि॒त्यासः॑ सदंतु नः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । प्रिया । मरुतः । या । वः । आश्वा । हव्या । मित्र । प्रयार्थन ।  
> आ । बर्हिः । इंद्रः । वरुणः । तुराः । नरः । आदित्यासः । सदंतु । नः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः प्रिया प्रियाणि या यानि वो युष्माकमश्वाश्च्यानि प्रियानश्वसंघानभि प्रयाथन । अस्मद्यज्ञं प्रति प्रापयत । यूयमश्वैर्युक्ताः संत
> आगच्छतेत्यर्थः । आथ हे मित्र । मित्रशब्देनान्ये वरुणादयोऽप्युच्यंते । हे
> मित्रादयो देवाः हव्या हव्यानि हवनयोग्यानि हवींषि स्वीकर्तुमागच्छतेत्यर्थः।
> सूयमाना आगच्छत ॥ प्रपूर्वाद्यातेर्लोटि तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चति धनादेशः ॥ अगत्य
> चेंद्रो वरुण इंद्रावरुणौ तुराः संग्रामे शत्रुवधार्थं त्वरमाणा नरो नेतार
> आदित्यासोऽदितेः पुत्रा मरुदादयो देवाश्च नोऽस्मदीये यज्ञॆ बर्हिबर्हिप्यासादित आ सदंतु । आसीदंतु । प्रविशंतु ॥ सदेः सीदादेशाभावश्चांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, the horses of yours that are dear, those teams of horses, bring them to our sacrifice; come yoked to your horses. Then, O Mitra: by the word Mitra the others, Varuṇa and the rest, are also addressed. O gods, Mitra and the others, come to accept the oblations that are fit for the offering (the words that follow, beginning सूयमाना (*sūyamānā*), are unclear). **NOTE** Further, Indra and Varuṇa (the Indra-Varuṇa pair), who hasten in battle to slay the enemies, the leaders, the Ādityas, the sons of Aditi, and the Maruts and the other gods, sit on the sacred grass that has been laid in our sacrifice; enter it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- या (*yā*)—which horses
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to you
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—are dear, such
- अश्वा (*aśvā*)—horses
- अभि प्रयाथन (*abhi prayāthana*)—urge on to our sacrifice
- मित्र (*mitra*)—O Mitra
- हव्या (*havyā*)—be pleased to accept our oblations
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- तुराः (*turāḥ*)—those who are skilled in battle **NOTE**
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—leaders
- आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*)—the Ādityas
- नः (*naḥ*)—in this sacrifice of ours
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—on the sacred grass
- आ सदंतु (*ā sadaṃtu*)—let them sit

### Printed p. 165

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, urge the horses that are dear to you to come to our sacrifice. O Mitra, be pleased to accept our oblations. May Indra and Varuṇa, and the Ādityas, who are skilled in battle and are leaders, sit on the sacred grass in this sacrifice of ours.

##### English translation
Direct, Maruts, your beloved horses (to our rite) : Mitra, (come to our) oblations; and may Indra, and Varuna and the swift leaders, the the Adityas, sit down on our sacred grass.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒यं वो॑ वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषो हि॒तप्र॑यस आनु॒षक् ।  
> सु॒तसो॑मासो वरुण हवामहे मनु॒ष्पदि॒द्दाग्न॑यः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वयं । वः । वृक्तबर्हिषः । हितप्रयसः । अनुषक् ।  
> सुतसोमासः । वरुण । हवामहे । मनुष्यत् । इद्दआग्नयः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुण वरुणादयो हे देवाः व्यक्तबर्हिष ऋत्विजो वयमानुषक्
> सुगादिष्पनुषक्तं यथा भवति तथा हितप्रयसः । प्रीणातीति प्रयोऽन्नं । तेषु
> निहितहविष्काः संतो वो युष्मान् हवामहे । एतानि हवींप्यादातुमाह्वयामः।
> कीदृशाः । सुतसोमासोऽभिषुतसोमा इद्दाग्नय आहुतिभिः समिद्धाग्नयो
> वयमाह्वयामः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । मनुष्वत् । मनुर्यथा यज्ञे युष्मानाजुहाव तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa and the other gods, we priests, with the sacred grass trimmed, in due order and with foods set out (prayas is food, that which pleases), having laid oblations in those foods, call you to take these oblations. What kind of priests? Those who have pressed the Soma and those who have kindled the fires with oblations. We invite you; the example is manuṣvat: as Manu called you in the sacrifice, so do we. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa and the other gods
- व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*)—those who prepare and make ready the sacred grass seat
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—in due order
- हितप्रयसः (*hitaprayasaḥ*)—who have the oblations that are offered
- सुतसोमासः (*sutasomāsaḥ*)—who have pressed and prepared the Soma
- इद्दाग्नयः (*iddāgnayaḥ*)—who have caused the fire to blaze with oblations

### Printed p. 166
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we (the priests)
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*)—as Manu in former times prayed to you and called you
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we also call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa and the other gods, we priests, who have prepared the sacred grass seat, who have the oblations to offer to you in due order, who have pressed and prepared the Soma and who have caused the fire to blaze with oblations, call you to our sacrifice as Manu in former times praised and called you.

##### English translation
Bearing the clipped sacred grass, offering in due order the(sacrificial) food, presenting the effused Soma, and having the fires kindled, we invoke you, Varuna, (and the rest), as did Manu.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ प्र या॑त॒ मरु॑तो॒ विष्णो॒ अश्वि॑ना॒ पूष॒न्माकी॑नया धि॒या ।  
> इंद्र॒ आ या॑तु प्रथ॒मः स॑नि॒ष्युभि॒र्वृषा॒ यो वृ॑त्र॒हा गृ॒णे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । प्र । यात । मरुतः । विष्णो इति । अश्विना । पूषन् । माकीनया । धिया ।  
> इंद्रः । आ । यातु । प्रथमः । सनिष्युभिः । वृषा । यः । वृत्रहा । गृणे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विश्वे देवाः प्र यात । प्रकर्षणास्मदीयकर्माण्यागच्छत । हे मरुतो
> हे विष्णो स्वबलेन सर्वतो व्याप्तैतन्नामक देव हे अश्विनाश्विन् पूषन् ।
> स्तोत्थानादिना पोषयतीति पूषा । एतन्नामक देव मरुदादयो देवाः
> माकीनया ॥ अस्मच्छब्दाद्युष्मदस्मदोः । पा. ४-३-१ । इति खञ् शैषिकः । ऐकदचने
> तवकममकाविति ममकादेशः । वर्णलोपश्रांदसः ॥ मया क्रियमाणया धिया
> स्तुत्या सहास्मद्यज्ञं प्रत्यागच्छत ॥ मरुदादेरामंत्रितस्य वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥
> किंच प्रथमो देवानां मुख्यः स इंद्रश्चा यातु । वृषा कामानां सेक्ता य
> इंद्रः सनिष्युभिः । सनिः संभजनं । तदात्मन इच्छद्भिः स्तोतृभिर्वत्रहापामावरकस्य
> वृत्रासुरस्य हंतेति गृणे स्तूयते ॥ गृ शब्द इत्यस्य कर्मणि लिट छांदसो विकरणः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Viśve Devāḥ, come forth; come to our rites. O Maruts; O Viṣṇu, the deity so named, who pervades everywhere by his own strength; O Aśvins; O Pūṣan, who nourishes by praise and the like, the deity so named: and the Maruts and the other gods, come to our sacrifice with the praise made by me, माकीनया (*mākīnayā*) (that is, made by me). Further, Indra also, first, that is, chief among the gods, let him come: he is the showerer, the one who pours out the desires. Sanisyubhiḥ means by praisers who desire the sharing (sani is partaking) of that. He is the slayer of Vṛtra, the demon who covers the waters, and so he is praised.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- विष्णो (*viṣṇo*)—O Viṣṇu
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O god Pūṣan
- माकीनया (*mākīnayā*)—recited by me
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—pleased with the praise
- आ प्रयात (*ā prayāta*)—all of you, come

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- सनिष्युभिः (*saniṣyubhiḥ*)—by his worshippers
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—as the slayer of Vṛtra
- गृणे (*gṛṇe*)—is praised, such a one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, O Viṣṇu, O Aśvin deities, O god Pūṣan, pleased with the praise recited by me, come, all of you. May Indra also come to us, Indra who is chief among the gods, the showerer of desires, whom his worshippers praise as the slayer of Vṛtra.

Maruts, Aswins, Pushan, come hither (induced) by my praise : may Indra, the first (of the gods). also come, the showerer (of benefits), he who is praised by (his) worshippers as the slayer of Vritra.

> न यद्दू॒राद्व॑सवो॒ नू चि॒दंति॑तो॒ वरू॑थमाद॒धर्ष॑ति ॥ ९ ॥

> वि । नः । देवासः । अद्रुहः । अच्छिद्रं । शर्म । यच्छत ।  
> न । यत् । दूरात् । वसवः । नु । चित् । अंतितः । वरूथं । आदधर्षति ॥ ९ ॥

> हे अद्रुहः स्तोतृणामद्रोग्यारः । यद्वा ॥ म्रुहेर्णादिकः कर्मणि
> क्विप् ॥ शत्रुभिरहिंस्याः । हे देवासो मरुदादयो देवाः अच्छिद्रं बाधकरहितं
> साधीयो वा शर्म । शृणाति दुःखादिकमिति शर्म गृहं । तन्नोऽस्मभ्यं वि यॆच्छत ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adruhaḥ, you who do not injure the praisers, or else you who cannot be harmed by enemies; O gods, Maruts and the others, give us a house (śarma, so called because it breaks sorrow and the like) that is faultless, free from obstruction, or very good. Give that to us.

### Printed p. 168

> हे वसवः शत्रूणां वासयितारो मरुदादयः दूराद्दूरदेशादंतितोऽंतिकदेशाद्वा कश्चिदागत्य नू चित्कदाचिदपि वरूथं वरणीयं संभजनीयं यद्गृहं
> नादधर्षति आधर्षणं हिंसनं न करोति तद्गृहं प्रयच्छतेति समन्वयः ॥ धृष
> प्रसहन इत्यस्य विभाषितणिच त्वात् यदा णिच् नास्ति तदा रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasus, Maruts and the others, who cause the enemies to dwell: whatever house is such that no one, coming from afar or from near, at any time assails or harms it, that desirable house, to be partaken of, give to us. This is the construction. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)—O you who do no harm
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O gods, Maruts and the others
- अच्छिद्रं (*acchidraṃ*)—faultless
- शर्म (*śarma*)—a house
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- वि यच्छत (*vi yacchata*)—give
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—O Maruts and the others, who overthrow enemies
- यत् (*yat*)—which house
- दूरात् (*dūrāt*)—from afar
- अंतितः (*aṃtitaḥ*)—from a near place also
- नू चित् (*nū cit*)—at any time (by anyone)
- न आदधर्षत् (*na ādadharṣat*)—cannot be harmed, such
- वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)—give an excellent house

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts and the other gods, who do no harm, give us a house free from fault. O Maruts and the others, who overthrow enemies, give us an excellent house, such that no one, whether from afar or from near, can besiege and harm it.

##### English translation
Unoppressive deities, bestow upon us a mansion without defect, so that, subduers (of foes), no one may injure our defences, whether from afar or nigh.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्ति॒ हि वः॑ सजा॒त्यं॑ रिशादसो॒ देवा॑सो॒ अस्ताप्यं॑ ।  
> प्र णः॒ पूर्व॑स्मै सुवि॒ताय॑ वोचत म॒क्षू सु॒म्नाय॒ नव्य॑से॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्ति । हि । वः । सजात्यं । रिशादसः । देवासः । अस्ति । अप्यं ।  
> प्र । नः । पूर्वस्मै । सुविताय । वोचत । मक्षु । सुम्नाय । नव्यसे ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 169

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे रिशादसो रिशतां हिंसतामसितारो देवासो देवा द्योतमाना
> मरुदादयः वो युष्माकं सजात्यमस्ति । परस्परं समानजातिभावोऽस्ति खलु ।
> किंचाप्यं । आपिर्बंधुः । तस्य भाव आप्यं । स्तोतृषु स्तुत्यलक्षणेन संबंधाद्वैवस्वतेन मनुना मया स्तोत्रा सह युष्माकं बंधुभावोऽस्ति खलु । ततः
> पूर्वस्मै प्रथमभाविने सुविताय । सुष्टीयते सर्वैरागम्यत इति सुवितोऽभ्युदयः । तस्मै नव्यसे नवीयसे नवतराय सुम्माय च उभयं मक्षु शीघ्रं
> नोऽस्माकं प्र वोचत । प्रकर्षण ब्रूत । अभ्युदयधनानि प्रयच्छतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O destroyers of the enemies who do harm, O shining gods, Maruts and the others: there is among you the condition of one kind (sajātya); you are of the same class with one another. Further, there is āpya: āpi is a kinsman, and his state is āpya. Through the relation that consists in praise, there is kinship between you and me, the praiser, Manu Vaivasvata. Therefore, for the earlier, first-arising suvita (what all attain well, prosperity), and for the newer, the very new, sumna (happiness): both of these, speak forth to us quickly. The meaning is: give us prosperity and wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*)—you who harm the enemies
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O gods
- वः (*vaḥ*)—among you
- सजात्यं (*sajātyaṃ*)—a relation of belonging to one group
- अस्ति हि (*asti hi*)—there is, is there not
- आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)—your kinship with your praisers
- अस्ति (*asti*)—there is
- पूर्वस्मै (*pūrvasmai*)—that has come from before
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—for prosperity
- नव्यसे (*navyase*)—new
- सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*)—for happiness
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- प्र वोचत (*pra vocata*)—recite the blessing (svasti-vācana)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, who harm the enemies, there is indeed a relation among you of belonging to one group. Your relation with your praisers is also well known. Recite the blessing for us quickly, for the prosperity that has come from before and for new happiness.

##### English translation
There is identity of race among you, deities, destroyers of foes ; there is kindred (with me your worshipper) ; therefore utter at once the command for our former prosperity and for new happiness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Rishādasaḥ: रिशतां हिंसतामसितारः (*riśatāṃ hiṃsatāmasitāraḥ*). Those who put down, who harm, the enemy people who do harm; that is, those who harm and kill enemies, destroyers of enemies, is the meaning. Yāska. For this word:
रिशादसः । अस्ति हि वः सजात्यं रिशादसो देवासो अस्त्याप्यं । अस्ति हि वः समानजातिता रेशयदारिणो देवाः । अस्त्याप्यं । आप्यमाप्नोषेः ॥ (*riśādasaḥ | asti hi vaḥ sajātyaṃ riśādaso devāso astyāpyaṃ | asti hi vaḥ samānajātitā reśayadāriṇo devāḥ | astyāpyaṃ | āpyamāpnoṣeḥ ‖*) (3. 6-14). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 170
The gods harm and kill the enemy people who needlessly do violence to others. Since this quality is seen in all the gods, it is said that there is a kind of kinship among the gods. The word āpya is derived from the root āpḷ vyāptau, meaning to obtain, and here it indicates the sense of kinship; so the explanation (nirvacana) has been given.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दा हि व॒ उप॑स्तुतिमि॒दा वा॒मस्य॑ भ॒क्तये॑ ।  
> उप॑ वो विश्ववेदसो नम॒स्कुरा असृ॒क्षन्या॑मिव ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदा । हि । वः । उपस्तुतिं । इदा । वामस्य । भक्तये ।  
> उप । वः । विश्ववेदसः । नमस्युः । आ । असृक्षि । अन्यां इव ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विश्ववेदसः सर्वधना हे देवाः नमस्युरन्नमिच्छन् मनुरहं वो
> युष्मद्विषयामुपस्तुतिमन्यामिवादृष्टपूर्वामिव स्थितां । कैश्चिदप्यकृतामित्यर्थः ।
> तादृशीमुपस्तुतिमिदा हि । हिरवधारणे । इदानीमेवोपासृक्षि । उपासृजामि ।
> करोमीत्यर्थः । किमर्थ० । वो युष्मत्संबंधिनो वामस्य वननीयस्येदेदानीमेव भक्तये संभजनाय । लाभायेत्यर्थः ॥ अस्पृक्षीति सृजेर्लुजि रूपं ।
> पादादित्वादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O all-wealthy gods: I, Manu, namasyu, desiring food, now indeed compose the praise relating to you, a praise that is as if of another, as if unseen before; the meaning is that no one has made it. Why? For the vāma, the desirable thing belonging to you, to partake of it now, that is, for gain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*)—O gods who possess all wealth
- नमस्युः (*namasyuḥ*)—I who desire food
- वः (*vaḥ*)—that belongs to you
- वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—and is attractive, wealth and the like
- इदा (*idā*)—now
- भक्तये (*bhaktaye*)—in order to obtain
- वः (*vaḥ*)—that praises you
- उपस्तुतिं (*upastutiṃ*)—the hymn
- अन्यां इव (*anyāṃ iva*)—as if newly made, not recited by others
- इदा हि (*idā hi*)—now
- उप आ अस्पृक्षि (*upa ā aspṛkṣi*)—having made it, I recite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods who possess all wealth, I, who desire food, make now the hymn that praises you, as if newly made, not made or recited by others, and recite it now, in order to obtain at once the wealth and the like that belong to you and are attractive.

### Printed p. 171

##### English translation
Deities, possessed of all wealth, I, desirous of offering worship, address to you verily unprecedented praise, for the sake of obtaining desired affluence.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदु॒ ष्य वः॑ सवि॒ता सु॑प्रणीत॒योऽस्था॑दू॒र्ध्वो वरे॑ण्यः ।  
> नि द्वि॒पाद॒श्चतु॑ष्पादो अ॒र्थिनोऽवि॑श्रन्पतयि॒ष्णवः॑ ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ऊं इति । स्यः । वः । सविता । सुप्रनीतयः । अस्थात् । ऊर्ध्वः । वरेण्यः ।  
> नि । द्विपादः । चतुःऽपादः । अर्थिनः । अविश्रन् । पतॆयिष्णवः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुप्रणीतयः । शोभनप्रणीति स्तुतिः । शोभनप्रणयनाः शोभनस्तुतयो
> मरुतः वो युष्माकं मध्य ऊर्ध्व ऊर्ध्व० गंता वरेण्यः सर्वैर्वर्णीयः
> संभजनीयः स सविता सर्वस्य स्वकर्मणि प्रेरक एतन्नामकः स देवो यदोदस्थात
> स्वतेजसोद्धतोऽभूत् तदार्थिनो द्विपादो पादद्वययुक्ताः पुरुषाश्चतुष्पादः
> पादचतुष्टययुक्ता आश्वादयः पतयिष्णवः पतनशीलाः दक्षिणश्च न्यविश्रन् ।
> स्वस्वकार्येषु निविशंते । सूर्य उदिते केचन पुरुषा अग्निहोत्रादिकं कुर्वंति
> केचन देवताविषयं स्तोत्रं कुर्वंति । पश्वादयस्तृणादिभक्षणार्थं सर्वत्र
> संचरंति ॥ न्यविश्रन् । निपूर्वाद्विशतेर्लज व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । बहुलं छंदसीति
> रुडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Suprāṇītayaḥ, those of good praise, the Maruts: the word means those who have good guidance, good praises. When that Savitṛ, the deity so named, the impeller of everyone in his own work, who goes upward among you, to be chosen and partaken of by all, rises up (udasthāt: has risen, uplifted by his own radiance), then those who are in need, the bipeds, men with two feet, the quadrupeds, horses and the like with four feet, and the flying ones, those that tend to fly, and the birds, enter upon their own tasks. **NOTE** When the sun has risen some men perform the agnihotra and the like, some make praise of the deities, and animals and the rest roam everywhere to eat grass and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुप्रणीतयः (*supraṇītayaḥ*)—O Maruts, worthy of excellent praise
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- वः (*vaḥ*)—among you
- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—who moves upward
- वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—worthy of worship by all
- स्यः सविता (*syaḥ savitā*)—Savitṛ, the impeller of the world
- उदस्थात् (*udasthāt*)—appears with his radiances (then)
- अर्थिनः (*arthinaḥ*)—who strive to accomplish each his own desired ends
- द्विपादः (*dvipādaḥ*)—men who have two feet
- चतुष्पादः (*catuṣpādaḥ*)—horses and the like that have four feet
- हतयिष्णवः (*hatayiṣṇavaḥ*)—the birds that fly about
- नि अविश्रन् (*ni aviśran*)—are intent on their own tasks

### Printed p. 172

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, worthy of excellent praise, when Savitṛ, who moves upward among you, worthy of worship by all, the impeller of the world, the renowned, appears with his radiances, then men who have two feet, horses and the like that have four feet, and the birds that fly about, all striving to accomplish their own desired ends, are intent on their own tasks.

##### English translation
Devoutly praised (Maruts), when the adorable Savitri has risen above you, then bipeds and quadrupeds, and the flying birds seeking (their objects), enter (upon their fuuctions).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवंऽदेवं । वः । अवसे । देवंऽदेवं । अभिष्टये ।  
> देवंऽदेवं । हुवेम । वाजसातये । गृणंतः । देव्या । धिया ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पंचमेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे देवंदेवमिति वैश्वदेवस्त्रृचः । सूत्रितं च ।
> देवंदेवं बृहदु गायिषे वचः । आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥
> वयं देव्या द्योतमानया धिया स्तुत्या गृणंतः स्तुवंतः संतो वो
> युष्माकं मध्ये देवं देवं दीप्यमानं देवमवसे कर्मरक्षणायाह्वयाम ।
> अनुक्रमेणाह । अभिष्टयेऽभिलषितप्राप्त्यर्थं च देवं देवं वयमाह्सयाम ।
> ततो वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभाय हुवेम । ह्वयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the fifth day, in the प्रउगशस्त्रे (*praugaśastre*), the triplet beginning देवंदेवमिति (*devaṃdevamiti*) is addressed to the Viśve Devāḥ; the sūtra is cited as Ā. 7-12, beginning देवंदेवं बृहदु गायिषे वचः (*devaṃdevaṃ bṛhadu gāyiṣe vacaḥ*). We, praising with shining praise, call, among you, each shining god for the protection of our rite. He says it in order: for the obtaining of what we desire we call each god; then for the gain of food we call.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- O gods
- देव्या (*devyā*)—with shining
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—praise
- गृणंतः (*gṛṇaṃtaḥ*)—we who praise
- वः (*vaḥ*)—who are among you
- देवंदेवं (*devaṃdevaṃ*)—each god

### Printed p. 173

- अवसे (*avase*)—for our protection we call
- देवंदेवं (*devaṃdevaṃ*)—each deity
- अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*)—for the accomplishment of our desires also we call
- वाजसाकये (*vājasākaye*)—for the gain of food also
- देवंदेवं (*devaṃdevaṃ*)—each god
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, praising with shining praise, we call each deity among you for our protection. We call each deity also for the accomplishment of our desires. We call each deity also for the gain of food.

##### English translation
We would invoke each deity among you (gods) for protection, each
deity for the attianment of our desires, each deity for the acquisition of
food, glorifying you with divine praise.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the fifth day of the sacrifice, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Prauga-śastra, the three Ṛks beginning with देवंदेवं (*devaṃdevaṃ*) are to be recited as the Vaiśvadeva triplet; this is elucidated by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, देवंदेवं बृहदु गायिषे वचः (*devaṃdevaṃ bṛhadu gāyiṣe vacaḥ*) (Ā. 7-12).

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वासो॒ हि ष्मा॒ मन॑वे॒ सम॑न्यवो॒ विश्वे॑ सा॒कं सरा॑तयः ।  
> ते नो॑ अ॒द्य ते अ॑प॒रं तु॒चे तु नो॒ भवं॑तु वरिवो॒विदः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवासः । हि । स्म । मनवे । समन्यवः । विश्वे । साकं । सरातयः ।  
> ते । नः । आद्य । ते । अपरं । तुचे । तु । नः । भवंतु । वरिवःविदः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समन्वयः समानमनसः यद्वा संग्रामेषु शत्रुहननार्थं समानक्रोधयुक्ता विश्वे सर्व एव देवासो हि ष्म मरुदादयो देवाः खलु मनव एतन्नामकार्यार्षये मह्यं साकं सह युगपदेव सरातयो धनादिदानेन सहिता भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Samanyavaḥ means of one mind; or, in battles, possessed of the same anger for the slaying of enemies. All the gods, the Maruts and the rest, being such, may be together, at one and the same time, givers of wealth and the like to me, Manu, the Ārya seer of that name.

### Printed p. 174

> पुनरपि प्रार्थयते । ते देवा नोऽस्माकमद्यास्मिन्निनेऽपरं च किं बहुना सर्वॆषु
> दिवसेषु धनदातारो भवंतु । न केवलमस्माकमेव किंतु तुचे । तुगित्युपत्यनाम॥
> तुजि पिजि हिंसादाननिकेतनेषु ॥ तोजयति हिनस्ति पितुर्दुःखादिकमिति तुक् पुत्रः ।
> तस्मै नोऽस्माकं पुत्राय वरिवोविदो वरणीयस्य धनस्य लंभयितारो
> भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He prays again. May those gods, today and afterwards (what need of more words: on all days), be givers of wealth to us. Not to us alone, but also to our offspring. Tuc is a name for offspring; the root tuj and the root pij have the senses of injuring, giving and dwelling; he who injures, that is, removes, his father's sorrow and the like, is tuk, a son. To that son of ours may they be procurers of the choicest wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समन्यवः (*samanyavaḥ*)—possessed of one mind
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- देवासो हि ष्म (*devāso hi ṣma*)—the gods also
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together, united
- मनने (*manane*)—to me, named Manu
- सरातयः (*sarātayaḥ*)—be givers of wealth
- ते (*te*)—those same gods
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- अपरं (*aparaṃ*)—on the remaining days
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us also
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- तुचे (*tuce*)—to sons and the like also
- वरिवोविदः (*varivovidaḥ*)—as givers of abundant wealth
- भवंतु (*bhavaṃtu*)—may they be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods, of one mind, together be givers of wealth to me, who am named Manu. May those same gods, today and on the remaining days, be givers of abundant wealth to us and to our sons and the rest.

##### English translation
May the universal gods with one consent be together the givers (of riches) to Manu ; may they, both to-day and hereafter, be the bestowers of wealth upon us and upon our posterity.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वः॑ शंसाम्यद्रुहः सं॒स्थ उप॑स्थुतीनां ।  
> न तं धू॒र्तिर्व॑रुण मित्र॒ मर्त्यं॒ योवो॒ थाम॒भ्योऽवि॑धत्॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वः । शंसामि । अद्रुहः । संस्थे । उपस्तुतीनां ।  
> न । तं । धूर्तिः । वरुण । मित्रे । मर्त्यं । यः । वः । धामभ्यः । अविधत् ॥ १५ ॥

### Printed p. 175

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अद्रुहोऽद्रोग्धारोऽहिंस्या वा मरुदादयः उपस्तुतीनामुपस्तोत्राणां संस्थॆ तासां यज्ञे क्रियमाणत्वादस्मत्स्थानभूतेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे वो
> युष्मान् प्र शंसामि । प्रकर्षेण सौमि । हे वरुण मित्र मित्रावरुणौ तं मर्त्यं
> मनुष्यं धूर्तिः ॥ धुर्वी हिंसार्थः ॥ शत्रुभ्यो हिंसा: तं न बाधते यो
> मनुष्यो वो युष्माकं धामभ्यस्तेजोभ्यः । धीयतेऽस्मिन्निति धाम शरीरं वा ।
> तेभ्योऽविधत् ॥ विध विधाने ॥ हवींषि विदधाति प्रयच्छति । एतेन तेजसामपि
> हविर्भक्षणमस्तीति ज्ञायते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O non-hostile (or inviolable) Maruts and others, in the sacrifice, which is the place of the praises (since those praises are made in it) and is therefore our own place, I praise you, I extol you excellently. O Varuṇa and Mitra, that mortal, that man, no affliction (dhūrti, from the root dhurv, injuring: injury from enemies) harms, who offers to your lustres; dhāma is the lustre, or else the body, since the self is placed in it. He offers, that is, gives, oblations to them. From this it is known that even lustres have a taking of oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)—O Maruts and others, free from injury
- उपस्तुतीनां (*upastutīnāṃ*)—joined with praises
- संस्थॆ (*saṃsthè*)—in the sacrifice
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- प्र शंसामि (*pra śaṃsāmi*)—I praise
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- मित्र (*mitra*)—O Mitra
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which man
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- धामभ्यः (*dhāmabhyaḥ*)—to the lustres
- अविधत् (*avidhat*)—offers worship
- तं मर्त्यं (*taṃ martyaṃ*)—that man
- धूर्तिः (*dhūrtiḥ*)—the affliction of the enemy
- न (*na*)—does not injure

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts and others, free from injury, in this sacrifice joined with praises I praise you. O Varuṇa, O Mitra, the affliction of the enemy does not injure that man who offers worship to your lustres.

##### English translation
I glorify you, innocuous deities, in the place of praises : no harm befalls the man who, Mitra and Varuna, offers (oblations) to your glories.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र स क्षयं॑ तिरते॒ वि म॒हीरिषो॒ यो वो॒ वरा॑य॒ दाश॑ति ।  
> प्र प्र॒जाभि॑र्जायते॒ धर्म॑ण॒स्पर्यरि॑ष्टः॒ सर्व॑ एधते ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । सः । क्षयं । तिरते । वि । महीः । इषः । यः । वः । वराय । दाशति ।  
> प्र । प्रजाभिः । जायते । धर्मणः । परि । अरिष्टः । सर्वः । विधते ॥ १६ ॥

### Printed p. 176

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुदादयः स मनुष्यः क्षयं । क्षियंति निवसंत्यत्रेति क्षयो गृहः ।
> तत्स मनुष्यः प्र तिरते । प्रकर्षण वर्धयति । तिरतिर्वृद्धिकर्मा । स एव महीर्महांतीषोऽन्नानि च वि वर्धयति यो मनुष्यो वराय वरणीयाय धनाय
> तदर्थं वो युष्मभ्यं दाशति हवींषि प्रयच्छति । धनादिभिर्वर्धयतीत्यन्वयः ।
> किंच धर्मणः । ध्रियत ऋत्विग्निरिति धर्म कर्म । युष्मद्विषयात्कर्मणः सकाशात्स
> मनुष्यः प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः परि परितः सर्वतः प्र जायते । प्रकर्षणाविर्भवति ।
> आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि । शत. १४-९-४-२६ । इति श्रुतेः । ततोऽरिष्टोऽन्यैरहिंसितः
> सर्वो युष्माकं हविष्पदानात्सकलो जन विधते । धनादिभिर्वर्धते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts and others, that man makes his kṣaya grow; kṣaya is the house, where people dwell (the root kṣi). He makes it grow excellently; tirati has the sense of growth. The same man makes great foods also grow, the man who gives, that is, offers oblations to you for the sake of choice wealth (vara, that which is to be chosen). The construction is: he makes them grow with wealth and the like. Further, from dharman: the priest bears the rite (dhriyate), and dharma means the rite. From the rite directed to you, that man is born forth on every side with offspring, with sons, grandsons and the rest, that is, he appears excellently. The Vedic text is आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि (*ātmā vai putranāmāsi*) (Śata. 14-9-4-26) **GLOSS** **NOTE**. Then, unharmed by others, every person prospers by the giving of oblations to you, increases with wealth and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- O Maruts and the other gods
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which man
- वराय (*varāya*)—as one seeking excellent wealth
- वः (*vaḥ*)—to you
- दाशति (*dāśati*)—offers oblations
- सः (*saḥ*)—that man
- क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)—the house
- प्रतीरते (*pratīrate*)—makes to grow
- सः (*saḥ*)—he himself
- महीः (*mahīḥ*)—abundant
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods also
- वि (*vi*) (supply: makes to grow)—increases greatly for himself
- धर्मणः (*dharmaṇaḥ*)—as the fruit of his rite
- प्रजाभिः (*prajābhiḥ*)—with sons, grandsons and the rest
- परि (*pari*)—surrounded
- प्रजायते (*prajāyate*)—attains prosperity
- सर्वः (*sarvaḥ*)—all people, your worshippers
- अरिष्टः (*ariṣṭaḥ*)—without falling to the injury of enemies
- विधते (*vidhate*)—attain increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts and the other gods, the man who, seeking excellent wealth, offers oblations to you makes his house grow. He makes abundant foods also grow for himself. As the fruit of his sacrificial and other rites he attains prosperity, surrounded by sons, grandsons and the rest.

##### English translation
He enlarges his dwelling, he has abundant food who offers you
(oblations) to obtain a blessing : through his pious acts he is born on every
side in his children ; all prosper (through your favour) unharmed (by
enemies).

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒ते स विं॑दते यु॒धः सु॒गेभि॑र्या॒त्यध्व॑नः ।  
> अ॒र्य॒मा मि॒त्रो वरु॑णः॒ सरा॑तयो॒ यं त्रायं॑ते  ॒॑
> सजोषसः ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यते । सः । विंदते । युधः । सुगेभिः । याति । अध्वनः ।  
> अर्यमा । मित्रः । वरुणः । सरातयः । यं । त्रायंते । सजोषसः ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोऽर्यमार्दीनां हविर्दाता मनुष्यो युधः ॥ युध संप्रहारे ।
> भावे क्विप् ॥ युद्धादृते विनापि विंदते । धनानि लभते । किंच सुगेभिः शोभनगमनैः
> सुष्टु गंतृभिर्वाश्वैः सहाध्वनो मार्गान् । गंतव्यान्देशानित्यर्थः । तान् याति ।
> गच्छति । यं जनमर्यमा सततं गच्छन् मित्रः स्तोत्कृणां यष्टृणां च धनप्रदानेन मित्रभूतो वरुणो निवारयिता शत्रूणां यद्वा वरणीयः संभजनीय
> एतन्नामकाः सरातयः समानदानास्त्रयो देवाः सजोषसः परस्परं संगताः संतो
> यं हव्यप्रदाशारं त्रायंते स्वरक्षणैः पालयंति स धनादीनि विंदतीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That man, the giver of oblations to Aryaman and the others, obtains wealth even without battle (yudh, from the root yudh in the sense of combat; the form is kvip in the sense of the action), that is, apart from war. Further, with horses of good going, that is, which travel well, he travels along the roads, that is, the lands to be travelled. The man whom Aryaman, who goes constantly, Mitra, who is a friend by the giving of wealth to praisers and sacrificers, and Varuṇa, the restrainer of enemies (or the one to be chosen and resorted to), the three gods of those names, sarātayaḥ, that is, of equal gifts, and sajoṣasaḥ, that is, united with one another, protect, guard with their protections, that giver of oblations obtains wealth and the rest: this is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom, the man
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- सराशयः (*sarāśayaḥ*)—as givers of constant gifts
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—as united together
- त्रायंते (*trāyaṃte*)—protect
- सः (*saḥ*)—that man
- युधः ऋते (*yudhaḥ ṛte*)—without war
- विंदते (*viṃdate*)—obtains wealth and the rest
- सुगेभिः (*sugebhiḥ*)—with horses that run well
- अध्वनः (*adhvanaḥ*)—the roads
- याति (*yāti*)—travels

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The man whom Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, as givers of constant gifts and as united together, protect, that man obtains wealth and the rest without war. He travels along the roads with horses that run well.

### Printed p. 178

##### English translation
He gains (wealth) without war, he travels along the roads with quick
(horses), whom Aryaman, Mitra and Varuna, alike munificent, and acting
in concert, protect.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अज्रे॑ चिदस्मै कृणुथा॒ न्यंच॑नं दु॒र्गे चि॒दा सु॑सर॒णं ।  
> ए॒षा चि॑दस्माद॒शनिः॑ प॒रोनु सास्रे॑धंती॒ वि न॑श्यतु ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अज्रे । चित् । अस्मै । कृणुथ ! निअंचनं । दुर्गे । चित् । आ । सुसरणं ।  
> एषा । चित् । आस्मात् । अशनिः । परः । नु । सा । अस्रेधंती । वि । नश्यतु ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवाः अज्रे चित् ॥ ज्रि अभिभवे ॥ परैरनभिभवनीयेऽपि परपुरे न्यंचनं
> नितरां गमनमस्मै मनवे कृणुथ । यूयं कुरुत । यद्वा । अज्र ऋजुगमने
> प्रस्थे गमनं कुरुत । तथा दुर्गे चिदगंतव्येऽपि स्थले सुसरणं ॥ सृ गतौ ॥ शोभनगमनमा समंतात्कुरुत । एवं सति सैषाशनिः शत्रूणां तदेतदायुधमस्मात्सर्वतो
> गंतुर्मनोर्नु क्षिप्रं परः परस्ताद्भवेत् । पश्चात्साशनिरस्रेधंती कांश्चिदप्यहिंसती
> वि नश्यतु । विनष्टा भवेत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, even in an ajra (from the root jri in the sense of overpowering), that is, an enemy's city that cannot be overpowered by others, you make for this Manu a nyañcana, a going down thoroughly. Or else, ajra from the sense of straight going: make for him going on a straight road. So also even in a durga, a place that cannot be traversed, make good going, susaraṇa (the root sṛ in the sense of going), on every side. This being so, may this weapon, the aśani of the enemies, be quickly far beyond Manu as he goes on every side. Afterwards, injuring none (asredhantī), may that weapon perish, that is, be destroyed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- O gods
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to this Manu
- अज्रे चित् (*ajre cit*)—even on a straight road
- न्यंचनं (*nyaṃcanaṃ*)—so that there is good travelling
- कृणुथ (*kṛṇutha*)—you help
- दुर्गॆ चित् (*durgè cit*)—even on a hard road
- सुसरणं (*susaraṇaṃ*)—so that there is easy travelling
- आ (*ā*) (supply: make)—you make
- एषा अशनिः (*eṣā aśaniḥ*)—this weapon discharged by the enemy
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—than this Manu
- परः (*paraḥ*)—may it pass far away
- सा (*sā*)—that same weapon
- अस्रेधंती (*asredhaṃtī*)—without injuring in the least
- वि नश्यतु (*vi naśyatu*)—may it be utterly destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, you help this Manu so that there is good travelling even on a straight road. You make easy travelling for him even on a hard road.

### Printed p. 179

May this weapon discharged by the enemy pass fiercely far away from this man. May that same weapon, without injuring even one who kills, be utterly destroyed.

##### English translation
You enable him (Manu) to proceed by an unobstructed road ; you grant him easy access to difficult passes : may the weapon (of the foe) be far from him, and inflicting no injury, perish.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद॒द्य सूर्य॑ उद्य॒ति प्रिय॑क्षत्रा ऋ॒तं द॒ध ।  
> यन्नि॒म्रुचि॑ प्र॒बुधि॑ विश्ववेदसो॒ यद्वा॑ म॒ध्यंदि॑ने दि॒वः ॥१९॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । अद्य । सूर्ये । उत्यति । प्रियक्षत्राः । ऋतं । दध ।  
> यत् । निम्रुचि । प्रबुधि । विश्ववेदसः । यत् । वा । मध्यंदिने । दिवः ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे प्रियक्षत्राः प्रीणयितृबला देवाः सूर्ये सर्वस्य स्वस्वकर्मणि प्रेरके
> सवितर्युद्यत्युद्धच्छति सत्यद्यास्मिन्निने यद्यदा ऋतं कल्याणभूतं गृहं दध
> धारयत ॥ दधातेर्लिट मध्यमबहुवचने रूपं ॥ यद्यदा हे विश्ववेदसः सर्वधना देवाः निम्मुचि । म्रुचिर्गत्यर्थः । सूर्यस्य निम्मोचने नितरां गमने ।
> सायमित्यर्थः । तस्मिन् धारयथ । यद्वा प्रबुधि तस्य प्रबोधने प्रातःकाले ।
> यद्वा दिवः सूर्यतेजसा दीप्यमानस्याहो मध्यंदिने मध्यॆ धनं मनवे
> धत्तेत्युत्तरत्र संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods of pleasing power (priyakṣatra, whose strength gratifies), when today the sun, the impeller of everyone to his own work, is rising, when you hold the ṛta, the auspicious house (dadha is the perfect, second person plural, of the root dhā); when, O gods of all wealth, at nimruc (mruc has the sense of going) that is, at the sun's setting, his going down thoroughly, in the evening, you hold it; or else at prabudh, at his awakening, in the morning; or else at the midday, the middle, of the day (diva) shining with the sun's light, then give wealth to Manu: this is the connection with what follows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*)—possessed of all wealth
- प्रियक्षत्राः (*priyakṣatrāḥ*)—possessed of a power agreeable to the world, O gods
- सूर्ये (*sūrye*)—when the sun
- उद्यति (*udyati*)—is rising
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the auspicious sacrificial house
- दध (*dadha*)—you hold
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- निम्रुचि (*nimruci*)—at the time of sunset also (or)

### Printed p. 180

- प्रबुधि (*prabudhi*)—in the morning also
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—or
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the shining day
- मध्यंदिने (*madhyaṃdine*)—at midday also

When you hold this sacrificial house, then you give wealth to Manu.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, possessed of all wealth and of a power agreeable to the world, whether at this time when the sun rises, or at the time of sunset, or in the morning, or in the middle of the shining day, whenever you hold this sacrificial house, then you give wealth to Manu.

##### English translation
Divinities of benevolent vigour, since you preside over the rite to-day, at the rising of the sun. since, possessors of all wealth, (you are present) at his setting, or at his waking, or at the meridian of the day ;

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒यं तद्यो॑ वसवो विश्ववेदस॒ उप॑ स्थेयाम॒ मध्य॒ आ ॥२०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे असुराः प्राज्ञाः संग्राम आप्तानां क्षेप्तारो वा देवाः यद्वाभिपित्वेऽस्मद्यज्ञं प्रति युष्माकमभिप्राप्तावृतं सत्यभूतं यज्ञं यते ॥ इणः शतरि

> तद्गृहं तेजो वा वि येम प्रयच्छथ । यद्येवं यूयं कुरुथ तर्हि वयं

> विश्ववेदसः सर्वधनाः सर्वज्ञाना वा हे देवाः वो युष्मत्संबंधि तत्कल्याणं गृहं।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O asuras, that is, wise gods, or throwers of those reached in battle: or else, at your approach, abhipitva, toward our sacrifice, the true sacrifice (ṛta) going (yate, the form of the root i with the affix śatṛ), to the sacrificer who has given oblations, the house (chardis; the root chard has the senses of shining and playing; that by which it shines is chardis, a lustre; or else, in which they shine, a house), that house or lustre you give (vi yema). If you do so, then we, O vasus (who cover the praisers with wealth and the like, or who drive away enemies), O gods of all wealth or of all knowledge, your auspicious house (the accusative is in the sense of the genitive)

> युष्मान्वविर्भिः पूजयेम ॥ तिष्यतेराशीर्लिज् लिङ्माशिष्यज्जत्यज्‌प्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

in the middle of this house may we stand near, may we approach; may we worship you with oblations. **NOTE**

O wise gods, when you give the house to the sacrificer who goes there for worship at the time when you come to the sacrificial house, then, O gods, possessed of all wealth and subduers of enemies, we shall come and gather for your worship in the middle of that same auspicious house that belongs to you.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, possessed of all wealth, that is, pervaded on all sides with wealth: when today, now; or else when the sun has risen; when at midday, in the middle of the day; or else at ātuc, ātuc being.

> नार्थः । सूर्यस्य निव्रोचने । सायमित्यर्थः । जुह्वानायाग्नौ हवींषि जुह्वते
> अत एव प्रचेतसे प्रकृष्टज्ञानाय मनव एतन्नामकायर्षये मह्यं वामं
> वननीयं धनं धत्थ दत्थ तद्वृणीमह इत्युत्तरत्र संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Ātuc has the sense of going: that is, at the setting of the sun, in the evening. To the one who pours oblations into the fire, and for that very reason to the one of excellent knowledge, to me, Manu, the Ārya seer of that name, you give desirable wealth; that we choose. This is the connection with what follows.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, possessed of wealth that pervades everywhere, when you give attractive wealth to me, who am named Manu, who offer you oblations at sunrise, at midday and in the evening, and who am of excellent knowledge, then we shall praise you.

##### English translation
(Gods), who are possessed of all wealth, bestow the desired (opulence)
upon the intelligent Manu, offering oblations to you at sunrise, mid-day
and sunset.

- हे सम्राजः (*he samrājaḥ*)—O gods, shining exceedingly

O gods, shining exceedingly, we, who are fit to be nourished like your sons, desire the wealth in your keeping that is enjoyed by many. ## Sūkta 28 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये त्रिंशतीति पंचर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रांतं । ये त्रिंशति
> पंचोपांत्या पुर उष्णिगिति । मनुर्यषिः । प्राग्वत्सप्रीयपरिभाषया गायत्री
> छंदः । उपांत्या पुरउष्णिक् । पूर्ववद्विश्वे देवे देवता ॥ तृतीये छंदोमे
> वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे ये त्रिंशतीत्येतत्सूक्तं वैश्वदेवनिविद्वानं । सूत्रितरं च । ये
> त्रिंशतीति वैश्वदेवं । आ. ८-११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta of five Ṛks beginning with ये त्रिंशतीति (*ye triṃśatīti*) is the eighth. The Anukramaṇikā says of it that the last but one of the five Ṛks is in the metre called Pura-uṣṇik. Manu is the seer. By the same rule of interpretation as before the metre is Gāyatrī; the last but one is Pura-uṣṇik. As before, the Viśve Devāḥ are the deity. In the Vaiśvadeva-śastra of the third Chandoma day this sūkta is used as the nivid-sūkta of the Viśve Devāḥ **NOTE**. It is also laid down by the sūtra (Ā. 8-11).

### Printed p. 184

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, ये त्रिंशति (*ye triṃśati*), is the eighth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. There are five Ṛks in it. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: ये त्रिंशति पंचोपांत्या पुरउष्टिक् (*ye triṃśati paṃcopāṃtyā purauṣṭik*). Manu is the seer of this sūkta; as in the preceding sūkta, the Viśve Devāḥ are the deity; the metre is Gāyatrī. But the Ṛk before the last (the fourth Ṛk) is in the metre called पुरउष्टिक् (*purauṣṭik*). In the third Chandoma, when the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra are recited, this sūkta ये त्रिंशति (*ye triṃśati*) is to be recited as the nivid-dhāna sūkta addressed to the Viśve Devāḥ; this is elucidated by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, ये त्रिंशतीति वैश्वदेवं (*ye triṃśatīti vaiśvadevaṃ*) (Ā. 8-11).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 28. Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 28. Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 2, Varga 35. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Manu Vaivasvata. Deity: the Viśve Devāḥ. Metre: Ṛks 1-3 and 5, Gāyatrī; Ṛk 4, पुरउष्टिक् (*purauṣṭik*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये त्रिं॒शति॒ त्रय॑स्प॒रो दे॒वासो॑ ब॒र्हिरास॑दन् ।  
> वि॒दन्न ह॑ द्वि॒तास॑नन् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । त्रिंशति । त्रयः । परः । देवासः । बर्हिः । आ । आसदन् ।  
> विदन् । अह । द्विता । आसनन् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मनुराह । त्रिंशति त्रिंशत्संख्यायाः परः परस्तात्रयः । त्रयस्त्रिंशद्देवता
> इत्यर्थः । ये देवासो देवा बर्हिरस्मदीययज्ञसंबंधिनि बर्हिषि हविःस्वीकरणार्थमासदन् आसीदंतु अथानंतरं विदन् ते देवा आस्मान्हविषां प्रदात्मनिति
> जानंतु । ततो द्विता द्विधा द्विप्रकारमसनन् । अस्मभ्यं धनं पश्वादिकं च प्रयच्छंतु । यद्वा । द्विता द्वैधं । अनेन पौनःपुन्यं लक्ष्यते । पुनःपुनरस्मैभ्यं
> धनादिकं ददत्त्व्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Manu speaks. Beyond thirty are three: that is, thirty-three deities. Those gods who, on our sacred grass that belongs to our sacrifice, may sit down to receive the oblations; and after that may those gods know us as givers of oblations; then dvitā, in two ways, twofold, may they give us wealth and cattle and the like. Or else dvitā means twofold, and by this repetition is meant: may they give us wealth and the like again and again.

### Printed p. 185

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रिंशति (*triṃśati*)—than thirty
- परः (*paraḥ*)—exceeding
- त्रयः (*trayaḥ*)—three in number (thirty-three in number)
- ये (*ye*)—which
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods there are, may they
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—upon the seat of sacred grass
- आसदन् (*āsadan*)—sit down
- विदन् (*vidan*)—may they know the devotion of the sacrificers
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—two kinds of wealth (exceedingly great riches)
- आसनन् (*āsanan*)—may they give us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods, renowned by the number thirty-three, come and sit down upon our seat of sacred grass. And knowing the exceeding devotion of the sacrificers, may they, as its fruit, give us exceedingly great riches.

##### English translation
May the three-and-thirty divinities sit down upon the sacred grass; may they accept (our offerings), and bestow upon us both (sorts of wealth).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा स्मद्रा॑तिषाचो अ॒ग्नयः॑ ।  
> पत्नी॑वंतो॒ वष॑ट्कृताः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वरुणः । मित्रः । आर्यमा । स्मद्रातिऽसाचः । अग्नयः ।  
> पत्नीऽवंतः । वषट्कृताः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वरुणो वरणीयः संभजनीयो मित्रः स्तोत्कृणां यष्टृणां च धनादिदानेन मित्रभूतोऽर्यमा स्तोत्रकारिणे धनं प्रापयन् यद्वा सततं गच्छन्
> एतन्नामकास्त्रयो देवाः स्मद्रातिषाचः । स्मत् सुमच्छोभना रातिर्हविष्प्रदानं
> येषामस्तीति स्मद्रातयो यजमानाः । तान् सचंते धनादिप्रदानेन सेवंतॆ इतितथोक्ताः । यद्वा । कल्याणं यथा भवति तथा हविषां दात्यन् सचंत इति ! शे:
> तादृशाः पत्नीवंतो देवपत्निसहिता अग्नयोऽंगनशीला नानाविधा अग्नयो
> वषट्कृताः । मया सोमस्याग्ने वीहि वौषडित्यादिना स्वाहाकृताः । सुहूताइत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Varuṇa, the one to be chosen and resorted to; Mitra, a friend of praisers and sacrificers by his gift of wealth and the like; Aryaman, bringing wealth to the praiser, or else going constantly: these three gods are smadrātiṣācaḥ. Smat means fine, rāti is the giving of oblations; those who have it are the sacrificers; the gods serve them, wait on them, with gifts of wealth and the like; so they are called. Or else, as it is auspicious, they attend those who give oblations **NOTE**. Such are the Agnis, patnīvantaḥ, that is, accompanied by the wives of the gods, Agnis of various kinds, of a nature that is **NOTE**; vaṣaṭkṛtāḥ, that is, made svāhā-offerings by me with the formula सोमस्याग्ने वीहि वौषडित्यादिना (*somasyāgne vīhi vauṣaḍityādinā*) **GLOSS**, which is to say well invoked.

### Printed p. 186

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- आर्यमा (*āryamā*)—Aryaman
- अग्नयः (*agnayaḥ*)—the fires, the Gārhapatya and the others
- पत्नीवंतः (*patnīvaṃtaḥ*)—accompanied by the wives of the gods
- वषट् कृताः (*vaṣaṭ kṛtāḥ*)—worshipped with the exclamation vaṣaṭ
- स्मद्रातिषाचः (*smadrātiṣācaḥ*)—show favour to the sacrificers who give oblations liberally

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman and the fires, the Gārhapatya and the others, accompanied by the wives of the gods and worshipped with the exclamation vaṣaṭ, show favour to the sacrificers who give liberally.

##### English translation
May Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman and the Agnis, with their wives, honouring the donors (of the oblation), and addressed with the sacrificial exclamation.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते नो॑ गो॒पा अ॑पा॒च्यास्त उद॒क्त इ॒त्था न्य॑क् ।  
> पु॒रस्ता॒त्सर्व॑या वि॒शा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । नः । गोपाः । अपाच्याः । ते । उदत् । ते । इत्था । न्यक् ।  
> पुरस्तात् । सर्वया । विशा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते वरुणादयो देवाः सर्वया सर्वेण विशानुचरवर्गेण सहापाच्याः ।
> अपाचे प्रतीची । ततो नोऽस्माकं गोपा गोपायितारो भवंतु । त एव
> उदगुदीच्याः ॥ अंचेर्लुगिति पंचम्यर्थे विहितस्यास्तातेर्लुक् ॥ ततोऽप्यस्माकं
> रक्षका भवंतु । इत्थेति शब्देनोध्वा० दिशं दक्षिणां च निदिशति । इत्थमनेन
> पूर्वोक्तेन प्रकारेणोध्वाया दक्षिणस्याश्च दिशस्त्रे देवा अस्माकं पालयितारो
> भवंतु । तथा न्यग्नीच्या दिशः ॥ अत्रापि पूर्ववदस्तातेर्लुक् ॥ अधस्तादेवाप्यस्माकं त्रातारो भवंतु । किंच पुरस्तात्पाच्या दिशश्च ते देवा अस्माकं गोपायि
> तारो भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those gods, Varuṇa and the rest, together with all their retinue, from the apāc, the western region, be our guardians. The same, from the udak, the northern region, be our protectors also. By the word ittha he indicates the upper region and the south: in the manner just said, from the upper and the southern regions those gods be our protectors. So also from the nyak, the lower region, be our saviours. And further, from the purastāt, the eastern region, may those gods be our guardians.

May those same gods, Varuṇa and the rest, together with all their attendants, be our protectors from the western region. May they be our protectors from the northern region also. ##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अरावा । चन । मर्त्यः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवा द्योतमानाः सर्वे देवा यथा वशंति यथा कामयंते ॥ वश
> कांतौ । संप्रसारणाच्चेति पूर्वरूपस्य छंदसि विकल्पितत्वाद्यणादेशः ॥ तथेद्यथोशंति तथैवासत् । तद्भवत्येव । तदेवाह । एषां देवानां तत्कामनं सकिर्न कश्चि दपि
> मिनत् । हिनस्ति ॥ मीज् हिंसायां । लेटि रूपं । मीनातेर्निगम इति प्रस्वत्वं ॥
> कथं देवानामभिलषितं तथा भवतीति चेत् तदाह । अरावा । यदि देवाः कस्यजिदप्यदातारं मनुष्यं कामयेरन् तदारावादाता । चनेत्यव्यर्थे । अवाशापि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, all the shining gods, as they wish, as they desire: so it will be; that comes to pass. He says that very thing: of these gods that desire no one at all injures. If it is asked how the wish of the gods thus comes to pass, he says: arāvā, a non-giver. If the gods were to desire any man who is a non-giver, then he would be a non-giver; cana is an indeclinable in the sense of "even".

### Printed p. 188

> मर्त्यो मनुष्य उशद्भ्यो देवेभ्यो हवींषि प्रयच्छति । तस्मात्तेषां यत्कामनं
> तत्तथा भवत्येवेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The mortal, the man, offers oblations to the gods who desire them; therefore what they desire comes to pass indeed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the shining gods
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever manner
- वशंति (*vaśaṃti*)—they wish
- तथेत् (*tathet*)—exactly as that wish
- असत् (*asat*)—everything comes to pass
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these gods
- तत् (*tat*)—that same wish
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—no one at all
- मिनत् (*minat*)—can obstruct
- अरावा चन मर्त्यः (*arāvā cana martyaḥ*)—even a man who is exceedingly miserly will assuredly offer oblations if the gods wish it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In whatever manner all the shining gods wish, everything comes to pass exactly so (happens so). No one can obstruct the wish of these gods. Even a man who is exceedingly miserly will assuredly offer oblations if the gods wish it.

##### English translation
Whatever the the gods desire, that assuredly comes to pass : no one can resist their (will), no mortal withholds (their) offerings.

> स॒प्ता॒नां स॒प्त ऋ॒ष्टयः॑ स॒प्त द्यु॒म्नान्ये॑षां ।  
> स॒प्तो अधि॒ श्रियो॑ धिरे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सप्तानां । सप्त । यष्टयः । सप्त । द्युम्नानि । एषां ।  
> सप्तो इति । अधि । श्रियः । धिरे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र पुरातनी कथा । इंद्रसमानं पुत्रमिच्छंत्या आदितेर्गर्भस्य केनचित्कारणेनेंद्रेण सप्तधा भिन्नत्वात्सगर्भः सप्तगणात्मकोऽभवत् । ततो मरुतः संपन्नाः ।
> सप्तगणा वै मरुतः । तै. सं. २-२-११-१ । इति श्रुतेः । एषा कथेदं पित्रॆ मरुतामुच्यते वचः । ऋ. १-११४-६ । इत्यस्मिन्वर्गे सप्रपंचेनाभ्यधायि । तथा चास्या
> ऋचोऽयमर्थः । सप्तानां मरुतां गणानां सप्त सप्तसंख्याका ऋष्टय

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here is an old story. Aditi, who wished for a son equal to Indra, had her embryo, for some reason, divided sevenfold by Indra, so that the embryo, divided, became of seven groups. From it the Maruts came into being. This accords with the Vedic text सप्तगणा वै मरुतः (*saptagaṇā vai marutaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-1). This story was told at length in the varga of the Ṛk beginning एषा कथेदं पित्रॆ मरुतामुच्यते वचः (*eṣā kathedaṃ pitrè marutāmucyate vacaḥ*) (Ṛ. 1-114-6) **GLOSS**. The meaning of this Ṛk is as follows: of the seven groups of the Maruts, seven in number are the ṛṣṭis,

### Printed p. 189

> आयुधविशेषा विभिन्नाः संति । तथा सप्त सप्तसंख्याकानि द्युम्नानि द्योतमानानि
> कुंडलादीन्याभरणानि । द्युम्नान्यन्नानि वा । एषां गणानां विभिन्नानि संति । ततः
> सप्त मरुतां गणाः सप्नो सप्नैव सप्तविधाः श्रियः सकला दीप्तीरधि धिरे । परस्परमधिकं दधिरे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

special weapons, which are distinct. So also seven in number are the shining ornaments, earrings and the rest (or dyumna may mean foods); these are distinct for these groups. Therefore the seven groups of the Maruts wear seven kinds of splendours, all their lights, one above another.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सप्तानां (*saptānāṃ*)—of the seven groups of Maruts
- ऋष्टयः (*ṛṣṭayaḥ*)—the special weapons
- सप्त (*sapta*)—are of seven kinds
- द्युम्नानि (*dyumnāni*)—their shining ornaments also
- सप्त (*sapta*)—of seven kinds
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—these groups of Maruts have
- सप्तो (*sapto*)—of seven kinds
- श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)—splendours also
- अधि धिरे (*adhi dhire*)—these Maruts wear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The special weapons of the seven groups of Maruts are of seven kinds. Their shining ornaments also are of seven kinds. These Maruts wear splendours of seven kinds also.

##### English translation
Seven are the lances of the seven (troops of the Maruts), seven are
their ornaments, they wear seven surpassing glories.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Maruts have seven groups (a group means a company). As to how these seven groups came about, the birth of the Maruts was explained at length earlier, that is, in the commentary on the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-6; and in this matter there is the Taittirīya Vedic text सप्तगणा वै मरुतः (*saptagaṇā vai marutaḥ*) as authority (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-2), as the commentator indicates here. We too have given a detailed explanation of this matter in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 9, p. 126. **NOTE**

## Sūkta 29 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बभ्रुरेक इति दशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं । मरीचिपुत्रः कश्यपो वैवस्वतो
> मनुर्वा ऋषिः । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । बभ्रुर्दश कश्यपो वा मारीचो द्वैपदमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning with बभ्रुरेक (*babhrureka*) is the ninth, of ten Ṛks. Its seer is Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, or Manu Vaivasvata. The Anukramaṇikā says so: बभ्रुर्दश कश्यपो वा मारीचो द्वैपदमिति (*babhrurdaśa kaśyapo vā mārīco dvaipadamiti*).

### Printed p. 190

> हशापि द्विपदा विंशत्यक्षरा विराजः । पूर्ववद्विश्वे देवा देवता ॥ तृतीये
> छंदोमे वैश्वदेवसूक्तात्पूर्वमेव दैपदं सूक्तं शंसनीयं । सूत्र्यते हि ।
> बभ्रुरेक इति द्विपदासूक्तानि पुरस्ताद्वैश्वदेवसूक्तानां । आ. ८-७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The metre of all of them is the dvipadā virāj of twenty syllables. As before, the Viśve Devāḥ are the deity. In the third Chandoma day the dvipadā sūkta is to be recited before the Vaiśvadeva sūkta, for this is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. 8-7).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, बभ्रुरेकः (*babhrurekaḥ*), is the ninth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. There are ten Ṛks in it. The seer of this sūkta is Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, or Manu, son of Vivasvat; in the Anukramaṇikā it is said: बभ्रुर्दश कश्यपो वा मारीचो द्वैपदं (*babhrurdaśa kaśyapo vā mārīco dvaipadaṃ*). All ten Ṛks of this sūkta are in the metre called dvipadā virāj, of twenty syllables. As in the preceding sūkta, the Viśve Devāḥ are the deity; in the third Chandoma, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, this sūkta in the dvipadā virāj metre is to be recited before the Vaiśvadeva sūkta addressed to the Viśve Devāḥ; this is elucidated by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, बभ्रुरेक इति द्विपदासूक्तानि पुरस्ताद्वैश्वदेवसूक्तानां (*babhrureka iti dvipadāsūktāni purastādvaiśvadevasūktānāṃ*) (Ā. 8-7).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 29. Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 29. Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 2, Varga 36. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Manu Vaivasvata or Kaśyapa Mārīca. Deity: the Viśve Devāḥ. Metre: Dvipadā.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब॒भ्रुरेको॒ विष्णु॑णः सू॒नरो॒ युवा॒ञ्ज्यं॑क्तेहिर॒ण्ययं॑ ॥१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बभ्रुः । एकः । विषुणः । सूनरः । युवा । अंजि । अंक्ते । हिरण्ययं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र दशानामृचां किंचित्पदं लिंगात्पथग्देवतं । अत्र प्रथमायां बभ्रुरित्यनेन सोमोऽभिदीयते । सौम्यं बभ्रुमा लभीत । तै. स. २-१-३-३ । इत्यादिषु
> दृष्टत्वात् । बभ्रुर्बभ्रुवर्णः शबलतादिषु परिपक्वः । यद्वा ॥ डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः । कुभ्रश्च । उ. १-२३ । इति कुप्रत्ययः ॥ सर्वस्य सुधामय्यैः किरणैस्तापदुद्धते चंद्रमसि दुःखोपशमनानि पुष्टानि खलु । तादृशो विष्णुणो विश्वगंचनः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, among the ten Ṛks, a certain word in each, by its indication, has a separate deity. In the first Ṛk, by the word babhru Soma is meant, because this is seen in texts such as सौम्यं बभ्रुमा लभीत (*saumyaṃ babhrumā labhīta*) (Tai. Sa. 2-1-3-3) **GLOSS** **NOTE**. Babhru is brown in colour, matured in variegated hue and the like. Or else, babhru is one who holds and nourishes. For the moon, with rays full of nectar, soothes the sorrows of everyone scorched by heat, and so nourishes. Such a one is viṣṇuṇaḥ **NOTE**

### Printed p. 191

> सूनरः सुष्टु रात्रीणां नेता । रात्रयश्चंद्रनेतृकाः खलु । एतादृशो युवा
> प्रतिदिवसमाविर्भूतत्वात्तरुण एको देवः सोमो हिरण्ययं हिरण्मयमंजि ।
> अभिव्यज्यते प्रकाश्यतेऽनेनेत्यंज्याभरणं । अभिव्यक्तिसाधनं कुंडलमुकुटादिकं
> स्वशरीरमंक्ते । अभिव्यंजयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sūnara is the good leader of the nights, for the nights have the moon as their leader. Such a one, young because he appears afresh every day, the one god Soma, adorns his own body with golden ornaments. Anji means the ornament, that by which one is made manifest, made visible: earrings, crown and the like, the means of manifestation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बभ्रुः (*babhruḥ*)—golden-brown in colour
- विषुणः (*viṣuṇaḥ*)—all-pervading
- सूनरः (*sūnaraḥ*)—leader of the night
- युवा (*yuvā*)—ever young
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the god Soma
- हिरण्ययं (*hiraṇyayaṃ*)—made of gold
- अंजि (*aṃji*)—ornaments
- अंक्ते (*aṃkte*)—puts on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Soma, golden-brown in colour, all-pervading, leader of the night and ever young, puts on ornaments made of gold.

##### English translation
One (Soma) brown of hue, all-pervading, leader of the nights, ever
young, decorates (himself) with golden ornaments.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> योनि॒मेक॒ आ स॑साद॒ द्यूत॑नो॒ऽन्तर्दे॒वेषु॒ मेधि॑रः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> योनिं । एकः । आ । ससाद । द्योतनः । अंतः । देवेषु । मेधिरः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र योनिरिति लिंगादग्निरुच्यते । आग्नये गृहपतय इत्यादिषु दृष्टत्वात् ।
> देवेषु देवानामंतर्मध्यॆ द्योतनः स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानो मेधिरो मेधावी।
> अथवा मेधाकांक्षिणां स्तोतृणां मेधादातृत्वेन मेधायुक्तः । एवंविध
> एकोऽग्निर्योनिं स्थानभूतमावहनीयादिकमा ससाद । हविःस्वीकरणार्थमासीदति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, by the word yoni, by its indication, Agni is meant, because this is seen in texts such as आग्नये गृहपतय (*āgnaye gṛhapataya*) **GLOSS**. Among the gods, in their midst, shining with his own lustre, he is medhira, possessed of understanding; or else, being the giver of understanding to the praisers who seek understanding, he is endowed with understanding. Such a one, the one Agni, has sat down in the yoni, the place, the Āhavanīya and the rest, to receive the oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवेषु अंतः (*deveṣu aṃtaḥ*)—in the midst of the gods
- द्योतनः (*dyotanaḥ*)—shining
- मेधिरः (*medhiraḥ*)—and intelligent
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—Agni alone
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—that place, the Āhavanīya and the rest
- आ ससाद (*ā sasāda*)—has taken and sits in

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni alone, shining and intelligent in the midst of the gods, has taken the Āhavanīya and the rest as his place and sits there.

##### English translation
One (Agni) intelligent, resplendent among the gods, is seated in his place (the altar).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वाशीं । एकः । बिभर्ति । हस्ते । आयसीं । अंतः । देवेषु । निध्रुविः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवेष्टंतर्देवानां मध्यॆ द्योतमानो निध्रुविर्निश्चले स्थाने वर्तमानः ।
> यद्वा । नितरां गमनमस्यास्तीति निध्रुविः सर्वदा गच्छन् । अथवा संग्रामेषु
> शत्रूणां पुरतोऽतिशयेन स्थैर्यवान् । एतादृश एकस्त्वष्टनामको देव
> आयसीमयोमयधारां वाशीं ॥ वाश्य शब्दे ॥ शब्दयत्याक्रंदयति शत्रूननयेति
> वाशी तक्षणसाधनं कुठारः । तं स्वकीये हस्ते बिभर्ति । धारयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among the gods, in their midst, shining, nidhruvi: abiding in an immovable place. Or else, he who has constant going is nidhruvi, always going; or, in battles, exceedingly firm before the enemies. Such a one, the one god named Tvaṣṭṛ, holds in his hand the vāśī, the axe made of iron (āyasī, with an iron edge): vāśī is so called because it makes the enemies cry out, an instrument of cutting.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवेषु अंतः (*deveṣu aṃtaḥ*)—in the midst of the gods

- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—Tvaṣṭṛ
- आयसीं (*āyasīṃ*)—having an edge made of iron
- वाशीं (*vāśīṃ*)—the weapon in the form of an axe
- हस्ते (*haste*)—in his hand
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—holds

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Tvaṣṭṛ, seated unmoving in the midst of the gods, holds in his hand his weapon, made of steel, with a shining edge, in the form of an axe.

##### English translation
One (Twashtri) immoveably stationed among the gods, holds his
iron axe in his hand.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृत्राण्यावरकाणि रक्षांसि पापानि वा जिघ्नते । भृशं हंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, by the indication of the word vajra, Indra is the deity. The one Indra holds the weapon named vajra, placed in his own hand; the same Indra, with that placed vajra, slays violently the vṛtras, the enveloping rākṣasas or sins.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The one, unequalled Indra holds the thunderbolt weapon in his own hand. With that thunderbolt weapon he slays the enemies, the rākṣasas and the rest.

##### English translation
One (Indra) holds his thuuderbolt wielded in his hand, by which he slays the Vritras.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ति॒ग्ममेको॑ बिभर्ति॒ हस्त॒ आयु॑धं॒ शुचि॑रु॒ग्रो जला॑षभेषजः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तिग्मं । एकः । बिभर्ति । हस्ते । आयुधं । शुचिः । उग्रः । जलापभेषजः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र जलाषभेषज इत्यनेन रुद्रोऽभिधीयते । शुचिः ॥ शुच दीप्ता ॥ सर्वतः
> स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानः । यद्वा ॥ शुच शोके ॥ शत्रुणां शोचयिता दुःखयिता ।
> XXIV 13

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, by the word jalāṣabheṣaja Rudra is meant. Śuci (the root śuc in the sense of shining): shining on every side with his own lustre; or else (the root śuc in the sense of grief): one who makes the enemies grieve, who causes them pain.

### Printed p. 194

> अत एवोऽग्र उद्धूर्णबलो जलापभेषजो रोगादनयनेन सुखकरभैषज्यवान् ।
> यद्वा ! स्तोतृणां दुःखरूपसंसारोच्छेदेन सुखकारिभिषग्रूपः । प्रथमो
> दैव्यो भिषगित्यादिश्रुतिभिरस्य भिषक्त्वं श्रूयते । तादृश एको रुद्रस्तिग्मं तीक्ष्णधारमायुधं । आयुध्यति संप्रहरति शत्रूननेनेत्यायुधं पिनाकः । तं स्वकीये
> हस्ते बिभर्ति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For that very reason he is ugra, of surging strength, and jalāṣabheṣaja, possessing remedies that give happiness by removing disease; or else he is a physician who gives happiness to the praisers by cutting off the sorrowful cycle of existence. His being a physician is heard from Vedic texts such as प्रथमो दैव्यो भिषगित्यादिश्रुतिभिरस्य (*prathamo daivyo bhiṣagityādiśrutibhirasya*) **GLOSS**. Such a one, the one Rudra, holds in his own hand the sharp-edged weapon, the āyudha, that with which one strikes enemies: the Pināka.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुचिः (*śuciḥ*)—shining with his own lustre
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—of exceeding strength
- जलाषभेषजः (*jalāṣabheṣajaḥ*)—providing medicines that destroy disease
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—Rudra
- तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)—with a keen edge
- आयुधं (*āyudhaṃ*)—his weapon called Pināka
- हस्ते (*haste*)—in his hand
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—holds

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Rudra, who shines with his own lustre, is of exceeding strength and provides medicines that destroy disease, holds in his hand his weapon called Pināka, with a keen edge.

##### English translation
One (Rudra) brilliant and fierce, (yet) the distributor of healing
medicines, holds his sharp weapon in his hand.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒थ एकः॑ पीपाय॒ तस्क॑रो यथा ए॒ष वे॑द निधी॒नां ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पथः । एकः । पीपाय । तस्करः । यथा । एषः । वेद । निधीनां ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पथ इति लिंगेन पूषा निगद्यते ! सं पूषन्नध्वनस्तिय । ऋ. १-४२-१ । इत्यादिषु
> दृष्टत्वात् ! एकः पूषनामको देवः पथो मार्गान् पीपाय । प्यायतिर्वर्धनकर्माप्यत्र रक्षणार्थः । येऽग्निहोत्रादि कर्म कुर्वंति तेषां स्वर्गमार्गं ये
> दुष्कृतं कर्म कुर्वंति तेषां यातनामार्गं च रक्षति ! उभयेषां मार्गविपर्ययो यथा न भवति तथा पालयतीत्यर्थः । एष सोऽयं पूषा निधीनां
> पृथिव्यां निहितानि धनानि वेद । वेत्ति ! ज्ञात्वा स्तोतृ णां तानि ददाशीत्यर्थः । तत्र

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By the indication of the word pathaḥ, Pūṣan is meant, because this is seen in texts such as सं पूषन्नध्वनस्तिय (*saṃ pūṣannadhvanastiya*) (Ṛ. 1-42-1) **GLOSS**. The one god named Pūṣan has made the paths, the roads, to grow; the root pyāy has the sense of increase, but here the sense is protection. He protects the path to heaven of those who perform rites such as the Agnihotra, and the path of torment of those who perform evil deeds; the meaning is that he guards them so that the paths of both are not reversed. This Pūṣan knows the treasures, the riches laid down on the earth; knowing them, he gives them to the praisers: this is the meaning.

### Printed p. 195

> दृष्टांतः । तस्करो यथा । यथा चोरः पथि गच्छतां पुरुषाणां धनहरणार्थं
> मार्गं रक्षति तथा च स चोरो गृहे निहितानि ज्ञात्वा तदाहृत्य स्वसहायेभ्यो
> यथा तानि ददाति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The illustration: as a thief, namely, as a robber watches the road for the sake of seizing the wealth of men going along it, and as that thief, having learnt what is laid down in a house, carries it off and gives it to his own helpers, so (Pūṣan does).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the one god named Pūṣan
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—the good roads
- पीपाय (*pīpāya*)—(for the sacrificers) protects
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this same Pūṣan
- निधीनां (*nidhīnāṃ*)—all the treasures
- तस्करो यथा (*taskaro yathā*)—as a thief knows the place of wealth lying even in a hiding-place
- वेद (*veda*)—he knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god named Pūṣan protects for the sacrificers all the good roads. As a thief knows all the places where wealth is hidden in a secret place, so this Pūṣan also knows all the wealth of heaven and earth.

##### English translation
One (Pushan) watches the roads like a robber, and is cognizant of hidden treasures.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रिणेक॑ उरुगा॒यो वि च॑क्रमे॒ यत्र॑ दे॒वासो॒ मदं॑ति ॥७॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रीणि ! एकः । उरुग्गायः । वि । चक्रमे । यत्र । देवासः । मदंति ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उरुगायो वि चक्रम इति पदलिंगाद्विष्णुरुच्यते । उरुगाय उरुभिर्बहुभिर्गातव्यः । यद्वा । बहुषु देशेषु गंता बहुकीर्तिर्ना । सर्वाइत्यून् स्वसामर्थ्येन शब्दयत्याक्रंदयतीति वोरुगायः । एतादृश एकोसहायो विष्णुस्त्रीणि
> पदानि भुवनानि वि चक्रमे । साधु पादेन विक्रांतवान् ॥ वेः पादविहरणे ।
> पा. १-३-४१ । इति क्रमतेरात्मनेपदं ॥ यत्र येषु लोकेषु देवास इंद्रादयो
> देवा मदंति यजमानदत्तैर्हविर्भिमाद्यंति तानि वि चक्रम इत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By the indication of the words उरुगायो वि चक्रम (*urugāyo vi cakrama*) Viṣṇu is meant. Urugāya is one to be sung by many; or else one who goes through many regions and has wide fame; or else one who by his own power makes all of them cry out. Such a one, Viṣṇu, unaccompanied, strode out over three steps, that is, over the worlds, taking a firm stride. **NOTE** The worlds in which the gods, Indra and the others, rejoice, delighting in the oblations given by the sacrificer: those he strode out over. This is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उरुगायः (*urugāyaḥ*)—praised by many hymns
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the unequalled Viṣṇu
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which worlds
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods, Indra and the others
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—are delighted with oblations

### Printed p. 196

- त्रीणि (*trīṇi*)—the three worlds
- वि चक्रमे (*vi cakrame*)—he stands pervading them in a special manner

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Viṣṇu, who is praised by the hymns of many and is unequalled, stands pervading in a special manner the three worlds in which the gods, Indra and the others, are delighted with oblations.

##### English translation
One (Vishnu) wide-stepping, has traversed the three worlds where the gods rejoice.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विभि॒दात् च॑रत॒ एक॑या स॒ह प्र प्र॑वा॒सेव॑ वसतः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विभिः । द्वा । चरतः । एकया । सह । प्र । प्रवासाइव । वसतः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकया सहेति लिंगादश्विनावभिधीयेते । द्वा द्वौ द्वित्वसंख्योपेतावश्विना
> विभिः ॥ वी गत्यादिषु । क्विप् । छांदसो द्रस्वः ॥ गमनसाधनैरश्वैश्चरतः । संचरेते ।
> किंचेमावश्विनावेकया सूर्याख्यया ताभ्यां स्वयंवृतया स्त्रिया सह प्र वसतः ।
> प्रवासं सर्वत्र गमनं कुरुतः । प्रवासे दृष्टांतः । प्रवासेव । यथा प्रवासिनौ
> द्वौ पुरुषावेकया स्त्रिया सह प्रवसतस्तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By the words एकया सह (*ekayā saha*) ("with one") the two Aśvins are meant. Dvā is two, the two Aśvins, who move about with vibhiḥ, that is, with horses, the means of going. Moreover, these two Aśvins dwell forth together with one woman, called Sūryā, chosen by them of her own will; they make a journey, going everywhere. The illustration of travelling: just as two travelling men dwell with one woman, so these.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- द्वा (*dvā*)—the two Aśvin gods
- विभिः (*vibhiḥ*)—with their horses
- चरत॥ (*carata‖*)—they move about
- प्रवासेव (*pravāseva*)—as, at a time of journeying abroad, two men travel together with one woman
- द्वा (*dvā*)—these two
- एकया सह (*ekayā saha*)—with their wife, the woman called Sūryā
- प्र वसतः (*pra vasataḥ*)—they travel together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The two Aśvin gods move about everywhere with their horses. As at a time of journeying abroad two men travel together with one woman, so these two travel together with one woman, Sūryā (their wife).

### Printed p. 197

##### English translation
Two (the Aswins) travel with swift (horses) along with one (bride Surya), lika travellers to foreign countries-

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सदो॒ द्वा च॑क्राते उप॒मा दि॒वि स॒म्राजा॑ स॒र्पिरा॑सुती ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सदः । द्वा । चक्राते इति । उपमा । दिवि । संराजा । सर्पिरासुती इति सर्पिः आसुती॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सम्राजाविति लिंगेन मित्रावरुणावभिधीयेते । उपमोपमौ परस्परं
> स्वकांत्योपमानभूतौ । यद्वा । उपमीयत आभ्यां सर्वमित्युपमौ सर्वस्य ।
> एतावेव सम्राजा सम्राज् सम्यग्गीप्यमान् सर्पिरासुती । सर्पिर्घृतमाभ्यामासूयत इति सर्पिरासुती । धृतहविष्कौ द्वा द्वौ मित्रावरुणौ दिवि द्युलोके सदः ।
> सीदंत्यत्रेति सदः स्थानं । तच्चक्राते । अकार्ष्टां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By the word सम्राजा (*samrājā*) Mitra and Varuṇa are meant. They are upamā, mutually the likeness of each other in their own splendour; or else, because everything is measured by these two, they are the measurers of all. These very two are samrājā, shining forth fully. They are sarpirāsutī: ghee is poured out for them, so they have ghee as their oblation. These two, Mitra and Varuṇa, made their seat in heaven, in the world of heaven; sadas is the place where they sit. This they made.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उपमा (*upamā*)—those of one and the same form
- सम्राजा (*samrājā*)—those of exceeding radiance
- सर्पिरासुती (*sarpirāsutī*)—those to whom the oblation in the form of ghee is offered
- द्वा (*dvā*)—the two, Mitra and Varuṇa
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the world of heaven
- सदः (*sadaḥ*)—their place
- चक्राते (*cakrāte*)—have established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra and Varuṇa, who are of one and the same form, of exceeding radiance, and to whom the oblation in the form of ghee is offered, have established their place in the world of heaven.

##### English translation
Two of like beauty and of royal rank (Mitra and Varuna), worshipped with oblations of clarified butter, have taken their seat in heaven.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अर्चं॑त॒ एके॒ महि॒ साम॑ मन्वत॒ तेन॒ सूर्य॑मरोचयन् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अर्चंतः । एके । महि । साम । मन्वत । तेन ! सूर्यं । अरोचॆयन् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकेत्रयो महि महत्साम त्रिवृत्पंचदशादि मन्वत । अमन्वत । तदेवार्चंतः
> पूजयंत एतादृशा अत्रयस्तेनोक्तेन साम्ना सूर्यमरोचयन् । अदीपयन्।
> त एवात्र देवता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Some, the Atris, thought of the great Sāman, the Trivṛt, the Pañcadaśa and the rest, as great. Worshipping that very Sāman, such Atris made the sun shine, lit it up, with the Sāman so spoken. They alone are the deity here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एके (*eke*)—the Atris, the best among the seers
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- साम (*sāma*)—the Sāman such as the Trivṛt
- मन्वत (*manvata*)—knew in the form of meditation
- अर्चंतः (*arcaṃtaḥ*)—worshipping (reciting) that very one
- तेन (*tena*)—by that very Sāman
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- आरोचयन् (*ārocayan*)—made to shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Atris, the best among the seers, knew in the form of meditation the great Sāman such as the Trivṛt. Worshipping (reciting) that very one, they made the sun shine by that same Sāman.

##### English translation
Some (the Atris) when worshipping, call to mind the great Saman, wherewith they light up the sun.

## Sūkta 30 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नहि व इति चतुर्यचं दशमं सूक्तं । आद्या गायित्री द्वितीया पुरउष्णिक्
> तृतीया बृहती चतुर्थ्यनुष्टप् । मनुर्वैवस्वत ऋषिः । पूर्ववद्विश्वे देवा
> देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । नहि वश्चतुष्कं पुरउष्णिग्पृहत्यनुष्टुबंतमिति ।
> विनियोगस्तु लिंगादवगंतव्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This hymn, beginning नहि व (*nahi va*), is a hymn of four Ṛks, the tenth of this section. The first is in Gāyatrī, the second Puraūṣṇik, the third Bṛhatī, the fourth Anuṣṭup. Manu Vaivasvata is the seer. As before, the Viśvedevas are the deity. The Anukramaṇī is cited, describing the hymn as having four verses with these metres. The ritual application is to be understood from the indication of the text.

Anuvāda: This hymn beginning नहि वः (*nahi vaḥ*) is the tenth hymn in the fourth Anuvāka. In it there are four Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is Manu Vaivasvata; as before, the Viśvedevas are the deity; in this hymn the first Ṛk is in the Gāyatrī metre, the second in Puraūṣṇik, the third Bṛhatī, the fourth in the metre called Anuṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated thus: the hymn is described as having four verses with these metres. The application is to be understood according to the sense.
