The Kanwas invoke you hither for protection and for food ; do you,
ruling yonder heaven, O radiant with oblations return thither.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दधा॑मि ते सु॒तानां॒ वृष्णे॒ न पू॑र्व॒पाय्यं॑ ।  
> दि॒वो अ॒मुष्य॒ शास॑तो॒ दिवं॑ य॒य दि॑वावसो ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दधामि । ते । सुतानां । वृष्णे । न । पूर्वपाय्यं ।  
> दिवः । अमुष्य । शासतः । दिवं । यय । दिवावसो इति दिवावसो ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तुभ्यं सुतानां । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । सुतान् सोमान्
> दधामि ! प्रयच्छामि । वृष्णे न यथा वायवे पूर्वपाय्यं यज्ञमुखे पेयं
> प्रयच्छंति तद्वदहं प्रयच्छामीत्यर्थः । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, I offer to you the pressed Somas. Here the genitive is used in the sense of the accusative. As at the opening of the sacrifice the first drink is offered to Vāyu, so I offer it to you; this is the meaning. The rest is well established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) पूर्वपाय्यं (*pūrvapāyyaṃ*)—the Soma fit to be drunk before all others in the sacrifice
- वृष्णे न (*vṛṣṇe na*)—as it is offered to Vāyu
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you
- सुतानां (*sutānāṃ*)—the Soma pressed and made ready
- दधामि (*dadhāmi*)—I offer
- अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—the world of heaven
- शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—while he rules (we are in comfort)
- दिवावसो (*divāvaso*)—O Indra, shining with oblations
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—to heaven
- ययॆ (*yayè*)—return again

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as the Soma that is fit to be drunk before all the gods in the sacrifice is offered to Vāyu, so I offer to you the Soma that has been pressed and made ready. While this Indra rules the world of heaven, we are in comfort. O Indra, shining with oblations, return again to heaven.

### Printed p. 282

##### English translation
I make offering to you of the libations as the first drink is presented
to the showerer ; do you, ruling yonder heaven, O radiant with oblations,
return thither.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्मत्पु॑रंधिर्न॒ आ ग॑हि वि॒श्वतो॑धीर्न ऊ॒तये॑ ।  
> वो अ॒मुष्य॒ शास॑तो॒ दिवं॑ य॒य दि॑वावसो ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्यत्पुरंधिः । नः । आ । गहि । विश्वतःथीः । नः । ऊतये ।  
> दिवः । अमुष्य । शासतः । दिवं । यय । दिवावसो इति दिवावसो ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र स्मत्पुरंधिः स्वर्गकुटंबी नोऽस्माना गहि । तथा विश्वतोधीः
> सर्वजगतो धारकस्त्वं नोऽस्माकमूतये रक्षणाया गहि । आगच्छ ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are the householder of heaven (the one with the family of heaven), come to us. Likewise you who are the supporter of the whole world, come to us for our protection; come.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra)
- स्मत्पुरंधिः (*smatpuraṃdhiḥ*)—you, the master of the family called heaven
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be pleased to come
- विश्वतोधीः (*viśvatodhīḥ*)—you, the sustainer of the whole world
- नः (*naḥ*)—for our
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—protection (come to us)
- अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—the world of heaven
- शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—while he rules (we are in comfort)
- विवावसो (*vivāvaso*)—O Indra, shining with oblations
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—to heaven
- यय (*yaya*)—return again

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you, the master of the family called heaven, be pleased to come to us. You, the sustainer of the whole world, come to us for our protection. While Indra rules the world of heaven, we are in comfort. O Indra, shining with oblations, return again to heaven.

### Printed p. 283

##### English translation
(Indra) master of the family of heaven, come to us : do you, who
are the sustainer of the universe, (come) for our protection : do you, ruling
yonder heaven, O radiant with oblations, return thither.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॑ याहि महेमते॒ सह॑स्रोते॒ शता॑मघ ।  
> दि॒वो अ॒मुष्य॒ शास॑तो॒ दिवं॑ य॒य दि॑वावसो ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । याहि । महेऽमते । सहस्रऊते । शतमघ ।  
> दिवः । अमुष्य । शासतः । दिवं । यय । दिवावसो इति दिवावसो ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे महेमते महाबुद्धे सहस्रोते सहस्ररक्षण शतामघ बहुधनेंद्र त्वं
> नोऽस्माना याहि । आगच्छ । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mahemati, of great understanding, O Sahasrūti, of a thousand protections, O Śatāmagha, Indra of much wealth, come to us. The rest is well established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महेमते (*mahemate*)—you who have a venerable understanding
- सहस्रोते (*sahasrote*)—you who are endowed with protections of many kinds
- शतमघ (*śatamagha*)—O Indra, who have abundant wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—heaven
- शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—while he rules (we are in comfort)
- दिवावसो (*divāvaso*)—O Indra, shining with oblations
- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—to heaven
- यय (*yaya*)—return

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who have a venerable understanding, who are endowed with protections of many kinds, who have abundant wealth, be pleased to come to us. While this Indra rules heaven, we are in comfort. O Indra, shining with oblations, return to heaven.

##### English translation
Sagacious (Indra) bestower of numerous protections, granter of infinite wealth, come unto us : do you, ruling yonder heaven, O radiant with oblations, return thither.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ त्वा॒ होता॒ मनु॑र्हितो देव॒त्रा व॑क्ष॒दीड्यः॑ ।  
> दि॒वो अ॒मुष्य॒ शास॑तो॒ दिवं॑ य॒य दि॑वावसो ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । त्वा । होता । मनुःहितः । देवत्रा । वक्षत् । ईड्यः ।  
> दिवः । अमुष्य । शासतः । दिवं । यय । दिवावसो इति दिवावसो ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां देवत्रा देवानां मध्य ईड्यः स्तुत्यो होता देवानामाह्वाताग्निर्मनुर्हितो मनुष्यैर्गृहेषु निहित आ वक्षत् । वहतु । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, among the gods, Agni, the adorable one, the Hotā, the invoker of the gods, and Manurhita, he who is placed in the houses by men, brings you hither; let him carry you. The rest is well established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra)
- देवत्रा (*devatrā*)—among the gods
- ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)—worthy of worship
- होता (*hotā*)—the one who calls the gods to the sacrifice
- मनुर्हितः (*manurhitaḥ*)—and beneficial to mankind, Agni
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ वक्षत् (*ā vakṣat*)—let him bring to our sacrifice
- अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—the world of heaven
- शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—while he protects (we are in comfort)
- दिवावसो (*divāvaso*)—O Indra, shining with oblations
- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—to heaven
- यय (*yaya*)—return

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may Agni, who is worthy of worship among the gods, who calls the gods to the sacrifice, and who is beneficial to mankind, bring you to the sacrifice. While this Indra protects the world of heaven, we are in comfort. O Indra, shining with oblations, return to heaven.

##### English translation
May (Agni) the invoker, adorable among the gods, the benefactor
of man, bring you hither : do you, ruling yonder heaven, O radiant with
oblations, return thither.

> आ । त्वा । मद्यच्युता । हरी इति । श्येनं । पक्षाइव । वक्षतः ।  
> दिवः । अमुष्य । शासतः । दिवं । यय । दिवावसो इति दिवावसो ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हरी अश्व श्वेनं श्येनाख्यं पक्षिणं पक्षेवात्मीयपक्षाविना वक्षतः । आवहतां ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, your two horses, which dislodge the pride of enemies, bring you here, as the two wings of the bird named Śyena, the falcon, carry it along. The rest is well established.

- (O Indra)

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मदच्युता (*madacyutā*)—those that destroy the pride of enemies
- हरी (*harī*)—your two horses
- आ वक्षतः (*ā vakṣataḥ*)—let them bring to us
- अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—heaven
- शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—while he protects (we are in comfort)
- दिवावसो (*divāvaso*)—O Indra, shining with oblations
- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—to heaven
- यय (*yaya*)—set out again

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as the two wings of the falcon bear it along, so may your two horses, which destroy the pride of enemies, bring you to us. While this Indra protects heaven, we are in comfort. O Indra, shining with oblations, set out again to heaven.

##### English translation
Let your two steeds, humiliators of the pride (of foes), bring you as
(his) two wings (bear) along) the falcon : do you, ruling yonder heaven,
O radiant with oblations, return thither.

- रणय (*raṇaya*)—make us glad
- अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—this Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—heaven
- शासतः (*śāsataḥ*)—while he rules (we are in comfort)

- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—to heaven
- यय (*yaya*)—return again

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, be pleased to come near us at the time of this our sacrifice, at the time of reciting the hymns of praise, to hear them. Make us glad. While this Indra rules heaven, we are in comfort. O Indra, shining with oblations, return again to heaven.

##### English translation
Come to listen to our praises, when they are being recited,—bestow upon us delight: do you, ruling yondor heaven, O radiant with oblations, return thither.

## Sūkta 35 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निनेंद्रेणेति चतुर्विंशत्यृचं पंचमं सूक्तं श्यावश्वस्यात्रेयस्यार्षं ।
> अत्रानुक्रमणिका । अग्निना चतुर्विंशतिः श्यावाश्व आश्विनमौपरिष्टाज्योतिषं पंक्तिमहाबृहतीपंक्त्यंतमिति । उपरिष्टाज्योतिश्चंदः चतुर्थपादस्याष्टाक्षरत्वात् ।
> यतोऽष्टकस्ततो ज्योतिः । अनु. ९-८ । इति तल्लक्षणं । द्वाविंशी पंक्तिः ।
> त्रयोविंशी महाबृहती चत्वारोऽष्टका जागतश्च महाबृहती । अनु. ९-९ ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the fifth sūkta, beginning अग्निनेंद्रेण (*agnineṃdreṇa*), of twenty-four Ṛks; its seer is Śyāvāśva Ātreya. As the Anukramaṇī says: अग्निना चतुर्विंशतिः श्यावाश्व आश्विनमौपरिष्टाज्योतिषं पंक्तिमहाबृहतीपंक्त्यंतमिति । (*agninā caturviṃśatiḥ śyāvāśva āśvinamaupariṣṭājyotiṣaṃ paṃktimahābṛhatīpaṃktyaṃtamiti |*). The metre is Upariṣṭāj-jyotis, because the fourth pāda has eight syllables; its definition is यतोऽष्टकस्ततो ज्योतिः (*yato 'ṣṭakastato jyotiḥ*), Anu. 9-8. The twenty-second Ṛk is a Paṅkti; the twenty-third is a Mahābṛhatī, with four octosyllabic pādas and a Jagatī pāda, Anu. 9-9. The deity is the Aśvins. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 294

> इत्युक्तलक्षणोपेतत्वात् । चतुर्विंशी पंक्तिः । अश्विनौ देवता ॥ अश्विनोर्यामे
> होतुरतिरिक्तोक्ष्येग्निनेंद्रेणेत्येतत्सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । अग्निनेंद्रेणा भात्यग्निः ।
> आ. ९-११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Ṛks are of the stated characteristics, and the twenty-fourth Ṛk is a Paṅkti. The deity is the Aśvins. This sūkta, beginning with अग्निनेंद्रेण (*agnineṃdreṇa*), is to be recited by the Hotṛ as the extra (atirikta) uktha in the Aśvins' yāma. It is also prescribed in the sūtra अग्निनेंद्रेणा भात्यग्निः (*agnineṃdreṇā bhātyagniḥ*), Ā. 9-11.

This sūkta beginning अग्निनेंद्रेण (*agnineṃdreṇa*) is the fifth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has twenty-four Ṛks. Its seer is Śyāvāśva, born in the family of Atri. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अग्निना चतुर्विंशतिः श्यावाश्व आश्विनमौपरिष्टाज्योतिषं पंक्ति महाबृहतीपंक्त्यंतं (*agninā caturviṃśatiḥ śyāvāśva āśvinamaupariṣṭājyotiṣaṃ paṃkti mahābṛhatīpaṃktyaṃtaṃ*). The Ṛks 1-21 of this sūkta are of the metre Upariṣṭāj-jyotis. A Ṛk of this metre has four pādas, of which the second has eight syllables and the other three twelve syllables each; such is its definition (Chandas Anu. 9-8). The twenty-second Ṛk is of the Paṅkti metre. The twenty-third Ṛk is of the Mahābṛhatī metre; a Ṛk with five pādas, the first four of eight syllables each and the last of twelve syllables as in the Jagatī metre, is called Mahābṛhatī; such is its definition (Chandas Anu. 9-9). The twenty-fourth Ṛk is of the Paṅkti metre. The Aśvin deities are the deity of this sūkta. The use of this sūkta, beginning अग्निनेंद्रेण (*agnineṃdreṇa*), is for the extra mantras to be recited by the Hotṛ in the Aṣṭoryāma sacrifice, as is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra अग्निनेंद्रेणा भात्यग्निः (*agnineṃdreṇā bhātyagniḥ*) (Ā. 9-11).

Sūkta 35. Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 5. Sūkta 35. Aṣṭaka 6. Adhyāya 3. Vargas 14, 15, 16, 17. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 24. Seer: Śyāvāśva. Deity: the Aśvins. Metre: 1-21 Upariṣṭāj-jyotis; 22, 24 Paṅkti; 23 Mahābṛhatī. **NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विन् आग्निनेंद्रेण वरुणेन विष्णुनादित्यै रुद्रैर्वसुभिश्च सचाभुवा
> सहभूतावुषसा सूर्येण च सजोषसा संगत् युवां सोमं पिबतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, associated with Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, the Rudras and the Vasus, being together with them, and united with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- अग्निना (*agninā*)—with Agni
- इंद्रेण (*iṃdreṇa*)—with Indra
- वरुणेन (*varuṇena*)—with Varuṇa
- विष्णुना (*viṣṇunā*)—with Viṣṇu
- आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—with the Ādityas
- रुद्रैः (*rudraiḥ*)—with the Rudras
- वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—with the Vasus
- सचाभुवा (*sacābhuvā*)—being together
- च (*ca*)—and
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—having equal affection
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, being together with Agni, with Indra, with Varuṇa, with Viṣṇu, with the Ādityas, with the Rudras, with the Vasus, and united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, having equal affection, drink the Soma.

##### English translation
Associated with Agni, with Indra, with Varuna, with Vishnu, with the Adityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus, and united with the dawn and with Surya, drink, Ashwins, the Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sacā: sacā means saha, "together with". Yāska, in the explanation (Ni. 5-5), says सचा सहेत्यर्थः । (*sacā sahetyarthaḥ |*) and वसुभिः सचाभुवा । वसुभिः सह भवौ (*vasubhiḥ sacābhuvā | vasubhiḥ saha bhavau*).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वा॑भिर्धि॒भिर्भुव॑नेन वाजिना दि॒वा पृ॑थि॒व्याद्रि॑भिः सचा॒भुवा॑ ।  
> स॒जोष॑सा उ॒षसा॒ सूर्ये॑ण च॒ सोमं॑ पिबतमश्विना ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वाभिः । धीभिः । भुवनेन । वाजिना । दिवा । पृथिव्या । अद्रिभिः । सचाभुवा ।  
> सजोषसौ । उषसा । सूर्येण । च । सोमं । पिबतं । अश्विना ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वाजिना बलिनावश्विन् विश्वाभिः सर्वाभिर्धीभिः प्रज्ञाभिर्भुवनेनाखिलेन
> भूतजातेन च दिवा द्युलोकेन च पृथिव्या चाद्रिभिश्च सचाभुवा सहभूतावुषसा
> सूर्येण च संगतौ युवां सोमं पिबतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O mighty Aśvins, together with all insights, with the whole of created beings, with heaven, with earth and with the mountains, being together, and united with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजिना (*vājinā*)—O powerful ones
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- विश्वाभिः (*viśvābhiḥ*)—all
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—with insights
- भुवनेन (*bhuvanena*)—with all created beings
- दिवा (*divā*)—with heaven
- पृथिव्या (*pṛthivyā*)—with the earth
- अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)—with the mountains
- सचाभुवा (*sacābhuvā*)—united together
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united and having equal affection
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O powerful Aśvin deities, being united with all insights, with all created beings, with heaven, with earth and with the mountains, and being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, having equal affection, drink the Soma.

##### English translation
Powerful (Aswins), associated with all intelligences, with all beings, with heaven, with earth, with the mountains, united with the dawn and with Surya, drink, Aswins, the Soma.

> विश्वै॑र्दे॒वैस्त्रि॒भिरे॑काद॒शैरि॒हाद्भिर्म॒रुद्भि॒र्भृगु॑भिः सचा॒भुवा॑ ।

> सचाभुवा ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ विश्वैर्देवैस्त्रिभिरेकादशैस्त्रयस्त्रिंशैरिह यज्ञेऽद्भिर्मरुद्भिर्भृगुभिश्च सचाभुवा सहभूतावुषसा सूर्येण च संगतौ युवां सोमं पिबतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, together with all the thirty-three gods, here in this sacrifice, with the waters, the Maruts and the Bhṛgus, being together, and united with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- त्रिभिः एकादशैः (*tribhiḥ ekādaśaiḥ*)—numbering thirty-three
- विश्वैः देवैः (*viśvaiḥ devaiḥ*)—with all the gods
- अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*)—with the water deities
- मरुद्भिः (*marudbhiḥ*)—with the Maruts
- भृगुभिः (*bhṛgubhiḥ*)—with the Bhṛgus
- सचाभुवा (*sacābhuvā*)—being together
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण चॆ (*sūryeṇa cè*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united and having equal affection
- सोमा (*somā*)—the Soma
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, in this sacrifice, being together with all the gods numbering thirty-three, with the water deities, with the Maruts and with the Bhṛgus, and being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, having equal affection, drink the Soma.

##### English translation
Associated with all the thrice-eleven deities at this ceremony, with the waters, with the Maruts, with the Bhrigus, united with the dawn and with Surya, drink, Aswins, the Soma.

> गच्छतं ।  
> स॒जोष॑सा उ॒षसा॒ सूर्ये॑ण॒ चेषं॑ नो वोळ्हमश्विना ॥ ४ ॥

> वोळ्हं । प्रापयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, enjoy the sacrifice; take notice of my invocation; in this sacrifice come to know and attain all the libations; bring us food.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवौ (*devau*)—O deities
- आश्विना (*āśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—our sacrifice
- जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*)—enjoy
- मे (*me*)—my
- हवस्य (*havasya*)—prayer
- बोधतं (*bodhataṃ*)—know
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- सवना (*savanā*)—rites
- आव गच्छतं (*āva gacchataṃ*)—know
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- आ वोळ्हं (*ā voḷhaṃ*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, being of divine nature, enjoy our sacrifice. Know my prayer. In this sacrifice understand all the rites. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, provide us with food.

##### English translation
Be gratified by the sacrifice ; hear my invocation ; recognize, deities, all the offerings in this ceremony ; united with the dawn and with Surya, bring us, Aswins, food.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्तोमं॑ जुषेथां युव॒शेव॑ क॒न्यनां॒ विश्वे॒ह दे॑वौ॒ सव॒नाव॑  
> गच्छतं ।

### Printed p. 299

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सप्तमं । णुषेथां । युवशाइव । कन्यनां । विश्वा । इह । देवौ । सवना । अव ।  
> गच्छतं ।  
> सजोषसौ । उषसा । सूर्येण । च । आ । इषं । नः । वोळ्हं । अश्विना ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दे आश्विन् देव् युवामिहास्मिन्नज्ञे स्तोमं जुषेथां । सेवेथां ।
> युवशेव यथा युवान् कन्यनां कन्यानामाह्वानं सेवेते । तद्वदित्यर्थः । इह
> यज्ञे विश्वा विश्वानि सवनान्यव गच्छतं ! प्राप्नुतं । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥
> ॥ ४, २६, २७ ॥
> देवा-देवतात्मराद । अश्विना--ऎलै अश्विनीदेवतॆगळे । कन्यनां-कन्यॆयर
> अड्डावन्नु केरि युवशेव-युवकरु अड्डावन्नु हॊंदुवंतॆ । इद-ई यज्ञदल्लि ।
> स्तोमं-नम्म स्तुतियन्नु ! जुषेथां - सेविसिरि ! विश्वा-समस्तवाद । सवनाउच्चकर्मगळन्नू अव गच्छतं - तिळिदु स्वीकरिसिरि । उषसा-उषस्सिनॊडनॆयू ।
> सूर्येण च-सूर्यनॊडनॆयू । सजोषसा-ऒंदूगूडिदवरागि ! नः-नमगॆ ।
> इषु-अन्नवन्नु । आ वोळ्हं-तंदॊदगिसिरि.
> २ श्रीरामचंद्र ।
> देवतात्तराद ऎलै अश्विनीदेवतॆगळे, कन्यॆयर आह्वानवन्नु केळि युवकरु आह्लादवन्नु
> हॊंदुवंतॆ ई यज्ञदल्लि नम्म स्तुतियन्नु सेविसिरि. समस्तवाद यज्ञकर्मगळन्नू अरितु
> स्वीकरिसिरि उषस्सिनॊडनॆयू, सूर्यनॊडनॆयू ऒंदुगूडिदवरागि नमगॆ अन्नवन्नु
> तंदॊदगिसिरि.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, enjoy our praise in this sacrifice. As young men take delight in the calling of maidens, so you, that is the meaning, enjoy it. In this sacrifice, attain all the libations. The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवा (*devā*)—being of divine nature
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- कन्यनां (*kanyanāṃ*)—of maidens
- युवशेव (*yuvaśeva*)—as young men take delight
- इद (*ida*)—in this sacrifice
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—our praise
- जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*)—enjoy
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- सवना (*savanā*)—sacrificial rites
- अव गच्छतं (*ava gacchataṃ*)—know and accept
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- इषु (*iṣu*)—food
- आ वोळ्हं (*ā voḷhaṃ*)—bring and provide

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, being of divine nature, as young men take delight on hearing the call of maidens, enjoy our praise in this sacrifice. Know and accept all the sacrificial rites. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, bring and provide us with food.

##### English translation
Be gratified by our praise as youths are delighted (by the voices) of maidens : recognize, deities, all the offering in th's ceremony ; united with the dawn and with Surya, bring us. Asvins, food.

O Aśvin deities, being of divine nature, enjoy our praises. Enjoy our sacrifice. In this sacrifice, knowing all our rites, accept them. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, bring and provide us with food.

> सजोषसौ । उषसा । सूर्येण । च । त्रिः । वर्तिः । यातं । अश्विना ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विन् युवां सुतमभिषुतं सोममुप पतथो हारिद्रनाविव यथा
> हारिद्रवौ पक्षिण् वना वनान्युदकानि वा । वनमित्युवकनामसु पाठात् । उपपततः ।
> तद्वदित्यर्थः । महिषाविव यथा पिपासितौ महिषावुदकान्युपगच्छतः तथा सुतं
> सोममव गच्छथः । उषसा सूर्येण च संगतौ त्रिर्वतिर्स्रिमार्गं यातं च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, you fly to the pressed Soma as two Haridrava birds fly to the waters (vana, since it is read among the names of water); that is the meaning. As two thirsty buffaloes go to the waters, so you go to the pressed Soma. United with Uṣas and Sūrya, come also by the threefold path. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- वना (*vanā*)—towards the water
- हारिद्रवाविव (*hāridravāviva*)—as water-fowl run up
- महिषाविव (*mahiṣāviva*)—as buffaloes, scorched by the sun, run up towards the water
- युवां (*yuvāṃ*)—you
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं इत् (*somaṃ it*)—towards the Soma
- उप पतथः (*upa patathaḥ*)—run up
- अव गच्छथः (*ava gacchathaḥ*)—knowing our offering, accept it
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- त्रिवर्तिः (*trivartiḥ*)—by the three paths
- यातं (*yātaṃ*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, as water-fowl run up towards the water, and as buffaloes scorched by the sun run up towards the water, so you run up towards the Soma pressed by us. Knowing our offering, accept it. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, come by the three paths.

##### English translation
You alight upon the effused Soma as the Haridrava plunges into the water: you fall upon it like two buffalos (plunging into a pool) ; united with the dawn and with Surya, come, Aswins, by the triple path.

> गच्छथः ।  
> स॒जोष॑सा उ॒षसा॒ सूर्ये॑ण च॒ त्रिर्व॒र्तिर्या॑तमश्विना ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवां हंसाविव यथा हंसावध्वगाविव यथा च पथिकावुदकं
> गच्छतः तथा वेगेन सुतं सोमं पतथः । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, as two swans, and as two thirsty travellers go to water, so you fly swiftly to the pressed Soma. The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- हंसाविव (*haṃsāviva*)—as swans run up towards the water
- अध्वगाविव (*adhvagāviva*)—as thirsty travellers run up towards the water
- महिषा इव (*mahiṣā iva*)—as buffaloes weary with the sun run up towards the water
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—towards our Soma
- पतथः (*patathaḥ*)—run up
- अव गच्छथः (*ava gacchathaḥ*)—knowing our Soma-offering, accept it
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- त्रिर्वर्तिः (*trirvartiḥ*)—by the three paths
- यातं (*yātaṃ*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, as swans run up towards the water, as thirsty travellers run up towards the water, and as buffaloes weary with the sun run up towards the water, so run up towards our pressed Soma. Knowing our Soma-offering, accept it. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, come by the three paths.

##### English translation
As two geese, as two travellers, as two buffalose (hasten to water) you alight, Aswins, upon the effused Soma ; united with the dawn and with Surya, come Aswins, by the triple path.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शै॒नासि॑व पतथो ह॒व्यदा॑तये॒ सोमं॑ सु॒तं म॑हि॒षेवाव॑

> सः शोषसा । उषसा । सूर्येण । च । त्रिः । वर्तिः । यातं । अश्विना ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कन्नड साहित्य परिषत्तु
> हे अश्विनौ युवां श्येनाविव यथा श्लेन् गगणं गच्छतः तथा वेगेन सुतं
> सोमं दव्यदातॆये यजमानार्थं पतथः । गच्छथः । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, as two falcons go to the sky, so you hasten swiftly to the pressed Soma for the sake of the sacrificer who offers the oblation; you go. The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- शैनाविव (*śaināviva*)—as falcons fly swiftly to the sky
- महिषाविव (*mahiṣāviva*)—as buffaloes run up towards the water
- युवां (*yuvāṃ*)—you
- सुकं (*sukaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—towards the Soma
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to favour the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- पतथः (*patathaḥ*)—come swiftly
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण चॆ (*sūryeṇa cè*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- त्रिवर्ति (*trivarti*)—by the three paths
- यातं (*yātaṃ*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, as falcons fly swiftly to the sky, and as buffaloes run up towards the water, so you come swiftly towards the Soma pressed by us, to favour the sacrificer who offers the oblation. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, come by the three paths.

##### English translation
You hasten like two falcons to the offerer of the libation, you alight upon the effused Soma as two buffeloes (hasten to water); united with the dawn and with Surya come, Aswins. by the triple path.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पिब॑तं च तृप्नु॒तं चा च॑ गच्छतं प्र॒जां च॑ ध॒त्तं द्रवि॑णं च  
> धत्तं ।  
> स॒जोष॑सा उ॒षसा॒ सूर्ये॑ण॒ चोर्जं॑ नो धत्तमश्विना ॥१०॥

> सजोषसौ । उषसा । सूर्येण । च । ऊर्ज० । नः । धत्तं । अश्विना ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवां सोमं पिबतं च । तृप्तुतं च । तृप्यतं च । पानार्थं
> तृप्त्यर्थं चा गच्छतं । सोमं पीत्वा तृप्तौ संतौ युवामस्मभ्यं प्रजां च धत्तं।
> धारयतं । द्रविणं धनं च धत्तं । उषसा सूर्येण च संगतौ नोस्मभ्यमूर्जं
> बलं च धत्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, drink the Soma and be satisfied; come for the drinking and for the satisfaction. Having drunk the Soma and being satisfied, bestow on us offspring and bestow wealth. United with Uṣas and Sūrya, bestow on us vigour, that is, strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- पिबतं च (*pibataṃ ca*)—drink our Soma
- तृप्तुतं च (*tṛptutaṃ ca*)—and obtain satisfaction
- आ च गच्छतं (*ā ca gacchataṃ*)—and come to our sacrifice
- प्रजां च (*prajāṃ ca*)—offspring and the like to us
- धत्त (*dhatta*)—give
- द्रविणं च (*draviṇaṃ ca*)—and wealth
- धत्त (*dhatta*)—give
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- ऊर्जं च (*ūrjaṃ ca*)—and strength
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, drink our Soma. Obtain satisfaction. Favour our sacrifice. Give us offspring and the like. Give us wealth. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, give us strength.

##### English translation
Drink, Aswins, the Soma, and satiate yourselves; come hither; give us progeny; give us wealth; united with the dawn and with Surya, give us, Aswins, strength.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, conquer; conquer the enemies, and protect the praised ones, that is, protect us. The rest is as before. **NOTE**

- जयतं च (*jayataṃ ca*)—conquer also your enemies

- प्रावतं च (*prāvataṃ ca*)—protect us
- प्रजां च (*prajāṃ ca*)—and offspring

- धत्त (*dhatta*)—give

- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya

- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, conquer your enemies. Praise the devotion of your worshippers. Protect us. Give us offspring and give wealth. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, give us strength.

##### English translation
Conquer (Aswins) your foes; protect and praise (your worshipper), grant pr geny, give wealth, and unite! with the dawn and with Surya, give us, Aswins strength.

- धत्त (*dhatta*)—give

- धत्त (*dhatta*)—give

- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya

- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, destroy your enemies. Come to your friends. Give us offspring and the like, and wealth. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, give us strength.

##### English translation
Destroy your foes, repair to your friends, grant progeny, give wealth, and, united with the dawn and with Surya, give us. Aswins strength.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Further, O Aśvins, you who are accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa, endowed with Dharma, and accompanied by the Maruts, go to the invocation of the worshipper (jaritṛ), that is, of the praiser; come to it. Come also with Uṣas, Sūrya and the Ādityas.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- मित्रावरुणवंतौ (*mitrāvaruṇavaṃtau*)—being accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa
- उत (*uta*)—and
- धर्मवंता (*dharmavaṃtā*)—being accompanied by righteousness
- मरुत्वंता (*marutvaṃtā*)—being accompanied by the Maruts
- जरितुः (*jarituḥ*)—of the praiser
- दवं (*davaṃ*)—hearing the prayer
- गच्छथः (*gacchathaḥ*)—come to him
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण चॆ (*sūryeṇa cè*)—and with Sūrya
- आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—with the Ādityas
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- यातं (*yātaṃ*)—come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, being accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa, being accompanied by the deity Dharma, and being accompanied by the Maruts, hear the prayer of the praiser and come to him. Being united with Uṣas, with Sūrya and with the Ādityas, come.

##### English translation
Associated with Mitra and Varuna, with Dharma, with the Maruts, repair to the invocation of the adorer; repair (to him), Aswins, united with the dawn, with Surya, and with Adityas.

> स॒जोष॑सा उ॒षसा॒ सूर्ये॑ण च॒ सोमं॑ सुन्व॒तो अ॑श्विना ॥  
> ॥ पदसापति ॥  
> ब्रह्म । जिन्वतं । उत । जिन्वतं । धियः ! हतं । रक्षांसि । सेधतं । अमीनाः ।  
> स॒जोष॑सौ । उ॒षसा॒ । सूर्ये॑ण । च॒ । सोमं॑ । सुन्व॒तः । अ॑श्विना ॥ १६ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विन् युवां ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणं जिन्वतं । प्रीणयतं । उतापि च धियः
> कर्माणि जिन्वतं । हंत च रक्षांसि । अवीना राक्षसांश्च सेधतं ! उषसा सूर्येण
> च संगत् सुन्वतो यजमानस्य सोमं पिबतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, gratify the brahma, that is, the Brāhmaṇa; and further, make the rites (dhiyaḥ) fruitful. Slay the Rākṣasas and drive away the diseases. United with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the Soma of the sacrificer who presses it, that is the meaning. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—hearing our praises
- जिन्वतं (*jinvataṃ*)—be gratified
- उत (*uta*)—and
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—our rites
- जिन्वतं (*jinvataṃ*)—make fruitful
- रक्षांसि (*rakṣāṃsi*)—the Rākṣasas
- हतं (*hataṃ*)—destroy
- अमीवाः (*amīvāḥ*)—diseases and the like
- सेधतं (*sedhataṃ*)—drive away
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united

- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—drink the Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, make our praises and our rites fruitful. Destroy the Rākṣasas; drive away diseases and the like. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, drink the Soma of the sacrificer who presses the Soma.

##### English translation
Be propitious to prayer, be propitious to sacred rites, slay the Rakshasas remedy diseases; united with the dawn and with Surya, (drink) Aswins, the Soma of the offerer.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शृणुतं । उषसा सूर्येण च संगतौ तिरोअह्न्यं सोमं पिबतं । तिरोहिते

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, you who bring down the pride of enemies **NOTE**, hear the chief praise of me, Śyāvāśva, who press the Soma, as you heard that of Atri, my grandfather. United with Uṣas and with Sūrya, drink the Soma prepared on the previous day. He adds that on the day that has passed, the offering to the Aśvins is made in the morning of the next day **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- मदच्युता (*madacyutā*)—you who destroy the pride of enemies
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—of him who presses the Soma and offers it

- अत्रेरिव (*atreriva*)—as the praise of Atri was heard
- शृणुतं (*śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- तिरोः अह्न्यं (*tiroḥ ahnyaṃ*)—drink the Soma prepared on the previous day

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, you who destroy the pride of enemies, hear the chief praise of Śyāvāśva, who presses the Soma and offers it, as you heard the praise of Atri. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, drink the Soma prepared on the previous day.

##### English translation
Humblers of the pride (of your enemies), hear the earnest praise of Shyavashwa offering libations as (you did) that of Atri, and, united with the dawn and with Surya. (drink), Aswins, (the Soma) prepared the previous day.

### Printed p. 314

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ श्यावाश्वस्य मम सुष्टुतीः शोभनाः स्तुतीः सर्गानिव । आभरणानि
> वा हवींषि वा सर्गाः । तान्यथा तथात्मन्युप सृजतं । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, bring to yourselves my, Śyāvāśva's, good praises, as one brings sargas. Sargas are either ornaments or oblations; as one fastens these on oneself, so fasten my praises on yourselves. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदच्युता (*madacyutā*)—you who destroy the pride of enemies
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—of him who presses the Soma and offers it
- श्यावाश्वस्य (*śyāvāśvasya*)—of Śyāvāśva
- सुष्टुतीः (*suṣṭutīḥ*)—excellent praises
- सर्गान् इव (*sargān iva*)—as one puts on ornaments
- उप सृजतं (*upa sṛjataṃ*)—offer to yourselves
- उषसा (*uṣasā*)—with Uṣas
- सूर्येण च (*sūryeṇa ca*)—and with Sūrya
- सजोषसा (*sajoṣasā*)—being united
- तिरो आह्न्यं (*tiro āhnyaṃ*)—drink the Soma prepared on the previous day

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, you who destroy the pride of enemies, take to yourselves the excellent praises of Śyāvāśva, who presses the Soma and offers it, as one puts on ornaments. Being united with Uṣas and with Sūrya, drink the Soma prepared on the previous day.

##### English translation
Humblers of the pride (of your enemies), accept the earnest praises of Shyavashwa offering you libations as if you were accepting oblations; and, united with the dawn and with Surya, (drink), Aswins, (the Soma) prepared the previous day.

## Sūkta 36 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अवितासीति सप्तर्चंषष्ठं सूक्तमात्रेयस्य श्यावाश्वस्यार्षं । आत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । अविता सप्त शाक्वरं महापंक्त्यंतमिति । षट्पंचाशदक्षरा शक्वरी छंदः।
> श्वावाश्वस्येति सप्तमी महापंक्तिः षळष्टका ना महापंक्तिः । अनु. १०-३ । इति लक्षणसध्भावात् ॥ दशरात्रे पंचमेऽहनि मरुत्वतीय इदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च ।
> अवितासीत्था हि ! अ. ७-१२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the sixth sūkta, beginning अवितासीति (*avitāsīti*), of seven Ṛks; its seer is Śyāvāśva of the family of Atri. The Anukramaṇī says अविता सप्त शाक्वरं महापंक्त्यंतमिति (*avitā sapta śākvaraṃ mahāpaṃktyaṃtamiti*). The metre is Śakvarī, of fifty-six syllables. The seventh Ṛk, beginning श्वावाश्वस्येति (*śvāvāśvasyeti*), is a Mahāpaṅkti, since it has the stated mark of six octosyllabic pādas (Anu. 10-3). On the fifth day of the Daśarātra this sūkta is used at the Marutvatīya, and the sūtra says so: अवितासीत्था हि (*avitāsītthā hi*) (A. 7-12) **NOTE**.

This sixth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka, beginning with Avitāsi, has seven Ṛks. Śyāvāśva is its seer. The Anukramaṇī says: Avitā sapta śākvaraṃ mahāpaṅktyantam. Indra is the deity. The first six Ṛks of the sūkta are in the Śakvarī metre, and the seventh Ṛk, beginning Śyāvāśvasya, is in the metre called Mahāpaṅkti. A Śakvarī Ṛk has seven pādas of eight syllables each; the Mahāpaṅkti has six pādas of eight syllables each, such being the marks of these metres (Chandaḥ Anu. 10-3). The use of this sūkta for the Marutvatīya-śastra mantras on the fifth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra is explained by the sūtra Avitāsītthā hi in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 7-12).

Sūkta 36. Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 5. Sūkta 36. Aṣṭaka 6. Adhyāya 3. Varga 18. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: Śyāvāśva. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1-6 Śakvarī; 7 Mahāpaṅkti. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒वि॒तासि॑ सुन्व॒तो वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः॒ पिबा॒ सोमं॒ मदा॑य॒ कं  ॑
> शतक्रतो ।

### Printed p. 320

> यं ते भागमधारयन्विश्वाः सेहानः पृतना उरु ज्रयः  
> समप्सुजिन्मरुत्वा इंद्र सत्पते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अविता । असि । सुन्वतः । वृक्तबर्हिषः । पिब । सोमं । मदाय । कं । शतक्रतो इति  
> शतक्रतो ।  
> यं । ते । भागं । आधारयन् । विश्वाः । सेहानः । पृतनाः । उरु । ज्रयति । सं ।  
> अप्सुऽजित् । मरुत्वान् । इंद्र । सत्ऽपते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन्निंद्र सुन्वतः सोमाभिषवं कुर्वतो व्यक्तबर्हिषः
> स्त्यीर्णबर्हिषो यजमानस्याविता रक्षितासि । भवसि । मदाय मदार्थं सोमं
> पिब । हे सत्पते सतां पत इंद्र ते तुभ्यं यं सोमस्य भागमधारयन् सर्वे
> देवा अकल्पयन् । तथा च यजुर्ब्राह्मणं । स एतं माहेंद्रमुद्धारमुदहरत
> वृत्रं हत्वान्यासु देवतास्वधि । तै. सं. ६-५-५-३ । इति । तं भागं विश्वाः पृतनाः
> शत्रूणां सर्वाः सेना उरु बहु ज्रयो वेगं च सं सेहानः सम्यगभिभवन्नप्सुजिदप्पुजेता च सन् पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śatakratu, many-deeded Indra, you are the protector of the sacrificer who presses the Soma and has strewn the sacred grass. Drink the Soma for your exhilaration. O Satpati, lord of the good, Indra, the portion of Soma that all the gods assigned to you: the Yajur Brāhmaṇa says स एतं माहेंद्रमुद्धारमुदहरत वृत्रं हत्वान्यासु देवतास्वधि (*sa etaṃ māheṃdramuddhāramudaharata vṛtraṃ hatvānyāsu devatāsvadhi*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-5-3) **GLOSS**. That portion, overcoming all the hosts of enemies and their great speed, being the conqueror in the waters, drink it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O Indra, who have done many deeds of valour
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—who has pressed the Soma juice to offer to you
- व्यक्तबर्हिषः (*vyaktabarhiṣaḥ*)—who has prepared and spread the cut darbha grass as a seat
- अविता (*avitā*)—protector
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- हे सत्पते (*he satpate*)—O protector of the good
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मरुत्तान् (*maruttān*)—who are with the Marut deities

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who have done many deeds of valour, you are the protector of the sacrificer who has pressed the Soma juice for you and has prepared and spread the cut darbha grass as a seat. O Indra, protector of the good, who are with the Marut deities **NOTE**, who defeat well the speed of the enemy hosts, who are the controller of the clouds, drink for your delight the portion of Soma which the gods have assigned to you.

> प्र त्र॒सद॑स्युमानिध॒ त्वमेक॒ इन्न॒षाह्य॒ इंद्र॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि व॒र्धय॑न् ॥ ७ ॥

> प्र । त्रसदस्युं । आविथ । त्वं । एकः । इत् । नृसह्ये । इंद्र । ब्रह्माणि । वर्धयन् ॥७॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, hear the praise of me, Śyāvāśva, who press the Soma, as you heard that of Atri, who was performing rites. Moreover, you alone, in battle, strengthening the prayers (the hymns of praise) by fulfilling desires, protected Trasadasyu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- कर्माणि (*karmāṇi*)—rites such as sacrifices, directed to you
- कृण्वतः (*kṛṇvataḥ*)—who was performing
- अत्रेः (*atreḥ*)—the praise of the seer Atri
- यथा अशृणोः (*yathā aśṛṇoḥ*)—as you listened with respect
- तथा (*tathā*)—so
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—who is pressing the Soma to offer to you
- श्यावाश्वस्य (*śyāvāśvasya*)—of me, named Śyāvāśva, also the praise
- शृणु (*śṛṇu*)—hear
- त्वमेक इत् (*tvameka it*)—you alone (without the help of others)
- नृषाह्ये (*nṛṣāhye*)—in battle
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—hymns of praise directed to you
- वर्धयन् (*vardhayan*)—who was reciting
- त्रसदस्युं (*trasadasyuṃ*)—the king named Trasadasyu
- प्र आविथ (*pra āvitha*)—you protected, did you not

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as you listened with respect to the praise of the seer Atri, who was performing sacrifices and other rites directed to you, so hear also the praise of me, named Śyāvāśva. You alone, in the past, without the help of others, protected, did you not, the king named Trasadasyu, who was entreating you with hymns of praise.

##### English translation
Hear (the praises) of Syavashwa offering the libations, as you have heard (those) of Atri engaged in holy rites : you alone, Indra, have defended Trasadasyu in battle, animating his prayers.

### Printed p. 329
## Sūkta 37 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रेदं ब्रह्मेति सप्तर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तमात्रेयस्य श्यावाश्वस्यार्षं । आद्या
> द्वापंचाशदक्षरातिजगती । शिष्टाः षडृचः षडष्टका महापंक्तयः । इंद्रो देवता।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्रेदं महापांक्तमाद्यातिजगतीति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य
> एतत्तूक्तं । तथा च सूत्रं । प्रेदं ब्रह्मेंद्रो मदाय । आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the seventh sūkta, beginning प्रेदं ब्रह्मेति (*predaṃ brahmeti*), of seven Ṛks; its seer is Śyāvāśva of the family of Atri. The first Ṛk is an Atijagatī of fifty-two syllables; the remaining six Ṛks are Mahāpaṅktis of six octosyllabic pādas. Indra is the deity. The Anukramaṇī says प्रेदं महापांक्तमाद्यातिजगतीति (*predaṃ mahāpāṃktamādyātijagatīti*). This sūkta is used at the Niṣkevalya of the Mahāvrata, and the sūtra says so: प्रेदं ब्रह्मेंद्रो मदाय (*predaṃ brahmeṃdro madāya*) (Ā. 7-12).

This sūkta beginning Prā-idaṃ brahma is the seventh sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Śyāvāśva, born in the family of Atri; its deity is Indra. The first Ṛk of the sūkta is in the metre called Atijagatī, of fifty-two syllables. The remaining six Ṛks are in the metre called Mahāpaṅkti, of six pādas of eight syllables each. The Anukramaṇī says: Preḍaṃ mahāpāṅktam ādyātijagatī. This sūkta is to be recited when the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited in the Mahāvrata sacrifice, as the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains by the sūtra Predaṃ brahmendro madāya (Ā. 7-12).

Sūkta 37. Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 5. Sūkta 37. Aṣṭaka 6. Adhyāya 3. Varga 19. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: Śyāvāśva **NOTE**. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1 Atijagatī; 2-7 Mahāpaṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रेदं ब्रह्म॑ वृत्र॒तूर्ये॑ष्टाविथ॒ प्र सु॑न्व॒तः श॑चीपत॒ इंद्र॒  
> विश्वा॑भिरू॒तिभिः॑ ।  
> माध्यं॑दिनस्य॒ सव॑नस्य वृत्रहन्ननेद्य॒ पिबा॒ सोम॑स्य वज्रिवः ॥१५॥

### Printed p. 330

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । इदं । ब्रह्म । वृत्रतूर्येषु । आविथ । प्र । सुन्वतः । शचीपते । इंद्र ।  
> विश्वाभिः । ऊतिभिः ।  
> माध्यंदिनस्य । सवनस्य । वृत्रहन् । अनेद्य । पिब । सोमस्य । वज्रिवः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शचीपत इंद्र त्वं वृत्रतूर्येषु संग्रामेष्टिदं ब्रह्मेमान् ब्राह्मणान्विश्वाभिः सर्वाभिरूतिभी रक्षाभिः प्राविथ । प्ररक्ष । सुन्वतः सोमाभिषवं कुर्वतो
> यजमानांश्च प्राविथ । आपि च हे अनेद्यानिंद्य वज्रिवो वज्रिन् वृत्रहन्निंद्र
> माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य संबंधिनं सोमस्य सोमं पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śacīpati, lord of rites, Indra, in the battles with Vṛtra and other foes you have fully protected these brāhmaṇas with all your protections, and you have protected the sacrificers who press the Soma. Moreover, O blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma belonging to the midday pressing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शचीपते (*śacīpate*)—O lord of all rites
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृत्रतूर्येषु (*vṛtratūryeṣu*)—in battles that destroy enemies
- इदं ब्रह्म (*idaṃ brahma*)—these brāhmaṇas
- विश्वाभिः (*viśvābhiḥ*)—all
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—with protections
- प्र आविथ (*pra āvitha*)—you have fully protected
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—the sacrificer who offers Soma
- प्र (*pra*)—you have protected
- अनेद्य (*anedya*)—blameless
- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—wielder of the thunderbolt
- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—slayer of Vṛtra
- माध्यंदिनस्य (*mādhyaṃdinasya*)—performed at midday
- सवनस्य (*savanasya*)—connected with the sacrifice
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—the Soma
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of all rites, in the battles that destroy enemies you have fully protected these brāhmaṇas with all your protections. You have protected also the sacrificer who offers Soma. O blameless one, wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of Vṛtra, Indra, drink the Soma offered in the sacrifice performed at midday.

##### English translation
You protect, Indra, lord of rites, with all protections in combats with enemies, this sacrifice of him who offers you the libations : slayer of Vritra, irrproachable wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the mid-day solemnity.

- विश्वाभिः (*viśvābhiḥ*)—all
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—with protections
- अवसि (*avasi*)—you protect everyone
- न आविथ (*na āvitha*)—but for your own protection you need no one's help
- अनेद्य (*anedya*)—blameless
- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—wielder of the thunderbolt
- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—slayer of Vṛtra, O Indra
- माध्यंदिनस्य (*mādhyaṃdinasya*)—performed at midday
- सवनस्य (*savanasya*)—offered in the sacrifice
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—the Soma
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, protector of rites, you alone are able to display true strength. With all your protections you yourself protect everyone, but for your own protection you need no one's help. Blameless one, wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of Vṛtra, O Indra, drink the Soma offered in the sacrifice performed at midday.

##### English translation
You are for the strength (of the world); you protect with all your protections, but you need no defender, Indra, lord of rites; slayer of Vritra. irreproachable wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the mid day solemnity.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as you heard the praises of the great seer Atri, who performs excellent sacrificial rites, so hear also my praises, mine, the praiser, known as Śyāvāśva. And increasing Trasadasyu's strength in battle, you, unequalled and without the help of others, protected Trasadasyu completely.

## Sūkta 38 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यज्ञस्य हीति दशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं श्वावाश्वस्यार्षं प्राग्वत्सप्रपरिभाषया
> गायत्रमिंद्राग्नि देवताकं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । यज्ञस्य दशैंद्राग्नमिति ॥ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवषडहयोः प्रातःसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्र आवापार्थमेतसूक्तं । सूत्रितं च ।
> यज्ञस्य हि स्थ इत्यच्छावाकस्य । आ. ७-५ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि प्रातःसवने
> यज्ञस्य हि स्थ इति षळहस्तोत्रियसंज्ञ कस्त्रचः । सूत्रितं च । इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे
> यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋज्जिजेत्यच्छावाकस्य । अ. ७-२ । इति ॥ अग्निष्टोमे प्रातःसवनेच्छावाकस्य प्रातर्यावभिरिति प्रातःसवनीयस्य प्रस्थितयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्रातर्यावभिरिति यजति । आ. ५-७ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिके प्रातःसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्रे श्यावाश्वस्येत्ययं पर्यासस्तृचः । अन्यत्राप्यहर्गणेषु द्वितीयादिष्टहःसु । सूत्र्यते हि ।
> श्यावाश्वस्य सुन्वत इति तृजाः पर्यासाः । आ. ७-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning यज्ञस्य हि (*yajñasya hi*) is the eighth hymn, of ten verses. Its seer is Śyāvāśva, as before; its metre is Gāyatra; its deity is Indra and Agni. The Anukramaṇī says that the ten verses beginning with this are addressed to Indra and Agni. At the morning pressing of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas this hymn is for the Acchāvāka's insertion into the Stomas, as the sūtra यज्ञस्य हि स्थ इत्यच्छावाकस्य (*yajñasya hi stha ityacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-5) shows. On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, the triplet beginning with this verse is the Ṣaḷahastotriya triplet, as the sūtra on the Acchāvāka (Ā. 7-2) shows. In the Agniṣṭoma, at the morning pressing, the Acchāvāka's offering-verse of the morning pressing is the verse प्रातर्यावभिः (*prātaryāvabhiḥ*) (Ā. 5-7). In the Acchāvāka's Śastra at the morning pressing of the Cāturviṃśika day, the triplet beginning श्यावाश्वस्य (*śyāvāśvasya*) is the Paryāsa triplet; likewise in the other aggregates of days, from the second day onward, as the sūtra श्यावाश्वस्य सुन्वत इति तृचाः पर्यासाः (*śyāvāśvasya sunvata iti tṛcāḥ paryāsāḥ*) (Ā. 7-2) says.

##### Anuvāda

This hymn beginning यज्ञस्य हि (*yajñasya hi*) is the eighth hymn in the fifth Anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. As for the preceding hymn, Śyāvāśva is the seer of this hymn; Indra and Agni are the deities; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: ten verses beginning यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*) are addressed to Indra and Agni. It is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra यज्ञस्य हि स्थ इत्यच्छावाकस्य (*yajñasya hi stha ityacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-5), that at the morning pressing of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭha and Abhiplavaṣaḍaha the priest called Acchāvāka should recite this hymn for the insertion of the Stomas. It is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra beginning इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāmime*) (Ā. 7-2), that at the morning pressing on the day called Cāturviṃśika the triplet यज्ञस्य हि स्थः (*yajñasya hi sthaḥ*) should be recited as the Ṣaḷahastotriya triplet. It is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra प्रातर्यानभिरिति यजति (*prātaryānabhiriti yajati*) (Ā. 5-7), that in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, at the morning pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka should recite the seventh Ṛk of this hymn, beginning प्रातर्यावभिः (*prātaryāvabhiḥ*), as the Prasthitayājyā mantra of the morning pressing.

### Printed p. 338
And in the Śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka at the morning pressing on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, the eighth Ṛk of this hymn, श्यावाश्वस्य (*śyāvāśvasya*), should be recited as the Paryāsa triplet. In other places also, such as the Ahargaṇa, from the second day onward, this mantra should be recited as the Paryāsa triplet, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra श्यावाश्वस्य सुन्वत इति तृचाः पर्यासाः (*śyāvāśvasya sunvata iti tṛcāḥ paryāsāḥ*) (Ā. 7-2).

Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 38 **NOTE**.
Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 3; Varga 20, 21.
Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 10.
Seer: Śyāvāśva.
Deity: Indra and Agni.
Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒ज्ञस्य॒ हि स्थ ऋ॒त्विजा॒ सस्नी॒ वाजे॑षु॒ कर्म॑सु ।  
> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ तस्य॑ बोधतं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यज्ञस्य । हि । स्थः । ऋत्विजा । सस्नी इति । वाजेषु । कर्मसु ।  
> इंद्राग्नी इति । तस्य । बोधतं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी सस्नि शुद्धौ युवां यजस्यर्त्विजा ऋत्विजौ स्थः । भवथः ।
> वाजेषु कर्मसु युद्देषु वोपतिष्ठंताविंद्राग्नी तस्य तं मां तस्य मम स्तुतिं
> ना बोधतं । जानीतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, pure ones, you are the priests of the sacrifice. In battles and in rites, being present, know me and my praise. The rest is established. **NOTE**

- ऋत्विजा (*ṛtvijā*)—in the form of priests
- स्थः हि (*sthaḥ hi*)—you are, are you not
- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—in battles
- कर्मसु (*karmasu*)—and in sacrificial rites
- तस्य (*tasya*)—this praise of mine
- बोधतं (*bodhataṃ*)—know

## Sūkta 39 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निमस्तोषीति दशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं काण्वस्य नाभाकस्यार्षं । षडष्टका ।
> महापांक्तिश्चंदः । अग्निर्देवता । अनुक्रांतं च । अग्निमस्तोषि नाभाक आग्नेयं
> महापांक्तं हीति ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning अग्निमस्तोषि (*agnimastoṣi*) is the ninth hymn, of ten verses. Its seer is Nābhāka of the Kaṇva line; its deity is Agni; its metre is Mahāpaṅkti, of six eights (eight-syllable pādas). The Anukramaṇī says that Nābhāka, in the hymn beginning अग्निमस्तोषि (*agnimastoṣi*), composed an Agni hymn in Mahāpaṅkti. The use is by indication (liṅga).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn beginning अग्निमस्तोषि (*agnimastoṣi*) is the ninth hymn in the fifth Anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is Nābhāka, born in the Kaṇva line; Agni is the deity; the metre is Mahāpaṅkti with six pādas of eight syllables. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अग्निमस्तोषि नाभाक आग्नेयं महापांक्तं हि (*agnimastoṣi nābhāka āgneyaṃ mahāpāṃktaṃ hi*). The use is by indication.

> अग्निक । देवान् । अनक्तु । नः । उभे इति । हि । विदथे इति । कविः । अंतरिति । चरति ।  
> दूत्यं । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ १ ॥

> ऋग्नियमृगर्हमग्निमस्तोषि । स्तौमि । अपि जाग्निं यजध्यै यॆष्टुमीळा

> हिंस्यंतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I praise Agni, who is worthy of praise; I also praise Agni with a hymn in order to sacrifice. May Agni at our sacrifice anoint the gods with the oblations. ##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise Agni, who is worthy of worship. In order to sacrifice I extol Agni with praise. May Agni make the gods shine at our sacrifice. The far-seeing Agni performs, in the middle of heaven and earth, the messenger's work of carrying the oblation. May all our enemies be destroyed together.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ मन्मा॑नि॒ तुभ्यं॒ कं घृ॒तं न जु॑ह्व आ॒सनि॑ ।  
> स दे॒वेषु॒ प्र चि॑कित्सिद्दि॒ त्वं ह्यसि॑ पू॒र्व्यः शि॒वो दू॒तो वि॒वस्व॑तो॒  
> नभं॑तामन्य॒के स॑मे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । मन्मानि । तुभ्यं । कं । घृतं । जुह्वे । आसनि ।  
> सः । देवेषु । प्र । चिकिद्दि । त्वं । हि । असि । पूर्व्यः । शिवः । दूतः । विवस्वतः ।  
> नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 350

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने शुभ्यं त्वदर्थमासन्यास्ये कं धृतं न यथा सुखकरं धृतं
> जुह्वत्यन्ये तद्वदहमपि तवास्ये मन्मानि मननीयानि स्तोत्राणि जुह्वे । जुहोमि ।
> स त्वं देवेषु देवानां मध्ये प्र चिकिद्धि । अस्मदीयाः स्तुतीर्जानीहि । अपि
> च त्वं पूर्व्यः प्रत्नोऽसि । शिवः सुखकरश्चासि । विवस्वतो दूतश्चासि । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, for you, in your mouth, as others offer pleasant ghee, so I too offer pleasing praises. Among the gods, know our praises. You are ancient and beneficent, and you are the messenger of Vivasvat. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—addressed to you
- आसनि (*āsani*)—in your mouth
- कं (*kaṃ*)—pleasant
- धृतं न (*dhṛtaṃ na*)—as others offer ghee
- मन्मानि (*manmāni*)—meditative praises
- जुह्वे (*juhve*)—I offer
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, the well known
- प्र चिकिद्दि (*pra cikiddi*)—fully know our praises
- त्वं हि (*tvaṃ hi*)—you yourself
- पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*)—ancient
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- शिवः (*śivaḥ*)—auspicious
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—to Vivasvat
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—a messenger as well
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—together
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them be destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, as others offer pleasant ghee into your mouth in your honour, so I offer meditative praises. You, well known among the gods, fully know our praises. You are ancient. You are auspicious, and a messenger to Vivasvat. May all our enemies be destroyed together.

##### English translation
I pour into your mouth, Agni, praises as others (fill it) with delicious butter ; do you amidst the gods acknowledge (them), for you are ancient, the giver of happiness, the messenger of Vivaswat ; may all our enemies perish.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तत्त॑द॒ग्निर्वयो॑ दधे॒ यथा॑यथा कृप॒ण्यति॑ ।  
> ऊ॒र्जाहु॑ति॒र्वसू॑नां॒ शं च॒ योश्च॒ मयो॑ दधे॒ विश्व॑स्यॆ  
> दे॒वहू॑त्यै॒ नभं॑तामन्य॒के स॑मे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत्त्वतः । अग्निः । वयः । दधे ! यथायथा । कृपण्यति ।  
> ऊर्जा आहुतिः । वसूनां । शं । च । योः । च । मयः । दधे । विश्वस्यै । देवहूत्यै । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यथा यथा यद्यदन्नं कृपण्यति स्तोतृभिर्याच्यते तत्तद्वयोऽग्निर्दधे !
> स्तोतृभ्यः । प्रयच्छति । आपि चोर्जाहुतिरन्नेनाहूयमानोऽग्निर्वसूनां हविषां
> वासकानां यजमानानां शं शांतिनिमित्तं योर्विषययोगजनितं च मयः सुखं
> दधे । करोति । विश्वस्यॆ देवहूत्यै सर्वस्मै देवानां ह्वानाय च भवति । यः
> कश्चनापि देवो यदि हूयते अग्निरेव सर्वं करोतीत्यर्थः । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Whatever food the worshippers ask of Agni in whatever way, Agni grants to them. Invoked with the oblation of food, he bestows on the sacrificers, who dwell with their offerings, happiness: that which comes from tranquillity and that which comes from the enjoyment of objects of sense. He is the means for the invocation of all the gods; whatever god is invoked, Agni alone does everything. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यथायथा (*yathāyathā*)—in whatever manner
- कृपण्यति (*kṛpaṇyati*)—(Agni) is asked for food
- तत्तत् (*tattat*)—all such kinds of
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- दधे (*dadhe*)—gives to the worshippers
- ऊर्जाहुतिः (*ūrjāhutiḥ*)—Agni, who has food for his oblation
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—to the sacrificers who offer oblations
- शं च (*śaṃ ca*)—that which is a cause of tranquillity
- योः च (*yoḥ ca*)—and that which removes sorrow
- मयः (*mayaḥ*)—happiness
- दधे (*dadhe*)—he produces
- विश्वस्यॆ (*viśvasyè*)—all
- देवहूत्यै (*devahūtyai*)—he is also the means for the invocation of the gods
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—all alike
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them be destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In whatever manner Agni is asked for food, he gives all such food to the worshippers. Agni, who has food for his oblation, produces for the sacrificers who offer oblations happiness that is a cause of tranquillity and a remover of sorrow. He is the means for the invocation of all the gods. May all our enemies be destroyed all alike.

##### English translation
Agni grants whatever food is solicited : invoked with offerings, he bestows on the worshippers happiness springing from tranquillity and the

### Printed p. 352

enjoymet (of objects of sense) ; he is requisite for all invocation of the gods : may all our adversaries perish.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स चि॑केत॒ सही॑यसा॒ग्निश्चि॒त्रेण॒ कर्म॑णा ।  
> स होता॒ शश्व॑तीनां॒ दक्षि॑णाभिर॒भीवृ॑त इ॒नोति॑ च प्रती॒व्यं१॒॑ग ॒॑ ॑
> नभंतामन्यके समे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । चिकेत । सहीयसा । अग्निः । चित्रेण । कर्मणा ।  
> सः । होता । शश्वतीनां । दक्षिणाभिः । अभिवृतः । इनोति । च । प्रतीव्यं । नभंतां ।  
> अन्यके । समे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोऽग्निः सहीयसाभिभावुकेन चित्रेण नानाविधेन कर्मणा व्यापारेण चिकेत ।
> ज्ञायते । सोऽग्निः शश्वतीनां बह्वीनां देवातानां होता ह्वाता दक्षिणाभिः
> पशुभिश्चाभीवृतः प्रतीव्यं प्रत्येकव्यं शत्रुमिनोति च । गच्छति च । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Agni is known by his most powerful and manifold deeds, his varied activity. That Agni is the invoker of the many gods, and, surrounded by the victims given as sacrificial gifts, he goes against the foe and attacks him. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*)—that same Agni
- सहीयसा (*sahīyasā*)—with power to overcome enemies
- चित्रेण (*citreṇa*)—and manifold
- कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*)—by deed
- चिकेत (*ciketa*)—is renowned
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- शश्वतीनां (*śaśvatīnāṃ*)—to many gods
- होता (*hotā*)—is the one who gives the invocation
- दक्षिणाभिः (*dakṣiṇābhiḥ*)—together with the cattle
- अभीवृतः (*abhīvṛtaḥ*)—surrounded
- प्रतीव्यं (*pratīvyaṃ*)—the foe
- इनोति च (*inoti ca*)—he withstands
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—all alike
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them be destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That renowned Agni is known by his manifold deeds, which have the power to overcome enemies. That same Agni is the one who gives invocation to many gods. Surrounded by cattle, he withstands the enemies. May all our enemies be destroyed all alike.

### Printed p. 353

##### English translation
Agni is known by his most powerful and manifold deeds : he is the invoker of the eternals: surrounded by victims he proceeds against the foe ; may all our adversaries perish.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निर्जा॒ता दे॒वाना॑म॒ग्निर्वे॑द॒ मर्ता॑नामपी॒च्यं॑ ।  
> अ॒ग्निः स द्र॑विणो॒दा अ॒ग्निर्द्वारा॒ व्य॑र्णुते॒ स्वा॑हुतो॒  
> नवी॑यसा॒ नभं॑तामन्य॒के स॑मे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निः । जाता । देवानां । अग्निः । वेद । मर्तानां । अपीच्यं ।  
> अग्निः । सः । प्रविणःवाः । अग्निः । द्वारा । वि । ऊर्णते । सुआहुतः । नवीयसा ।  
> नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवानां जाता जातानि जन्मान्यग्निर्वेत्ति मर्तानां मनुष्याणां
> चापीच्यं गुह्यमग्निर्वेद । वेत्ति । सोऽग्निर्द्वनिहोदा धनस्य दाता । नवीयसा
> नवतरेण हविषा स्वाहुतः सम्यग्गुतोऽग्निर्दार्वा धनस्य द्वाराणि व्यूर्णुते च ।
> सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni knows the births of the gods and likewise the secrets of mortals, men. That same Agni is the giver of wealth. Duly offered to with a newer oblation, Agni opens the doors of wealth. The rest is established. **NOTE**

- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them be destroyed

### Printed p. 354

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni knows the births of the gods. He also knows the secrets of men. That same Agni is also the giver of wealth. Agni, well worshipped with a new oblation, opens fully the doors of wealth. May all our enemies be destroyed together.

##### English translation
Agni knows the births of the gods; Agni knows the secrets of mankind: Agni is the giver of riches; Agni, duly worshipped with a new (oblation), sets open the doors (of opulence): may all our adversaries perish.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स मु॒दा काव्या॑ पु॒रु विश्वं॒ भूमे॑व पुष्यति दे॒वो दे॒वेषु॑

> सः । मुदा । काव्या । पुरु । विश्वं । भूमइव । पुष्यति । देवः । देवेषु । यज्ञियः ।

> यज्ञार्हश्च भवति । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among the gods Agni dwells together with them; that same Agni dwells also among the peoples who are fit for sacrifice. Further, that Agni cherishes with pleasure many deeds, as the earth cherishes the whole world. Among the gods, the god Agni is worthy of sacrifice. The rest is established.

- काव्या (*kāvyā*)—deeds
- मुदा (*mudā*)—with joy
- पुष्यति (*puṣyati*)—he nourishes

- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—Agni, who is of the nature of a god
- यज्ञियः (*yajñiyaḥ*)—is worthy of sacrifice
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them be destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni dwells happily among the gods. That same Agni dwells among the peoples fit for sacrifice. As the earth nourishes all, that same Agni joyfully nourishes many kinds of deeds. Agni, who is of the nature of a god, is worthy of sacrifice among the gods. May all our enemies be destroyed at the same time.

##### English translation
Agni has his abode among the gods; he (dwells) among pious people: he cherishes with pleasure many pious acts, as the earth all (beings); a god adorable among the gods : may all our adversaries perish.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमाग॑न्न त्रिप॒स्यं मं॑धा॒तुद॑स्यु॒हंत॑मम॒ग्निं य॒ज्ञेषु॑  
> पू॒र्व्यं नभं॑तामन्य॒के स॑मे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यति । अग्निः । सप्तमानुषः । श्रितः । विश्वेषु । सिंधुषु ।  
> तं । आ । अगन्म । त्रिपस्यं । मंधातुः ! दस्युहन्तमं । अग्निं । यज्ञेषु ।  
> पूर्व्यं । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निः सप्तमानुषो विश्वेषु सर्वॆषु सिंधुषु नदीषु श्रितस्त्रिपस्यं
> त्रिस्थानं मंधातुर्यौवनाश्वस्य मांधातुर्गस्युहंतमं दस्यूनां हंतारं
> यज्ञेषु पूर्व्यं मुख्यं तमग्निं वयमागन्म । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, served by seven priests, who has taken refuge in all the rivers, who has a triple abode, who is the slayer of the Dasyus for Māndhātṛ, the son of Yuvanāśva, and who is chief in the sacrifices: that Agni we approach. The rest is established. **NOTE**

- यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*)—and chief
- तं अग्निं (*taṃ agniṃ*)—that same Agni
- आ अगन्म (*ā aganma*)—let us approach
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them be destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us approach that same Agni, who has seven kinds of priests, who has taken refuge in all the rivers, who has three abodes, who destroyed the demons for Māndhātṛ, and who is chief in the sacrifices. May all our enemies be destroyed at the same time.

##### English translation
Let us approach that Agni who is ministered to by seven priests: who takes refuge in all rivers, who has a triple dwelling place, the slayer of the Dasya for Mandhatri, who is foremost in sacrifices : may all our adversaries perish.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कविः क्रांतदर्शग्निस्त्रीणि त्रिधातूनि त्रिदंधनादीनि पृथिव्यादीनि विदथा वेदनीयानि स्थानान्या क्षेति . अवसति । अपि च सोऽग्निर्दूतो देवानां विप्रः प्राज्ञः
> परिष्कृतोऽलंकृतश्च सन्निह यज्ञे त्रिनेकादशांत्रयस्त्रंशद्देवान्यक्षत् । यजतु ।
> नोऽस्मान् पिप्रयच्च । कामैः पूरयतु च । सिद्धमन्यत् .

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the far-seeing sage, dwells in the three places, which are to be known: the threefold-based worlds, the earth and the rest. **NOTE** Further, that Agni, the messenger of the gods, wise and adorned, shall worship here in the sacrifice the thrice eleven gods, the thirty-three. Let him worship them, and let him fulfil us with our desires. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the far-seeing
- अग्नि (*agni*)—Agni
- त्रीणि (*trīṇi*)—of three kinds
- त्रिधातूनि (*tridhātūni*)—pervading the three worlds, the earth and the rest
- विदथा (*vidathā*)—in the places that are well known
- आ क्षेति (*ā kṣeti*)—dwells
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—as the messenger of the gods
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—wise
- परिष्कृतः (*pariṣkṛtaḥ*)—and adorned
- इह (*iha*)—here in this sacrifice
- त्रीनेकादशान् (*trīnekādaśān*)—the gods who are thirty-three in number
- यक्षत् (*yakṣat*)—let him worship
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पिप्रयच्च (*piprayacca*)—let him fill with the objects of our desire
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them be destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the far-seeing, dwells in the three places, threefold and pervading the three worlds, the earth and the rest. That same Agni, being the messenger of the gods, wise and adorned, shall worship the gods, thirty-three in number, in this sacrifice. Let him fill us with the objects of our desire. May all our enemies be destroyed at the same time.

##### English translation
Agni, the sage, inhabits the three elementary regions; may he, intelligent, and richly decorated, the messenger (of the gods), here perform worship to the thrice eleven deities, and satisfy all our desires: may all our enemies perish.

> हे पूर्वाग्ने त्वमेक एवायुषु मनुष्येषु । द्रुह्यव आयव इति मनुष्यनामसु पाठात् । नोऽस्माकं वस्वो धनस्येरज्यसि । ईशिषे । देवेष्वपि त्वमेक एव

> यंति । परिगच्छंति । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O ancient Agni, you alone among the Āyus, that is, among men, since the word is read among the names of men together with Druhyu, are lord of wealth for us. Among the gods too you alone are lord of wealth. Further, the waters, which have made their own banks and flow all around, go about you. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूर्व्य (*pūrvya*)—ancient
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni

- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—of wealth

- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you alone are the lord
- स्वसेतवः (*svasetavaḥ*)—those that have obtained their own limit for themselves
- परिस्रुतः (*parisrutaḥ*)—and flow
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- परि यंति (*pari yaṃti*)—flow around
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O ancient Agni, among all men you alone are the lord of our wealth. Among the gods too you alone are the lord. The waters, which have made their own banks and flow, flow around you. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
You, ancient Agni, among men and gods, are alone to us the lord of wealth; the flowing waters confined within their own banks flow around you : may all our enemies perish.

## Sūkta 40 (Maṇḍala 8)

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्राग्नी युवमिति द्वादशर्चं दशमं सूक्तं नाभाकस्यार्षं । द्वितीया
> षट्पंचाशदक्षरा तक्वरी द्वादशी तिष्युन् शिष्टा महापंक्तयः । इंद्राग्नी देवता ।
> तथा चानुत्रांतं । इंद्राग्नी द्वादशेंद्राग्नं त्रिष्टुबंतं द्वितीया शक्वरीति ॥
> महाव्रते नित्येवल्य ऊरुभाग एव सूक्तं ! पथा च पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं । ऊरू
> इंद्राग्नी युवं सु नः । ऐ. आ. ५-३-१ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि तृतीयसवने
> मैत्रावरुणो यदि महानालभिदं शंसेत्तदानीं माध्यंदिनसवने होत्रकाः
> स्वशस्त्र आरंभणीयाभ्य ऊर्ध्वं नाभाकतृचावावपेरन् । तत्र ता हि मध्यमित्यच्छावाकस्य नाभाकतृचः । सूत्रितं चॆ । ता हि मध्यं भराणामित्यच्छावाकः । अ. ७-२ ।
> इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः पूर्विष्ट इंद्रेति
> नाभाकतृचः ! सूत्रितं चॆ । पूर्विष्ट इंद्रोपमातय इति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी ।
> अ. ७-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning इंद्राग्नी युवं (*iṃdrāgnī yuvaṃ*) is the tenth hymn, of twelve Ṛks, and its seer is Nābhāka. The second Ṛk is Takvarī (Śakvarī) of fifty-six syllables; the twelfth is Triṣṭubh; the rest are Mahāpaṅktis. The deity is Indra and Agni. So it is also stated in the Anukramaṇī, in the words इंद्राग्नी द्वादशेंद्राग्नं त्रिष्टुबंतं द्वितीया शक्वरी (*iṃdrāgnī dvādaśeṃdrāgnaṃ triṣṭubaṃtaṃ dvitīyā śakvarī*). In the Mahāvrata, the hymn stands in the thigh part of the niṣkevalya (shastra); and in the fifth Āraṇyaka it is laid down in the words ऊरू इंद्राग्नी युवं सु नः (*ūrū iṃdrāgnī yuvaṃ su naḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-3-1). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the third pressing, if the Maitrāvaruṇa recites the Mahānālabhid, then at the midday pressing the Hotrakas, after the beginning of their own shastra, are to insert the Nābhāka tṛca after the introductory verses: there the Nābhāka tṛca of the Acchāvāka is the verses beginning ता हि मध्यं (*tā hi madhyaṃ*); and it is laid down in a sūtra: ता हि मध्यं भराणामित्यच्छावाकः (*tā hi madhyaṃ bharāṇāmityacchāvākaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-2). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the Nābhāka tṛca of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is the verses beginning पूर्विष्ट इंद्र (*pūrviṣṭa iṃdra*); and it is laid down: पूर्विष्ट इंद्रोपमातय इति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी (*pūrviṣṭa iṃdropamātaya iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī*) (Ā. Sū. 7-2). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This hymn beginning इंद्राग्नी युवं (*iṃdrāgnī yuvaṃ*) is the tenth hymn in the fifth Anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is one named Nābhāta **NOTE**; Indra and Agni are the deity; the second Ṛk of this hymn is of the metre called Śakvarī, of fifty-six syllables; the twelfth Ṛk is of the Triṣṭup metre. The remaining Ṛks are of the Mahāpaṅkti metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इंद्राग्नी द्वादशैंद्राग्नं त्रिष्टुबंतं द्वितीया शक्वरी (*iṃdrāgnī dvādaśaiṃdrāgnaṃ triṣṭubaṃtaṃ dvitīyā śakvarī*). In the Mahāprateṣṭi **NOTE**, this hymn is to be recited among the niṣkevala shastra mantras; this is indicated in the Pañcama Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence ऊरू इंद्राग्नी युवं सु नः (*ūrū iṃdrāgnī yuvaṃ su naḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-3-1). On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the third pressing, if the priest named Maitrāvaruṇa recites the mantra called महावालभित् (*mahāvālabhit*), then, at the midday pressing, after the Ṛks of the Hotṛ class have begun the shastra mantras that they are to recite, the Nābhāka tṛca are to be recited for the purpose of insertion. There, the three Ṛks beginning ता हि मध्यं (*tā hi madhyaṃ*) (Ṛks 3-5 of this hymn) are named the Nābhāka tṛca to be recited by the Acchāvāka. This matter is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, by the sūtra ता हि मध्यं भराणामित्यच्छावाकः (*tā hi madhyaṃ bharāṇāmityacchāvākaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-2). Further, on the day called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, the priest named Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite as the Nābhāka tṛca Ṛks 9-11 of this hymn, beginning पूर्विष्ट इंद्र (*pūrviṣṭa iṃdra*); this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पूर्विष्ट इंद्रोपमातॆय इति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी (*pūrviṣṭa iṃdropamātèya iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī*) (Ā. Sū. 7-2).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, who overcome your enemies, you two give us wealth well. He qualifies that wealth: with which wealth we may overcome in battle the enemy forces, even the firm and steady ones, as fire overcomes the forests when driven by the wind. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वनेव (*vaneva*)—as he burns up the whole forest
- येन (*yena*)—with the help of which wealth
- समत्सु चित् (*samatsu cit*)—in battles
- दृढाचित् (*dṛḍhācit*)—even when exceedingly powerful

- वीळु (*vīḷu*)—the enemy forces
- सहिषीमहि (*sahiṣīmahi*)—we shall overcome
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—such wealth
- सहंता (*sahaṃtā*)—you who have the power to overcome enemies
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सु दासथः (*su dāsathaḥ*)—give in full
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, Agni, impelled by the wind, burns up the whole forest. With the help of which wealth we overcome the enemy forces in battles even when they are exceedingly powerful, such wealth do you, the destroyers of enemies, give to us in abundance. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Victorious Indra and Agni bestow upon us riches whereby we may destroy our powerful enemies in combats as fire fanned by the wind consumes the forests: may all our enemies perish.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, we do not ask you two for wealth. But then we worship Indra alone, the most powerful, the leader even of leaders of men.

> मिदिंद्रमेव यजामहे । स इंद्रो नोस्मानर्वताश्वेन कदा चिद्वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभाया गमत् । आगच्छति । कदाचिन्मेधसातये यज्ञ भजनाया गमत् । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra comes to us with his horse, sometimes for the gain of food; sometimes he comes for the sharing in the sacrifice. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजामहे (*yajāmahe*)—we worship
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अर्वता (*arvatā*)—with his horse
- कदाचित् (*kadācit*)—many times
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the gain of food
- आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—comes
- मेधसातये (*medhasātaye*)—also for the conduct of the sacrifice
- आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—comes

- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, we do not ask you two together. But we worship Indra alone, the exceedingly powerful, the leader of men. That Indra comes to us with his horse many times for the gain of food. He comes also for the conduct of the sacrifice. May all our enemies perish at the same time.

##### English translation
Do we not invoke you both ? we worship especially Indra, who is the strongest leader of men : he comes occasionally with his horses to bestow upon us food ; he comes to partake of the sacrifice : may all our enemies perish.

> ता । ऊं इति । कवित्वना । कवी इति । पृच्छ्यमाना । सखियते । सं । धीतं । अश्नुतं ।  
> नरा । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ३ ॥

> अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । हे नरा नेतारौ कवित्वना कवित्वेन कवी क्रांतकर्माणौ पृच्छ्यमाना

> धीतं तत्कृतं कर्म समश्नुतं । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those two well-known, Indra and Agni, dwell in the midst of battles. Then a direct praise: O leaders, sages, men of far-reaching deeds through sagehood, when asked by the wise, you two accept the work done for the sacrificer who desires your friendship. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पा (*pā*)—the well known **NOTE**
- इंद्राग्नि (*iṃdrāgni*)—both Indra and Agni
- भराणां (*bharāṇāṃ*)—of battles
- मध्यं (*madhyaṃ*)—in the midst
- अधिक्षितः हि (*adhikṣitaḥ hi*)—are able to stand firm
- नरा (*narā*)—the leaders
- कवित्वना (*kavitvanā*)—by their poetic deeds
- कवी (*kavī*)—the best doers of deeds
- पृच्छ्यमाना (*pṛcchyamānā*)—who are implored by the priests
- ता उ (*tā u*)—and well known, O Indra and Agni
- सखीयते (*sakhīyate*)—of him who desires your friendship
- धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)—the work endowed with wisdom
- समश्नुतं (*samaśnutaṃ*)—you accept
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—together
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The well-known Indra and Agni are able to stand firm in the midst of battles. O Indra and Agni, leaders, the best doers of deeds through your poetic deeds, who are implored by the priests, and well known, you accept the wise work of him who desires your friendship. May all our enemies perish together.

##### English translation
They two, Indra and Agni. are present in the midst of battles : do you two, leaders of rites. who are really sages, when solicited (by the wise), accept the offering (from him) who seeks your friendship : may all our enemies perish.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अभि । अर्च । नभाकवत् । इंद्राग्नी इति । यजसा । गिरा ।  
> ययोः । विश्वं । इदं । जगत् । इयं । द्यौः । पृथिवी । मही । उपस्थे । बिभृथः ।  
> वसु । नभंतां । अन्यके । समे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नाभाक नभाकवदिंद्राग्नी यजसा यागेन गिरा स्तुत्या चाभ्यर्च ।
> अभिपूजय ! ययोरिंद्राग्नोर्विस्त्वं सर्वमिदं जगत्तिष्ठति । ययोश्चोपस्थ
> इयं दौर्मही महती पृथिवी च द्यावापृधिव्यावुभे वसु धनं बिभृतः धारयतः।
> सिद्धमन्यत् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Nābhāka, worship Indra and Agni as Nābhāka did, with sacrifice and with praise. On those two, Indra and Agni, this whole world stands; and in the lap of those two, heaven and the great earth, both of them, bear wealth. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इदं जगत् (*idaṃ jagat*)—this whole world stands
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—on the lap of which Indra and Agni
- इयं द्यौः (*iyaṃ dyauḥ*)—this heaven
- मही (*mahī*)—the great
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—earth
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- बिभृतः (*bibhṛtaḥ*)—cause to be borne, such as they are
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—Indra and Agni
- यजसा (*yajasā*)—with sacrifice
- गिरा (*girā*)—and with praise
- अभ्यर्चॆ (*abhyarcè*)—worship
- अन्यके (*anyake*)—all our enemies
- समे (*same*)—at the same time
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—let them perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Nābhāka, on the support of which Indra and Agni this whole world stands, on the lap of which Indra and Agni this heaven and the great earth are made to bear wealth, such are those whom you are to worship. May all our enemies perish at the same time. **NOTE**

##### English translation
Worship, like Nabhaka, Indra and Agni with sacrifice and praise, of whom is this universe, upon whose lap this heaven and the spacious earth deposit their treasure : may all our enemies perish.

> या । सप्तबुध्वं । अर्णवं । जिह्मजारं । अपूर्णुतः । इंद्रः । ईशानः । ओजसा ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणींद्राग्निभ्यां नभाकवत्प्रेरज्यत । नाभाकः प्रेरयते । या

> तेजोभिराच्छादयतः तयोर्मध्य ओजसा बलेनेंद्र ईशान ईश्वरो भवति ।
> सिद्दमन्यत् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Praises are sent forth to Indra and Agni as Nābhāka sends them. Those two, Indra and Agni, who cover with their splendours the seven-rooted ocean whose door is closed: among them, by his might, Indra is the lord. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- या (*yā*)—the Indra and Agni who
- सप्तबुध्नं (*saptabudhnaṃ*)—having roots seven in number
- जिह्मजारं (*jihmajāraṃ*)—and having a closed door
- अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*)—the ocean
- अपोर्णुत (*aporṇuta*)—cover with their splendours
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—and (among whom) by his own valour
