### Printed p. 516

> चक्रम स्तुतिं हविर्वा । सद्यश्चित्तदानीमेव तवागमनानंतरमेव चक्रम महि
> महतो धनस्य दावने दात्रे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk, beginning with आ नो वायो (*ā no vāyo*), is the third in the Vāyavya tṛca in the Prauga śastra on the fifth day, as laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 7-12). O Vāyu, come to us. For what? For great wealth and for venerable strength, to give both. What is there here? We, indeed, have made praise or an oblation for you, the giver of abundant wealth. Immediately, that is, just after your coming, we have made it for you, the giver of great wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वायो (*vāyo*)—O Vāyu
- महे (*mahe*)—for great
- तने (*tane*)—giving of wealth
- मखाय (*makhāya*)—and venerable
- पाजसे (*pājase*)—giving of strength
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be gracious and come
- वयं हि (*vayaṃ hi*)—we indeed
- भूरि दावने (*bhūri dāvane*)—who gives most abundantly
- ते (*te*)—towards you
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—we compose excellent praise
- महि (*mahi*)—of great wealth
- दावने (*dāvane*)—to you, the giver
- सद्यश्चित् (*sadyaścit*)—as soon as you come, we offer it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, be gracious and come to us, to give great wealth and venerable strength. We, indeed, compose excellent praise towards you, who give most abundantly. To you, the giver of great wealth, we offer it as soon as you come.

##### English translation
Come to us, Vayu, to bestow great wealth and glorious strength; we have offered (libations) to you the giver of abundant (wealth), we have offered immediately to you the giver of gerat (gifts).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk, आ नो वायो (*ā no vāyo*), is to be recited as the third Ṛk among the three Ṛks of the Vāyavya tṛca **NOTE** in the Prauga-śastra mantras on the fifth day of the sacrifice; this is made clear by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra आ नो वायो महे तन इत्येका रथेन कृथुपाजसा (*ā no vāyo mahe tana ityekā rathena kṛthupājasā*) (Ā. Sū. 6 12) **NOTE**.

> यः पृथुश्रवा अश्वेभिरश्वैर्वहते गृहं वस्ते जोष्रा गाः । ताभिश्च गच्छतीत्यर्थः । त्रिः सप्तति तासां गवां संख्योक्ता । सा संख्या विशेष्यते । सप्ततीनां त्रिः
> सप्त । उक्तसंख्याकाभिर्गॊभिरश्वैश्च यो गच्छति स पृथुश्रवा एभिः सोमेभिः
> सोमैः सोमसुद्धिः सोममभिषुण्वद्भिश्च हे सोमपाः । सोमस्य पातरिति
> वायोः संबोधनं । जे शुक्रपूतसा दीप्तपूतस्य च सोमस्य पातर्वायो
> दानाय तुभ्यं सोमं दातुं सोमैर्युक्तो भवतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Pṛthuśravas goes with horses to his house, and with cows **NOTE**; that is the meaning. The number of those cows is stated as thrice seven seventies; the number is specified: thrice seven of seventies. That Pṛthuśravas, who goes with cows and horses of the stated number, with these Somas, that is, Soma juices, and with those who press Soma, is addressed: O Soma-drinker, drinker of Soma, which is a vocative of Vāyu; O drinker of bright and pure Soma, Vāyu. He is furnished with Soma, to give Soma to you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)—drinker of Soma
- शुक्रपूतपाः (*śukrapūtapāḥ*)—drinker of Soma that is pure and bright, O Vāyu
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- अश्वेभिः (*aśvebhiḥ*)—by horses
- वस्ते (*vaste*)—towards the house
- वहते (*vahate*)—is carried, and
- सप्ततीनां त्रिः सप्त (*saptatīnāṃ triḥ sapta*)—numbering seventy multiplied by twenty-one (70-20=140) **NOTE**
- उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)—provided with cows, such King Pṛthuśravas
- विभिः सोमेभिः (*vibhiḥ somebhiḥ*)—with these Somas
- सोमसुद्दिः (*somasuddiḥ*)—and with these priests who press Soma
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—is ready to offer to you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, drinker of the pure and bright Soma, the king named Pṛthuśravas, who is carried by horses towards his house and who is provided with cows numbering 1420 **NOTE**, is ready to offer a gift to you, together with these Somas and with these priests who press Soma.

##### English translation
He who is borne on horses and surrounds himself with thrice seven times seventy cows,—he comes to you with these Soma libations and Soma-priests, to offer to you, drinker of the Soma, drinker of the bright pure Soma.

> यो म॑ इ॒मं चि॑दु॒ त्मनामं॑दच्चि॒त्रंदा॒वने॑ ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । मे । इमं । चित् । ऊं इति । त्मना । अमंदत् । चित्रं । दावने ।  
> अरट्वे । अक्षे । नडुषे । सुकृत्वनि । सुकृत्तराय । सुक्रतु ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः पृथुश्रवा मे मह्यमिमं पुरतोवर्तमानं चित्रं चायनीयं
> गवाश्वादिकं दावने दानाय त्मनात्मना स्वबुद्धैवामंदत् आमंदत अमाद्यत । स
> च सुक्रतुः शोभनकर्मा राजा सुकृत्तराय सुकृतकर्तृत्वायारट्टेऽक्षे नहुषे
> सुकृत्वनि च । एते तस्य राज्योऽध्यक्षाः । तेप्वन्वशात् अस्मै गवाडिकान् संयोजयतेति । यद्वा। अरट्वादयोऽन्ये राजानः । तेषु मध्यॆ सुकृत्तरायामंददिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Pṛthuśravas, to me, this honourable gift before him, cows, horses and the rest, for giving, of his own accord, by his own mind, was pleased. And he, the king Sukratu, of good works, for greater good action, among Aratva **NOTE**, Akṣa, Nahuṣa and Sukṛtvan. These are the overseers of his kingdom; among them **NOTE**. Or else Aratva and the others are other kings; among them he was pleased for the sake of Sukṛttara.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- मे (*me*)—to me
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—described here
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—and attractive, wealth of cows and the rest
- दानवे (*dānave*)—for giving
- त्मना उ (*tmanā u*)—by his own impulse
- अमंदत् (*amaṃdat*)—has been pleased, such
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—the king named Pṛthuśravas, doer of excellent deeds
- अरट्टे, अक्षे, नहुषे, सुकृत्वनि (*araṭṭe, akṣe, nahuṣe, sukṛtvani*)—among these kings called Araṭṭa, Akṣa, Nahuṣa and Sukṛtva
- सुकृत्तराय (*sukṛttarāya*)—to perform the most excellent action (has resolved)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The king named Pṛthuśravas, the doer of excellent deeds, who of his own impulse is pleased to give me the wealth of cows and the rest described above, attractive as it is, has resolved to perform the most excellent action among these kings called Araṭṭa, Akṣa, Nahuṣa and Sukṛtva.

##### English translation
He who of his own will has been plased to give me this honoured gift,- he, performer of good works, (has determined) on a pre-emminetly good action, amidst Aradwa, Aksha, Nahusha and Sukritwan.

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒च्॒ये॒३॒॑ऽऽ वपु॑षि॒ यः स्व॒राळु॒त वा॑यो धृत॒स्नाः ।  
> अश्वे॑षितं॒ रजे॑षितं॒ रुने॑षितं॒ प्राज्ञ॒ तदि॒दं नु तत् ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उचथ्ये । वपुषि । यः । स्वराट् । उत । वायो इति । धृतस्नाः ।  
> अश्वइषितं । रजःइषितं । शुनाइषितं । प्र । अज्म । तत् । इदं । नु । तत् ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उचथ्ये वक्तव्ये स्तुत्ये वपुषि शरीरे यः स्वराट् स्वयं राजते । यद्वा।
> उचथ्यो वपुश्चोभौ राजान् । तयोरपि यः स्वराट् स्वाराज्यं करोति अतिशयेन
> वर्तते । हे वायो यश्च घृतस्ना घृतवच्चुद्धः स राजाश्वेषितमश्वैः प्रापितं रजेषितं । रजःशब्देनोष्टो गर्दभो वोच्यते । तेनाप्यानीतं कुनेषितं चाज्मान्नं
> प्रादात् । तदन्नमश्वाद्यानीतमिदं पुरतो दृश्यते । तत्तवैवानुग्रहादित्यर्थः ।
> अथवैकस्तच्छब्दः पूरणः । अश्वाद्यानीतं यदस्ति तदिदं खल्विति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He who is self-ruling, shining by himself, in the praiseworthy, that is, to be spoken of, body. Or else: Ucathya and Vapus are both kings; he who is self-ruling over both of them also, who exercises sovereignty and excels. O Vāyu, that king who is pure like ghee gave food brought by horses; and brought by camel or ass, for the word for dust denotes a camel or an ass **NOTE**; and brought by dogs **NOTE**. That food, brought by horses and the rest, is seen here in front; it is by your favour alone, such is the meaning. Or else the single word for "that" is a filler: what is brought by horses and the rest, that is this, indeed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वायो (*vāyo*)—O Vāyu
- उचथ्ये (*ucathye*)—praiseworthy
- वपुषि (*vapuṣi*)—having a body
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which king
- स्वराट् (*svarāṭ*)—is self-shining
- उत (*uta*)—and
- धृतस्नाः (*dhṛtasnāḥ*)—who is pure like ghee, such a king
- अश्लेषितं (*aśleṣitaṃ*)—drawn by horses
- रजेषितं (*rajeṣitaṃ*)—drawn by camels
- शुनेषितं (*śuneṣitaṃ*)—drawn by dogs
- अज्म (*ajma*)—food (nourishment)
- प्र (*pra*)—has given as a gift
- तत् इदं (*tat idaṃ*)—all that is seen before
- नु (*nu*)—certainly
- तत् (*tat*)—all this is the fruit of your favour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, the king who, having a praiseworthy body, is self-shining, and who is pure like ghee, has given as a gift food (nourishment) drawn by horses, drawn by camels, and drawn by dogs.

### Printed p. 520

##### English translation
He who is self-resplendent in his glorious body, who is bright, O Vayu, like ghee, has given me this food, brought by horses, brought by camels, brought by dogs.

Now, to the king Iṣira, the impeller of wealth and the rest, a dear and trustworthy thing, like horses, of the bulls (of cows that sprinkle), of sixty thousand, a dear thing, I received (अभजं (*abhajaṃ*)). **NOTE**

- षष्ठिं सहस्रा (*ṣaṣṭhiṃ sahasrā*)—numbering sixty thousand

- आसनं (*āsanaṃ*)—I received

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I received as a gift, from this king who gives generously, a herd of bulls that were dear to him, powerful like horses, and numbering sixty thousand.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As cows go to their herd at the time of union, so the bulls, with their testicles cut, given by Pṛthuśravas, come उप यंति (*upa yaṃti*), that is, approach, me; they reach my neighbourhood. The words "the oxen come to me" are a repetition, meant for respect.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गावति (*gāvati*)—cattle
- यूथं न (*yūthaṃ na*)—as they go to their herds
- उप यंति (*upa yaṃti*)—and join them
- वध्रयः (*vadhrayaḥ*)—the bulls given by Pṛthuśravas
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- उप यंति (*upa yaṃti*)—come and join
- वध्रयः (*vadhrayaḥ*)—the same bulls
- आ (यंति) (*ā (yaṃti)*)—come and join me

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As cattle go and join their herds, so the bulls given by Pṛthuśravas come and join me.

##### English translation
As the cows to the herd, so repair the oxen ; so the oxen repair to me.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Then, when": चरथं (*carathaṃ*) means going or moving; in such a herd of camels, which is being driven in order to move about,

> शतमचिक्रदत् अस्मभ्यं प्रदानायाजुहाव । अधापि चास्मदर्थमेव श्चित्वेषु श्वेतवर्णेषु गोयूथेषु विंशतिं च शता शतानि च अथवा शतानां विंशतिमचिक्रदत् ॥

he called a hundred camels in order to give them to us. And again, for our sake alone, among the white herds of cows, he called twenty hundreds, or twenty times a hundred.

- अध (*adha*)—afterwards
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- गणे (*gaṇe*)—all the herds of cattle of that king

- शतं उष्ट्रान् (*śataṃ uṣṭrān*)—a hundred camels
- अचिक्रदत् (*acikradat*)—he called, so as to give them to me

When all the herds of that king went to the pasture to graze, he called to himself, in order to give them to me, a hundred camels from among them and two thousand white cows.

Since, when the herd were wandering (to the wood), he called a hundred camels (to give them to me), and two thousand from among the white herds (of cows).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते । ते । वायो इति । इमे । जनाः । मदंति । इंद्रगोपाः । मदंति ।  
> देवगोपाः ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आयं विप्रो मेधावी वशो जनोऽहं बल्भूथ एतन्नामके दासे तरुक्षे
> गवाश्वादीनां तारके गवाद्यधिकृते राजा स्माकं प्रदिष्टधनदातर्या वदे । किं दानं।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sage, the intelligent man, I, the person Vaśa, from the slave named Balbūtha, the tarukṣa (the conveyer of cows, horses and the like), the one set over cattle and the rest, speak of the king who is the giver of wealth assigned to us. What gift? **NOTE**

### Printed p. 523

> गवाश्वादीनां शतं । शतशब्दोऽपरिमितवचनः । हे वायो ते तव स्वभूतास्ते
> स्तोतार इमे जनाः । वयमित्यर्थः । आत्मन एव परोक्षत्वेन वादः । त्वयानुगृहीतत्वदिंद्रगोपाः । इंद्रो गोपायिता येषां ते तथोक्ताः । इंद्रेण रक्षिता
> मदंति । तथा देवगोपा मदंति । इंद्रं देवांश्च राज्यो लब्धेन धनेन यजंतो
> मदुतीत्यर्थः !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

A hundred of cattle, horses and the like; the word "hundred" denotes an unlimited number. O Vāyu, these people, your own praisers, that is, we, are yours; he speaks of himself in the third person. Being favoured by you they are इंद्रगोपाः (*iṃdragopāḥ*), those whose protector is Indra: protected by Indra, they rejoice. Likewise देवगोपा (*devagopā*), those protected by the gods, rejoice: the meaning is that, worshipping Indra and the gods with the wealth received from the king, they rejoice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दासे (*dāse*)—by the one appointed by the king
- तरुक्षे (*tarukṣe*)—the protector of cows and horses
- बल्भधे (*balbhadhe*)—by this Balbūtha **NOTE**
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—I, the intelligent one
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred in number
- आ ददे (*ā dade*)—have received
- वायो (*vāyo*)—O Vāyu
- ते (*te*)—belonging to you
- ते इमे जनाः (*te ime janāḥ*)—all these praisers
- इंद्रगोपाः (*iṃdragopāḥ*)—(through your favour) brought under Indra's protection
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—enjoy gladness
- देवगोपाः (*devagopāḥ*)—for that very reason, protected also by the gods
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—enjoy gladness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, the intelligent one (called Vaśa), have received a hundred cattle from this Balbūtha, the servant of the king and a herdsman. O Vāyu, all these praisers who belong to you, through your favour, become worthy of Indra's protection and rejoice. Through that same favour they are also protected by the gods and enjoy gladness.

##### English translation
I, the sage, accept the hundred from the slave Balbutha, the cowherd ; we here are yours, O Vayu,—those who have Indra and the gods for protectors rejoice (through your favour).

#### Ṛk 33

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध॒ स्या योष॑णा म॒ही प्र॑ती॒ची वश॑म॒श्वं ।  
> अधि॑रुक्मा॒ वि नी॑यते ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । स्या । योषणा । मही । प्रतीची । वशं । अश्वं ।  
> अधिरुक्मा । वि । नीयते ॥ ३३ ॥

### Printed p. 524

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अधाधुना स्या सा योषणा योषा राज्ञा प्रदत्ता मही महती पूज्या
> प्रतीच्यस्मदभिमुख्यश्वमश्वपुत्रं वशं मां प्रति साधिरुक्माभरणा सती वि नीयते ।
> तां कन्यां मां प्रत्यानयंतीत्यर्थः । अत्र वायव्यास्वक्षु यत्र वायुर्न
> स्तूयते परं दानप्रशंसैव तासु सर्वासु हे वायो त्वदुनुग्रहादेवमिति
> योज्यं वायुपरत्वमवगंतव्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now, at present, that woman, the maiden given by the king, great, that is, venerable, facing us, is led towards me, Vaśa, the son of Aśva, adorned with gold ornaments; the meaning is that they bring that maiden to me. Here, in the Ṛks addressed to Vāyu, where Vāyu is not praised, there is only praise of the gift; in all of them the words "O Vāyu, through your favour it is so" are to be supplied, and the reference to Vāyu is to be understood.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध (*adha*)—now
- मही (*mahī*)—the excellent one
- अधिरुक्मा (*adhirukmā*)—adorned with gold and other ornaments
- स्या (*syā*)—who was given by the king
- योषणा (*yoṣaṇā*)—the maiden
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—the son of Aśva
- वशं (*vaśaṃ*)—named Vaśa, my
- प्रतीची (*pratīcī*)—towards
- वि नीयते (*vi nīyate*)—is being brought

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The excellent maiden, adorned with gold and other ornaments and given by the king, is being brought towards me, the son of Aśva, named Vaśa.

##### English translation
This tall maiden, adorned with gold, is led towards me. Vasha, the son Ashwa.

The forty-seventh sūkta

## Sūkta 47 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महि व इत्यष्टादशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमाप्त्यस्य त्रितस्यार्षं । षडष्टका
> महापंक्तिश्चंदः । आद्यास्त्रयोदशर्च आदित्यदेवताकाः । यच्च गोष्ठित्याद्याः
> पंचर्च उषोदेवताका आदित्यदेवताकाश्च । तथा चानुक्रमणिका । महि वो
> द्व्यूना त्रित आप्त्य आदित्येभ्योंत्याः पंचोषसेऽपि महापांक्तमिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The fifth sūkta, of eighteen Ṛks, beginning महि व (*mahi va*), has Trita Āptya as its seer; the metre is Mahāpaṅkti of six octosyllabic pādas. The first thirteen Ṛks have the Ādityas as deity; the five beginning यच्च गोष्ठित्याद्याः (*yacca goṣṭhityādyāḥ*) have Uṣas and the Ādityas as deity. So says the Anukramaṇikā: त्रित आप्त्य आदित्येभ्योंत्याः पंचोषसेऽपि महापांक्तमिति (*trita āptya ādityebhyoṃtyāḥ paṃcoṣase 'pi mahāpāṃktamiti*). The application of the sūkta is according to the Liṅga (the indication in the text).

This sūkta beginning "Mahi vaḥ" is the fifth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It contains eighteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is named Trita Āptya; its metre is Mahāpaṅkti, with six pādas of eight syllables each. The first thirteen Ṛks of this sūkta have the Ādityas as deity.

### Printed p. 525

For Ṛks 14 to 18, beginning यच्च गोषु (*yacca goṣu*), Uṣas and the Ādityas are the deities. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: महिवो ह्यूना त्रित आप्त्य आदित्येभ्योऽन्त्याः पंचोषसेऽपि महापांक्तं (*mahivo hyūnā trita āptya ādityebhyo 'ntyāḥ paṃcoṣase 'pi mahāpāṃktaṃ*). The application of the sūkta is Laiṅgika.

Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 47. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 4; Varga 7, 8, 9, 10. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 18. Seer: Trita Ātmāḥ. **NOTE** Deity: Ṛks 1–13 Avityāḥ **NOTE**; Ṛks 14–18 Ādityas and Uṣas. Metre: Mahāpaṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> महि॑ वो मह॒तामवो॒ वरु॑ण॒ मित्र॑ दा॒शुषे॑ ।  
> यमा॑दित्या अ॒भि द्रु॒हो रक्ष॑था॒ नेम॒घं न॑शदने॒हसो॑ व  
> ऊ॒तयः॑ सु॒ऊतयो॑ व ऊ॒तयः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महि । वः । महतां । आवः । वरुण । मित्र । दाशुषे ।  
> यं । आदित्याः । अभि । द्रुहः । रक्षथ । न । ईं । अघं । नशत् । अनेकसः । वः ।  
> ऊतयः । सुऊतयः । वः । ऊतयः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुण हे मित्र । एतद्वयमर्यन्नोऽप्युपलक्षणं । हे वरुणादयः
> महतां वो युष्माकमवो रक्षणं महि महत् । कस्यै । दाशुषे हविर्दात्रे
> यजमानाय क्रियमाणं । किंच हे आदित्याः यं यजमानं द्रुहो द्रोग्गुः
> सकाशादभि रक्षथ ईमेनं यजमानमघं पापं न नशत् । न प्राप्नोति । कुत एवमिति
> तत्रोच्यते । वो युष्माकमूतयो रक्षणान्यनेहसोऽपापान्यनुपद्रवाणि च ।
> ऊतयो युष्माकं रक्षणानि सुलूतय॥ । शोभनरक्षणानि । पुनरुक्तिरादरार्था ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa, O Mitra; these two are also indicative of Aryaman. O Varuṇa and the rest, your protection, being great, is great. For whom is it made? For the sacrificer who gives the oblation. Further, O Ādityas, the sacrificer whom you protect from the harm of an injurer, to him sin does not come; it does not reach him. Why so? On this it is said: your protections are free from sin and free from troubles; your protections are excellent protections. The repetition is for the sake of respect.

O Varuṇa, O Mitra, the protection of you, the great ones, is exceedingly great in regard to the performer of the sacrifice. Your protections are of a beneficial nature.

Mitra and Varuna, you are great, and great is your protection to the offerer ; no evil, Adityas, harms him whom yon guard from the injurer ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, O Ādityas, you know the removal of evils, that is, of sorrows; you know the manner of averting them. Since it is so, as birds spread their wings over (their young) for their happiness, so grant us happiness, that is, create it for us. The word अधीति (*adhīti*) merely repeats the sense of the locative; or else अस्मे (*asme*) means "upon us". **NOTE**

- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are of a beneficial nature

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Ādityas, you know the means of destroying sins. As birds spread their wings over their young and make them happy, so make us exceedingly happy. O Varuṇa and the other gods, your protection is free from sin; your protections are of a beneficial nature.

##### English translation
Divene Adityas, you know the averting of evils ; as birds (spread) their wings over (their) young, grant us happiness ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ādityas, you, upon us, that is, the unique happiness that is in you alone: that, तद्वि यंतन (*tadvi yaṃtana*), bestow in a special manner. O विश्ववेदसः (*viśvavedasaḥ*), possessors of all wealth, from you we ask विश्वानि (*viśvāni*), all, वरूथ्या (*varūthyā*): वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*) is a house, and so we ask for the riches that are fit for it.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, as birds spread their wings and give happiness to their young, so give widely, in regard to us, the unique happiness that only you can give. O Ādityas, who possess all wealth and riches, we ask of you the whole house of protection. Your protections are free from sin; they are productive of good for us.

> यस्मै मनुष्याय क्षयं निवासं जीवातुं जीवनसाधनमन्नं च प्रचेतसः
> प्रकृष्टमतयोऽरासत प्रयच्छंति तस्मै यजमानाय तदर्थमिदु आदित्या विश्वस्य
> फेत् सर्वस्याप्ययष्टुर्मनोर्मनुष्यस्य धनिकस्य रायो धनस्येशते ! स्वामिनो
> भवंत्यपहृत्य यजमानाय प्रदातुं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To whatever man those of excellent understanding give a dwelling, क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*), and जीवातुं (*jīvātuṃ*), food as the means of life, for that sacrificer, for that very purpose, the Ādityas become lords of the wealth of every man who is not a sacrificer, a rich man; they take it away in order to give it to the sacrificer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*)—possessed of excellent knowledge
- इमे आदित्याः (*ime ādityāḥ*)—these Ādityas
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—to whatever man
- क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)—a dwelling-place
- जीवातुं चॆ (*jīvātuṃ cè*)—and food, the means of life
- अरासते (*arāsate*)—they give
- मनोः (*manoḥ*)—for the benefit of such a man
- विश्वस्य घेत् (*viśvasya ghet*)—of all rich men who do not perform sacrifice
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of the wealth
- ईशते (*īśate*)—they are the lords
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are of a beneficial nature

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

If these Ādityas, who possess excellent knowledge, wish to give to any sacrificer a dwelling-place and food as the means of life, then, for the benefit of such a sacrificer, they take away the wealth of the other rich men who are not sacrificers and give it to him. O Ādityas, your protections are free from sin. Your protections are of a beneficial nature.

### Printed p. 530

##### English translation
To whomsoever these wise Adityas grant a dwelling and the means of life, (for him) they master the wealth of every man ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

> स्यामेदिंद्र॑स्य॒ शर्म॑ण्यादि॒त्याना॑मु॒ताव॑स्यने॒हसो॑ व ऊ॒तयः॑ ॒॑ ॒॑

> स्याम । इत् । इंद्रस्य । शर्मणि । आदित्यानां । उत । अवसि । अनेहसः । वः ।

> परि वृणजन् परिवर्जयंतु नोऽस्माकमघानि पापानि । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> दुर्गाणि दुर्गमनान् प्रदेशानवटु ष्णादिकान् यथा परिवर्जयंति तद्वत् ।
> इंद्रस्य शर्मणि स्याम । भवेम वयं ! उतापि चादित्यानामवसि रक्षणे च स्याम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Let sins avoid us, परि वृणजन् (*pari vṛṇajan*), let them turn away from us. The illustration is this: as men avoid impassable places, दुर्गाणि (*durgāṇi*), so let sins avoid us. May we be in the shelter of Indra; and also may we be in the protection of the Ādityas. **NOTE**

- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are of a beneficial nature

### Printed p. 531

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As charioteers avoid difficult roads and keep away from them, so may our sins also avoid us and keep away. May we be in the happiness given by Indra and in the protection of the Ādityas. O Indra and the other gods, your protections are free from sin. Your protections are of a beneficial nature.

##### English translation
May our sins avoid us as charioteers, inaccessible places ; we abide in Indra's happiness and in the protection of the Adityas ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, divine and swift-going, a living man can obtain the wealth given by you only through the hardships of austerity, restraint and the like. The man whom you favour and to whom you go obtains abundant wealth. O Ādityas, your protections are free from sin. Your protections are auspicious.

##### English translation
Only by painful means does a living man obtain the wealth which you bestow; but he whom you, divine Adityas, visit, wins great (riches); your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

Likewise that man, a grievous, heavy sorrow that is hard to remove, does not

- गुरु (*guru*)—heavy sorrow

- ऊतॆयः (*ūtèyaḥ*)—protections

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, you who pervade widely, neither sharp anger nor heavy sorrow approaches or injures that sacrificer to whom you give happiness. Your protections are free from sin and productive of good.

##### English translation
Him fierce wrath touches not, nor heavy (calamity), to whom, Adityas, you have given great happiness ; your aids are void of harm. your aids are true aids.

- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Ādityas, as heroes who fight obtain protection in their battle-armours, so may we find shelter in you. Protect us from great sin and from small sin. Your protections are free from sin and auspicious.

##### English translation
Deities, may we abide in you as warriors in their armour; defend us from great evil, defend us from little; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

May Aditi, the mother of the wealthy Mitra, of Aryaman and of Varuṇa, protect us. May Aditi, the mother of the gods, give us happiness. O gods, your protections are most excellent, free from sin and auspicious.

May Aditi defend us, may Aditi grant us happiness, the mother of the wealthy Mitra, Aryaman and Varuna; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

> त्रिधातु । यत् । वरूध्यं । तत् । आस्मासु । वि । यंतन । आनेहसः । वः । ऊशयः ।  
> सुऊतयः । वः । ऊतॆयः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवा आदित्याः यच्छर्म सुखं शरणं शरणीयं । यद्भद्रं सर्वैर्भजनीयं । यदनातुरं रोगरहितं । यत्रिधातु त्रिगुणं । यद्वरूढ्यं ! वरूथं
> गृहं । तवर्हं । तदुक्तगुणकं शर्मास्मासु वि यंतन । पियच्छत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, O Ādityas: whatever happiness, शर्म (*śarma*), is a refuge, शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*), to be taken as a refuge; whatever is auspicious, भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*), to be shared in by all; whatever is free from disease, अनातुरं (*anāturaṃ*); whatever is threefold, त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*), having three qualities; whatever is वरूथ्यं (*varūthyaṃ*), for वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*) is a house, and so fit for a house: that happiness having the stated qualities, bestow upon us, वि यंतन (*vi yaṃtana*), give it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O Ādityas
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*)—is a refuge for us
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—is auspicious
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- अनातुरं (*anāturaṃ*)—is free from disease
- त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—which is endowed with the three qualities
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- वरूथ्यं (*varūthyaṃ*)—protects like a house
- तत् (*tat*)—such
- अस्मासु (*asmāsu*)—to us
- वि यंतन (*vi yaṃtana*)—give
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, give us such happiness as is a refuge for us, as is auspicious, as is free from disease, as is endowed with the three qualities, and as protects like a house. Your protections are free from sin. Your protections are most excellent.

##### English translation
Grant to us, deities, that happiness which is a refuge, auspicious and free from sickness, which is threefold and fit for a (secure) shelter ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आदि॑त्या॒ अव॒ हि ख्यताधि॒ कूला॑दिव॒ स्पशः॑ ।  
> सु॒ती॒र्थमर्व॑तो य॒थानु॑ नो नेषथा सु॒गम॑ने॒हसो॑ व  
> ऊ॒तयः॑ सु॒ऊतयो॑ व ऊ॒तयः॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आदित्याः । आप । हि । ख्यत । अधि । कूलात् इव । स्पशः ।  
> गुतिर्थं । आर्वतः । यथा । अनु । नः । नेषथ । सुगं । अनेहसः । वः । ऊतयः ।  
> सूऊतयः । वः । ऊतयः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आदित्याः यूयमव हि ख्यत । अव हि पश्यताधस्तात्स्थितानस्मान् । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । कूलादधि कूले स्पशः स्पष्टाः । स्थिता इत्यर्थः । यथा कूलस्थः पुरुषोऽधोगतमुदकं जिज्ञासुस्तत्रस्थं मनुष्यं वा विलोकयितुमवाक्ष्यति तद्वत् ।
> तथा कृत्वा सुतीर्थं शोभनावतारप्रदेशमर्वतोऽश्वान्यथा प्रापयंत्यश्वररक्षकाः
> तद्वन्नोऽस्मान् सुगं सुपंथानमनु नेषथ । अनुनयथ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ādityas, look down upon us, अव हि ख्यत (*ava hi khyata*): look at us who stand below. The illustration is this: कूलादधि (*kūlādadhi*), upon the bank, those who stand there, स्पशः (*spaśaḥ*): as a man standing on the bank, wishing to know the water below, or wishing to see a man there, looks down, so do you. And as keepers of horses lead their horses to a good ford, सुतीर्थं (*sutīrthaṃ*), a place of easy descent, so lead us, अनु नेषथ (*anu neṣatha*), along a good road, सुगं (*sugaṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*)—O Ādityas
- कूलात् अधि स्पशः (*kūlāt adhi spaśaḥ*)—as a man on the bank looks down kindly at a man who has fallen into the water
- अव हि ख्यत (*ava hi khyata*)—look down from the sky upon us who are on the earth
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—horses
- सुतीर्थं (*sutīrthaṃ*)—as lords of horses take them to a place with a good bank
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सुगं (*sugaṃ*)—to the good road
- अनु नेषथ (*anu neṣatha*)—lead
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेकसः (*anekasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, as a man on the bank looks down kindly at a man who has fallen into the water, look down from the sky upon us who are on the earth. As lords of horses

### Printed p. 538

take their horses to a place with a good bank, so lead us also to the good road. Your protections are free from sin and auspicious.

##### English translation
Adityas, look down upon us as those who look from the shore ; as (men lead) their horses to a secure Ghat, so conduct us along a good path ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नेह भ॒द्रं र॑क्ष॒स्विने॒ नाव॒य्य नोप॒या उ॒त ।  
> गवे॑ च भ॒द्रं धे॒नवे॑ वी॒राय॑ च श्रवस्य॒ते॑ऽने॒हसो॑ न  
> ऊ॒तयः॑ सु॒ऊतयो॑ न ऊ॒तयः॑ ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । इह । भद्रं । रक्षस्विने । न । अव्यय्य । न । उपय्य । उत ।  
> गवे । च । भद्रं । धेनवे । वीराय । च । श्रवस्यते । अनेहसः । वः । ऊतयः ।  
> सुऊतयः । वः । ऊतयः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आदित्याः इह भूमौ भद्रं कल्याणं सुखं रक्षस्विने । रक्षो बलं । बलवतेऽस्मद्वेष्टे न भवत्विति शेषः । अवया आस्मान् हिंसितुमवगच्छते न भवतु भद्रं ।
> तथोपया उपगच्छते न भवतु । तर्हि कस्य भवत्विति उच्यते । गवे च भद्रं युष्मदीयं भवतु । चशब्दो वक्ष्यमाणधेन्वाद्यपेक्षः । किंच धेनवे नवप्रसूतिकायै
> भद्रं भवतु । वीरायास्मत्पुत्रादिकाय भद्रं भवतु । कीदृशाय वीराय । श्रवस्यतेऽन्नमिच्छते । अथवोत्तरार्धेऽपि नेत्यनुवर्तते । अस द्विरोधिनो गवादिकाय
> भद्रं न भवत्विति तस्यार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ādityas, here on earth let no welfare, भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*), that is, happiness, be for the strong one, रक्षस्विने (*rakṣasvine*) (रक्षो (*rakṣo*) is strength), our hater who is powerful; let there be none for him who comes, अवया (*avayā*), to injure us, nor for him who approaches. For whom then? It is said: for the cow let your welfare be; the word च (*ca*) looks to the milch cow and the others still to be mentioned. Further, for the milch cow that has newly calved let there be welfare; for the hero, our son and the rest, let there be welfare. For what kind of hero? For him who desires food, श्रवस्यते (*śravasyate*). Or else the word न (*na*) continues also in the latter half: let there be no welfare for the cows and the rest of our enemy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इह (*iha*)—on this earth
- रक्षस्विने (*rakṣasvine*)—to our powerful enemy
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—welfare
- न (*na*)—may not come
- अवय्यॆ (*avayyè*)—also to those who wish to injure us

### Printed p. 539

- न (*na*)—may not be good
- उत (*uta*)—and
- उपय्यॆ (*upayyè*)—also to him who opposes us
- न (*na*)—may not be good
- गवे च (*gave ca*)—to our cows
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—let welfare come
- धेनवे (*dhenave*)—to our milch cows too let it be good
- श्रवस्यते (*śravasyate*)—who desires food
- वीराय च (*vīrāya ca*)—to our heroic sons too let it be good
- व (*va*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, on this earth let there be no welfare for our powerful enemy. Let there be no good for him who wishes to injure us. And let there be no good for him who opposes us. May it always be well with our cows and with our heroic sons, who desire food. Your protections are free from sin. Your protections are auspicious.

##### English translation
Let there not be prosperity here to our powerful (foe), nor to him who threatens or assaults us; but let there be prosperity to our cattle, our milch cows, and our male offspring desirous of food; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दे देवासो देवा आदित्याः यदाविर्हुत्पापमाविर्भूतमस्ति । दुष्कृतं
> यच्चापीच्यमंतर्हितमस्ति । अपीच्यमित्यंतर्हितनाम । तद्विश्वं तदुभयमाप्त्वे
> त्रिते मयि मा भूत् । किंत्वस्मदारे दूरे दधातन । स्थापयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Devas, that is, the Ādityas, are addressed. Whatever sin is manifest (āvis) and whatever is hidden (apīcya, which means "hidden") **NOTE**, let both of these, all of it, not be in Trita Āptya, that is, in me. But place it far from us (dadhātana, "place").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O Ādityas, divine beings
- यत् आविः अस्ति (*yat āviḥ asti*)—whatever sin has become manifest
- यत् दुष्कृतं (*yat duṣkṛtaṃ*)—whatever evil deed (a cause of sin)
- अपीच्यं (*apīcyaṃ*)—is hidden
- तद्विश्वं (*tadviśvaṃ*)—all these causes of sin, belonging to the two groups
- त्रिते आप्त्ये (*trite āptye*)—let them not be in me, who am called Trita Āptya
- तत् (*tat*)—all of that
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—than us
- अरे (*are*)—very far away
- दधातन (*dadhātana*)—place
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, divine beings, whatever sin has become manifest, whatever evil deed is hidden, let all these causes of sin, belonging to both groups, not be in me, Trita Āpta. Place all of that very far away from us. Your protections are free from sin. Your protections are auspicious.

##### English translation
Deities, whatever evil is manifest, whatever is concealed, (let it be not found) in Trita Aptya, keep it far from us; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

> सुऊतयः । वः । ऊतयः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यच्च गोष्टित्यादिसूक्तशेषेण दुष्स्वप्नं दृष्ट्वादित्यमुपतिष्ठेत् । तथा च
> स्वप्नमनोज्ञं दृष्ट्वेत्युपक्रम्य यच्च गोषु दुष्स्वप्नमिति पंचभिरादित्यमुपतिष्ठेत् । आ. गृ. ३-६-६ । इति सूत्रितं ॥
> हे दिवो दुहितरुष उषोदेवते यच्च गोष्टस्मदीयासु दुष्स्वप्नमनर्थसूचकं दृष्टं ॥ स्वार्थिको यत् ॥ किंच यच्च दुष्स्वप्नमस्मे अस्मासु
> दृष्टं । गोपीडानिमित्तकमस्माकं पीडानिमित्तकं च यद्दुःस्वप्नं पश्याम इत्यर्थः।
> तत्सर्वं हे विभावरि । उषोनामैतत् । हे व्युच्छनवति देवि आप्त्याय त्रिताय परा
> वह । दूरे परिहर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With the rest of the sūkta beginning यच्च गोषु (*yacca goṣu*), one who has seen a bad dream should worship Āditya; this is laid down in the sūtra that begins with seeing an unpleasing dream and says that one worships Āditya with the five verses beginning यच्च गोषु (*yacca goṣu*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-6-6) **NOTE**. O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, whatever inauspicious bad dream, a sign of calamity, has been seen concerning our cows, and whatever bad dream has been seen by us, a sign of trouble for the cows and for ourselves, all that, O Vibhāvarī (a name of Uṣas), O goddess who dawns, carry far away for Trita Āptya; remove it far off.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः दुहितः (*divaḥ duhitaḥ*)—O daughter of heaven
- विभावरि (*vibhāvari*)—O radiant goddess Uṣas
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—to our cows
- यत् दुष्स्वप्नं (*yat duṣsvapnaṃ*)—whatever bad dream appears
- यच्च (*yacca*)—and whatever bad dreams
- अस्मे (*asme*)—appear to us as well
- तत् (*tat*)—all of that
- त्रिताय आप्ताय (*tritāya āptāya*)—away from Trita Āpta
- परा वह (*parā vaha*)—cause to move far away
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, radiant goddess, whatever bad dream appears to our cows, whatever bad dreams appear to us as well, cause all of that to move away from me, Trita Āpta. O Uṣas and the other deities, your protections are free from sin. Your protections are auspicious.

##### English translation
Daughter of heaven, (Ushas), whatever ill-omened dream threatens our cattle or ourselves, keep it, O brilliant one, far from Trita Aptya ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

### Printed p. 542

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When anyone has a bad dream, he should look at Āditya and pray, reciting from the fourteenth ṛk of this sūkta, beginning यच्च गोषु (*yacca goṣu*), to the end of the sūkta. This is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-gṛhya-sūtra that begins with स्वप्नममनोज्ञं (*svapnamamanojñaṃ*) and continues यच्च गोषु दुःस्वप्न्यमिति पंचभिरादित्यमुपतिष्ठेत (*yacca goṣu duḥsvapnyamiti paṃcabhirādityamupatiṣṭheta*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-6 6) **NOTE**.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि॒ष्कं वा॑ घा कृ॒णव॑ते॒ स्रजं॑ वा दुहितर्दिवः ।  
> त्रि॒ते दु॒ष्पप्नं॒ सर्व॑मा॒प्त्ये परि॑ दद्मस्यने॒हसो॑ व ऊ॒तयः॑  
> सु॒ऊतयो॑ व ऊ॒तयः॑ ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> निष्कं । वा । घ । कृणवते । स्रजं । वा । दुहितः । दिवः ।  
> त्रिते । दुःस्वप्नं । सर्वं । आप्त्ये । परि । दद्मसि । अनेकहसः । वः । ऊतयः ।  
> सुऊतयः । वः । ऊतयः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे दिवो दुहितरुषः निष्कं वा घाभरणविशेषं वा कृणवते कुर्वते
> स्वर्णकाराय यद्दुष्ट्स्वप्नं दृष्टं । स्वर्णकारेण निर्माणसमये दृष्टमित्यर्थः ।
> घेति पूरणः । वाशब्दश्चार्थे । वाथवा स्रजं माल्यं कृणवते । कुर्वाण इत्यर्थः ।
> तस्मिन्नपि मालाकारे मालानिर्माणसमये यदुष्ट्स्वप्नं दृष्टं तमभयविषयं
> दुःस्वप्नमाप्त्येऽपां पुत्रे त्रिते वर्तमानं परि दद्मसि । उपरि दद्मः । वयं
> त्रिताः परित्यजामेत्यर्थः । अथवा त्रिते मयि यद्दुष्ट्स्वप्नं दृष्टं तत्कर्णकाराय
> मालाकाराय वा परि दद्मसि । अस्मत्तोऽपि निष्कृष्ट्य तयोरुपरि स्थापयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Uṣas, daughter of heaven: whatever bad dream is seen by a goldsmith who makes a niṣka, that is, a kind of ornament, at the time of his making it (the particle घा (*ghā*) is an expletive and वा (*vā*) has the sense of "and"), or by one who makes a garland (sraj), by the maker of the garland also at the time of making it, that dream, concerning fear, which rests in Trita, the son of Āptya (Āpa), we hand over (pari dadmasi), that is, we, the Tritas, give it up. Or else: whatever bad dream has been seen in me, Trita, that we hand over to the goldsmith or to the maker of garlands, drawing it out from ourselves and placing it upon those two. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः दुहितः (*divaḥ duhitaḥ*)—O Uṣas, daughter of the sky (antarikṣa) **NOTE**
- त्रिते आप्त्ये (*trite āptye*)—upon me, Trita Āptya, who am affected
- सर्वं मस्वप्नं (*sarvaṃ masvapnaṃ*)—all bad dreams
- निष्कं ना कृणवते (*niṣkaṃ nā kṛṇavate*)—upon the goldsmith who makes ornaments and the like
- स्रजं वा (*srajaṃ vā*)—or upon him who ties garlands
- परि दद्मसि (*pari dadmasi*)—we make its effect fall
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are auspicious

### Printed p. 543

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, all the bad dreams that have an effect on me, Trita Āpta, we make their effect fall upon the goldsmith who makes ornaments and the like, or upon him who ties garlands. Your protections are free from sin. Your protections are auspicious.

##### English translation
Daughter of heaven, whatever ill-omened dream threatens Trita Aptya, we transfer it to the worker of gold ornaments or to the maker of garlands your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊ॒तयः॑ सु॒ऊतयो॑ व ऊ॒तयः॑ ॥ १६ ॥

> शॆत् 5 अन्नाय । शॆत् 5 अवसे । तं । भागं । उपसेदुषे ।  
> त्रिताय । च । द्विताय । च । उषः । दुःस्वप्नं । वह । अनेहसः । वः । ऊतॆयः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तदन्नाय । यदेव जागरावस्थायां भोज्यत्वेन प्रसिद्धं मधुषायसादि
> स्वैर्णपि तदेवान्नं यस्य सः । तादृशाय । प्रत्यक्षभोजनवत् स्वप्नेऽपि भोक्त्र
> इत्यर्थः । तथातेदवसे । यदेवापः कर्म निंदितं जाग्रदवस्थायां क्रियते तदेव

### Printed p. 544

> कर्म स्वप्ने यस्य स तत्कर्मा । तादृशाय देवाय तं भागं मस्वप्नस्यांशमुपसेदुषे प्राप्नुवते त्रिताय द्विताय च हे उषो देवि दुष्कृत्यै मन्न कर्मविषयं
> वह । अन्यत्र प्रापय । स्वप्ने दृष्टं मधुभोजनादिकं जाग्रदवस्थानुरूपवत्सुखकरं भवत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word तदन्नाय (*tadannāya*) means one whose food, even in a dream, is that very food which in the waking state is known as fit to eat, honey, milk-rice and the like **NOTE**; that is, one who eats in a dream as in actual eating. Likewise तदपसे (*tadapase*): whatever blameworthy deed (apas) is done in the waking state, that same deed is his in a dream; for such a god, who has obtained that portion, that share of the bad dream, for Trita and for Dvita, O goddess Uṣas, carry the bad dream concerning that deed **NOTE** elsewhere; direct it to another place. The meaning is: let the honey-food and the like seen in a dream be pleasant, corresponding to the waking state.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas
- तदन्नाय (*tadannāya*)—to him who is seen to eat in a dream the very food that he eats when awake
- तदपसे (*tadapase*)—to him who is seen to do in a dream the very deed that he does when awake
- तं भागं (*taṃ bhāgaṃ*)—the fruit of that very bad dream
- उपसेदुषे (*upaseduṣe*)—who obtains
- त्रिताय (*tritāya*)—for Trita
- द्विताय च (*dvitāya ca*)—and for Dvita also
- दुःस्वप्नं (*duḥsvapnaṃ*)—that bad dream
- वह (*vaha*)—turn to another place
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, for Trita and for Dvita, who are seen to eat in a dream the very food that they eat when awake, who are seen to do in a dream the very deed that they do when awake, and who obtain the fruit of that very bad dream, turn that bad dream to another place. O Uṣas and the other deities, your protections are free from sin. Your protections are auspicious.

##### English translation
Ushas, bear (elsewhere) the ill-omened dream for Trita and Dwita, who eat and do (in dreams) that (which is eaten and done amiss when awake) and who obtain that (inauspicious) portion ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

### Printed p. 545

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । कलां । यथा । शफं । यथा । ऋणं । संनयामसि ।  
> एव । दु-sत्त्वं । सर्वं । आप्त्ये । सं । नयामसि । अनेहसः । वः । ऊतयः ।  
> सुऊतयः । वः । ऊतयः ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> संज्ञापितं पशुं दानार्थं संस्कुर्वंतो यथा येन प्रकारेण कलां
> शफमिति संदायान्यत्र संनयंति । अथापरो यथाशब्दः पूरणः । अथवा । यथा
> कलां हृदयाद्यवयवमनदानार्हं संनयंति यथा च शफं शफोपलक्षितमनवदानार्हं शफास्थ्यादिकं संनयंति । यथा ना ऋणं शनैः संनयंति एवैवं
> दुष्टत्वं सर्वमाप्त्ये वर्तमानं सं नयामसि । संनयामः । अपसारयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Just as those who prepare the slaughtered animal for the offering put together the parts (kalā) and the hoofs (śapha) and bring them together elsewhere; or else, just as they put together the part (kalā), such as the heart and other limbs that are not fit for the cutting of the oblation, and the hoofs, the hoof-bones and the like, which are also not fit for it; and just as a man gradually puts together, that is, pays off, a debt; so we remove, that is, put away, all the bad dream that rests in Āptya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- कलां (*kalāṃ*)—the heart and other limbs of the animal
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- शफं (*śaphaṃ*)—the hoof parts (which in the sacrifice we offer, collecting them together)
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- ऋणं (*ṛṇaṃ*)—a debt
- सं नयामसि (*saṃ nayāmasi*)—we discharge in due order
- एव (*eva*)—in the same manner
- अप्प्ये (*appye*)—clinging to Trita Āptya
- सर्वं (*sarvaṃ*)—all the …
- सं नयामसि (*saṃ nayāmasi*)—we shall drive far away
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतॆयः (*ūtèyaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतॆयः (*ūtèyaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतॆयः (*suūtèyaḥ*)—are most excellent

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Just as we offer together in the sacrifice the heart and other limbs of the animal and the hoof parts, and just as we gradually discharge a debt, so we shall drive far away all the … that clings to Trita Āptya. O gods, your protections are free from sin. Your protections are most excellent.

##### English translation
As (in the sacrifice) we put severally together the proper parts and the hoofs, and as we discharge a debt, so we transfer all the ill-omened dream that rests on Aptya ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

> उषः । यस्मात् । दुःस्वप्नात् । अभैष्म । अप । तत् । उच्छतु । अनेकसः । वः ।

> वयं त्रिता अद्याजैष्म । जयेम । असनाम च । संभजेम च सुस्वप्नं सुखं
> वा । अनागसोऽपापा अभूम । भवेम । हे उषः यस्माद्दुष्स्वप्नादभैष्म भीताः
> स्म तत्पापमपोच्छतु । अपगच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the Tritas, have today conquered (ajaiṣma, "may we conquer"), and have obtained (asanāma, "may we share in") a good dream or happiness, and have become free from sin (anāgasaḥ). O Uṣas, may that sin go away (apocchatu, "go away") from which bad dream we were afraid.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- अजैष्म (*ajaiṣma*)—may we obtain victory
- आसनाम च (*āsanāma ca*)—may we obtain all happiness
- अनागसः (*anāgasaḥ*)—may we also be free from sin
- अभूम (*abhūma*)—may we be
- यस्मात् दुःस्वप्नात् (*yasmāt duḥsvapnāt*)—from which bad dream
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- अभ्यैष्म (*abhyaiṣma*)—have been afraid
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- अप उच्छतु (*apa ucchatu*)—may it go far away and perish
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—are free from sin
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—protections
- सुऊतयः (*suūtayaḥ*)—are most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, may we now obtain victory; may we obtain all happiness; may we also be free from sin. May the bad dream of which we have been afraid go far away and perish. O gods, your protections are free from sin. Your protections are most excellent.

##### English translation
May we be to-day victorious, and obtain (happiness) ; may we be free from evil ; Ushas, may that illdream depart, of which we were afraid ; your aids are void of harm, your aids are true aids.

The forty-eighth sūkta

## Sūkta 48 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वादोरभक्षीति पंचदशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं काण्वस्य प्रगाथस्यार्षं सोमदेवताशं त्रैष्टुभं । पंचमी जगती । सोमो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> स्वादोः पंचोना प्रगाथः सौम्यं त्रैष्टुभं पंचमी जगतीति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो
> लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning स्वादोरभक्षि (*svādorabhakṣi*), of fifteen Ṛks, is the sixth sūkta. Its seer is Pragātha, of the Kāṇva line; its deity is Soma; its metre is Triṣṭubh, and the fifth Ṛk is Jagatī. So says the Anukramaṇikā: स्वादोः पंचोना प्रगाथः सौम्यं त्रैष्टुभं पंचमी जगतीति (*svādoḥ paṃconā pragāthaḥ saumyaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ paṃcamī jagatīti*). The application of the sūkta is according to the Liṅga (the indication in the text itself).

This sūkta beginning "Svādor abhakṣi" is the sixth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It contains fifteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is named Pragātha Kāṇva; Soma is the deity; the fifth Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Jagatī metre, and the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: स्वादोः पंचोना प्रगाथः सौम्यं त्रैष्टुभं पंचमी जगती (*svādoḥ paṃconā pragāthaḥ saumyaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ paṃcamī jagatī*). The application of the sūkta is Laiṅgika.

Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 48 **NOTE**. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 4; Varga 11, 12, 13. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Pragātha Kāṇva. Deity: Soma. Metre: Ṛks 1–4, 6–15 Triṣṭubh; Ṛk 5 Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वादोरभक्षि वयसः सुमेधाः स्वाध्यो वरिवोवित्तरस्य ।  
> विश्वे यं देवा उत मर्त्यासो मधु ब्रुवंतो अभि  
> संचरंति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्वादोः । अभक्षि । वयसः । सुमेधाः । सुआध्यः । वरिवोवित्तरस्य ।  
> विश्वे । यं । देवाः । उत । मर्त्यासः । मधु । ब्रुवंतः । अभि । संचरंति ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 548

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं प्रगाथः सुमेधाः शोभनप्रज्ञः स्वाध्यः स्वाध्ययनः सुकर्मा वरिवोवित्तरस्यातिशयेन पूजां लभमानस्य स्वादोः सुष्पदनीयस्य स्वादुभूतस्य वयसोऽन्नस्य ॥ एताः कर्मणि षष्ठ्यः ॥ उक्तलक्षणं वयोऽन्नं सोमाख्यमभक्षि ।
> भक्षयेय । यं यदन्नं विश्वे देवाः सर्वॆऽपींद्रादय उतापि च मर्त्यासो
> मर्त्या मनुष्या मधु ब्रुवंतो मनोहरमेतदिति शब्दायंतोऽभि संचरंति
> अभिसंगच्छंते प्राप्नुवंति तदन्नमभक्ष्ति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Pragātha, of good understanding (sumedhāḥ) and good study and works (svādhyaḥ), may I enjoy (abhakṣi, "may I eat") the food (vayas) called Soma, which is very sweet and receives the highest honour (varivovittara) **NOTE**. The food which all the gods, Indra and the rest, and also mortals, men, calling it "honey", that is, delightful, approach and obtain, that food may I enjoy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Soma
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- उत (*uta*)—and
- मर्त्यासः (*martyāsaḥ*)—men
- मधु ब्रुवंतः (*madhu bruvaṃtaḥ*)—saying that it is exceedingly delicious
- अभि संचरंति (*abhi saṃcaraṃti*)—eat it
- स्वादोः (*svādoḥ*)—delicious
- वरिवोवित्तरस्य (*varivovittarasya*)—exceedingly worthy of worship
- वयसः (*vayasaḥ*)—food
- सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—possessed of excellent understanding
- स्वाध्यः (*svādhyaḥ*)—possessed of excellent works, I
- अभक्षि (*abhakṣi*)—may I enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May I, possessed of excellent understanding and excellent works, enjoy that delicious food, exceedingly worthy of worship, which all the gods and all men, saying that Soma is exceedingly delicious, eat.

##### English translation
May I, the wise and devout, enjoy the delicious, abundantly honoured Soma food, which all gods and mortals, pronouncing sweet, seek to obtain.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अंतश्च प्रागा अदितिर्भवास्यवयाता हरसो दैव्यस्य ।  
> इंदविंद्रस्य सख्यं जुषाणः श्रौष्टीव धुरमनु राय ऋध्याः ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंतरिति । च । प्र । अगाः । अदितिः । भवासि । अवयाता । हरसः । दैव्यस्य ।  
> इंदो इति । इंद्रस्य । सख्यं । जुषाणः । शौष्ट्री इव । धुरं । अनु । राये । ऋढ्याः ॥

### Printed p. 549

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्नीषोमप्रणयनेऽंतश्चेत्येषा । तथा च सूत्रितं । अंतश्च प्रागा अदितिर्भवासि श्येनो न योनिं सदनं धिया कृतं । आ. ४-१० । इति ॥
> हे सोम त्वमंतश्च प्रागाः । हृदयस्य यागागारस्य वांतर्गच्छसि । गत्वा
> चादितिरदीनस्त्वं दैव्यस्य हरसः क्रोधस्यावयाता पृथक्कर्ता भवासि । भवसि । हर इति
> क्रोधनाम । हे इंदो सोम त्वमिंद्रस्य सख्यं जुषाणः सेवमानः श्रौष्टि ।
> श्रुष्टिति क्षिप्रनाम । तत्संबंधी श्रौष्टि । क्षिप्रगाम्यश्वो धुरमिव रायेऽस्माकं
> धनलाभायान्वृध्याः । अनुगच्छसि । अथवाश्वो यथा धुरं वृत्त्वाभिमतदेशं
> प्रापयति तद्वदस्मान्प्रापय । अनुपूर्व ऋधिर्गत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Ṛk beginning अंतश्च (*aṃtaśca*) is used in the Agnīṣoma-praṇayana, as the sūtra says (Ā. 4-10). O Soma, you go within, into the heart or into the sacrificial house; and having gone, you, the undiminished one, become the separator of divine anger (hara, which means "anger"). O Indu, Soma, enjoying (juṣāṇaḥ, "serving") the friendship of Indra, as a swift-going horse (śrauṣṭi, from śruṣṭi, "swift") follows its yoke, so you follow, for our gain of wealth. Or else: as a horse, having taken up the yoke, brings one to the desired place, so bring us there.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंतश्च (*aṃtaśca*)—and into the heart
- प्रागाः (*prāgāḥ*)—you enter
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—you, of perfect form
- दैव्यस्य (*daivyasya*)—belonging to the gods
- हरसः (*harasaḥ*)—of anger
- अवयाता (*avayātā*)—as the destroyer
- भवासि (*bhavāsi*)—you are
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—friendship
- जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)—enjoying
- श्रौष्टी (*śrauṣṭī*)—a swift horse
- धुरं इव (*dhuraṃ iva*)—as it bears a burden
- राये (*rāye*)—for our gain of wealth
- अनु ऋध्याः (*anu ṛdhyāḥ*)—take us to that place and bring us together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you enter also into the hearts of the gods and remove their anger. O Soma, of perfect form, enjoying the friendship of Indra, as a swift horse bears a burden, take us to that place for the gain of wealth and bring us together.

##### English translation
You enter within, and, unimpaired, you avert the anger of the gods; Soma, enjoining the friendship of Indra, may you bring us to wealth as a swift (horse) its burden.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrificial act called Agnīṣoma-praṇayana this Ṛk beginning अंतश्च (*aṃtaśca*) is to be recited, as is set forth by the sūtra of the Ātvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra अंतश्च प्रागा अदितिर्भवासि श्योनो न योनिं सदनं धिया कृतं (*aṃtaśca prāgā aditirbhavāsi śyono na yoniṃ sadanaṃ dhiyā kṛtaṃ*) (Ā. 4-10) **NOTE**.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अपाम सोमममृता अभूमागन्म ज्योतिरविदाम देवान् ।  
> किं नूनमस्मान्नृणवदरातिः किमु धूर्तिरमृत मर्त्यस्य ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपाम । सोमं । अमृताः । अभूम । अगन्म । ज्योतिः । अविदाम । देवान् !  
> किं । नूनं । अस्मान् । कृणवत् । आरातिः । किं । ऊं इति । धूर्तिः । अमृत । मर्त्यस्य ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपाम सोममित्यादिके द्वे सोमपानोत्तरकालीनस्याभिमर्शने हृदयाभिमर्शने च क्रमेण विनियुक्ते । तथा च सूत्रितं । अपाम सोमममृता अभूम
> शं नो भव हृद आ पीत इंदविति मुखहृदये अभिमृशेरन्निति ॥
> हे अमृतामरण सोम त्वामपाम । पानं करपाम । कुर्मः । ततोऽमृता
> अभूम । भवेम । यस्मात्त्वममृतः अतस्तव पानाद्वयमप्यमृताः स्याम ।
> पश्चाज्योतिर्द्योतमानं स्वर्गमगन्म । अविदाम ज्ञातवंतो देवान् ! तथाभूतानस्मान्नूनमिदानीमरातिः शत्रुः किं कृणवत् । कुर्यात् । किमु किंवा मर्त्यस्येदानीं मनुष्यभूतस्य मम धूर्तिर्हिंसकः किं कृणवत् । कुर्यात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two verses beginning अपाम सोमं (*apāma somaṃ*) are applied, in order, to the touching after the drinking of Soma and to the touching of the heart; so the sūtra says that they should touch the mouth and the heart. O immortal Soma, we drink you, and thereby we become immortal; since you are immortal, we too may become immortal by drinking you. Afterwards we went to the light, the shining heaven. We have come to know the gods. Such as we are, what will the enemy (arāti) do to us now? Or what will the injurer (dhūrti) do now to me, who am a mortal?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- असाम (*asāma*)—we shall drink
- अमृताः (*amṛtāḥ*)—free from death
- अभूम (*abhūma*)—we shall become
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—to the shining heaven
- अगन्म (*aganma*)—we shall go and reach
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- अविदाम (*avidāma*)—we shall know
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—surely
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- अरातिः (*arātiḥ*)—the enemy
- किं कृणवत् (*kiṃ kṛṇavat*)—what can he do
- अमृत (*amṛta*)—O Soma, free from death
- मर्त्यस्य (*martyasya*)—in the case of me, a man
- धूर्तिः (*dhūrtiḥ*)—the enemy who is of the nature of injury
- किमु (*kimu*)—what indeed can he do

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We drink Soma. We become free from death. We go and reach the shining heaven. We come to know the gods. O Soma, free from death, what can the enemy do to us? What can the enemy, who is of the nature of injury, do to me, a man?

### Printed p. 551

##### English translation
We drink the Soma, may we become immortal; we have attained the the light of (heaven), we have know the gods! what now should the enemy do to us, or what, O immortal, should the aggriever do to the mortal?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk beginning अपाम सोमं (*apāma somaṃ*) and the next Ṛk, beginning शं नो भव (*śaṃ no bhava*), are to be applied in order to the touching (abhimarśana means touching) done after the drinking of Soma and to the touching of the heart, as is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra अपाम सोमममृता अभूम शं नो भव हृद आ पीत इंदविति मुखहृदये अभिमृशेरन् (*apāma somamamṛtā abhūma śaṃ no bhava hṛda ā pīta iṃdaviti mukhahṛdaye abhimṛśeran*) (Ā. 5-6).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शं नो॑ भव हृ॒द आ पी॒त इं॑दो पि॒तेव॑ सोम सू॒नवे॑  ॒॑
> सुशेवः ।  
> सखे॑व॒ सख्य॑ उरुशंस॒ धीरः॒ प्र ण॒ आयु॑र्जी॒वसे॑ सोम

> सुशेवः ।  
> सखाइव । सख्ये । उरुशंस । धीरः । प्र । नः । आयुः । जीवसे । सोम । तारीः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम अस्माभिः पीतस्त्वं नोऽस्माकं हृदे हृदयाय शंसुखमा भव । सुखभवने दृष्टांतद्वयं । पिता सूनवे स्वात्मजाय यथा सुखाय
> भवति यथा वा सखाहितान्निवर्त हिते स्थापयिता सखायं स्वसख्यॆ यथा सुशेवः
> सुसुखो भवति । शेवमिति सुखनाम । तद्वत्त्वमपि भव । किंच हे उरुशंस बहुभि-

### Printed p. 552

> र्बहुधा ना शंसनीय बहुकीर्ते सोम धीरो धीमांस्त्व नोऽस्माकं जीवसे
> जीवनायायुरायुष्यं प्र तारीः । प्रवर्धय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, drunk by us, be bliss (śam) to our heart. He gives two illustrations of becoming bliss: as a father is for the happiness of his own son, or as a friend who turns his friend back from what is harmful and establishes him in what is beneficial is very pleasant (suśeva; śeva means happiness) to his friend, so be you also. And further, O Soma, you who deserve to be praised in many ways by many and are of wide fame, wise as you are, increase for our living the span of our life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma, of the form of a stream
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- नोनवे (*nonave*)—to a son
- सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*)—who gives happiness
- पिता इव (*pitā iva*)—like a father
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—who does good to a friend
- सखा इव (*sakhā iva*)—like a friend
- पीतः (*pītaḥ*)—you who are drunk by us
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- हृदे (*hṛde*)—to the heart
- शं आ भव (*śaṃ ā bhava*)—become a giver of happiness
- उरुशंस (*uruśaṃsa*)—who deserve abundant praise
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- धीरः (*dhīraḥ*)—you who are wise
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—in order to live
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life
- प्रतारीः (*pratārīḥ*)—increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, of the form of a stream, drunk by us, become a giver of happiness to our heart, like a father who gives happiness to his son and like a friend who does good to his friend. O Soma, who deserve abundant praise, wise as you are, increase our life that we may live.

##### English translation
O Soma, drunk by us, be bliss to our hearts, as a father is indulgent to a son or friend to a friend; O Soma, worthy of wide praise, wise one, extend our years that we may live.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमे पीता यशसो यशस्कुरा उरुष्यवोऽस्माकं रक्षाकामाः सोमा
> गावो गोविकारभूता वध्यो रथं न रथमिव ता यथा रथं विस्त्रस्तं पर्वसु
> समनाह संदधते तद्वन्मां पीताः सोमाः पर्वसु संनह्यंतु । किंच ते सोमा
> मा मां विप्रसो विप्रस्ताच्चरित्राच्चरणादनुष्ठानाद्रक्षंतु । सोमः पीतश्चेत्कर्म
> ह्यविस्त्रस्तं भवति । उतापि च मा मां सामाप्वाधेः सकाशादिंदवः पीता यवयंतु । प्रथक्कुर्वंतु :

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These drunk Somas, which confer fame (yaśasaḥ) and desire to protect us (uruṣyavaḥ), as the leather thongs, products of the cow, bind together at its joints a chariot that has fallen loose, so may the drunk Somas bind me together at my joints. Further, may those Somas protect me from loose (disjointed) performance of the rite; for when Soma has been drunk the rite is not loose. And may the drunk Indus separate me from affliction **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—oxen
- रथं न (*rathaṃ na*)—as they draw, putting together the separate parts of a cart
- पीताः (*pītāḥ*)—drunk by us
- यशसः (*yaśasaḥ*)—which give fame
- उरुष्यवः (*uruṣyavaḥ*)—which wish to protect me
- इमे (*ime*)—these Soma-juices
- पर्वसु (*parvasu*)—our loosened joints
- समनाद (*samanāda*)—put together and heal
- ते (*te*)—those same Somas
- मा (*mā*)—me
- विप्रसः (*viprasaḥ*)—from the disjoined
- चरित्रात् (*caritrāt*)—from practices
- रक्षंतु (*rakṣaṃtu*)—may they protect
- उत (*uta*)—and
- मा (*mā*)—me
- सामात् (*sāmāt*)—from disease
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—these Soma-juices of the form of a stream
- यवयंतु (*yavayaṃtu*)—may they separate

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As oxen draw a cart, putting together its separate parts, so these Soma-juices, drunk by us, which give fame and wish to protect us, put together and heal our loosened joints. May those same Somas protect me from disjoined practices, and may these Soma-juices of the form of a stream separate me from disease.

##### English translation
May these glory conferring protecting Soma-streams knit together my joints as cows draw together a chariot falling in pieces; may they keep us from a loosely knit worship; may they deliver me from sickness.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम पीतस्त्वं मा मां मथितमग्निं नाग्निमिव सं दिदीपः । संदीपय ।
> प्र चक्षय च चक्षुषः संधुक्क्षणेन । नोऽस्मान् वस्यसोऽतिशयेन वसुमतः कृणुहि ।
> कुरु । अथाधुनां हि खलु ते त्वां हे सोम मदे मदाय मन्ये । स्तौमि । तथा
> सति रेवानिव धनवानिह । इवेति संप्रत्यर्थे । पुष्टिमस्मत्पोषमच्छ प्र चर । अभिगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, drunk by you **NOTE**, kindle me like a fire that has been churned. And open our sight, by rekindling the eye (sandhukṣaṇa). Make us, exceedingly, possessed of wealth. Now indeed, O Soma, I praise you for exhilaration. That being so, come to our nourishment like a wealthy man; the word इव (*iva*) is used here in the sense of "now" **NOTE**. Approach.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मथितं (*mathitaṃ*)—churned by the araṇis
- अग्निं न (*agniṃ na*)—as one makes a fire blaze
- मा (*mā*)—me
- सं दिदीपः (*saṃ didīpaḥ*)—make me full of vigour
- प्र चक्षय (*pra cakṣaya*)—open our eyes and make them bright
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- वस्यसः (*vasyasaḥ*)—so as to be possessed of wealth
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- अध हि (*adha hi*)—now
- ते (*te*)—you
- मदे (*made*)—for joy
- मन्ये (*manye*)—I praise
- रेवान् (*revān*)—you who are rich
- पुष्टिं अच्छ (*puṣṭiṃ accha*)—for our nourishment
- प्र चर (*pra cara*)—graciously come here

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, as one makes a fire churned by the araṇis blaze, make me full of vigour. Open our eyes and make them bright; make us possessed of wealth. O Soma, I praise you now for the gain of joy. You who are rich in wealth, graciously come here for the gain of our nourishment.

##### English translation
Soma, kindle me like the fire ignited by attrition, brighten (our eyes) and make us rich; I praise you now for exhilaration; come now, full of wealth to nourish us.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒षि॒रेण॑ ते॒ मन॑सा सु॒तस्य॑ भक्षी॒महि॒ पित्र्य॑स्येव रा॒यः ।  
> सोम॑ राज॒न्प्र ण॒ आयूं॑षि तारी॒रहा॑नीव॒ सूर्यो॑ वास॒राणि॑॥

> सोम । राजन् । प्र । नः । आयूंषि । तारीः । अहानि इव । सूर्यः । वासराणि ॥७॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इषिरेणाच्छावता मनसा सुतस्य ते सुतमभिषुतं त्वां भक्षीमहि । पित्रस्य
> पितृसंबंधिनो धनस्येव धनमिव । पित्रं धनं यथैषणेन मनसोपभुंजते
> तद्वत् । भक्षिते हे सोम राजन् स्वामिन् नोऽस्माकमायूंषि प्र तारीः ।
> प्रवर्धय वासराणि जगद्वासकान्यहानि सूर्य इव । अत्रेषणेन वैषणेन
> वार्षन्सेन वा । नि. ४-७ । इत्यादिनिरुक्तं ज्ञातव्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With a mind full of longing (iṣireṇa, "with a desiring mind") may we enjoy you, the pressed Soma, as people enjoy with a desiring mind the wealth of their fathers. When you have been enjoyed, O Soma, king, lord, prolong our lives, as the sun prolongs the days (vāsarāṇi, "those that make the world dwell"). Here the Nirukta beginning अत्रेषणेन वैषणेन वार्षन्सेन वा (*atreṣaṇena vaiṣaṇena vārṣansena vā*) (Ni. 4-7) is to be known **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजन् (*rājan*)—O lord
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- इषिरेण (*iṣireṇa*)—filled with reverence
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with the mind
- पित्र्यस्य रायः इव (*pitryasya rāyaḥ iva*)—as one enjoys wealth inherited from the fathers
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—pressed
- ते (*te*)—you
- भक्षीमहि (*bhakṣīmahi*)—we enjoy
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—as the sun
- वासराणि (*vāsarāṇi*)—pervading the world
- अहानि (*ahāni*)—increases the days
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- आयूंषि (*āyūṃṣi*)—lives
- प्रतारीः (*pratārīḥ*)—increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, lord, we now enjoy gladly you who have been pressed, with a mind full of reverence, as one enjoys inherited wealth. As the sun increases the days that pervade the world, increase our lives.

##### English translation
May we partake of you, eſtused, with a longing mind as (men enjoy) paternal wealth; King Soma, prolong our lives, as the sun the world-establishing days. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given an etymology for this Ṛk:

ईषणेन वैषणेन वार्षणेन वा ते मनसा सुतस्य भक्षीमहि पित्र्यस्येव धनस्य प्रवर्धय च न आयूंषि सोमराजन् । अहानीव सूर्यो वासराणि । वासराणि वेसराणि विवासनानि गमनानीतिवा ॥ (*īṣaṇena vaiṣaṇena vārṣaṇena vā te manasā sutasya bhakṣīmahi pitryasyeva dhanasya pravardhaya ca na āyūṃṣi somarājan | ahānīva sūryo vāsarāṇi | vāsarāṇi vesarāṇi vivāsanāni gamanānītivā ‖*) (Ni. 4-7)

### Printed p. 556

Here three kinds of meaning have been given for the word इषिरेण (*iṣireṇa*). This word is an adjective of the word मनसा (*manasā*). (1) ईषणेन (*īṣaṇena*). ईषति, फणति इति गतिकर्मसु पठितं (*īṣati, phaṇati iti gatikarmasu paṭhitaṃ*). सर्वात्मना गतेनेत्यर्थः (*sarvātmanā gatenetyarthaḥ*). Since the root īṣati has the sense of going, the word ईषणेन (*īṣaṇena*), formed from this root, means: with a mind fixed there, that is, on you. (2) एषणेन (*eṣaṇena*)-इच्छावता फलप्रार्थनावतेत्यर्थः (*icchāvatā phalaprārthanāvatetyarthaḥ*). The meaning is: with a mind that desires you for the attainment of fruit. (3) ऋषणेनेति वा (*ṛṣaṇeneti vā*)-दर्शनवता (*darśanavatā*). The meaning is: looking, that is, with a mind that desires while looking at that alone.

O Soma, king, with a mind fixed on you alone, let us drink the Soma-juice as one happily enjoys inherited property. The main sense is: as the sun lengthens the days of the spring season, so lengthen our life.

Here वासराणि (*vāsarāṇi*) means days, daytimes. वासराणि (*vāsarāṇi*) means वेसराणि (*vesarāṇi*). शीतोष्णाभ्यां तानि सरंति, तेषु हि शीतोष्णं भवति ! रात्रौ शीतं दिवा उष्णं । (*śītoṣṇābhyāṃ tāni saraṃti, teṣu hi śītoṣṇaṃ bhavati ! rātrau śītaṃ divā uṣṇaṃ |*). The word वासर (*vāsara*) is formed from the root सृ-सरि (*sṛ-sari*). Time, that is, the time of the day, goes on moving forward. While it moves so, accompanied in the night by a cold atmosphere and in the day by heat, the measure of the time of the day goes away, that is, passes away. Therefore the days (mainly the daytime) are called vāsarāṇi or vesarāṇi. Besides, विवासनानि-तानि हि तत् शीतं निवासयंति नाशयंतीत्यर्थः (*vivāsanāni-tāni hi tat śītaṃ nivāsayaṃti nāśayaṃtītyarthaḥ*). Because the day destroys by its (the sun's) heat the cold that arises in the night, the days may be said to have the meaning निवासनानि (*nivāsanāni*). गमनानीति ना विसृतानि विस्तीर्णानि संति वासराणीति उच्यंते । यथा तानि सूर्यः वर्धयति मंदगतिश्वात् एवमस्माकं त्वमायुः प्रवर्धयेत्याशीः ॥ (*gamanānīti nā visṛtāni vistīrṇāni saṃti vāsarāṇīti ucyaṃte | yathā tāni sūryaḥ vardhayati maṃdagatiśvāt evamasmākaṃ tvamāyuḥ pravardhayetyāśīḥ ‖*). Because the daytime, especially in summer, is long, the extended days may be called vāsarāṇi. The sun, moving slowly in the day, increases the measure of the time of the day. Likewise, O Soma, increase our life: this prayer is expressed here.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोम॑ राजन्मृ॒ळया॑ नः स्व॒स्ति तव॑ स्मसि व्र॒त्या॒३॒॑ ३ स्तस्य॑ विद्धि ।  
> अल॑र्ति॒ दक्ष॑ उ॒त म॒न्युरिं॑दो॒ मा नो॑ अ॒र्यो अ॑नुका॒मं ॑ 
> परा दाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोम ! राजन् ! मृळय । नृ । स्वस्ति । तव । स्मसि । व्रत्याः । तस्य । विद्धि ।  
> आलतिर् । दक्षः । उत । मन्युः । इंदो इति मा । नः । अर्यः । अनुकामं । परा ।  
> दाति ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम राजन् नोऽस्मान् स्वस्वविनाशाय मृळय ! सुखय च । व्रत्या
> व्रतिनोः वयः तव स्मसि स्वभूताः स्म । तस्य तं स्वकीयं तप विद्धि । जानीहि ! अथवा
> तव त्वमित्यर्थः । त्वं जानीहि । किःच हे इंदो दक्षः प्रवृद्धोऽस्मच्छत्रुरलर्ति ।
> गच्छति । उतापि च मन्युः क्रोधः क्रुद्धो वालर्ति । तादृशस्योभयविधस्यार्योऽरेनुकामं यथाकामं नोऽस्मान्मा परा दाः ! परादेहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing King Soma, the seer Pragātha asks him to bring happiness to us, **NOTE**. We who keep the vows are his own: "we are yours". Let him know us as his own devoted ones; or else (or else) the sense is "you (Soma) know it". Further, O Indu, the strong and swollen enemy comes against us, and the wrathful one, or the enemy in wrath, comes; let Soma not hand us over (मा परा दाः (*mā parā dāḥ*)) to such an enemy of either kind, to do with us as he wishes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजन् (*rājan*)—the lord
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—so that it may be well
- मृळय (*mṛḷaya*)—make happy
- व्रत्याः (*vratyāḥ*)—we who perform the sacrificial rites
- तव (*tava*)—as belonging to you
- स्मसि (*smasi*)—we are
- तस्य (*tasya*)—us who belong to you
- विद्धि (*viddhi*)—know as devoted
- उत (*uta*)—and
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O flowing Soma
- दक्षः (*dakṣaḥ*)—the strong enemy
- अलर्ति (*alarti*)—comes to confront us
- मन्युः (*manyuḥ*)—shows wrath
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—to the enemy
- अनुकामं (*anukāmaṃ*)—as he desires
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा परा दाः (*mā parā dāḥ*)—do not give up

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O lord Soma, make us happy so that it may be well with us. We who perform the sacrificial rites are indeed yours. Know us, who are yours, as devoted. O Soma, a strong enemy comes to confront us and shows his wrath. Do not give us over to the enemy, to do with us as he desires.

##### English translation
King Soma, bless us for our welfare; we worshippers are yours, recognize it ; the enemy goes strong and fierce, O Soma ; give us not over to him as he desires.

> यत् । ते । वयं । प्रमिनाम । व्रतानि । सः । नः । मृळ । सुसखा । देव । वस्यति ॥९ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम देव त्वं नोऽस्माकं तन्नस्तनोरंगस्य गोपा हि रक्षिता खलु ।
> अतो गात्रे गात्रे सर्वेष्टंगेषु नृचक्षसा नृणां कर्मनेतृणां द्रष्टा त्वं निषसत्थ ।

> स त्वं वस्यः श्रेष्ठान्नोऽस्मान् सुषखा शोभनसखा सन् मृळ । सुखय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O divine Soma, you are the guardian of our body, that is, of our limbs. Therefore you sit in every limb, as the beholder of men, that is, of those who lead the rites. Even if we offend against your rites (व्रतानि (*vratāni*)) and harm them, still, O god, being a good friend, make happy us who are the better ones (वस्यः (*vasyaḥ*), श्रेष्ठान् (*śreṣṭhān*)). **NOTE**

- व्रतानि (*vratāni*)—rites

- प्रविनाम (*pravināma*)—even if we make blunted
- देव (*deva*)—O divine Soma
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- वस्यः (*vasyaḥ*)—the better ones
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सुषखा (*suṣakhā*)—being an excellent friend
- मृळ (*mṛḷa*)—make happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you are the guardian of our body. In every limb of our body you sit, having taken possession of it, watching the conduct of us mortals. O divine Soma, even if we blunt your rites, being an excellent friend to us, make us happy.

O Soma, you are the guardian of our bodies, you dwell in each limb as the beholder of men; though we impair your rites, yet, divine one, bless us, you who are possessed of most excellent food and good friends.
#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒दू॒दरे॑ण॒ सख्या॑ सचेय॒ यो मा॒ न रिष्ये॑द्धर्यश्व पी॒तः ।  
> अ॒यं यः सोमो॒ न्यधा॑य्य॒स्मे तस्मा॒ इंद्रं॑ प्र॒तिर॑मे॒म्यायुः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋदूदरेण । सख्या । सचेय । यः । मा । न । रिष्येत् । हरिऽश्व । पीतः ।  
> आयुं । यः ! सोमः । नि । अधायि । अस्मे इति । तस्यै । इंद्रं । प्रतिरं । एमि ।  
> आयुतः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं प्रगाथ ऋदूदरेणोदराबाधकेन सोमेन सख्या सचेय ।
> संगच्छेय । संगतो भवामि । ऋदूवरः सोमो मृदूदरः । नि. ६-४ । इति
> यास्कः । यः सोमः पीतः सन् मा मां न रिष्यत् न हिंस्यत् हे हर्यश्चंद्र
> सौम्ये सूक्त इंद्रस्य कीर्तनं सोमस्येंद्रस्वामिकत्वान्न विरुद्धं । योऽयं
> सोमोऽस्मै अस्मासु न्यधायि निहितोऽभूत् तस्मै सोमाय प्रतिरमायुर्जठरे
> चिरकालावस्थानमिंद्रमेमि । याचे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Pragātha, would unite with Soma as a friend, Soma who does not hurt the belly (ऋदूदरेणोदराबाधकेन (*ṛdūdareṇodarābādhakena*)). Yāska says that Soma is ऋदूदरः (*ṛdūdaraḥ*), "soft in the belly", with the reference Ni. 6-4 **NOTE**. O lord of bay horses, let the Soma which, when drunk, does not injure me, not harm me. In this Soma hymn the praise of Indra is not out of place, since Soma belongs to Indra. To that Soma which has been placed in us I come to Indra and ask for a long abiding in the belly. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- पीतः (*pītaḥ*)—when drunk
- मा (*mā*)—me

- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—friendship
- सचेय (*saceya*)—may I obtain
- हर्यश्व (*haryaśva*)—O Indra, whose horses are called Hari
- यः आयं सोमः (*yaḥ āyaṃ somaḥ*)—this Soma which
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- न्यधायि (*nyadhāyi*)—has been placed

### Printed p. 560
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—for that Soma
- प्रतिरं (*pratiraṃ*)—long
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life; make it last
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—you, Indra, the lord
- एमि (*emi*)—I ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I shall obtain friendship with that Soma which fills the belly and which, when drunk, does not harm me. O Indra, lord of the horses called Hari, I ask of you, the lord, that the Soma I have drunk may remain long in my belly.

##### English translation
May I obtain a wholesome friend who, when quaffed, will not harm me, O lord of bay horses; I ask of Indra a long permanence for this Soma which has been placed within us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the word ऋदूदरेण (*ṛdūdareṇa*) Yāska has given the explanation ऋदूदरः सोमो मृदूदरो मृदुरुदरेष्टिति वा । ऋदूदरेण सख्या सचेय इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*ṛdūdaraḥ somo mṛdūdaro mṛdurudareṣṭiti vā | ṛdūdareṇa sakhyā saceya ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-4). Ṛdūdara means the Soma, or the Soma juice. Because the inside of this Soma is soft, or because it is soft in the belly of the one who drinks it (soft means gentle, without pain or harm), the Soma is called Ṛdūdara. In this matter the present Ṛk itself, ऋदूदरेण सख्या सचेय (*ṛdūdareṇa sakhyā saceya*), is the example. That is, the chief meaning is that from drinking Soma no pain comes to the belly, and it remains delightful.

### Printed p. 561

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्यास्ता अनिराः प्रेरयितुमशक्या आमीवा बलवत्यः पीडाः अपास्थुः । अपगच्छंतु । यास्तमिषीचीर्बलवत्योऽस्मान्निर्तरामत्रसन् प्राप्नुवन् कंपयंति
> तथाभ्येषुः ! अपगमे कारणमाह ! यस्मात्सोमो विहाया महान् सन्नस्मानारुहत् आगमत् प्राप्तवान् अतोपास्थुरिति भावः । यत्र यस्मिन् सोमे पीत
> आयरायुष्यं प्रतिरंते वर्धयंति मनुष्यास्तं सोममगन्नेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those irremovable (अनिराः (*anirāḥ*), "that cannot be driven away") strong afflictions (आमीवा (*āmīvā*)) are to depart. Those mighty ones (तमिषीचीः (*tamiṣīcīḥ*)) that have made us tremble are likewise to be afraid. He states the reason for their departure: because Soma, being great (विहाया (*vihāyā*)), has climbed upon us and reached us, therefore they have departed. We have come to that Soma in which, when drunk, men prolong their life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्याः (*tyāḥ*)—those that constantly afflict
- अनिराः (*anirāḥ*)—that cannot be removed
- अमीवाः (*amīvāḥ*)—diseases
- अप अस्थुः (*apa asthuḥ*)—let them depart far away
- निः (*niḥ*)—completely
- आत्रसन् (*ātrasan*)—those that made us tremble
- तमिषीचीः (*tamiṣīcīḥ*)—and powerful maladies
- अभैषुः (*abhaiṣuḥ*)—let them go away in fear of Soma
- विहायाः (*vihāyāḥ*)—of great form
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- आरुहन् (*āruhan*)—has entered
- यत्र (*yatra*)—by which Soma satisfied
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—the life of man
- प्रतिरंते (*pratiraṃte*)—grows
- अगन्न (*aganna*)—that Soma we have attained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the diseases that afflict us constantly and cannot be removed depart far from us. Let the powerful maladies that made us tremble go away in fear of Soma. The Soma of great form has entered us. We have attained that Soma by which, when a man is satisfied, his life grows.

##### English translation
May those irremovable sicknesses depart ; let those strong (pains) which have made us tremble, be afraid; the mighty Soma has climbed into us,— we have attained that (draught) by which men prolong life.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पितरः य इंदुर्हृत्सु पीतः सन्नमर्त्यो मृतिरहितः सन्नाविवेश
> मर्तान्योऽस्मान् तस्यॆ सोमाय हविषा विधेम । परिचरेम । अस्य सोमस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O fathers, the Indu which, when drunk in our hearts, has entered us mortals while itself immortal, that is, free from death: to that Soma we would do service with an oblation. In the bliss and in the favourable thought, that is, the benevolent mind, of this Soma may we be.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O fathers, to that immortal Soma which, drunk by us with a willing mind, has entered the hearts of us men, we do service with oblation. May we abide in the bliss that comes from this Soma and in its favourable mind.

##### English translation
That Soma which, drunk into our hearts, has entered, immortalai, into us mortals,—to him, fathers, let us do worship with oblations; may we abide in his bliss and favour. **NOTE**
