##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । सोम । पितृभिः । संविदानः । अनु । द्यावापृथिवी इति । आ । ततंथ ।  
> तस्मै ! त्रैः । इंदो इति । हविसा । विधेम । वयं । स्याम । पतयः । रयाणां ॥१३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महापितृयज्ञे सोमाय पितृमते पुरोडाशमित्यत्र त्वं सोमेति
> याज्या । सूत्रितं च । त्वं सोम पितृभिः संविदानो बर्हिषदः पितर ऊत्यर्वाक् ।
> आ. २-१९ । इति ॥ तृतीयसवने सोमस्य चरोरपीयं याज्या! त्वं सोम पितृभिः
> संविदान इति सौम्यस्य । आ. ५-१९ । इति हि सूत्रितं ॥
> हे सोम त्वं पितृभिः सह संविदानः संगच्छमानो द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यावन्वा ततंथ । क्रमेण विस्तारयसि । तस्मै सोमाय हविषा विधेम ।
> परिचरेम । वयं रयाणां धनानां पतयः स्याम । भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Mahāpitṛyajña, in the offering of the cake to Soma accompanied by the fathers, the verse त्वं सोम (*tvaṃ soma*) is the yājyā. It is laid down in the sūtra त्वं सोम पितृभिः संविदानो बर्हिषदः पितर ऊत्यर्वाक् (*tvaṃ soma pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidāno barhiṣadaḥ pitara ūtyarvāk*) (Ā. 2-19). This is also the yājyā for the cooked offering to Soma at the third pressing; it is laid down that the verse त्वं सोम पितृभिः संविदान इति सौम्यस्य (*tvaṃ soma pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidāna iti saumyasya*) (Ā. 5-19). O Soma, you, in company with the fathers, stretch out heaven and earth in succession, that is, you extend them step by step. To that Soma we would do service with an oblation. May we become lords of riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O flowing one
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- पितृभिः (*pitṛbhiḥ*)—with the fathers
- संविदानः (*saṃvidānaḥ*)—united
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- अनु आ ततंध (*anu ā tataṃdha*)—you have caused to be extended
- तस्मै ते (*tasmai te*)—to such a you
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblation
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—we shall serve
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- रयाणां (*rayāṇāṃ*)—of riches
- पतयः (*patayaḥ*)—as lords
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, of the nature of a stream, you, united with the fathers, have caused heaven and earth to be extended. To such a you we do service with oblation. May we become lords of riches.

##### English translation
Soma, you in conjunction with the fathers stretch out successively heaven and earth,—to you let us do worship with oblations, may we be lords of wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the offering called the Mahāpitṛyajña, when the oblation सोमाय पितृमते पुरोडाशं (*somāya pitṛmate puroḍāśaṃ*) is made, this Ṛk त्वं सोम (*tvaṃ soma*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-Śrautasūtra,

### Printed p. 564
त्वं सोम पितृभिः संविदानो बर्हिषदः पितर ऊत्यर्वाक् (*tvaṃ soma pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidāno barhiṣadaḥ pitara ūtyarvāk*) (Ā. 2-19). Also in the offering of the cooked oblation made to the deity Soma at the time of the third pressing, this Ṛk is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-Śrautasūtra त्वं सोम पितृभिः संविदान इति सौम्यस्य (*tvaṃ soma pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidāna iti saumyasya*) (Ā. 5-19).

> वयं । सोमस्य । विश्वह । प्रियासः । सुवीरासः । विदथं । आ । वदेम ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे त्रातारो रक्षितारो हे देवाः नोऽस्मानधि पोचत अधिवचनं कुरुत ।
> किंच नोऽस्मान्निद्राः स्वप्ना :मेशत । ईश्वरा मा भूवन् बाधितुं । उषपि च
> जल्पिर्निंदकोऽस्मान्मा निंदतु । वयं सोमस्य प्रियासः प्रियाः स्यामः विश्वह
> सर्वेष्टप्यहःसु । सर्वदेत्यर्थः । सुवीरासः शोभनपुत्राः संतो विदथं स्तोत्रमा
> वदेम । अभिमुख्येन वदेम । अथवा ! सुपुत्रा विदथं गृहमा वदेम । आवदनं
> पुत्रपौत्राणां धनेनोपछंदनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O protectors, O gods, speak on our behalf, that is, plead for us. Further, let sleep and dreams not become lords over us, to afflict us **NOTE**. Let the babbler, the censurer, not revile us. May we be always dear to Soma, on all days, that is, at all times. Having good sons, may we utter the hymn (विदथं (*vidathaṃ*)), speaking it directly towards the god. Or else (अथवा (*athavā*)), having good sons, may we speak in the house (meaning the house); the speaking is the enriching of sons and grandsons with wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रातारः (*trātāraḥ*)—protectors
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अधि वोचक (*adhi vocaka*)—bless us, that it may be well with us
- नः (*naḥ*)—upon us
- निद्राः (*nidrāḥ*)—bad dreams
- मा ईशत (*mā īśata*)—let them not exert their influence
- उत (*uta*)—and
- जल्पिः (*jalpiḥ*)—the censurer
- मा (*mā*)—let him not revile us
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- विश्वह (*viśvaha*)—on all days
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—to Soma
- प्रियासः (*priyāsaḥ*)—may we be dear
- सुवीरासः (*suvīrāsaḥ*)—together with excellent sons
- विदथं (*vidathaṃ*)—the hymn
- आ वदेम (*ā vadema*)—we shall recite

### Printed p. 565

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O protecting gods, bless us, that it may be well with us. Let bad dreams not exert their influence upon us. Let the censurer not revile us. May we be dear to Soma on all days. Together with excellent sons we shall recite the hymn.

##### English translation
Guardian gods, speak favourably to us; let no dreams nor the censurer overpower us; may we be ever dear to Soma ; possessed of brave offspring, may we utter our hymn.

> पुरस्तात् ॥ १५ ॥

> त्वं । न ॥ इंदो इति । ऊतिभिः । सजोषाः । पाहि । पश्चातात् । उत । वा ।  
> पुरस्तात् ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वं नः सोम विश्वत इति सौम्ये पशौ हविषोऽनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । त्वं
> नः सोम विश्वतो वयोधा या ते धामानि दिवि या पृथिव्यां । आ ३-७ । इति ॥
> हे सोम त्वं नोऽस्माकं विश्वतः सर्वाभ्यो दिग्भ्यो वयोधा अन्नदाता ।
> तथा त्वं स्वर्वित् स्वर्गलंभको नृचक्षाः सर्वमनुष्यद्रष्टा त्वमा विश । हे इंदो
> त्वं सजोषाः सह प्रीयमाणः सन्नूतिभिः सह । अथवोतयो गंतारो मरुतः ।
> तैः सहितः सन् पश्चातात् पश्चादुत वा पुरस्ताच्च पाहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse त्वं नः सोम विश्वतः (*tvaṃ naḥ soma viśvataḥ*) is the anuvākyā for the oblation at the animal sacrifice to Soma; it is laid down in the sūtra with the words या ते धामानि दिवि या पृथिव्यां (*yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyāṃ*) (Ā. 3-7). O Soma, you are the giver of food (वयोधा (*vayodhā*), अन्नदाता (*annadātā*)) to us from every side, from all directions. So too you are the obtainer of heaven (स्वर्वित् (*svarvit*), स्वर्गलंभको (*svargalaṃbhako*)) and the beholder of all men; enter us. O Indu, being pleased together with your protections (ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)), or else (अथ (*atha*)) the ūtayaḥ are the goers, the Maruts, together with them protect us from behind and also from in front.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—from all directions
- वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—be the giver of food
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- स्वर्वित् (*svarvit*)—you are the beholder of heaven

### Printed p. 566
- नृचराः (*nṛcarāḥ*)—you are the beholder of the conduct of men
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter into us
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—joined with love
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—with protections
- पश्चातात् (*paścātāt*)—from behind
- उत वा (*uta vā*)—and also
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—from the front
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, be the giver of food to us in all directions. You are the beholder of heaven. You are the beholder of the conduct of men. Enter into us. O Soma, joined with love, protect us with your protections both from behind and from the front.

##### English translation
You, Soma, give us food from every side; you are the bestower of heaven; enter us, beholder of men; O Soma, rejoicing with your protecting powers, guard us from behind and before.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk त्वं नः सोम विश्वतः (*tvaṃ naḥ soma viśvataḥ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra when the oblation is offered in the animal sacrifice addressed to the deity Soma, as is explained by the sutra of the Āśvalāyana-Śrautasūtra, the words या ते धामानि दिवि या पृथिव्यां (*yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyāṃ*) (Ā. 3-7).

### Printed p. 567
## Sūkta 49 (Maṇḍala 8)
**Vālakhilya Sūkta 1** **NOTE**
**Bhāṣya**
श्रुतिकंजार्थलक्ष्मीं यो विकासयति हृद्गतं (तां) । स पायात्सच्चिदानंदः सूर्यमंडलगो हरिः ॥ (*śrutikaṃjārthalakṣmīṃ yo vikāsayati hṛdgataṃ (tāṃ) | sa pāyātsaccidānaṃdaḥ sūryamaṃḍalago hariḥ ‖*)
'अभि प्र वः' इति दशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं प्रस्कण्वस्यार्षमैंद्रं । अनुक्रांतं च- 'अभि प्र दश प्रस्कण्वः प्रागाधं तत्' इति । आयुजां बृहती छंदः । युजां सतोबृहती छंदः ! विनियोगः सूत्रादवगंतव्यः ॥ (*'abhi pra vaḥ ' iti daśarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktaṃ praskaṇvasyārṣamaiṃdraṃ | anukrāṃtaṃ ca- 'abhi pra daśa praskaṇvaḥ prāgādhaṃ tat ' iti | āyujāṃ bṛhatī chaṃdaḥ | yujāṃ satobṛhatī chaṃdaḥ ! viniyogaḥ sūtrādavagaṃtavyaḥ ‖*)
In the eighth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, after the 48 sūktas, there is the part called Vālakhilya. In it there are in all eleven sūktas and 80 Ṛks. For the first five sūktas Indra is the deity; in the sixth sūkta Indra and the Viśvedevas are praised; in the seventh sūkta there is the praise of the gift of the seer Praskaṇva. In the eighth sūkta, besides the praise of Praskaṇva's gift as in the preceding sūkta, Agni and Sūrya are praised (in the fifth Ṛk). For the ninth sūkta the Aśvins are the deities; for the tenth sūkta the Viśvedevas are the deities; for the eleventh sūkta Indra and Varuṇa are the deities. The seers of these sūktas also differ.
Sāyaṇa has not written a commentary on the Vālakhilya sūktas. No other commentary on them seems to exist, or if it exists it has not been found. Western scholars such as Max-Muller too have said nothing about these sūktas. Since the word खल (*khala*) **NOTE** has the meaning "left over, remainder", these sūktas may be called supplementary mantras. Since some mantras of these sūktas are also found in other Vedas such as the Taittirīya-saṃhitā, then, according to the saying that mantras found in another recension are to be regarded as supplementary mantras, these sūktas must be supplementary mantras. In their style too the profundity, excellence and antiquity found in the other Vedic mantras are not seen. Even so, the earlier tradition of studying these sūktas as included in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā has come down through the lineage of teachers, and the mantras have accents and a Pada-pāṭha as prescribed.
We have said above that these sūktas have no Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya. But in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya published by the Vaidika Saṃśodhana Maṇḍala of the city of Pūnā, in the 3rd volume, on page 779, there is a remark concerning these sūktas.

### Printed p. 568
वाराणसीस्थ राजकीय संस्कृतपाठशालायाः प्राप्ते (ज्ञ) संज्ञकलिखितपुस्तके वालखिल्यसूक्तानां भाष्यं लिखितमुपलभ्यते । परं त्वितरेषु सर्वेष्टपि पुस्तकेष्टनुपलंबात् व्याख्याशैल्या विभिन्नत्वाच्च नैतत्सायणाचार्यकृतमिति व्यक्तं प्रतीयते । तथाप्येतद्विदुषामुपयोगाय स्यादिति मत्वात्र दीयते । (*vārāṇasīstha rājakīya saṃskṛtapāṭhaśālāyāḥ prāpte (jña) saṃjñakalikhitapustake vālakhilyasūktānāṃ bhāṣyaṃ likhitamupalabhyate | paraṃ tvitareṣu sarveṣṭapi pustakeṣṭanupalaṃbāt vyākhyāśailyā vibhinnatvācca naitatsāyaṇācāryakṛtamiti vyaktaṃ pratīyate | tathāpyetadviduṣāmupayogāya syāditi matvātra dīyate |*)
एतस्मिन्विषयेऽस्माभिः पृष्टा एतत्पारशालाधिकारिणः एवं लिखंति-एतद्भस्तलिखितं पाठशालायाः कृते रेवानगरे क्रीतमासीत् । तस्य लेखनं पुण्यपत्तन एवाभूदिति श्रूयते । एतल्लिखितपुस्तकगतवालखिल्यसूक्तभाष्यं केन विरचितमिति निश्चितं वक्तुमशक्यं । न केनापि वाराणसीस्थेन पंडितेनैतद्विरचितमिति निश्चितमेव ॥ (*etasminviṣaye 'smābhiḥ pṛṣṭā etatpāraśālādhikāriṇaḥ evaṃ likhaṃti-etadbhastalikhitaṃ pāṭhaśālāyāḥ kṛte revānagare krītamāsīt | tasya lekhanaṃ puṇyapattana evābhūditi śrūyate | etallikhitapustakagatavālakhilyasūktabhāṣyaṃ kena viracitamiti niścitaṃ vaktumaśakyaṃ | na kenāpi vārāṇasīsthena paṃḍitenaitadviracitamiti niścitameva ‖*)
The commentary on the Vālakhilya sūktas given here is taken from a handwritten copy bearing the number (Jña) in the Government Sanskrit Pāṭhaśālā at Kāśī. Because the commentary on the Vālakhilya sūktas is not found in any other commentary books, and because the style of this commentary is not like the style of Sāyaṇa's commentary, it can be said clearly that this commentary is not composed by Sāyaṇācārya. Even so, in the hope that it may be useful to those who study the meaning of the Veda, it is published here.
When we wrote to the authorities of that Pāṭhaśālā and asked about this book, they wrote in reply: it has become known that this handwritten book was bought at the city of Revā when books were being collected for the library of the Pāṭhaśālā, and that it was written in the city of Pūnā. But as to by whom this commentary on the Vālakhilya sūktas was composed, nothing at all is known. But this much can be said with certainty, that it was not composed by any pandit living at Kāśī.
**Commentary on the first sūkta**
श्रुतिकंजार्थलक्ष्मीं यो विकासयति हृद्गणां । स पायात्सच्चिदानंदः सूर्यमंडलगो हरिः ॥ (*śrutikaṃjārthalakṣmīṃ yo vikāsayati hṛdgaṇāṃ | sa pāyātsaccidānaṃdaḥ sūryamaṃḍalago hariḥ ‖*)
Translation: This sūkta अभि प्र वः (*abhi pra vaḥ*) is the first of the Vālakhilya sūktas. In it there are ten Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva; Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अभि प्र दश प्रस्कण्वः प्रागाथं तत् (*abhi pra daśa praskaṇvaḥ prāgāthaṃ tat*). The odd-numbered Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Bṛhatī metre; the even-numbered Ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre. The application (viniyoga) is to be learnt from the sūtra.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि प्र वः॑ सु॒राध॑स॒मिंद्र॑मर्च॒ यथा॑ वि॒दे ।  
> यो ज॑रि॒तृभ्यो॑ म॒घवा॑ पुरू॒वसुः॑ स॒हस्रे॑णेव॒ शिक्ष॑ति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । प्र । वः । सुराधसं । इंद्रं । अर्च । यथा । विदे ।  
> यः । जरित्यभ्यः । मघवा । पुरुषवसुः । सहस्रेण इव । शिक्षति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरात्मानं ब्रूते । हे प्रस्कण्ण वः युष्माकं । बहुवचनं पुत्रपौत्राभिप्रायेण । युष्मत्स्वामिभूतमिंद्रमभिलक्ष्य प्रार्थ प्रकर्षण पूजय । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । यथा विदे विद्वांसं स्वगुरुं पूजयसि तद्वत् । कीदृशं । सुराधसं ।
> शोभनं राधो धनं यस्य तं । कोऽसाविंद्र इत्युच्यते । य इंद्रः मघवा
> धनवान् पुरूवसुः बहूनां वासयिता जरितृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः सहस्रेणेव अपरिमितमेव शिक्षति ददाति । धनादिकमिति शेषः । अत्र यःशब्दोऽवधारणार्थः । सहस्रेणेव
> ( ? इवशब्दोऽवधारणार्थः । सहस्रेणैव)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer speaks of himself. O Praskaṇva, "of you" (वः (*vaḥ*)) is in the plural with a view to your sons and grandsons: worship eagerly, with fitting praise, Indra, who is your lord. An example is given: as you honour your own teacher, a learned man (विदे (*vide*)), so worship him. What kind of Indra? One of good wealth (सुराधसं (*surādhasaṃ*)), that is, whose wealth is excellent. Who is this Indra? He who is मघवा (*maghavā*), wealthy, पुरूवसुः (*purūvasuḥ*), one who gives a dwelling to many, and who gives to the singers (जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)), the praisers, as if by thousands (सहस्रेणेव (*sahasreṇeva*)), that is, without measure, wealth and the like; this is to be supplied. Here the word यः (*yaḥ*) has the sense of emphasis, and the word इव (*iva*) has the sense of emphasis: "by thousands indeed". **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवा (*maghavā*)—wealthy
- पुरूवसुः (*purūvasuḥ*)—giver of dwelling to many
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)—to his praisers
- सहस्रेणेव (*sahasreṇeva*)—by the thousand
- शिक्षति (*śikṣati*)—gives, such a one
- सुराधसं (*surādhasaṃ*)—possessed of excellent wealth
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your kinsman
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- यथा विदे (*yathā vide*)—as one worships a learned man
- अभि प्रार्थ (*abhi prārtha*)—go to meet and worship

### Printed p. 570

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Worship Indra, the wealthy, the giver of dwellings to many, who gives to his praisers by the thousand, the possessor of excellent wealth, your kinsman, going to meet him as one worships a learned teacher.

##### English translation
That I may attain wealth I invoke Indra, Lord of precious wealth and sing his praise, Maghavan, Lord of abundance he gives to his worshippers thousands and thousands.
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तानी॑केव॒ प्र जि॑गाति धृष्णु॒या हंति॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ दा॒शुषे॑ ।  
> गि॒रेरि॑व॒ प्र रसा॑ अस्य पिन्निरे॒ दत्ता॑णि पुरु॒भोज॑सः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतानीकाइव । प्र । जिगाति । धृष्णुया । हंति । वृत्राणि । दाशुषे ।  
> गिरेः इव ! प्र । रसाः । अस्य । पिन्निरे । दत्ताणि । पुरुभोजसः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धृष्णुया शत्रुधर्षणशील इंद्रः शतानीकेव अपरिमितान्येव रिपुसैन्यानि प्र
> जिगाति प्रकर्षेण गच्छति । स्ववशीकरोति । किंच य इंद्रः दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवतो
> यजमानस्य वृत्राणि पापानि शत्रून् वा हंति नाशयति । तस्यास्य पुरुभोजसः
> बहुपालकस्येंद्रस्य दशाणि हिरण्यादीनि धनानि । दत्तमत्र हिरण्यं मरुत् दत्रं
> इति हिरण्यनामसु पातात् । प्र पिन्निरे प्रकर्षेण प्रीणयंति तर्पयंति जगत् । अत्र
> दृष्टांतः । गिरेरिव पर्वतस्य मेघस्य वा संबंधिनो यथा रसाः जलानि जगत्
> प्रीणयंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the one who assails enemies (धृष्णुया (*dhṛṣṇuyā*)), goes forth against countless hosts of foes, as though they were hundreds (शतानीकेव (*śatānīkeva*)), that is, he brings them under his own control. Further, that Indra destroys the Vṛtras, the sins or the enemies, of the sacrificer who has given the oblation. The riches, gold and the like, given by this Indra, the protector of many, delight and satisfy the world abundantly. **NOTE** An example is given: as the waters (रसाः (*rasāḥ*)) belonging to a mountain or a cloud satisfy the world, so do these.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धृष्णुया (*dhṛṣṇuyā*)—Indra, the assailer of foes
- शतानीका इव (*śatānīkā iva*)—like the leader of a host of a hundred troops
- प्र जिगाति (*pra jigāti*)—moves in splendour
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—for the benefit of the sacrificer

### Printed p. 571
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the sinful enemies
- हंति (*haṃti*)—he destroys
- रसाः (*rasāḥ*)—waters
- गिरेः इव (*gireḥ iva*)—as from a mountain, welling up and flowing
- पुरुभोजसः (*purubhojasaḥ*)—protector of many
- अस्य (*asya*)—by this Indra
- दत्राणि (*datrāṇi*)—the given riches
- प्र पिन्निरे (*pra pinnire*)—flow forth and satisfy the world

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the assailer of foes, moves in splendour like the leader of a host of a hundred troops. For the benefit of the sacrificer he destroys the sinful enemies. As streams of water welling up from a mountain satisfy the world, the riches given by Indra satisfy the world in the form of a stream.

##### English translation
He is walking magistically as if Lord of hundred forces, for the sacrificers he is killing Vritra, protector of many. Gifts proceeds from him as streams spring out of a mountain.

> श्वरसप्रदानेन त्वां तर्पयंतीत्यर्थः । कथं । आपो न सरः । ता यथा महाजलाशयं पूरयंति तद्वत् । किमर्थं । राधसे यजमानस्य धनलाभाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, to be won with songs (गीर्वणः (*gīrvaṇaḥ*)), O bearer of the thunderbolt, O hero: the Somas that are pressed, delight-giving, fill you on all sides, you who are worthy to be gathered to the home (ओक्यं (*okyaṃ*); the text adds in brackets समवेतुमर्हं (*samavetumarhaṃ*) **NOTE**). The meaning is that they satisfy you by giving their juice **NOTE**. How? As waters fill a great reservoir (आपो न सरः (*āpo na saraḥ*)). For what purpose? For राधसे (*rādhase*), for the sacrificer's gain of wealth.

### Printed p. 572

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O mighty one
- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—worshipped with praises
- वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)—bearer of the thunderbolt
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters
- ओक्यं (*okyaṃ*)—their destined place
- सरः अनु न. (*saraḥ anu na.*)—as they go to the lake and fill it
- मदाः (*madāḥ*)—delight-giving
- ये इंदवः (*ye iṃdavaḥ*)—which Soma juices
- सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)—have been pressed, such Soma juices
- राधसे (*rādhase*)—for the sacrificer's gain of wealth
- त्वा (*tvā*)—drawing near to you
- आ पृणंति (*ā pṛṇaṃti*)—fill your belly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, mighty, worshipped with praises, bearer of the thunderbolt, as waters go to their destined place, the lake, and fill it, may the delight-giving Soma juices that have been pressed fill your belly for the sacrificer's gain of wealth and be a source of joy to you.

##### English translation
Worshipable Indra, the exhilarating Soma is being effused for the hero, wielder of thunder-bolt; may abundance go to you as water fills its dwelling, the Lake.
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ने॒हसं॑ प्र॒तर॑णं वि॒वक्ष॑णं॒ मध्वः॒ स्वादि॑ष्टमीं पिब ।  
> आ यथा॑ मंदसा॒नः कि॒रासि॑ नः॒ प्रक्षु॒द्रेव॒ त्मना॑ धृ॒षत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनेहसं । प्रतरणं । विवक्षणं । मध्वः । स्वादिष्टं । ईं । पिब ।  
> आ । यथा । मंदसानः । किरासि । नः । प्र । क्षुद्रा इव । त्मना । धृषत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अनेहसं यथाकालं ईं एनं सोमं पिब । कीदृशं । प्रतरणं
> प्रवर्धनं । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः । विवक्षणं अतिशयेन स्तुत्यं मध्वः मधुनः
> सकाशादपि स्वादिष्टं स्वादुतमं ! कमेतं । यस्य पानेन मंदसानः हवींषि संभजमानस्त्वं नोऽस्सभ्यं यजमानेभ्यः यथा यथावत् फलमाकिरासि कार्त्स्न्येन

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, in due time drink this Soma, अनेहसं (*anehasaṃ*). What kind of Soma? प्रतरणं (*prataraṇaṃ*), that is, promoting growth; the root of increase with the prefix. विवक्षणं (*vivakṣaṇaṃ*), exceedingly praiseworthy; स्वादिष्टं (*svādiṣṭaṃ*), sweeter even than honey (मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)). Which one is it? That by drinking which you, rejoicing (मंदसानः (*maṃdasānaḥ*)) and enjoying the oblations, pour out fully upon us, the sacrificers, the fruit as is fitting.

### Printed p. 573

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> निक्षिससि । ददासीत्यर्थः । केभ्य इव । धृषत् शत्रुधर्षकस्त्वं त्मना आत्मना स्वयमेव
> क्षुद्रेव दीनेभ्य इव तेभ्यो यथा प्र ददासि तद्वत् । उपसर्गवशादोग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The meaning is that you give. To whom, and as to whom? You, assailer of foes (धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*)), of your own accord (त्मना (*tmanā*)) give as to the poor (क्षुद्रेव (*kṣudreva*)): as you give to them, so to us. By the force of the prefix a suitable verb of giving is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*)—you, assailer of foes
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—of your own accord
- क्षुद्रा इव प्र (*kṣudrā iva pra*)—as one gives generously to the poor and needy
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way
- मंदसानः (*maṃdasānaḥ*)—you, satisfied
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us also
- आ किरासि (*ā kirāsi*)—you give abundantly
- अनेहसं (*anehasaṃ*)—faultless
- प्रतरणं (*prataraṇaṃ*)—promoting growth
- विवक्षणं (*vivakṣaṇaṃ*)—highly praiseworthy
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—than honey
- स्वादिष्ठं (*svādiṣṭhaṃ*)—most delicious
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Soma juice
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, assailer of foes, drink this Soma juice, faultless **NOTE**, promoting growth, sweeter than honey, in such a way that you, satisfied, give to us also abundantly, as of your own accord you give generously to the poor and needy.

##### English translation
Drink the sweet Soma, Sinless, salvation-giving and leader to heaven; when you are exhilarated you become proud and like kshudra give us desired wealth.
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नः॒ स्तोम॒मुप॑ द्र॒वद्धि॑या॒नो अश्वो॒ न सोतृ॑भिः ।  
> यं ते॑ स्वधावन्त्व॒दयं॑ति धे॒नव॒ इंद्र॒ कण्वे॑षु रा॒तयः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । स्तोमं । उप । द्ववत् । हियानति । अश्वः । न । सोतृभिः ।  
> यं । ते । स्वधावन् । स्वदयंति । धेनवः । इंद्र । कण्वेषु । रातयः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र स भवान् नोऽस्मदीयैः सोतृभिः सोमाभिषवकर्तृभिरध्वयार्वादिभियृग्भिः कृतं स्तोत्रविशेषं आ अभिमुख्येन उप द्रवत् उपगच्छतु समीपं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, may you, facing us, come near (उप द्रवत् (*upa dravat*)) to the special hymn made by our pressers of Soma (सोतृभिः (*sotṛbhiḥ*)), the Adhvaryu and other priests **NOTE**, and reach it.

### Printed p. 574

> प्राप्नोतु । क इव । हियानः प्रेर्यमाणः अश्वो न आश्व इव । स यथा अभिलषितं
> देशं प्राप्नोति तद्वत् । हे स्वधावन् अन्नवन्निंद्र ते तव स्वभूतानि धेनवः तर्पकाणि
> कण्वेषु अस्मासु वर्तमानानि राशयः हविर्दानानि यं त्वां स्वदयंति स्वादयंति ।
> त्वदुदरे प्रविश्य त्वां तर्पयंतीत्यर्थः । स भवान् उप द्रवत् इति पूर्वेण
> संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like a driven horse (हियानः (*hiyānaḥ*)), who reaches the place he desires, so may you. O possessor of food (स्वधावन् (*svadhāvan*)), O Indra, the satisfying cows or the gifts of oblations (राशयः (*rāśayaḥ*) **NOTE**) that are yours and abide among us, the Kaṇvas, delight you (स्वदयंति (*svadayaṃti*)); the meaning is that, entering your belly, they satisfy you. You, such as you are, come near: this is to be connected with the earlier part.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वधावन् (*svadhāvan*)—possessor of food
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—belonging to you
- कण्वेषु (*kaṇveṣu*)—among us of the Kaṇva line
- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—cows that give milk
- रातयः (*rātayaḥ*)—oblations and the like given by us
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which you
- स्वदयंति (*svadayaṃti*)—satisfy; such a you
- हियानः (*hiyānaḥ*)—running swiftly
- अश्वः न (*aśvaḥ na*)—like a horse
- स्तोतृभिः (*stotṛbhiḥ*)—made by the praisers
- नः स्तोमं (*naḥ stomaṃ*)—towards our praises
- उप आ द्रवत् (*upa ā dravat*)—come running

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, possessor of food, the milk-giving cows belonging to you that are among us of the Kaṇva line, and the oblations and the like given by us, satisfy you. Such as you are, come running towards our praises, made by the praisers, like a swiftly running horse.

##### English translation
Indra, Lord of food, the gifts you offered to us are making the Soma sweet, the effusers are invoking you ; come to it quickly running like a horse.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒ग्रं न वी॒रं नम॒सोप॑ सेदिम॒ विभू॑ति॒मक्षि॑तावसुं ।  
> उ॒द्रीव॑ वज्रिन्नव॒तो न सिं॑च॒ते क्षरं॑तींद्र धी॒तयः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

> उग्रं । न । वीरं । नमसा । उप । सेदिम । विभूतिं । अक्षितवसुं ।  
> उद्रीऽइव । वज्रिन् । अवतः । न । सिंचते । क्षरंति । इंद्र । धीतयः ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 575

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दे इंद्र वीरं विशेषेण शत्रुभटान् प्रेरयंतं त्वां नमसा हविर्लक्षणेन्नान्नेन सह । यद्वा नमसा प्रह्वीभावेन सह उप सेदिम शरणं प्राप्पुनो
> वयं । कमिव । उग्रं न उद्धूर्णबलमिव । तं यथा केचन दीनाः शरणं प्राप्पुवंति तद्वत् । कीदृशं त्वां । विभूतिं विविधैश्वर्योपेतं । अथवा विविधभवनस्वभावं ।
> इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयत इति श्रुतेः । रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो
> बभूव इति श्रुत्यंतरात् । अक्षितवसुं आक्षेणधनं । किंच हे वज्रिन् वज्रवन्निंद्र
> सिंचते स्वर्गादिफलसेक्रे शुभ्यं त्वदर्थं धीतयः अस्मदंगुलयः क्षरंति स्रवंति
> सोमरसं । क इव, उद्रीव । उदकान् ( ? उदकवान्) अवतो न कूप इव । स
> यथा सस्यादिसेक्रे जलं क्षरति तद्वत् । अत्र इवशब्दोऽनर्थकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, we approach you, the hero who drives the enemy warriors apart, with a salutation, that is, with an offering of food, or else with humble bowing, and take refuge, as helpless people go for refuge to one of exceeding strength. You are Vibhūti, possessed of manifold lordship, or else of the nature of becoming manifold; he supports this with the śruti that Indra goes about in many forms through his magic powers, and with another śruti that he became a counterpart to each form. Akṣitavasu is one whose wealth does not decay. Further, O wielder of the thunderbolt, our fingers pour the Soma juice for you, for the sprinkling that yields heaven and the other fruits, as water flows from a well when it is used for watering plants and the like. The word *iva* here has no meaning of its own. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वीरं (*vīraṃ*)—the valiant one
- विभूतिं (*vibhūtiṃ*)—the possessor of lordship
- अक्षितवसुं (*akṣitavasuṃ*)—the one with imperishable wealth, Indra
- उग्रं न (*ugraṃ na*)—as the powerless approach one of exceeding strength with humility
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with salutation (with humility)
- उप सेदिम (*upa sedima*)—approaching, we take refuge
- वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)—O wielder of the thunderbolt
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अवतः (*avataḥ*)—a well (a spring)
- उद्री इव (*udrī iva*)—as it makes water well up and flow
- धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—our fingers
- सिंचते (*siṃcate*)—for you, the giver of the fruit of heaven and the like
- क्षरंति (*kṣaraṃti*)—press out the Soma and make it flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the powerless approach one of exceeding strength with humility, so we approach Indra, the valiant, the possessor of lordship, the owner of imperishable wealth, with salutation and humility, and take refuge in him. O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, as a spring makes water well up and flow, so our fingers press out the Soma and make it flow towards you, the giver of the fruit of heaven and the like.

##### English translation
We shall now go to Indra with salute he is covered with Vibhuti, Lord of inexhaustible wealth ; ferocious hero, wielder of thunder-bolt as a gushing fountain rushes forth so do our prayers spring forth.

> अतो॑ नो य॒ज्ञमा॒शुभि॑र्महेमत उ॒ग्र उ॒ग्रेभि॒रा  ॑
> गहि ॥ ७ ॥

> यत् । ह । नूनं । यत् । वा । यज्ञे । यत् । वा । पृथिव्यां । अधि ।  
> अतः । नः । यज्ञं । आशुभिः । महेमते । उग्रः । उग्रेभिः । आ । गहि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे महेमते पूजासक्तबुद्धे इंद्र यद्ध यत्र क्वचित् स्थानविशेषे नूनं
> निश्चितं वर्तसे । यत् यत्र वा यज्ञे अध्वरे वर्तसे । यत् यत्र वा पृथिव्यां
> अधि अधिकं वर्तसे । अतः अस्मात्स्थानविशेषात् उग्रः उद्धूर्णबलत्वं उग्रेभिः
> उद्धूर्णबलैः आशुभिः शीघ्रगामिभिरश्वैः नोऽस्माकं यज्ञं आ गहि आगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, of reverent mind, wherever you may be at present, whether in some particular place, or at a sacrifice, or somewhere over the earth, from that place come to our sacrifice, you who are strong, with strong and swift-going horses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महेमते (*mahemate*)—O Indra, of reverent mind
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—you who are of exceeding strength
- यत् ह (*yat ha*)—wherever you may be
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—surely
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—to the place of sacrifice
- आशुभिः (*āśubhiḥ*)—swift-going
- उग्रेभिः (*ugrebhiḥ*)—and very strong horses
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—or, if
- यज्ञे (*yajñe*)—you are at the sacrifice of others
- पृथिव्यां अधि (*pṛthivyāṃ adhi*)—in whatever other place on the earth
- आतः (*ātaḥ*)—from there

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, of reverent mind, being of exceeding strength, wherever you may be, graciously come to our place of sacrifice with swift and very strong horses. Whether you are at the sacrifice of others, or in any other place on the earth, come from there towards our sacrifice.

##### English translation
Wherever you may be now, ferocious, noble Indra, whether in ther ite or in the earth, do come from there to this our rite with speedy and ferocious horses.

> तीघ्रगामिनश्च । येभिः यैरश्वैः मनुषः मनोः अपत्यं अपतनहेतुं यजमानं
> परीयसे सर्वत आगच्छसि येभिः यैश्चाश्वैः विश्वं स्वः सर्वं स्वर्लोकं दृशे
> व्रष्टुमिच्छसि शैरा गहि इति पूर्वेणान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, those horses of yours, the Haris, are as winds, moving swiftly together. They throw down the enemies and are swift-going. With these horses you come all round to the sacrificer, the offspring of Manu, who is the cause of no falling, and with them you wish to see the whole heaven. The connection is with the preceding verse: come with them. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—belonging to you
- ये (*ye*)—which
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—horses called Hari
- अजिरासः (*ajirāsaḥ*)—throwing down enemies
- आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)—swift-going
- वाता इव (*vātā iva*)—like winds
- प्रसक्षिणः (*prasakṣiṇaḥ*)—of exceeding movement
- येभिः (*yebhiḥ*)—with which horses
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—of Manu
- अपत्यं (*apatyaṃ*)—to the sacrificer, who is as his son
- परिईयसे (*pariīyase*)—you go
- येभिः (*yebhiḥ*)—with which horses
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—the whole
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—heaven
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—you wish to see (come to our sacrifice with such horses)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the horses called Hari that belong to you throw down enemies, are swift-going, and move exceedingly like winds. With whichever horses you wish to see the whole heaven, with such horses come to our sacrifice.

##### English translation
Your horses named Hari have the speed of winds and are vanquishers of enemies, with that help you go to men and go to the earth overgrown with many things born.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र धने निमित्तभूते सति यथा येन प्रकारेण
> मेध्यातिथिं एतन्नामकऋषिं प्रावः प्रकर्षेण रक्षितवानसि यथा येन च प्रकारेण
> नीपातिथिं एतन्नामानमृषिं प्रावः एतावतः इयदेव ते तव स्वभूतं गोमतः
> गवाश्वाद्युपेतं सुम्मस्य सुखं ईमहे याचामहे वयं कण्वाः । सर्वत्र
> कर्मणि षष्ठ्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Maghavan, the wealthy Indra, as you protected well the seer named Medhyātithi, and as you protected the seer named Nīpātithi, when wealth was the occasion, so we, the Kaṇvas, ask of you this much of your own: happiness together with cattle. In every such case the genitive stands in the sense of the object.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- धने (*dhane*)—for the sake of wealth
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- मेधातिथिं (*medhātithiṃ*)—the seer named Medhātithi
- प्रावः (*prāvaḥ*)—you protected
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- नीपातिथिं (*nīpātithiṃ*)—the seer named Nīpātithi, you protected
- एतावतः (*etāvataḥ*)—of the same kind
- गोमतः (*gomataḥ*)—and accompanied by cattle
- सुम्मस्य (*summasya*)—happiness
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, as you protected the seer named Medhātithi and the seer named Nīpātithi by giving them wealth when they strove for wealth, in the same manner we ask of you happiness, in the form of wealth, accompanied by cattle.

##### English translation
Give us wealth, cattle, we solicit of you Maghavan, because you did help Medhatithi and Nipatithi in their obtaining of wealth.

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy one

O wealthy Indra, as you gave wealth accompanied by cattle and made of gold to the seer Kaṇva and to the kings Trasadasyu, Pakva, Daśavraja, Gośarya and Ṛjiśvan, so we ask you to give to us also. **NOTE**

## Sūkta 50 (Maṇḍala 8)

**Introduction**

The fiftieth sūkta (Vālakhilya sūkta 2). प्र सु श्रुतं इति दशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं काण्वस्य पुष्टिगोरार्षमैंद्रं । अनुक्रम्यते च—प्र सु श्रुतं पुष्टिगुः इति । कण्वस्य पुत्रः पुष्टिगुः ऋषिः । इंद्रो देवता । आयुजां बृहती छंदः । युजां सतो बृहती छंदः । विनियोगः सूत्रादवगंतव्यः ॥ (*pra su śrutaṃ iti daśarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktaṃ kāṇvasya puṣṭigorārṣamaiṃdraṃ | anukramyate ca—pra su śrutaṃ puṣṭiguḥ iti | kaṇvasya putraḥ puṣṭiguḥ ṛṣiḥ | iṃdro devatā | āyujāṃ bṛhatī chaṃdaḥ | yujāṃ sato bṛhatī chaṃdaḥ | viniyogaḥ sūtrādavagaṃtavyaḥ ‖*)

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning *pra su śrutam* is the second among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has ten Ṛks. Its seer is Puṣṭigu Kāṇva. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: *pra su śrutam puṣṭiguḥ*. Indra is the deity. The seer is Puṣṭigu, the son of Kaṇva. The odd-numbered Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Bṛhatī metre; the even-numbered Ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra. **NOTE**

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 50; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 16, 17. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Puṣṭiguḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: Indraḥ. Metre: Prāgātha (odd Ṛks Bṛhatī, even Ṛks Satobṛhatī).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र सु श्रु॒तं सु॒राध॑स॒मर्चा॑ श॒क्रम॒भिष्ट॑ये ।  
> यः सु॑न्व॒ते स्तु॑व॒ते काम्यं॒ वसु॑ स॒हस्रे॑णेव॒ मंह॑ते ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 581

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । सु । श्रुतं । सुराधसं । अर्च । शक्रं । अभिष्टये ।  
> यः । सुन्वते । स्तुवते । काम्यं । वसु । सहस्रेण इव । मंहते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरात्मानं ब्रूते । हे पुष्टिगो त्वं अभिष्टये अभिलषितसिद्धये तं
> शक्रं सर्वकर्मसु शक्तमिंद्रं सु सुष्टु यथा तथा प्र अर्च प्रकर्षण पूजय ।
> कीदृशं । श्रुतं विख्यातं सुराधसं शोभनधनोपेतं । तं कं । य इंद्रः सुन्वते
> सोमाभिषवं कुर्वते स्तुवते स्तुतिं कुर्वते यजमानाय काम्यं कामिनं
> (? कमनीयं) वसु धनं सहस्रेणेव असंख्यातमेव मंहते ददाति तं । मंहतिर्दानार्थः । दानकर्मसु तत्पारात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: the seer addresses himself. O Puṣṭigu, for the accomplishment of what you desire, worship well that Śakra, Indra, who is capable in all rites. He is renowned and possessed of splendid wealth; he is the one who gives to the sacrificer who presses the Soma and who praises him the desired wealth, as it were by thousands, that is, without count. The root *maṃh* has the sense of giving, since it is listed among the verbs of giving. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—to the one who presses the Soma
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—to the one who offers praise
- काम्यं (*kāmyaṃ*)—desired
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- सहस्रेणेव (*sahasreṇeva*)—in thousands
- मंहते (*maṃhate*)—gives, such a one
- श्रुतं (*śrutaṃ*)—the renowned
- सुराधसं (*surādhasaṃ*)—the possessor of excellent wealth
- शक्रं (*śakraṃ*)—Indra
- अभिष्टये (*abhiṣṭaye*)—for the fulfilment of your wish
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O seer, worship exceedingly, for the fulfilment of your wish, that renowned Indra, possessor of excellent wealth, who gives desired wealth in thousands to one who presses the Soma and offers it, and to one who offers praise.

##### English translation
Desiring wealth I worship Shakra, Lord of precious wealth, he gives, wealth in thousands to the worshipper and effuser.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तानी॑का हे॒तयो॑ अस्य दु॒ष्टरा॒ इंद्र॑स्य स॒मिषो॑ म॒हीः ।  
> गि॒रिर्न भु॒ज्मा म॒घव॑त्सु पिन्वते॒ यदीं॑ सु॒ता अमं॑दिषुः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 582

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतऽनीकाः । हेतयः । अस्य । दुस्तराः । इंद्रस्य । संइषः । महीर् ।  
> गिरिः । न । भुज्मा । मघवत्सु । पिन्वते । यत् । ईं । सुताः । अमंदिषुः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुता अभिषुताः सोमा यद्यदा ईमेनमिंद्रं अमंदिषुः आमादयन्
> तदा अस्येंद्रस्य हेतॆयः हननसाधनान्यायुधानि मघवत्सु हविर्लक्षणधनवत्सु
> यजमानेषु पिन्नते । तदीयशत्रुधनानि तेषु समर्प्य तान् प्रीणयंतीत्यर्थः । क
> इव । भुज्मा गिरिर्न पालको मेघ इव । स यथा भुवि जलानि समर्प्य तां प्रीणयति
> तद्वत् । शत्रुधनाहरणं तु “शत्र्युतामा भरा भोजनानि” (ऋ. सं. ५-४-५)
> इत्यादिश्रुतिप्रसिद्धं । कीदृश्यो हेतॆयः । शतानीकाः । शतमपरिमितानि अनीकानि
> मुखानि यासां ताः । सर्वतोमुखा इत्यर्थः । अत एव दुस्तरा दुर्निनार्याः ।
> समिषः सम्यक् इट् अन्नं याभ्यस्ताः । महीः महत्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: when the pressed Soma juices exhilarate this Indra, then his weapons, the instruments of killing, flow to the sacrificers who have wealth in the form of oblations; that is, he bestows on them the wealth of their enemies and so gratifies them, as a cloud, the protector, pours waters on the earth and gratifies it. The taking away of enemies' wealth is well known from the śruti beginning शत्र्युतामा भरा भोजनानि (*śatryutāmā bharā bhojanāni*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-4-5). Such are the weapons: *śatānīkāḥ*, with hundreds, that is, countless, faces, meaning facing in every direction, and therefore hard to resist; *samiṣaḥ*, having ample food; *mahīḥ*, great. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—the pressed Soma juices
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Indra
- अमुंदिषुः (*amuṃdiṣuḥ*)—exhilarate, then
- भुज्मा (*bhujmā*)—protecting
- गिरिः न (*giriḥ na*)—as a cloud fills the earth with water and gratifies it
- अस्य इंद्रस्य (*asya iṃdrasya*)—of this Indra
- शतानीताः (*śatānītāḥ*)—having hundreds of faces
- दुस्तराः (*dustarāḥ*)—not to be overcome by the resistance of enemies
- समिषः (*samiṣaḥ*)—provided with full food
- महीः (*mahīḥ*)—of great form
- हेतयः (*hetayaḥ*)—the weapons
- मघवत्तु (*maghavattu*)—among the sacrificers who have wealth in the form of oblations
- पिन्वते (*pinvate*)—fill with the enemy's wealth and gratify

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the pressed Soma juices bring joy to Indra, then, as a cloud, the protector of the world, pours rain and fills the earth, so the weapons of this Indra, with hundreds of faces, not to be overcome by the resistance of enemies, provided with full food and of great form, fill the sacrificers who have wealth in the form of oblations with the enemy's wealth and gratify them.

##### English translation
Of immeasurable Indra, your weapons are hundreds and food abundant when the effused Soma exhilarates him then being food-giver lika a mountain delights the wealthy.

> उपगम्य आ धायि कार्त्स्यन सफलीकृतः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अपो न । ता यथा
> स्नानपानादिना सफलीक्रियंते तद्वत् । अपरो दृष्टांतः । दुघा इव । हविर्दुघा
> धेनवो यथा सांनाय्यसेवनादिना सफलीक्रियंते तद्वत् सोमपानादिना यज्ञः
> सफलीकृत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, when the pressed Soma juices, directing themselves towards you, the beloved, exhilarate you, then, O Vasu, the one who causes to dwell, you have made my sacrifice, coming to it, wholly fruitful for me, who have given the oblation. The first illustration is waters: as waters are made fruitful by bathing, drinking and the like. The second illustration is milch cows: as cows that yield the oblation are made fruitful by the use of the *sāṃnāyya* and so on; so the sacrifice is made fruitful by the drinking of the Soma and the rest. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसो (*vaso*)—O Indra, giver of dwelling
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—the Soma juices
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—the beloved
- ईं अभि (*īṃ abhi*)—coming towards you
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अमंदिषुः (*amaṃdiṣuḥ*)—they gratify, then
- आपः न (*āpaḥ na*)—like waters fit for bathing and the like
- दुघा इव (*dughā iva*)—like cows that give milk and the like
- मे सवनं (*me savanaṃ*)—my sacrifice
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—me, who offer the oblation
- उप (*upa*)—approaching
- आ धायि (*ā dhāyi*)—makes my purpose fruitful

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of dwelling, when the pressed Soma juices approach you, the beloved of the world, and gratify you, then my sacrifice, approaching me who offer the oblation, makes my purpose fruitful, as waters fit for bathing and drinking, and as cows that give milk and the like.

### Printed p. 584

##### English translation
When the effused Soma has exhilarated Indra the giver of dwellings, I offer you Soma like water—you are like the milch cow to your worshipper.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ने॒हसं॑ वो॒ हव॑मानमू॒तये॒ मध्वः॑ क्षरंति धी॒तयः॑ ।  
> आ त्वा॑ वसो॒ हव॑मानास॒ इंद॑व॒ उप॑ स्तो॒त्रेषु॑ दधिरे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनेहसं । वः । हवमानं । ऊतये । मध्वः । क्षरंति । धीतयः ।  
> आ । त्वा । वसो इति । हवमानासः । इंदवः । उप । स्तोत्रेषु । दधिरे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋत्विजः वः युष्मत्संबंधिन्यः धीतयोऽंगुलयः ऊतये रक्षार्थं
> हवमानं स्तूयमानमिंद्रमुद्दिश्य मध्वः मधुररसं सोमं क्षरंति । कीदृशं ।
> अनेहसं । न आहन्यत इत्यनेहः तं । शत्रुभिरनभिभाव्यमित्यर्थः । हे वसो वासयितरिंद्र हवमानासः स्तूयमानाः इंदवः सोमाः स्तोत्रेषु निमित्तेषु त्वा त्वां
> उप समीपे आ दधिरे आखिमुख्येन स्थापितवंतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O priests, your fingers pour out the sweet Soma juice for protection, directed to Indra who is being praised. Indra is *anehas*, one who is not struck, that is, not to be overcome by enemies. O Vasu, you who cause to dwell, the praised Soma juices place themselves near you at the praises, taking the first place. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—fingers
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for your protection
- हवमानं (*havamānaṃ*)—directed to the venerable Indra
- आनेहसं (*ānehasaṃ*)—faultless
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—and sweet Soma juice
- क्षरंति (*kṣaraṃti*)—press out
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Indra, giver of dwelling
- हवमानासः (*havamānāsaḥ*)—worthy of praise
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—the Soma juices
- स्तोत्रेषु (*stotreṣu*)—at the times of praise
- त्वा उप (*tvā upa*)—approaching you
- आ दधिरे (*ā dadhire*)—are established in you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, your fingers press out, for your protection, faultless and sweet Soma juice directed to the venerable Indra. O Indra, giver of dwelling, the Soma juices worthy of praise are established in you at the time of praise, after establishing you.

### Printed p. 585

##### English translation
Worshippers, for your protection all righteous actions are dropping sweets in invocation of Indra. Giver of dwelling, Soma being effused goes to you.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नः॒ सोमे॑ स्वध्व॒र इ॑या॒नो अत्यो॒ न तो॑शते ।  
> यं ते॑ स्वदाव॒न्त्वदं॑ति गू॒र्तयः॑ पौ॒रे छं॑दयसे॒ हवं॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । सोमे । सुअध्वरे । इयानः । अत्यः । न । तोशते ।  
> यं । ते । स्वदावन् । स्वदंति । गूर्तयः । पौरे । छंदयसे । हवं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्माकं यजमानानां संबंधिनि स्वध्वरे शोभनयज्ञे सोमे सोमपाने निमित्तभूते सति अत्यो न सततगमनशीलोऽश्व इव इयानः गच्छन्निंद्रः आ
> तोशते अस्मच्छत्रून् हिनस्ति । तोशतिर्वधकर्मा । नितोषते निबर्हयति इति
> वधकर्मसु पाठात् । इंद्रं प्रत्यक्षीकृत्य ब्रूते । हे स्वदावन् आस्वादनकुशलेंद्र
> ते तव स्वभूताः गूर्तयः उद्यताः स्तुतयः यं त्वां स्वदंति आत्मानमास्वादयंति
> स त्वं पौरे पुरजनसमूहे हवमात्मनः स्तुतिं छंदयसे कामयसे । यत्विग्भिः
> स्वस्तुतिः कर्त व्येत्यभिलषसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: when, at our good sacrifice, the Soma-drinking has come about, Indra, going like a horse that is ever on the move, strikes our enemies. The root *toś* has the sense of killing, since it is read among the verbs of killing, with the form *nitoṣate* meaning he destroys. Addressing Indra directly he says: O Svadāvan, skilled in tasting, the raised praises that belong to you gratify you, who are such; you desire, among the multitude of townspeople, the invocation, that is, praise of yourself; the meaning is that you wish that the priests should offer you praise. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- स्वध्वरे (*svadhvare*)—in the good place of sacrifice
- सोमे (*some*)—on account of the drinking of Soma
- अत्यः न (*atyaḥ na*)—like an excellent horse
- इयानः (*iyānaḥ*)—Indra, who goes about
- आ तोशते (*ā tośate*)—strikes down and destroys the enemies
- स्वदावन् (*svadāvan*)—O Indra, skilled in tasting
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which you
- ते (*te*)—directed to you
- गूर्तयः (*gūrtayaḥ*)—the praises
- स्वदंति (*svadaṃti*)—gratify, such a one
- पौरे (*paure*)—among the townspeople, the priests and others
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the prayer in the form of praise
- छंदयसे (*chaṃdayase*)—you desire

### Printed p. 586

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At our good place of sacrifice, on account of the drinking of Soma, Indra, who goes about like an excellent horse, strikes down and destroys the enemies. O Indra, skilled in tasting, you whom the praises directed to you gratify, you desire among the townspeople, the priests and others, the prayer in the form of praise.

##### English translation
Indra being invoked to our good rite is going like a horse ; relishing Indra, your worshippers are sweetening this Soma. Honour invocation of the Sons of Puru.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वी॒रमु॒ग्रं विवि॑चं धन॒स्पृतं॒ विभू॑तिं॒ राध॑सो म॒हः ।  
> उ॒द्रीव॑ वज्रिन्नव॒तो व॑सुत्व॒ना सदा॑ सीपेथ दा॒शुषे॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वीरं । उग्रं । विविचं । धन्वस्पृतं । विभूतिं । राधसः । महः ।  
> उद्रीऽइव । वज्रिन् । अवतः । वसुत्वना । सदा । पीपेथ । दाशुषे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वीरं विशेषेण शत्रुणां प्रेरयितारं महः महत् राधसः राधो
> धनं । कर्मणि षष्ठ्य । प्र प्रार्थये याचामि । उपसर्गवशादोग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । कीदृशं त्वां । उग्रमुद्गूर्णबलं विविचं पुण्यापुण्ययोर्निवेक्तारं
> धनस्पृतं धनदातारं विभूतिं विविध्यॆश्वर्योर्वेतान् ( ? पेतं) यतः हे वज्रन्
> वज्रवन्निंद्र त्वं दाशुषे हविषां दातारं । कर्मणि चतुर्थी । सदा सर्वदा
> वसुत्वना धनदानेन पीपेथ आप्याययसि । वर्धयसीत्यर्थः । क इव । उद्रीव अवतः
> उदकवान् कूप इव । स यथा उदकदानेन जगदाप्याययति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, I ask for, I beg, great wealth from you, the hero, who drives the enemies apart; the genitive of *rādhasaḥ* stands in the sense of the object, and the verb of begging is supplied by force of the prefix. You are fierce, of mighty strength; *vivica*, one who discriminates between merit and demerit; *dhanaspṛt*, the giver of wealth; *vibhūti*, possessed of manifold lordship. Since, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you ever make the giver of oblations thrive with gifts of wealth, as a well full of water gladdens the world by giving water, I ask thus; the dative stands in the sense of the object. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वीरं (*vīraṃ*)—the valiant one
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—the one of exceeding strength
- विविचं (*vivicaṃ*)—the one who knows the difference between merit and demerit
- धनस्पृतं (*dhanaspṛtaṃ*)—the giver of wealth
- विभूतिं (*vibhūtiṃ*)—the one possessed of lordship

### Printed p. 587

- इंद्रनिंद (*iṃdraniṃda*)—from Indra
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)—wealth
- प्र (*pra*)—I ask
- वज्रैन् (*vajrain*)—O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अवतः (*avataḥ*)—a spring
- उद्री इव (*udrī iva*)—as it makes water flow
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- वसुत्वना (*vasutvanā*)—by the gift of wealth
- पीपेथ (*pīpetha*)—you bring satisfaction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I ask great wealth from Indra, the valiant, the one of exceeding strength, the one who knows the difference between merit and demerit, the giver of wealth, the one possessed of lordship. O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, as a spring makes water flow and gives satisfaction to people, so you always bring satisfaction, by the gift of wealth, to the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

##### English translation
We worship Indra, hero, ferocious, speedy, pleasing by gifts of wealth and having abundance of Vibhuti, wielder of thunder-bolt, like a well do you with spreading wealth drink Soma like water for the wel-being of your worshipper.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद्ध॑ नू॒नं प॑रा॒वति॒ यद्वा॑ पृथि॒व्यां दि॒वि ।  
> यु॒जा॒न इं॑द्र॒ हरि॑भिर्महेमत ऋ॒ष्व ऋ॒ष्वेभि॒रा ग॑हि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । ह । नूनं । परावति । यत् । वा । पृथिव्यां । दिवि ।  
> युजानः । इंद्र । हरिभिः । महेमते । ऋष्ट्वः । ऋष्टेभिः । आ । गहि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे महेमते पूजासक्तबुद्धे इंद्र यद्ध यत्र क्वचित् परावति दूरदेशे
> नूनं निश्चितं वर्तसे । यद्वा यत्र वा पृथिव्यां भुवि दिवि द्युलोके वा वर्तसे ।
> अस्मात् स्थानविशेषात् ऋष्टैः महद्भिः हरिभिः एतत्संज्ञकैरश्वैः रथं युजानः
> युक्तं कुर्वाणः ऋष्टैः महांस्वमा गहि आगच्छास्मद्यज्ञं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, of reverent mind, wherever you may be, whether in a far place, or on the earth, or in the heaven, from that particular place come to our sacrifice, yoking your chariot with great horses, those named Hari, and being yoked with them. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महेमते (*mahemate*)—O Indra, most venerable
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- यद्ध (*yaddha*)—if perhaps
- परावति (*parāvati*)—in a very distant place
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the heavenly world
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—or

- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—with your horses

O most venerable Indra, if at this time you are in the very distant heavenly world, or on the earth, from that place come to our sacrifice, you the venerable, joined with your horses of great form.

##### English translation
Loving, noble Indra whether you be away or in this earth or in the heaven come harnessing the loving horses, in your chariot.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये हरयोऽश्वाः ते तव स्वभूताः रथिरासः रथार्हाः अस्त्रिधः । स्त्रिधो
> हिंसकाः शत्रवः । तद्रहिताः संति । येभिर्यैरश्वैः मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य
> संबंधिनं दस्युमुपक्षपयितारं शत्रुं निः निरंतरं निघोषयः नितरामाक्रोशयसि । अश्वशफप्रहारैस्तं चूर्णयन् विशब्दितं करोषीत्यर्थः । किंच येभिर्यै-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: those horses of yours, the Haris, are fit for the chariot and are *astridhaḥ*, that is, free from *stridhaḥ*, the hostile enemies. With which horses you make the *dasyu*, the destroying enemy of the sacrificer, cry out continually, crushing him with blows of the horses' hooves and making him sound aloud. Further, the horses with which you go about the heavenly world,

### Printed p. 589

> रश्वैः स्वः स्वर्लोकं परीयसे परितो गच्छसि ! ते हरयो वातस्य वायोः ओजः
> बलं पिप्रति पूरयंति । वायोः सामर्थ्यमात्मनि संपादयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

- नि (*ni*)—always

- एप्रति (*eprati*)—fill themselves with

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, your horses, fit for an excellent chariot, are free from hostile enemies. With the help of which horses you always cause the hostile enemy of the performer of the sacrifice to sound a sound of destruction, and with which horses you move about heaven everywhere, those horses fill themselves with the strength of the wind.

##### English translation
Your horses carrying chariot are envyless and competing the speed of wind. To their help you have killed the Dasyus, you have made them famous and all things known.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसो वासयितः हे शूर विक्रांतेंद्र यथा येन प्रकारेण कृत्वे
> कर्तव्ये धने निमित्ते सति एतशं एतन्नामानमृषिं प्रावः प्रकर्षेण रक्षितवानसि ।
> किंच यथा येन प्रकारेण दशव्रजे दशसंख्याकशत्रुसमूहे वशं एतस्संज्य कमृषिं
> प्रावः प्रकर्षेण रक्षितवानसि । एतावतः एतावत्पराक्रमोपेतं ते त्वां नव्यसः
> स्तुत्यं विद्याम जानीमो वयं . सर्वत्र कर्मणि षष्ठि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O Vasu, O hero, valiant Indra, in what manner, when wealth was to be won, you protected well the seer named Etaśa, and in what manner you protected the seer named Vaśa among the host of ten enemies, so we know you, who are possessed of so great valour, as worthy of praise. In every such case the genitive stands in the sense of the object. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसो (*vaso*)—O giver of dwelling
- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- कृत्वे (*kṛtve*)—for the accomplishment of a task
- धने (*dhane*)—on account of wealth
- एतशं (*etaśaṃ*)—the seer
- प्रावः (*prāvaḥ*)—you protected
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- दशव्रजे (*daśavraje*)—among the host of enemies
- वशं (*vaśaṃ*)—the seer named Vaśa, you protected
- एतावतः (*etāvataḥ*)—of such greatness
- नव्यसः (*navyasaḥ*)—and venerable
- विद्याम (*vidyāma*)—we know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of dwelling, valiant, in what manner you protected the seer named Etaśa on account of wealth for the accomplishment of a task, and in what manner you protected the seer named Vaśa among the host of ten enemies, so we know the greatness of you who are of such greatness and venerable.

##### English translation
Hero, keeper of dwellings, Indra we know of so much your wealth for which you did protect Yetasha and Vashaya with Dasavraja.

> हे अद्रिवः वज्रिवन् (?) इंद्र मेधे यज्ञे यथा येन प्रकारेण कण्णे
> एतन्नामके ऋषौ निमित्ते हरिश्रियं । हरिः जगत्पापहर्त्री हरितवर्णा वा श्रीः
> जललक्ष्मीर्यस्य तादृशं । गोत्रं मेघं असिसासः दत्तवानसि । ईदृशे कण्णे अध्वरे ।
> ध्वरतिर्हिंसाकर्मा ! तद्रहिते दीर्घनीथे दीर्घं स्वर्लोकपर्यंतं नीथं हविः
> प्रापणं यस्य तथाभूते । पुनः कीदृशे । दमूनसि दानमनसि उदारे । यथा चॆ
> गोशर्ये एतन्नामके ऋषौ मेघं दत्तवानसि तथा मयि पुष्टिगौ हरिश्रियं
> गोत्रं देहि । यथा तयोरनुग्रहदृष्ट्या मेघवृष्टिं कृतवानसि तथा मय्यपि
> कृपादृष्ट्या अभिलषितवृष्टिं कुर्वित्यभिप्रायः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: O wielder of the stone, Indra, at the sacrifice, in the manner that you gave a cloud to the seer named Kaṇva, *haritriyam*, whose glory is the water-wealth that takes away the sins of the world, or whose glory is green; at this Kaṇva's sacrifice, free from violence (the root *dhvar* has the sense of harming), where the means of carrying the oblation extends far, up to the heavenly world, and who is generous; and as you gave a cloud to the seer named Gośarya, so give to me, Puṣṭigu, a cloud of such glory. The intention is: as you sent rain for those two out of favour, so also for me, out of gracious regard, send the rain that I desire. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O wielder of the thunderbolt
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra
- दीर्घनीथे (*dīrghanīthe*)—which carries the oblation up to heaven
- आध्वरे (*ādhvare*)—and is free from violence
- मेधे (*medhe*)—at the sacrifice
- दमूनसि (*damūnasi*)—for the generous
- कण्णी (*kaṇṇī*)—Kaṇva
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- हरिश्रियं (*hariśriyaṃ*)—provided with the water-wealth that takes away sin
- गोत्रं (*gotraṃ*)—a cloud
- असिषासः (*asiṣāsaḥ*)—you provided
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- गोशर्यॆ (*gośaryè*)—to Gośarya you provided (in the same manner)
- मयि (*mayi*)—provide for me also

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, as you provided, at the sacrifice that carries the oblation up to heaven and is free from violence, for the generous Kaṇva a cloud provided with water-wealth that takes away the heat, and poured rain, and as you provided for Gośarya also, in the same manner provide for me and bring satisfaction. **NOTE**

##### English translation
Maghavan wielder of thunder-bolt do protect us as you did protect in secret rite, Kanwa, Gosharya and Dirghanith.

## Sūkta 51 (Maṇḍala 8)

**Introduction**

The fifty-first sūkta (Vālakhilya sūkta 3). यथा मनौ सांवरणौ इति दशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं काण्वस्य श्रुष्टिगोरार्षमैंद्रं । अनुक्रांतं च । यथा मनौ श्रुष्टिगुः इति । आयुजां बृहती छंदः । युजां सतोबृहती छंदः । विनियोगः सूत्रादवगंतव्यः ॥ (*yathā manau sāṃvaraṇau iti daśarcaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sūktaṃ kāṇvasya śruṣṭigorārṣamaiṃdraṃ | anukrāṃtaṃ ca | yathā manau śruṣṭiguḥ iti | āyujāṃ bṛhatī chaṃdaḥ | yujāṃ satobṛhatī chaṃdaḥ | viniyogaḥ sūtrādavagaṃtavyaḥ ‖*)

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning *yathā manau sāṃvaraṇau* is the third among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has ten Ṛks. Its seer is Śruṣṭigu Kāṇva; Indra is the deity. The odd-numbered Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Bṛhatī metre; the even-numbered Ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: *yathā manau śruṣṭiguḥ*. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra. **NOTE**

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 51; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 18, 19. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Śruṣṭiguḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: Indraḥ. Metre: Prāgātha (odd Ṛks Bṛhatī, even Ṛks Satobṛhatī).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॒ मनौ॒ सांव॑रणौ॒ सोम॑मिं॒द्रापि॑बः सु॒तं ।  
> नीपा॑तिथौ मघव॒न्मेध्या॑तिथौ॒ पुष्टि॑गौ॒ श्रुष्टि॑गौ॒ सचा॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । मनौ । सांवरणौ । सोमं । इंद्र । आपिबः । सुतं ।  
> नीप अतिथौ । मघवन् । मेध्य अतिथौ । पुष्टिगौ । शुष्टिगौ । सचा ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 593

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यथा येन प्रकारेण सांवरणौ संवरणस्य पुत्रे मनौ वर्तमानं
> सुतमभिषुतं सोममपिबः । पीतवानसि । तथा हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र नीपातिथौ ।
> नयति हनिर्देवान् पाति रक्षति यजमानं चेति नीपः । शादृशोऽतिथिर्यस्य तस्मिन् ।
> एतेष्टके ऋषौ मेध्यातिथौ । मेध्यः यज्ञार्हः अतिथिर्यस्य तादृशे एतन्नामके
> ऋषौ पुष्टिगौ । पुष्टिः कुटुंबपोषिका गौर्यस्य तादृशे ऋषौ । क्तिच्‌क्तौ च
> संज्ञायां इति पुषिधातो कर्तरि क्तिज् । श्रुष्टिगौ । श्रुष्टिः शीघ्रव्यापिनी गौर्यस्य
> तादृशे मयि च । श्रुष्टिति क्षिप्रनाम आशु अष्टि इति निरुक्तमत्रानुसंधेयं ।
> एतेश्वास्यासु वर्तमानमभिषुतं सोमं सजा सहैव पिबेति शेषः । इह सचापदेन
> युगपदनेकरूपधारणशक्तिः सूच्यते । संभवति च सा । इंद्रो मायाभिः
> पुरुरूप ईयते इत्यादिश्रुतेः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, in the manner in which you drank the pressed Soma offered to Manu, the son of Saṃvaraṇa, so, O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, drink it with Nīpātithi, Medhyātithi, Puṣṭigu and Śruṣṭigu. Nīpa is explained as one who leads the oblation to the gods and protects the sacrificer; the one who has such a guest is Nīpātithi. Medhyātithi is a seer of that name, whose guest is fit for sacrifice. Puṣṭigu is a seer whose cow nourishes the family; the formation is by the suffix क्तिच्‌क्तौ च संज्ञायां (*kticktau ca saṃjñāyāṃ*) added to the root पुषि (*puṣi*) in the agent sense. Śruṣṭigu is one whose cow quickly pervades; the word श्रुष्टि (*śruṣṭi*) is the name for "swift", from आशु अष्टि (*āśu aṣṭi*), as the Nirukta is to be consulted here; it also applies to the speaker. The word सजा (*sajā*) means "together": drink the pressed Soma standing in these (seers) together with them, which is the supplied remainder. By the word सचा (*sacā*) the power to assume many forms at once is indicated, and that is possible for Indra, as the Śruti says इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते (*iṃdro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate*) and so on.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- सांवरणौ (*sāṃvaraṇau*)—in the son of Saṃvaraṇa
- मनौ (*manau*)—in Manu
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- आपिबः (*āpibaḥ*)—you drank, in the same way
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- नीपातिथौ (*nīpātithau*)—in the seer called Nipātithi **NOTE**
- मेध्यातिथौ (*medhyātithau*)—in the seer called Medhyātithi
- पुष्टिगौ (*puṣṭigau*)—in the seer called Puṣṭigu
- श्रुष्टिगौ (*śruṣṭigau*)—in the seer called Śruṣṭigu
- सचा (*sacā*)—drink together, united

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in the manner in which you drank the pressed Soma offered to Manu, the son of Saṃvaraṇa, in the same way, O wealthy Indra, drink it together, united, in the seer called Nipātithi, in the seer called Medhyātithi, in the seer called Puṣṭigu, and in the seer called Śruṣṭigu.

##### English translation
Indra as you did drink Soma for the priest Samvanin, so drink for Medhatithi and Nipatithi, Pushtigu and Srushtigu.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पार्षद्वाणः पुरुषवाक् श्चिछत्तुः ( ? कश्चिच्छत्रुः) । वाण इति
> वाङ् नाम वाणीची वाणः इत तन्नामसु पाठात् । शयानं स्वपंतं प्रस्कण्वं कण्वस्य
> पुत्रं यदा समसादयत् सम्यगपीडयत् । कीदृशं । जिव्रिं जराजीर्णं उद्दितं
> ऊर्ध्वदेशे स्थापितं तदा त्वोतः त्वया इंद्रेण रक्षितः स ऋषिः प्रस्कण्वः दस्यवे
> उपक्षपयितुः शत्रोः वृकः विकर्तनः सन् तदीयानि गवां सहस्राणि आसिसासत्
> संभजते स्म । इत्यंप्रभावस्त्वमसि तस्मात्त्वां स्तुम इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when the Pārṣadvāṇa, the one of cruel speech (the printed gloss reads a certain enemy), वाण इति वाङ् नाम (*vāṇa iti vāṅ nāma*): वाण (*vāṇa*) is a name of speech, as it is read among its names, oppressed completely Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva, who lay asleep, aged and set in an elevated place, then that seer Praskaṇva, protected by you, Indra, became a cutter-down of the harassing enemy and obtained (आसिसासत् (*āsisāsat*)) that enemy's thousands of cows. Such is your power, therefore we praise you: this is the sense. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पार्षद्वाणः (*pārṣadvāṇaḥ*)—the enemy of cruel speech
- जिविं (*jiviṃ*)—the aged one
- उद्दितं (*udditaṃ*)—the one set in the upper part
- शयानं (*śayānaṃ*)—the one who was sleeping
- प्रस्कण्वं (*praskaṇvaṃ*)—Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva
- समसादयत् (*samasādayat*)—oppressed completely
- त्वोतः (*tvotaḥ*)—protected by you at that time
- ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—the seer Praskaṇva
- दस्यवे (*dasyave*)—for the enemy
- वृकः (*vṛkaḥ*)—being a destroyer
- सहस्राणि (*sahasrāṇi*)—numbering a thousand
- गवां (*gavāṃ*)—of cows, the herd
- असिषासत् (*asiṣāsat*)—obtained from the enemy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the enemy of cruel speech oppressed completely Praskaṇṇa, the son of Kaṇva, who was aged, set in the upper part and sleeping. The seer Praskaṇṇa, protected by you at that time, became a destroyer of the enemy and obtained a herd of a thousand cows from the enemy's place. **NOTE**

##### English translation
Old Parshardvan sat laying Prakasana up. The Rishi who was a terror to Dashyu protected thousand cows.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरात्मानं ब्रूते । हे श्रुष्टिगो य इंद्रः न संप्रति उक्षेभिः उक्षैः
> स्तोत्रैः स्तुतः सन् चिकित् स्तोतुः ज्ञानं विंधके परिचरति । विधतिः परिचरणकर्मा ।
> मत्सेवने तव सम्यक् ज्ञानमस्तीत्या (?त्य) भिनंदति ! यश्चेंद्रः ऋषिचोदनः
> ऋषीणां मंत्राणां तद्द्रष्ट्मणां वा चोणनः प्रवर्तकोऽस्ति तमिंद्रं परमेश्वरं अच्चाभिलक्ष्य नव्यस्या नवतना ( ? नवतरां ) मती मतिं स्तुतिं वद ब्रूहि । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः ! अरिष्यंतं न भोजसे । यथा कश्चिदरिष्यंतं अहिंसंतं स्वामिनं
> भोजसे स्वपालनाय नवतरां स्तुतिं ब्रूते तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer speaks of himself. O Śruṣṭigu, the Indra who, praised now with chants, finds (विंधते (*viṃdhate*), serves) the knowledge of the praiser, विधति (*vidhati*) being a word for service, so that he approves, "you have right knowledge in serving me"; and who is the impeller of seers, of mantras or of their seers: to that Indra, the Supreme Lord, direct and utter a newer praise. An illustration: as one speaks a newer praise to a master who does no harm, for his own protection and sustenance, so do here. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- न (*na*)—now
- उक्षेभिः (*ukṣebhiḥ*)—praised with hymns
- चिकित् (*cikit*)—the knowledge of the praiser
- विंधते (*viṃdhate*)—he approves
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- ऋषिचोदनः (*ṛṣicodanaḥ*)—the impeller of the seers' good works
- तं (*taṃ*)—such
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- अरिष्यंतं न (*ariṣyaṃtaṃ na*)—as one praises a master who does no harm
- नव्यसा (*navyasā*)—new
- मती (*matī*)—with praise
- अच्छ (*accha*)—exceedingly
- वद (*vada*)—praise and extol

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O seer, praise and extol exceedingly with a new praise, as one praises a master who does no harm for protection, that Indra who, praised now with hymns, approves the knowledge of the praiser, and who is the impeller of good works for the seers.

##### English translation
Who is attainable by chants who being roused by Rishi is all knowing ; intending protection for his pleasure utter praises.

> यस्मा॑ अ॒र्कं स॒प्तिशी॑र्षाणमानृ॒चुस्ति॒धातु॑मुत्त॒मे प॒दे ।  
> स त्वि१॒॑ १ मा विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि चक्रद॒दादिज्ज॑निष्ट॒ पौंस्यं॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । तु । इमा । विश्वा । भुवनानि । चक्रदत् । आत् । इत् । जनिष्ट । पौंस्यं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्मै इंद्राय परमेश्वराय तदर्थं उत्तमे पदे उत्कृष्टतमे स्थाने
> द्युलोकाख्यॆ स्थितं अर्क० अर्चनीयमादित्यमानृचुः अर्चंति सर्वे । अथ य
> एषोऽंतरादित्ये हिरण्मयः पुरुषो दृश्यते (छां. उ. १-६-६) इत्यादि श्रुत्युक्तं
> यदीयं स्वरूपमुपलब्धं ! सर्वॆ सूर्यमाराधयंतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशमर्क० ।
> सप्तशीर्षाणं ! सप्तसंख्याकाः शीर्षवत् प्रधानभूता रश्मयो यस्य तादृशं ।
> त्रिधातुं त्रयाणां भूरादिलोकानां पोषकं । सूर्यस्य त्रिलोकीपोषकत्वं तु
> वृष्ट्यादिव्यापारेण प्रसिद्धं । यत्स्वरूपलाभाय अर्कमर्चंति स तु परमेश्वरः
> इमा इमानि दृश्यमानानि विश्वा सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातानि देवासुरमनुष्यरूपाणि उद्दिश्य अचिक्रदत् आक्रंदति ! माध्यमिक्या वाचा दददशब्दैर्गम ( ? र्दम)
> दयादानवाचकैः ! आदित् अनंतरमेव पौंस्यं बलं शिक्षालक्षणं जनिष्ट जनयति
> आविर्भावयति ! अयं भावः । परमेश्वर आदौ मेघस्तनितलक्षणया स्ववाण्या
> भूक्षेभ्यो (? भूस्थेभ्यो) हितमुपदिशति । अनाकर्णिते च तस्मिन् पश्चाद्दारिद्र्यादिलक्षणां शिक्षामाविष्करोतीति ! अत्राभिहितोऽर्थो बृहदारण्यके खिलकांडे त्रया
> ह वै प्राजापत्याः इत्यादिना ग्रंथेन प्रपंचतः (बृ. उ. ५-२) ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For which Indra, the Supreme Lord, all worship the Sun, the worshipful, set in the highest place called the heavenly world: the form of whom is obtained according to the Śruti अथ य एषोऽंतरादित्ये हिरण्मयः पुरुषो दृश्यते (*atha ya eṣo 'ṃtarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate*) (Chā. U. 1-6-6) and so on; the meaning is that all worship the Sun. What kind of Sun? Seven-headed, that is, having seven principal rays like heads; three-elemented, the nourisher of the three worlds, Bhūḥ and the rest; the Sun's nourishing of the three worlds is well known through the work of rain and so on. He for whose form they worship the Sun is the Supreme Lord, who cries out (अचिक्रदत् (*acikradat*)) towards all these visible worlds, the beings of the gods, the Asuras and men, with the middle (atmospheric) speech, through the syllables द (*da*) द (*da*) द (*da*) that signify self-control, mercy and giving. Immediately after, he brings forth (जनिष्ट (*janiṣṭa*)) strength in the form of instruction. The sense is that the Supreme Lord first teaches what is good for the beings of the earth by his own voice in the form of thunder, and when that is not heard, afterwards he brings forth instruction in the form of poverty and the like. The meaning stated here is set out at length in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, in the Khila section, by the passage beginning त्रया ह वै प्राजापत्याः (*trayā ha vai prājāpatyāḥ*) (Bṛ. U. 5-2). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सप्तशीर्षाणं (*saptaśīrṣāṇaṃ*)—the one with seven rays
- त्रिधातुं (*tridhātuṃ*)—the nourisher of the three worlds
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—the worshipful Āditya
- उत्तमे पदे (*uttame pade*)—in the highest place, the heavenly world
- आनृचुः (*ānṛcuḥ*)—all worship
- स तु (*sa tu*)—that same Indra in the form of the Āditya
- इमा विश्वा भुवनानि (*imā viśvā bhuvanāni*)—all these worlds
- चक्रदत् (*cakradat*)—made them resound
- आदित् (*ādit*)—immediately after
- पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)—strength
- जनिष्टॆ (*janiṣṭè*)—produced

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the satisfaction of which Indra all worship the Āditya, who has seven rays, who nourishes the three worlds, who is worshipful and who stands in the highest heavenly world, that same Indra, in the form of the Āditya, made all these worlds

full of sound. Immediately after, he also produced strength.

##### English translation
For whom is good places who is worshipping mantras with seven points and three places, he has made this universe, full of sounds and is producer of strength.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो नो॑ दा॒ता वसू॑ना॒मिंद्रं॒ तं हू॑महे व॒यं ।  
> वि॒द्या ह्य॑स्य सुम॒तिं नवी॑यसीं ग॒मेम॒ गोम॑ति व्र॒जे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । नः । दाता । वसूनां । इंद्रं । तं । हूमहे । वयं ।  
> विद्म । हि । अस्य । सुमतिं । नवीयसीं । गमेम । गोमति । व्रजे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रः नोऽस्माकं वसूनां वासहेतूनां धनानां दाता भवति तमिंद्रं
> परमेश्वरं हूमहे आह्वयामो वयं स्तोतारः । हि यस्मादस्येंद्रस्य नवीयसीं
> नवतरामकृतपूर्वां सुमतिं कल्याणीं मतिमनुग्रहबुद्धिं विद्म जानीमः ।
> आतस्तमाह्वयामेति पूर्वेण संबंधः । यया सुमत्या वयं गोमति गवोपेते
> व्रजे गजाश्वादिपशुसमूहे गमेम स्वामित्वेन प्राप्नुयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who is the giver to us of treasures (वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*), wealth that is the cause of dwelling), that Indra, the Supreme Lord, we the praisers invoke. For we know (विद्म (*vidma*)) this Indra's newer, hitherto unmade, auspicious good will, his gracious disposition, by which we may come, as masters, to a cow-filled pen, a herd of cattle such as elephants and horses. The words आतस्तमाह्वयाम (*ātastamāhvayāma*) connect with the preceding. **NOTE**

- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—excellent gracious disposition

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We invoke with prayer that Indra who gives us the gift of wealth. May we, knowing the new and excellent gracious disposition of this Indra, obtain as a result a good herd of cows.

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्मै॒ त्वं व॑सो दा॒नाय॒ शिक्ष॑सि॒ स रा॒यस्पोष॑मश्नुते ।  
> तं त्वा॑ व॒यं म॑घवन्निंद्र गिर्वणः सु॒तावं॑तो हवामहे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्मै । त्वं । वसो इति । दानाय । शिक्षसि । सः । रायः । पोषं । अश्नुते ।  
> शं । त्वा । वयं । मघवन् । इंद्र । गिर्वणः । सुतवंतः । हवामहे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसो वासयितरिंद्र त्वं यस्मै यजमानाय दानाय धनदानार्थं
> शिक्षसि आज्ञापयसि स यजमानः रायः धनस्य पोषं पुष्टिमश्नुते व्याप्न्नोति ।
> यं यजमानं धनं दातुं प्रवर्तयसि स त्वदाज्ञया धनत्यागेन वसुसमृद्धो
> भवतीत्याश्चर्यं । अतो हे गिर्वणः गीर्भिर्वननीय मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र तं तादृशं
> त्वा त्वां सुतावंतः अभिषुतसोमा वयं हवामहे आह्वयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasu, Indra, who causes to dwell, the sacrificer for whom you appoint (शिक्षसि (*śikṣasi*), command) the giving of wealth, that sacrificer obtains the increase of wealth. The sacrificer whom you impel to give wealth becomes, by your command, rich in treasure through the giving up of wealth: this is the wonder. Therefore, O Girvaṇas, to be adored with songs, O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, to you, such as you are, we, having pressed the Soma, call.

- वसो (*vaso*)—giver of a dwelling
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—to which sacrificer
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—for the manner of giving wealth
- शिक्षसि (*śikṣasi*)—you instruct
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- सुतावंतः (*sutāvaṃtaḥ*)—who have pressed the Soma juice
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—call with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wealthy, worshipful through praises, giver of a dwelling, the sacrificer to whom you teach the way of giving wealth obtains the increase of riches. We, who press the Soma juice, pray to and call such an excellent one as you.

##### English translation

> क॒दा च॒न स्त॒रीर॑सि॒ नेंद्र॑ सच्चसि दा॒शुषे॑ ।  
> उपो॒पेन्नु म॑घव॒न्भूय॒ इन्नु ते॒ दानं॑ दे॒वस्य॑ पृच्यते ॥७॥

> पृच्यते ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र नु क्षिप्रं दानं हविःसमर्पणं नु निश्चितं भूय इत्
> प्रचुरं सदेव ते तव देवस्य द्योतमानस्य परमेश्वरस्य उपोपेत् समीपमेव
> पृच्यते त्वया संपृक्तं भवति । स्वल्पमपि शीघ्रं सत्पात्रे समर्पितं बहुलीभूय
> ईश्वरे संगतं भवतीत्यभिप्रायः । अतः हे इंद्र परमेश्वर दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवतो
> यजमानस्य स्तरीः हिंसकः कदाचन कदापि नासि न भवसि । आपि तु सश्चसि तेन संगच्छसे ।
> तदीयं सख्यं संपादयसीत्यर्थः । प्रसमुपोदः पादपूरणे (पा. सू. ८-१-६)
> इत्यनेन उप इत्यस्य द्विवचनं (द्विर्वचनं) पादपूरणार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, the offering of oblation, quickly and certainly, in abundance, comes near you, the shining Supreme Lord, and is joined with you. Even a little offered quickly to a worthy recipient becomes abundant and reaches the Lord: this is the idea. Therefore, O Indra, Supreme Lord, you are never a harmer (स्तरीः (*starīḥ*)) of the sacrificer who has given the oblation; rather you cleave (सश्चसि (*saścasi*)) to him, that is, you are united with him and bring about friendship with him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—wealthy
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of you, of divine nature
- ते (*te*)—offered with you in view
- दानं (*dānaṃ*)—the gift of oblation
- उपोप इन्नु (*upopa innu*)—just as it approaches you
