- भूय इन्नु (*bhūya innu*)—growing exceedingly
- पृच्यते (*pṛcyate*)—is accepted by you
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- स्तरीः (*starīḥ*)—a harmer of the sacrificer
- कदाचन (*kadācana*)—ever
- न आसि (*na āsi*)—you are not
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblation
- सश्चसि (*saścasi*)—you cling as a friend

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, the gift of oblation offered with you, of divine nature, in view, grows exceedingly just as it approaches you and is accepted by you. O Indra, you are never a harmer of the sacrificer. You cling as a friend to the sacrificer who offers oblation.

##### English translation
Indra you never cease producing, you come to the sacrificer. You are God ; your gift comes once and oft.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र यो न॑न॒क्षे अ॒भ्योज॑सा॒ क्रिविं॑ व॒ध्यैः शुष्णं॑ निघो॒षय॑न् ।  
> य॒देदस्तं॑भीत्प्र॒थय॑न्न॒मूं दिव॒मादिज्ज॑निष्ट॒ पार्थि॑वः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । यः । ननक्षे । अभि । ओजसा । क्रिविं । वधैः । शुष्णं । निघोषयन् ।  
> यदा । इत् । अस्तंभीत् । प्रथयन् । अमूं । दिवं । आत् । इत् । जनिष्ट ।  
> पार्थिवः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रः वधैः आयुधप्रहारैः क्रिविं विकृत्तं शुष्णमेतन्नामानमसुरं
> ओजसा बलेन निघोषयन् निकरां शब्दयन् सन् अभि अभितः प्र प्रकर्षण ननक्षे
> व्याप्नोति स्म । आसुरं हत्वा स्वसामर्थ्यं सर्वतः प्रकाशितवानित्यर्थः । कदेत्यवेक्षायामाह । यदेत् यदैव सोऽसुरः प्रथयन् आत्मानं पृथुं कुर्वन् अमूं
> दूरे दृश्यमानं दिवं द्युलोकं अस्तंभीत् स्तब्धं कृतवान् । आदित् अनंतरमेव
> प्रार्थिवोग्निः जनिष्ट प्रादुरभूत् । लोकान् प्राणनिरोधेन अग्निः समजनि यदा
> तदेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who, with blows of his weapons (वधैः (*vadhaiḥ*)), makes loud noise (निघोषयन् (*nighoṣayan*)) with his strength against Kriva, the mutilated one, the asura named Śuṣṇa, and pervades (ननक्षे (*nanakṣe*)) forth on every side: that is, having killed the asura he displayed his own power everywhere. When? He answers: when that asura, making himself broad, stopped (अस्तंभीत् (*astaṃbhīt*)) the heaven seen yonder in the distance, immediately after, the terrestrial Agni was born, appeared; the sense is: when Agni was produced together in the worlds by the stopping of breath.

### Printed p. 601

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यदा इत् (*yadā it*)—at what time
- अमूं दिवं (*amūṃ divaṃ*)—the whole well-known heaven
- प्रथयन् (*prathayan*)—pervading
- अस्तंभीत् (*astaṃbhīt*)—this asura obstructed
- आत् इत् (*āt it*)—immediately
- पार्थिवः (*pārthivaḥ*)—in the form of terrestrial fire
- जनिष्ट (*janiṣṭa*)—this Indra was born
- यः (*yaḥ*)—that same Indra who
- क्रिविं (*kriviṃ*)—grown
- शुष्णं (*śuṣṇaṃ*)—that same asura called Śuṣṇa
- वध्यैः (*vadhyaiḥ*)—with weapons that are instruments of killing **NOTE**
- निघोषयन् (*nighoṣayan*)—afflicting so that it sounds
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with his own power
- अभि (*abhi*)—everywhere
- प्र ननक्षे (*pra nanakṣe*)—has pervaded and become extended

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At what time this asura, pervading the whole well-known heaven, obstructed it, immediately after that Indra was born in the form of terrestrial fire. That same Indra, afflicting with weapons that are instruments of killing the grown asura called Śuṣka, with his own power, has pervaded everywhere and become extended. **NOTE**

##### English translation
He who filled the well by killing Shushna by weapon hurled with might, who surprised the heaven, who coming to earth produced all things.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्या॒यं विश्व॒ आर्यो॒ दासः॑ शेवधि॒पा अ॒रिः ।  
> ति॒रश्चि॑द॒र्ये रुश॑मे॒ पवी॑रवि॒ तुभ्येत्सो अ॑ज्यते र॒यिः । ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्य । आयं । विश्वः । आर्यः । दासः । शेवधिपाः । अरिः ।  
> शिरः । चित् । आर्ये । रुशमे । पवीरवि । तुभ्य । इत् । सः । अज्यते । रयिः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वः सर्वः आयं दृश्यमानः आर्यः असुरस्वामिको गणः यस्येंद्रस्य अरिः
> शत्रुर्भवति । कीदृशः सः । दासः धनादेरुपक्षपयिता शेवधिपाः । शेवधिनिर्धिस्तं पाति
> रक्षतीति ! तथा असुरादिधनस्यापहर्ता स्वधनस्य च रक्षितेत्यर्थः । तेनेंद्रेण रुशमे
> अकल्याणे आर्ये अरिगणे तस्मिन् तिरश्चित् अंतर्हितमेव पवीरवि । पवी रथनेमिस्त-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The whole of this visible host of Āryas, whose lord is the asuras, is the enemy of Indra. Of what kind is he? A Dāsa, a diminisher of wealth and the rest; Śevadhipā, one who guards (पाति (*pāti*)) the treasure (शेवधि (*śevadhi*)), who is likewise a taker of the wealth of asuras and others and a protector of his own wealth: this is the sense. By that Indra, in that inauspicious (रुशमे (*ruśame*)) enemy host, a hidden (तिरश्चित् (*tiraścit*)) wheel with felly (पवीरवि (*pavīravi*)): पवी (*pavī*) is the felly of a wheel, the spokes that are attached to it are पवीराः (*pavīrāḥ*), and the wheel provided with them is पवीरवि (*pavīravi*).

### Printed p. 602

> द्वंतोऽराः पवीराः । तदुपेतं चक्रं पवीरवि। अत्र पवी रथनेमिर्भवति (निरु. ५-५)
> इत्यादि निरुक्तं द्रष्टव्यं । तादृशं चक्रमज्यते प्रक्षिप्यते । चतुर्थपादे प्रत्यक्षीकृत्य
> उच्यते। हे इंद्र तुभ्यमेव त्वदर्थमेव सः असुरगणे विद्यमानः रयिः निधिलक्षणो
> धनराशिः अज्यते प्रक्षिप्यतेऽरिगणेन । असुरगणे गुप्तं चक्रदानमपि इंद्राय
> निधिप्रदमभवत् तदा सत्पात्रे गुप्तं धनदानं महाफलदं स्यादिति किमु वक्तव्यमित्याशयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here the Nirukta is to be seen, अत्र पवी रथनेमिर्भवति (*atra pavī rathanemirbhavati*) (Ni. 5-5), and so on. Such a wheel is cast (अज्यते (*ajyate*)). In the fourth pāda, making it direct, he says: O Indra, for you alone, for your sake alone, that mass of wealth in the form of treasure, existing in the host of asuras, is cast by the enemy host. Even a gift of a wheel hidden in the asura host became a giver of treasure to Indra; then what need is there to say that a gift of wealth hidden away in a worthy recipient would bring great fruit: such is the intention.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—to which Indra
- विश्वः (*viśvaḥ*)—the entire
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—host of asuras
- अरिः (*ariḥ*)—is an enemy
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—that same Indra
- दासः (*dāsaḥ*)—is the taker of the enemy's wealth **NOTE**
- शेवधिपाः (*śevadhipāḥ*)—and the protector of his own wealth
- रुशमे (*ruśame*)—inauspicious
- पवीरवि (*pavīravi*)—revolving like a wheel
- आर्यॆ (*āryè*)—in the enemy
- तिरश्चित् (*tiraścit*)—even though hidden
- सः रयिः (*saḥ rayiḥ*)—all that wealth
- तुभ्य इत् (*tubhya it*)—for you alone
- अज्यते (*ajyate*)—is offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the Indra to whom the entire host of asuras is an enemy, that same Indra is the taker of the enemy's wealth and the protector of his own wealth. O Indra, even though hidden in the enemy, inauspicious and revolving like a wheel, all that wealth is offered for you alone.

##### English translation
Aryans and slaves are protector of wealth and worshipper who came before Arya, fair coloured, Paveru, he is united with you, dispenser of wealth.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तु॒र॒ण्यवो॒ मधु॑मंतं घृत॒श्चुतं॒ विप्रा॑सो अ॒र्कमा॑नृचुः ।  
> अ॒स्मे र॒यिः प॑प्रथे॒ वृष्ण्यं॒ शवो॒ऽस्मे सु॑वा॒नास॒ इंद॑वः ॥१०॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तुरण्यवः । मधुमंतं । धृतश्चुतं । विप्रासः । अर्कं । आन्रुचुः ।  
> अस्मे इति । रयिः । पप्रथे । वृष्ट्यं । शवः । अस्मे इति । सुवानासः । इंदवः ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 603

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तुरण्णवः श्वरमाणाति विप्रासो मेधाविनो यजमानाः अर्कमर्चनीयसुंद्रं अन्रुचु अर्चंति । कीदृशं । मधुमंतं मधुरामृतरसोपेतं धृतश्चुतं
> जलस्रविणु मेघभेदनेन वृष्टिं कुर्वंतमित्यर्थः । केनाभिप्रायेणार्चंतीत्युच्यते ! अस्मै अस्मासु रयिः धनराशिः पप्रथे प्रथितो भवतु । तथा वृष्णं अपत्योत्पादकं शवः बलमस्तु । किंचास्मे अस्मासु सुवानासः अभिषुता इंदवः सोमाः
> संतु । इंद्रानुग्रहेणैव तत्सर्वमस्मासु संपद्यतामित्याशयेनेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hastening (तुरण्णवः (*turaṇṇavaḥ*)) wise sacrificers worship (अन्रुचु (*anrucu*)) the worshipful Indra **NOTE**. Of what kind? Possessed of honey, endowed with sweet nectar-juice (मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)); water-dripping (धृतश्चुतं (*dhṛtaścutaṃ*)), that is, making rain by splitting the cloud. With what intention do they worship? It is said: may a mass of wealth be spread (पप्रथे (*paprathe*)) in us; likewise may there be manly strength (शवः (*śavaḥ*)), generative of offspring; and may pressed Soma drops be in us. With the intention that all that be accomplished in us by Indra's favour alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- रयिः (*rayiḥ*)—wealth
- पप्रथे (*paprathe*)—may it be spread and filled
- वृष्ट्यं (*vṛṣṭyaṃ*)—generative of offspring
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—may strength arise
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- सुवानासः (*suvānāsaḥ*)—pressed
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—may the Soma juices be filled, endowed with this intention
- तुरण्यवः (*turaṇyavaḥ*)—those who are quick in rites
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—and wise, the sacrificers
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—filled with sweet nectar
- धृतश्चुतं (*dhṛtaścutaṃ*)—one who pours down rain
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—and worshipful, Indra
- आनृचुः (*ānṛcuḥ*)—they worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

"May wealth be abundantly filled in us; may there arise in us strength that begets sons; may the pressed Soma juices be filled in us": with this intention the sacrificers, quick in the rite and wise, worship Indra, who is filled with sweet nectar, who pours down rain, and who is worshipful.

##### English translation
Quickly the Vipras are uttering worshipping mantras with sweet honey and thrifting ghee, wealth is being sent to them. Manly strength and effused Soma are coming to us.

## Sūkta 52 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यथा मना विवस्वति इति दशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं आयवमैंद्रं । अनुक्रांतं
> च - यथा मनावायुः इति । काण्व आयुर्यषिः । इंद्रो देवता । आयुजां बृहती
> छंदः । युजां सतो बृहतीछंदः । विनियोगः सूत्रादवगंतव्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta of ten Ṛks beginning यथा मना विवस्वति (*yathā manā vivasvati*) is the fourth, Āyava and addressed to Indra. It is listed in the Anukramaṇikā: यथा मनावायुः (*yathā manāvāyuḥ*). The seer is Āyu Kāṇva **NOTE**; the deity is Indra. The metre of the odd-numbered Ṛks is Bṛhatī and that of the even-numbered is Satobṛhatī. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

### Printed p. 604

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta beginning यथा मनौ विवस्वति (*yathā manau vivasvati*) is the fourth among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has ten Ṛks. Its seer is one called Āyuḥ Kāṇvaḥ; Indra is the deity. The odd-numbered Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Bṛhatī metre; the even-numbered Ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: यथा मनावायुः (*yathā manāvāyuḥ*). The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 52; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 20, 21. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Āyuḥ Śāṇdhaḥ **NOTE**. Deity: Indraḥ. Metre: Prāgāthaṃ (Āyujaḥ bṛhatya, yajaḥ gatobṛhatya) **NOTE**.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॒ मनौ॒ विव॑स्वति॒ सोमं॑ श॒क्रापि॑बः सु॒तं ।  
> यथा॑ त्रि॒ते छंद॑ इंद्र॒ जुजो॑षस्या॒यौ मा॑दयसे॒ सचा॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । मनौ । विवस्वति । सोमं । शक्र । अपिबः । सुतं ।  
> यथा । त्रिते । छंदः । इंद्र । जुषोषसि । आयौ । मादयसे । सचा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शक्र समर्थेंद्र यथा येन प्रकारेण विवस्वति विवस्वतः पुत्रे वैवस्वते
> मनौ वर्तमानु सुतमभिषुतं सोमं अपिबः पीतवानसि । हे इंद्र परमेश्वर
> यथा च त्रिते एतन्नामके ऋषौ वर्तमानं छंदः वेदजातं जुजोषसि भृशं
> सेवसे । तथा आयौ एतन्नामके मयि सचा सह वर्तमानं सोमं छंदोलक्षणं
> तदुभयं संसेव्य मादयसे आनंदयसि मामात्मानं च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śakra, mighty Indra, as you drank the pressed Soma standing in Manu Vaivasvata, the son of Vivasvat; and, O Indra, Supreme Lord, as you greatly enjoy (जुजोषसि (*jujoṣasi*)) the Veda, the sacred metre (छंदः (*chaṃdaḥ*)) standing in the seer called Trita; so, in me called Āyu, you take Soma standing together (सचा (*sacā*)) with the metre, enjoy both, and delight (मादयसे (*mādayase*)) me and yourself.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शक्र (*śakra*)—endowed with ability
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- विवस्वति (*vivasvati*)—in the son of Vivasvat

### Printed p. 605

- मन् (*man*)—in Manu
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the pressed Soma
- अपिबः (*apibaḥ*)—you drank
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- त्रिते (*trite*)—made in Trita
- छंदः (*chaṃdaḥ*)—the praise formed of metre
- जुजोषसि (*jujoṣasi*)—you served, in the same way
- आयौ (*āyau*)—in me, called Āyu
- सचा (*sacā*)—being one with me
- मादयसे (*mādayase*)—be satisfied with my Soma and praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, endowed with ability, in the manner in which you drank the Soma that was in Manu, the son of Vivasvat, in the manner in which you served the praise formed of metre made in Trita, in the same way, being with me, called Āyu, may the Soma offered by me serve me and the praise, and may you be satisfied.

##### English translation
Indra, as you drunk the Soma of Manu as you fulfilled the wishes of Triti as you were exhilarated.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पृष॑ध्रॆः॒ मेध्ये॑ मात॒रिश्व॒नींद्र॑ सुवा॒ने अमं॑दथाः ।  
> यघा॒ सोमं॒ दश॑शिप्रे॒ दशो॑ण्ये॒ स्यूम॑रश्मा॒वृजू॑नसि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सृषध्रे । मेध्ये । मातरिश्वनि । इंद्र । सुवाने । अमंदथाः ।  
> मथा । सोमं । दशशिप्रे । दशओण्ये । स्यूमरश्मा । ऋजूनसि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र सुवाने सोमाभिषवं कुर्वाणे पृषध्रे एतन्नामके ऋषौ
> वर्तमानं सोमं पीत्वा यथा अमंदथाः हृष्टपानसि। यथा च मेध्यॆ मातरिश्वनि
> दशशिप्रे दशोण्ये सूमरश्मौ ऋजूनसि च एतेषु सर्वेष्टृषिसु वर्तमानं सोमं
> पीत्वा अमंदथाः । तदा मां मादयसे इति पूर्वेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, as you rejoiced (अमंदथाः (*amaṃdathāḥ*)) after drinking the Soma standing in the seer named Pṛṣadhra, who was pressing Soma; and as, in the case of all these seers, Medhya, Mātariśvan, Daśaśipra, Daśonya, Sūmaraśmi and Ṛjūnas, you rejoiced after drinking the Soma standing in them, then delight me: this connects with what precedes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सुवाने (*suvāne*)—who performs the pressing of Soma
- पृषध्रे (*pṛṣadhre*)—in the seer called Pṛṣadhra
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—having drunk the Soma
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner

### Printed p. 606

- अमंदथाः (*amaṃdathāḥ*)—you attained delight (so also)
- मेध्यॆ (*medhyè*)—in Medhya
- मातरिश्वनि (*mātariśvani*)—in Mātariśvan
- दशशिप्रे (*daśaśipre*)—in Daśaśipra
- दशोण्ये (*daśoṇye*)—in Daśonya
- स्यूमरश्मि (*syūmaraśmi*)—in Syumaraśmi
- ऋजूनसि (*ṛjūnasi*)—in Ṛjūna; having drunk the Soma that was prepared there, in the manner in which you attained delight, in the same way drink the Soma offered by me and attain delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, having drunk the Soma offered by all these seers who performed the pressing of Soma, Pṛthu, Medhya, Mātariśvan, Daśaśipra, Daśonya, Sūmaraśmi and Ṛjūna, in the manner in which you attained delight, in the same way drink the Soma offered by me and attain delight. **NOTE**

##### English translation
As you become exhilarated with Prishadra when Matararishva effuses Soma at the rite. As you did drink the radiant Soma with Dasashipra and Dashonya.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य उ॒क्ता केव॑ला द॒धे यः सोमं॑ धृषि॒तापि॑बत् ।  
> यस्मै॒ विष्णु॒स्त्रीणि॑ प॒दा वि॑चक्र॒म उप॑ मि॒त्रस्य॒ धर्म॑भिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । उक्ता । केवला । दधे । यः । सोमं । धृषिता । अपिबत् ।  
> यस्मै । विष्णुः । त्रीणि । पदा । विचक्रमे । उप । मित्रस्य । धर्मभिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रः केवला केवलानि आत्मस्वामिकानि उक्था उक्थानि शस्त्राणि दधे अवधारयति । शृण्वतीत्यर्थः (? शृणोति) । यश्चेंद्रः धृषितः शत्रूणां धर्षकः अभिभविता
> सन् सोममपिबत् पीतवान् । यस्मै इंद्राय तदर्थं विष्णुर्वापक उपेंद्रः
> मित्रस्य । मित्रोऽहरभिमानी देवः । अहर्वै मित्रो रात्रिर्वरुणः (ऐ. ब्रा. ४-१०)
> इति श्रुतेः । तस्य धर्मभिः धर्मैः उवयास्तमय्यैन्व्यापारैरुपलक्षितः सन् त्रीणि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who holds (दधे (*dadhe*)), that is, attends to **NOTE**, the exclusive (केवला (*kevalā*)) recitations (उक्था (*ukthā*)), the śastras that belong to him alone; and the Indra who, bold, an assailant and overcomer of enemies, drank Soma; for whom Viṣṇu, the pervader, Upendra, marked by the functions of Mitra (Mitra is the deity presiding over the day, according to the Śruti अहर्वै मित्रो रात्रिर्वरुणः (*aharvai mitro rātrirvaruṇaḥ*), Ai. Brā. 4-10), that is, by the activities of rising and setting, strode with three steps

### Printed p. 607

> पदा त्रिभिः पादैः विचक्रमे विशेषेण आक्रांतवान् त्रिलोकीं । स इंद्रोऽस्मान्
> मादयत्वति आशीः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

across the three worlds in particular. May that Indra delight us: this is a blessing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- केवला (*kevalā*)—that gives self-satisfaction
- उक्था (*ukthā*)—the praises in the form of śastras
- दधे (*dadhe*)—obtained
- धृषिता (*dhṛṣitā*)—who assails enemies
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- अपिबत् (*apibat*)—drank
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—for whom
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu, the pervader
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of the god Mitra
- धर्मभिः (*dharmabhiḥ*)—by the qualities of rising and setting
- उप (*upa*)—being indicated
- त्रीणि पदा (*trīṇi padā*)—his three steps
- विचक्रमे (*vicakrame*)—spread and pervaded; may such an Indra drink our Soma and be satisfied

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Indra who has obtained the praises in the form of śastras that give self-satisfaction, that Indra, the assailant of enemies, who drank the Soma, for whom the all-pervading Viṣṇu, indicated by the qualities of the god Mitra, which consist of rising and setting, spread and pervaded with his three steps, drink our Soma and be satisfied.

##### English translation
He who has taken for himself the hymns, who has dared heroically drink Soma, in whose presence Vishnu put three steps as directed by Mitra.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्य॒ त्वमिं॑द्र॒ स्तोमे॑षु चा॒कनो॒ वाजे॑ वाजिञ्चितक्रतो ।  
> तं त्वा॑ व॒यं सु॒दुघा॑मिव गो॒दुहो॑ जुहू॒मसि॑ श्रव॒स्यवः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्य । त्वं । इंद्र । स्तोमेषु । चाकनः । वाजे । वाजिन् । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो ।  
> तं । त्वा । वयं सुदुघां इव । गोदुहः । जुहूमसि । श्रवस्यवः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वाजिन् अन्नवन् हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मवन्निंद्र त्वं यस्य यजमानस्य
> स्तोमेषु स्तोत्रेषु निमित्तेषु वाजे हविर्लक्षणे अन्ने च निमित्तभूते सति चाकनः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vājin, possessor of food, O Śatakratu, possessor of many rites, Indra, you take delight (चाकनः (*cākanaḥ*)) in the sacrificer whose praises are the occasion, and when the food of the oblation is the occasion

### Printed p. 608

> तृप्यसि तं तादृशं त्वा त्वामिंद्रं श्रवस्यवः । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम । अन्नकामा वयं
> यजमानाः जुहुमः हविर्दद्मः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सुदुघामिव गोदुहः ।
> गोदोग्धारः सुदोग्धिं गां प्रति यथा हरिततृणादिकं ददति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

such as you are, Indra, we, who desire food (श्रवस्यवः (*śravasyavaḥ*); श्रव (*śrava*) is a name for food), sacrificers, make offering of oblation (जुहुमः (*juhumaḥ*)). An illustration: as milkers of cows give green grass and the like to a good milch cow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—doer of many rites
- वाजिन् (*vājin*)—possessor of food
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which sacrificer
- स्तोमेषु (*stomeṣu*)—at the time of praise
- वाजे (*vāje*)—for his food
- चाकनः (*cākanaḥ*)—you show your satisfaction
- तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*)—you, who belong to that same sacrificer
- श्रवस्यवः (*śravasyavaḥ*)—desirous of food
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- गोदुहः (*goduhaḥ*)—those who wish to milk a cow
- सुदुघां इव (*sudughāṃ iva*)—as one approaches and calls an excellent milch cow
- जुहूमसि (*juhūmasi*)—we call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, doer of many rites and possessor of food, in the sacrificer at whose praises you show your satisfaction for the sake of his food, you who belong to that same sacrificer we, who desire food, call with prayer, as those who wish to milk a cow approach and call an excellent milch cow.

##### English translation
Indra of great speed who desires praises in the rite, we are invoking you desirous of food like milkers calling cows giving milk.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो नो॑ दा॒ता स नः॑ पि॒ता म॒हा उ॒ग्र ई॑शान॒कृत् ।  
> अया॑मन्नु॒गो म॒घवा॑ पुरू॒वसु॒र्गॊरश्व॑स्य॒ प्र दा॑तु नः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । नः । दाता । सः । नः । पिता । महान् । उग्रः । ईशानकृत् ।  
> आयामन् । उग्रः । मघवा । पुरुवसुः । गोः । अश्वस्य । प्र । दातु । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यॆ इंद्रः नोऽस्मभ्यं दाता धनादेर्ददति (? ददाति) सः इंद्रः नोऽस्माकं
> पिता पालको भवतु । कीदृशः सः । महान् प्रौढः उग्रः उद्धूर्णबलः ईशानकृत् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who is our giver of wealth and the like, may that Indra be our father, our protector. What is he like? Great, mature; mighty (उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)), of surging strength; ईशानकृत् (*īśānakṛt*),

### Printed p. 609

> दीनमहानां प्रभुं करोतीति तथा । दीनदयालुरित्यर्थः । तादृशः स मघवा
> धनवानिं व्रति नोऽस्मभ्यं गोः गामश्वस्य अश्वं च । उभयत्र कर्मणि षष्ठि । प्रदातु
> प्रकर्षण वदातु । कीदृशो मघवा । आयामन् । यांत्यनेनेति यामा मार्गः ।
> स न विवृते यस्यासावयामा । तस्मिन्नयामनि । सुपां सुलुक् इति सप्तम्या लुक् ।
> मार्गदर्शिते पाधिनि पुंसि उग्रः उद्दूर्णबलः तस्मिन् आविष्कृतप्रभुशक्तिरित्यर्थः ।
> पुरुषसुश्च प्रभूतगवाश्वादिधनोपेतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

one who makes lords of the poor **NOTE**; the meaning is that he is compassionate to the poor. May such a Maghavan, a wealthy one, give to us (प्रदातु (*pradātu*), give forth) a cow and a horse. What is the Maghavan like? आयामन् (*āyāman*): यामा (*yāmā*) is a path, that by which one goes; the sense is that, in a man who has been shown the way, he is mighty, of surging strength, and has made manifest his lordly power; and he is पुरुवसुः (*puruvasuḥ*), possessed of abundant wealth in cattle, horses and the like. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महान् (*mahān*)—the great
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—of exceeding strength
- ईशानकृत् (*īśānakṛt*)—who makes even the powerless a lord
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दाता (*dātā*)—is an excellent giver
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- पिता (*pitā*)—may be a protector
- अयामन् (*ayāman*)—free of the path of sin
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—terrible
- पुरूवसुः (*purūvasuḥ*)—possessed of abundant wealth
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- गोः (*goḥ*)—cows
- अश्वस्य (*aśvasya*)—horses
- प्र दातु (*pra dātu*)—may he supply and give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Indra, who is great, of exceeding strength, one who makes the powerless a lord, and who is an excellent giver to us, be our protector. May Indra, free of the path of sin, terrible, and possessed of abundant wealth, supply and give us cows and horses.

##### English translation
He is our giver, he is our father, he is noble, ferocious, Lord of wealth. Ferocious Maghavan, May Indra Lord of abnndance grant us cattle and horses.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्मै॒ त्वं व॑सो दा॒नाय॒ मंह॑से॒ स रा॒यस्पोष॑मिन्वति ।  
> व॒सू॒यवो॒ वसु॑पतिं श॒तक्र॑तुं॒ स्तोमै॒रिंद्रं॑ हवामहे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्मै । त्वं । वसो इति । दानाय । मंहसे । सः । रायः । पोषं । इन्वति ।  
> वसुयवः । वसुपतिं । शतक्रतुं । स्तोमैः । इंद्रं । हवामहे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 610

> हे वसो वासयितरिंद्र त्वं यस्मै यजमानाय दातव्यं धनादिकं मंहसे
> ददासि स तादृशो यजमानः रायः धनस्य पोषं पुष्टिं इन्वति व्याप्नोति ! धनसमृद्धिं प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । आतो हे इंद्र वसूयवः धनकामा वयं यजमाना
> वसुपतिं धनपालकं शतक्रतुं बहुकर्माणं इंद्र परमेश्वर ( ? इंद्रं परमेश्वरं)
> त्वां स्तोत्रैः हवामहे आह्वयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasu, Indra, who causes to dwell, the sacrificer to whom you give (मंहसे (*maṃhase*)) the wealth and the like that is to be given obtains (इन्वति (*invati*)) the increase of wealth; that is, he attains abundance of wealth. Therefore, O Indra, we sacrificers who desire wealth (वसूयवः (*vasūyavaḥ*)) call with praises you, the lord of wealth, protector of wealth, doer of many rites, Indra, the Supreme Lord. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसो (*vaso*)—O Indra, giver of a dwelling
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—to which sacrificer
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—things fit to be given
- मंहसे (*maṃhase*)—you give
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- पोषं (*poṣaṃ*)—the increase
- इन्वति (*invati*)—obtains
- वसुयवः (*vasuyavaḥ*)—we who are desirous of wealth
- वसुपतिं (*vasupatiṃ*)—the lord of wealth
- शतक्रतुं (*śatakratuṃ*)—the doer of many rites
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- स्तोमैः (*stomaiḥ*)—with praises
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of a dwelling, the sacrificer to whom you give things fit to be given obtains the increase of wealth. We, who are desirous of wealth, call with prayer with praises Indra, the lord of wealth and the doer of many rites.

##### English translation
Indra, whom you wishes to give, his wealth goes increasing Desirous of wealth we invoke Vasumati and Satakritu with praises.

> क॒दा च॒न प्र यु॑च्छस्यु॒भे नि पा॑सि॒ जन्म॑नी ।

> इदानीमृषिः सूर्यरूपेणेंद्रं सौति । हे अंद्र कदाचन कदापि त्वं प्र

> जगदात्वरूपेणेशि द्वे जनुषी । नि पासि नितरां पालयसि । न ह्यसावधानः प्रपंचं
> परमार्थं च उभयं कर्तुं शक्नुयात् कश्चितिति भावः । हे तुरीय प्रत्यगात्मरूपेण अवस्थात्रयातीत दे आदित्य आदितिपुत्र इंद्र ते तव स्वभूतमिंद्रियमिंद्रस्य
> तव लिंगं होतकं हवनं । हूयतेऽस्मिन्निति हवनमादित्यमंडलं । अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते इति स्मृतेरादित्यमंडलस्य होमाधिष्ठानत्वं प्रसिद्धं ।
> तादृशं मंडलं अमृतं मरणधर्मरहितं सत् दिवि द्युलोके आ तस्मा अभिमुख्येनातिष्ठत् ! यस्मात्त्वं जगदात्मासीत्यतस्त्वां हवामह इति पूर्वणान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now the seer praises Indra in the form of the Sun. O Indra, you never become heedless; the sense is that you are wakeful by day and by night. For you have two births: the first as Indra, from Aditi, and the second, from the knowledge of Brahman, in the form of the Self of the world **NOTE**. You protect both thoroughly, for no one who was not attentive could accomplish both the world and the highest reality. O Turīya, who in the form of the inner Self are beyond the three states, O Āditya, son of Aditi, O Indra, your own indriya, the mark that makes you known, is the havana, that is, the orb of the Sun, since that is where the oblation is offered. That the orb of the Sun is the seat of the homa is well known from the Smṛti: अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते (*agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate*). That orb, free from mortality, stood facing you in heaven. Because you are the Self of the world, we call upon you; thus it is connected with the earlier part.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कदा चन (*kadā cana*)—when, ever
- प्र युच्छसि (*pra yucchasi*)—do you forget your duty
- उभे जन्मनी (*ubhe janmanī*)—both births, in their eternal and non-eternal forms
- नि पासि (*ni pāsi*)—you protect completely
- तुरीय (*turīya*)—you who stand in the most excellent fourth state
- आदित्य (*āditya*)—O Indra, who are of the form of Āditya
- ते (*te*)—your
- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—that which reveals your nature
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—that which is everlasting
- हवनं (*havanaṃ*)—the orb of Āditya
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the world of heaven
- आ तस्थौ (*ā tasthau*)—has been established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, there is no time at all when you forget your duty. You are always watchful, and you protect completely both births, in their eternal and non-eternal forms. O Indra, of the form of Āditya, who stand in the most excellent fourth state, your orb of Āditya, which reveals your nature and is everlasting, has been established in the world of heaven.

##### English translation
Never do you fall into error ; you protect both kind. Speedy Aditya the blazing invocation for you rests in heaven.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्मै॒ त्वं म॑घवन्निंद्र गिर्वणः॒ शिक्षो॒ शिक्ष॑सि दा॒शुषे॑ ।  
> अ॒स्माकं॒ गिर॑ उ॒त सु॑ष्टु॒तिं व॑सो कण्व॒वच्छृ॑णुधी॒ हनं ॥ ८ ॥॑

### Printed p. 612

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्मै । त्वं । मघवन् । इंद्र । गिर्वणः । शिक्षो इति । शिक्षसि । दाशुषे ।  
> आस्माकं । गिरः । उत । सुस्तुतिं । वसो इति । कण्ववत् । शृणुधि । हवं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन् हे गिर्वणः गीर्भिर्वननीय हे शिक्षो शिक्षकेंद्र दाशुषे
> हविर्दत्तवते यस्मै यजमानाय शिक्षसि अपेक्षितं धनादि ददासि तत्संबंधिनामस्माकं
> गिरः प्रार्थनावाचः शृणुधि शृणु । उतापि च हे वसो वासयितरिंद्र सुष्टुतिं
> शोभनां स्तुतिं शृणुधि । किंच कण्ववत् यथा कण्वस्य हवमाह्वानमकृणोः
> एवमस्माकं हवं शृणु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, possessor of wealth; O Girvaṇaḥ, you who are to be served with songs; O Śikṣu, Indra the giver: to whichever sacrificer has offered the oblation you give the wealth and other things he desires; hear the prayer-words of us who belong to that sacrificer. And, O Vasu, Indra who causes dwelling, hear the good praise. Further, as you answered the call of Kaṇva, so hear our call.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—you who are praised with hymns
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—you who possess wealth
- शिक्षो (*śikṣo*)—you who are the instructor
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—who offers the oblation
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—to whichever sacrificer
- शिक्षसि (*śikṣasi*)—you give the gift of wealth
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—of us, who belong to that same sacrificer
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the words of praise
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सुष्टुतिं (*suṣṭutiṃ*)—the praise-accompanied
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—invocation
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Indra, giver of dwelling
- कण्ववत् (*kaṇvavat*)—as you heard the prayer of Kaṇva
- शृणुधि (*śṛṇudhi*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, praised with hymns, wealthy, an instructor: to whichever sacrificer who offers the oblation you give the gift of wealth, the words of praise of us who belong to that same sacrificer, and our invocation accompanied by praise, O Indra, giver of dwelling, hear as you heard the prayer of Kaṇva.

##### English translation
Worshipable, liberal Maghavan you give to the sacrificer; giver of dwellings, as you did hear of the invocation of Kanwa likewise do you hear our words, praises and invocation.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्ता॑वि॒ मन्म॑ पू॒र्व्यं ब्रह्मेंद्रा॑य वोचत ।  
> पू॒र्वीर्यु॒तस्य॑ बृह॒तीर॑नूषत स्तो॒तुर्मे॒धा अ॑सृक्षत ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 613

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्तावि : मन्म । पूर्व्यं । ब्रह्म । इंद्राय । वोचित ।  
> पूर्वः ' यतस्य । बृहतीः । अनूषत । स्तोतुः । मेधाः । अस्पृश्यत ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋत्विजः मन्म मननीयं पूर्व्यं पुरातनं यत् ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं असावि
> (अस्ताः स्तुतिविषयीकृतं भवद्भिस्तत् ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं इंद्राय परमेश्वराय
> तदर्थं वोचत ब्रूत । यतो भवंतः ऋतस्य सत्यस्येंद्रस्य संबंधिनीः पूर्वीः
> बृहतिः बृहतीः महतीः । सामर्थ्यार्ति मूर्तिः इंद्रस्य प्रचुरान् महतो गुणावतारानित्यर्थः । अनूषत स्तुतिविषयीकृतवंतः किंच स्तोतुर्मम आयोः मेधाः
> धारणावतीः बुद्धीः असृक्षत सृष्टवंतः । अतः प्रार्थये ब्रह्मेंद्राय वोचतेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests, the ancient hymn that is fit for contemplation, the brahma, which has been praised, direct to Indra, the Supreme Lord. For you have praised the many great manifestations connected with Ṛta, that is, with the true Indra; that is, the many great incarnations of his qualities **NOTE**. Moreover you have produced the retentive understandings of me, the praiser **NOTE**. Therefore I pray: speak the hymn for Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—belonging to Indra, who is of the nature of truth
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—many
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—great, the hymns
- अनूषत (*anūṣata*)—you have recited
- स्तोतुः (*stotuḥ*)—of me, the praiser
- मेधाः (*medhāḥ*)—the understanding
- आसृक्षत (*āsṛkṣata*)—you have refined; therefore
- मन्म (*manma*)—that which is of the nature of meditation
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—ancient
- अस्तावि (*astāvi*)—which praise has been recited in former times
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—such an excellent hymn
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—addressed to Indra
- वोचत (*vocata*)—recite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, you have recited many kinds of great hymns belonging to Indra, who is of the nature of truth, and have refined the understanding of me, the praiser. Therefore recite, addressed to Indra, that excellent hymn which is of the nature of meditation, which is ancient, and which has been recited in former times.

##### English translation
Sing ancient hymns in praise of Indra, Sing the grand hyman before the rite and animate the body of the worshippers.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रः बृहतीः महांति रायः हिरण्यादिधनानि समधूनुत सम्यगकरोत् ।
> यश्चेंद्रः क्षोणी द्यावापृथिव्यौ समधूनुत समक् रचयांचक्रे । क्षोणी इति
> द्यावापृथिव्योर्नामधेयं । रोदसी क्षोणी अंधसी इति तन्नामसु पातात् ।
> किंच य इंद्रः सूर्यं मंगलात्मानु समधूनुत समजनयत् । तमिंद्रं शुक्रासः
> शुक्लाः दीप्ताः शुचयः पूताः आपः वसतीवर्येकधनाः लक्षणाः सममंदिषुः
> सम्यगमावयन् ॥ किंच गवाशिरः गोदुग्धं सोमाः तद्रसाश्च तमिंद्रं
> सममंदिषुः । इत्थं महानुभाव इंद्रोऽसीति त्ववर्थं ब्रह्म पोचत इति पूर्णेण
> संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who shook together, that is, rightly produced, great riches, gold and the like; and who fashioned together heaven and earth, for kṣoṇī is a name of heaven and earth, as in the lists of their names, rodasī, kṣoṇī, andhasī **NOTE**; and who also brought forth the Sun, the auspicious one **NOTE**: that Indra the bright, shining, pure waters exhilarated together **NOTE**. And the Somas, the juices of the cow's milk, exhilarated that Indra. Thus you are of great power, Indra; therefore speak the hymn for you; so it is connected with the earlier part.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—great
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- समधूनुत (*samadhūnuta*)—has provided
- क्षोणी (*kṣoṇī*)—heaven and earth
- सं (*saṃ*)—has rightly fashioned
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the Sun
- समु (*samu*)—has created
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—that same Indra
- शुक्रासः (*śukrāsaḥ*)—the radiant
- शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*)—the pure
- गवाशिरः (*gavāśiraḥ*)—mixed with milk and other supporting substances
- सोमाः (*somāḥ*)—the Soma juices
- सं अमंदिषुः (*saṃ amaṃdiṣuḥ*)—have made content

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra has provided all of us with great wealth. He has rightly fashioned heaven and earth. He has created the Sun. The Soma juices, radiant, pure and mixed with milk and other supporting substances, have made that same Indra content.

### Printed p. 615

##### English translation
Indra sends vast wealth, sends to the world the sun, creates the heaven and earth; white coloured, pure Soma mixed with milk exhilarated Indra.

## Sūkta 53 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta of eight Ṛks beginning उपमं त्वा (*upamaṃ tvā*) is the fifth, the vision of Medhya Kāṇva. It is listed in the Anukramaṇikā: उपमं त्वाष्ट मेध्यः (*upamaṃ tvāṣṭa medhyaḥ*). The metre of the odd-numbered Ṛks is Bṛhatī; the metre of the even-numbered is Satobṛhatī. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning उपमं त्वा (*upamaṃ tvā*) is the fifth among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is one called Medhyaḥ Kāṇvaḥ; Indra is the deity. The odd-numbered Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Bṛhatī metre; the even-numbered Ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: उपमं त्वाष्टौ (*upamaṃ tvāṣṭau*). The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 53; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 22, 23. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Seer: Medhyaḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: Indraḥ. Metre: Prāgāthaṃ (odd Ṛks Bṛhatī; even Ṛks Satobṛhatī).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒प॒मं त्वा॑ म॒घोनां॒ ज्येष्ठं॑ च वृष॒भाणां॑ ।  
> पू॒र्भित्त॑मं मघवन्निंद्र गो॒विद॒मीशा॑नं रा॒य ई॑महे ॥

### Printed p. 616

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उपमं । त्वा । मघोनां । ज्येष्ठं । च । वृषभाणां ।  
> पूर्भित्सतमं । मघवन् । इंद्र । गोऽविदं । ईशानं । रायः । ईमहे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघुवन् धनवन्निंद्रॆ मघोनां धनवतां मध्ये उपमं उपमाभूतं
> वृषभाणां कामवर्षित्यणां मध्ये ज्येष्ठं अतिशयेन प्रशस्यं च त्वा त्वा रायः
> गवाश्वादिधनानि ईमहे याचामहे वयं । कीदृशं त्वां । पूर्भित्तमं अतिशयेनशत्रुपुरां भेत्तारमत एव गोविदं गवां लंभयितारं ईशानं सर्वपिद्यानां
> नियंतारं । ईशानः सर्वविद्यानां—(त्रै. आ. १०-४७) इति श्रुतेः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, Indra, wealthy one: among the wealthy you are the model, and among the bulls, the showerers of desires, you are the eldest, that is, the most to be praised. We ask of you riches, cows, horses and the like. What kind of you? One who most splits the cities of enemies, and so a finder of cows, a ruler, the controller of all knowledge, according to the Śruti ईशानः सर्वविद्यानां (*īśānaḥ sarvavidyānāṃ*) (Trai. Ā. 10-47) **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—you who possess wealth
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—among all the wealthy
- उपमं (*upamaṃ*)—the model
- वृषभाणां (*vṛṣabhāṇāṃ*)—among all the bestowers of desired things
- ज्येषं च (*jyeṣaṃ ca*)—and the foremost
- पूर्भित्तमं (*pūrbhittamaṃ*)—who splits the enemy's cities
- गोविदं (*govidaṃ*)—who obtains the cows held by enemies
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—the lord of all
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you, from you
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, you are the model among all the wealthy, the foremost among the bestowers of desired things, one who splits the enemy's cities, one who obtains the cows held by enemies, and the lord of all. From you I ask wealth.

##### English translation
We approach you Maghavan, the chief amongst the wealthy, penetrator into enemies fortress, Lord of wealth and our Lord, I pray for wealth from you.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य आ॒युं कुत्स॑मतिथि॒ग्वमर्द॑यो वावृधा॒नो दि॒वेदि॑वे ।  
> तं त्वा॑ व॒यं हर्य॑श्वं श॒तक्र॑तुं वाज॒यंतो॑ हवामहे ॥

### Printed p. 617

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । आयुं । कुत्सं । अतिथिग्वं । आर्दयः । ववृधानः । दिवेऽदिवे ।  
> तं । त्वा । वयं । हरिऽश्वं । शतक्रतुं । वाजयंतः । हवामहे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यस्त्वं दिवेदिवे प्रतिदिनं नावृधानः स्तुत्यः अतिशयेन वर्धमानः
> सन् आयुं एतन्नामानदृषिं उत्सं एतत्संज्ञमृषिं अतिथिग्वं एतत्संज्ञमृषिं
> च आर्दयः वरप्रदाने (?वरप्रदानेन) पीडयसि । आत्मानं अलं मन्यमानाः
> वारयंति । त्वं तु हठात् अभिष्टवरं याचते (? याचत) इत्युक्ता तान्
> क्लेशयसीत्यर्थः ! तं तादृशं हर्यश्वं हरिसंज्ञौ अश्वै यस्य तादृशं बहुकर्माणं
> त्वा त्वां वाजवंतः (?यंतः) अन्नकामा वयं यजमानाः हवामहे आह्वयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who, being praised day by day, grow exceedingly, afflict the seers Āyu, Kutsa and Atithigva by granting boons. Those who think themselves sufficient refuse; but you, saying "he asks the boon he wishes" without hesitation, trouble them **NOTE**. Such a one, having the two horses named Hari, the doer of many rites, you, we sacrificers who desire food, call upon.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who (O Indra)
- दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)—every day
- वद्वधानः (*vadvadhānaḥ*)—obtaining increase
- आयुं (*āyuṃ*)—Āyu
- कुत्सं (*kutsaṃ*)—Kutsa
- अतिथिग्वं (*atithigvaṃ*)—Atithigva
- आर्दयः (*ārdayaḥ*)—have afflicted by granting boons and the like (have protected)
- तं (*taṃ*)—such
- हर्यश्वं (*haryaśvaṃ*)—one who has horses named Hari
- शतक्रतुं (*śatakratuṃ*)—doer of many rites
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- षयं (*ṣayaṃ*)—we
- वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring food
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call, praying

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who, growing day by day, have protected Āyu, Kutsa and Atithigva by granting boons and the like, you who have horses named Hari and do many rites, you we call, praying, desiring food.

##### English translation
He who every day increasing in strength protected Ayu, Kutsa, and Athithigva, we invoke that Indra Satakritu, Lord of horses named Hari, for food.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॒ विश्वे॑षां॒ रसं॒ मध्वः॑ सिंचं॒त्वद्र॑यः ।  
> ये प॑रा॒वति॑ सुन्वि॒रे जने॒ष्टा ये अ॑र्वा॒वतींद॑वः ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 618

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अ । नः । विश्वेषां । रसं । मध्वः । सिंचंतु । अद्रयः ।  
> ये । परावति । सुन्विरे । जनेषु । आ । ये । अर्वावति । इंदवः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वेषां सर्वॆषां नोऽस्माकं संबंधिनः अद्रयः । तात्स्थात् ताच्छब्दं ।
> अद्रिप्रभवास्ते सोमाः मध्वः मधुरं । कर्मणि षष्ठी । रसमात्मीयं द्रवमासिंचंतु कार्त्स्नन क्षरंतु । इंद्रार्थमिति शेषः । ते के । ये इंदवः सोमाः
> परावति दूरदेशे वर्तमानाः । जनेषु यजमानलक्षणेषु निमित्तेषु आ सुन्विरे
> अभिमुख्येन अभिषुता ऋत्विग्निः । ये च इंदवः अर्नवति समीपदेशे वर्तमानाः
> सुन्विरे अभिषुतास्ते सर्वॆऽपि मिलित्वा इंद्रार्थं स्वरसं सिंचंतित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Let the Somas born from the stones, which belong to all of us, pour out completely their own sweet juice; the supplement is "for Indra". Which are they? The Somas that are pressed far away, on account of the sacrificers, facing Indra, by the priests; and those that are pressed near at hand. All of them, joining together, pour their own juice for Indra. That is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये इंदवः (*ye iṃdavaḥ*)—which Soma juices
- परावति (*parāvati*)—in a distant region
- जनेषु (*janeṣu*)—for the sacrificers
- आ सुन्विरे (*ā sunvire*)—are pressed by the priests
- ये (*ye*)—which juices
- अर्वावति (*arvāvati*)—are pressed in a near region, such ones also
- विश्वेषां नः (*viśveṣāṃ naḥ*)—belonging to all of us
- अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*)—the Somas pressed with the stones
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—sweet
- रसं (*rasaṃ*)—juice
- आ सिंचंतु (*ā siṃcaṃtu*)—let them pour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma juices that are pressed by the priests for the sacrificers in a distant region, and those that are pressed in a near region, such ones, belonging to all of us, the Somas pressed with the stones, let them pour sweet juice.

##### English translation
All the Somas that are effused far away and those that are effused here, all the Soma that are effused by grinding stone become sweet.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वा॒ द्वेषां॑सि ज॒हि चाव॒ चा कृ॑धि॒ विश्वे॑ सन्वं॒त्वा वसु॑ ।  
> शीष्टे॑षु चित्ते मदि॒रासो॑ अं॒शवो॒ यत्रा॒ सोम॑स्य तृं॒पसि॑ ॥

### Printed p. 619

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पत्वा । द्वेषांसि । जहि । च । अव । च । आ । कृधि । विश्वे । सन्वंतु । आ । वसु ।  
> तीष्टेषु । चित् । ते । मदिरासः । अंशवः । यत्र । सोमस्य । शृंपसि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दे इंद्र विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि द्वेषांसि अस्माकममित्राणि जहि नाशय । किंचास्मान् अव रक्ष । आ च कृधि आ समंतात् प्रशस्तान् कुरु च । किंच विश्वे सर्वे जनाः
> पसु धनं आ सन्वंतु अभिमुख्येन ददतु । अस्मभ्यमिति शेषः । अथ च यत्र येष्टस्मासु
> स्थितस्य सोमस्य तृंपसि पानेन तृप्तो भवसि । तेषु शीष्टेषु विशिष्टेष्टस्मासु
> वर्तमानाः अंशवः सोमाः ते चित् तवैव मदिरासः मादकाः संतु नेतरस्य
> कस्यचित् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, destroy all our hatreds, that is, our enemies. Further, protect us, and make us well praised on every side. Moreover let all people bestow wealth upon us, facing us; "to us" is the supplement. And among those of us in whom you become satisfied by drinking the Soma, among those distinguished ones of us, let the Soma stalks be intoxicating to you alone, not to anyone else.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*)—the enemy people
- जहि चॆ (*jahi cè*)—defeat
- अव चॆ (*ava cè*)—protect us
- आ कृधि (*ā kṛdhi*)—do us fully good
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all **NOTE**
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth also
- आ सन्वंतु (*ā sanvaṃtu*)—let it come together for us
- यत्र (*yatra*)—among which sacrificers
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by the drinking of Soma juice
- तृंपसि (*tṛṃpasi*)—you attain satisfaction
- शीष्टेषु (*śīṣṭeṣu*)—among all such of us
- अंशवः (*aṃśavaḥ*)—the Somas
- ते चित् (*te cit*)—to you alone
- मदिरासः (*madirāsaḥ*)—let them be delight-giving

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, defeat all the enemy people and protect us. Do us fully good. Let all wealth also come together for us. Let the Somas among all of us, among whom you attain satisfaction by the drinking of Soma juice, be delight-giving to you alone.

##### English translation
Whereeever you are satisfied with the drink of Soma you subdue and and destroy all enemies; even among the well-behaved Soma is exhilarating you.

### Printed p. 620

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॒ नेदी॑य॒ एदि॑हि मि॒तमे॑धाभिरू॒तिभिः॑ ।  
> आ शं॑तम॒ शंत॑माभिर॒भिष्टि॑भि॒रा स्वा॑पे स्वा॒पिभिः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । नेदीयः । आ । इत् । इहि । मितमेधाभिः । ऊतिभिः ।  
> आ । शंततम । शंतमाभिः । अभिष्टिभिः । आ । सुआपे । स्वापिभिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र परमेश्वर त्वं मितमेधाभिः मिताः परिच्छिन्नाः मेधाः अनुग्रहबुद्धयः याभिस्ताभिरनुग्रहसहिताभिः ऊतिभिः रक्षाभिः सह नेदीय इत् अंतिकतममेव एहि आगच्छ । किंच हे शंतम सुखतमेंद्र शंतमाभिरभिष्टिभिरभितः प्रियाभिश्च
> ऊतिभिः एहि । अथ च हे स्वापे सुतरामाप्तेंद्र स्वापिभिः शोभना आपयः आप्ता
> बंधवः यासु ताभिरूतिभिरेहि । उपसर्गवशादोग्य क्रियाध्याहारः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, Supreme Lord, come to the very nearest, together with protections that are accompanied by favour; the "limited thoughts" are the thoughts of favour that they contain. Further, O Śantama, most pleasant Indra, come with protections that are dear on every side. And O Svāpi, Indra who are exceedingly near, come with protections in which there are good kinsmen, that is, trusted friends. By the force of the prefix the verb "come" is supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मितमेधाभिः (*mitamedhābhiḥ*)—accompanied by your thought of favour
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—with protections
- नेदीयः इत् (*nedīyaḥ it*)—so as to be very near to us
- एहि (*ehi*)—come graciously
- शंतमाभिः (*śaṃtamābhiḥ*)—most pleasant-making
- अभिष्टिभिः (*abhiṣṭibhiḥ*)—with the fulfilments of our desires
- शंतम (*śaṃtama*)—O Indra, giver of the best happiness
- आ (इहि) (*ā (ihi)*)—come graciously
- स्थापे (*sthāpe*)—O Indra, the excellent kinsman
- स्वापिभिः (*svāpibhiḥ*)—with your excellent kinship
- आ (इहि) (*ā (ihi)*)—come graciously

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, come graciously so as to be very near us, with protections accompanied by your thought of favour. O Indra, the best, come graciously with the fulfilments of our desires that give most happiness. O Indra, the trusted one, come graciously with your excellent kinship.

##### English translation
Indra you are the first blessings, very much a friend, properly wise, granter of blessings, fulfiller of desires like a friend come with protection.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒जि॒तुरं॒ सत्प॑तिं वि॒श्वच॑र्षणिं कृ॒धि प्र॒जास्वाभ॑गं ।  
> प्र सू ति॑रा॒ शची॑भि॒र्ये त॑ उ॒क्षिनः॒ क्रतुं॑ पुन॒त आ॑नु॒षक् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अजितुरं ; सत्पतिं । विश्वचर्षणिं । कृधि । प्रजासु । आभगं ।  
> प्र । सु । तिर । शचीभिः । ये । ते । उक्तिनः । क्रतुं । पुनते । अनुषक् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं प्रजासु अस्मत्पुत्रपौत्रादिषु आभगं अभिमख्येन भगं भजनीयं
> धनं कृधि कुरु । कीदृशं । आजितुरं संग्रामे त्वरमाणं । जित्वरमित्यर्थः । सत्पतिं
> सतां पालकं विश्वचर्षणिं । विश्वाः सर्वाश्चर्यणयो मनुष्याः दासदासीलक्षणा
> यस्मिन् तं । किंच ये यजमानाः उक्तिनः स्तुतिमतस्ते तव अनुषक् अनुषक्तं ।
> त्वया संगतमित्यर्थः । क्रतुं कर्मविशेषं पुनते कुर्वते । तानस्मान् शचीभिः
> धनप्रदानादिकर्मभिः सु सुतरां प्रतिर प्रवर्धय । प्र पूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, make for us among our progeny, sons, grandsons and the rest, a share, that is, desirable wealth, facing us. What kind of wealth? Hastening in battle, that is, victorious; protector of the good; that in which all people, in the form of male and female servants, are included. Moreover those sacrificers who have praise perform for you, in union with you, a particular rite. Increase us, those same ones, thoroughly by your deeds such as the giving of wealth. The verb meaning "increase" is the one made with the prefix.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रजासु (*prajāsu*)—among our sons, grandsons and the rest
- आजितुरं (*ājituraṃ*)—that brings victory in battle
- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—that protects good people
- विश्वचर्षणिं (*viśvacarṣaṇiṃ*)—that is filled with all people, sons, grandsons and the rest
- आ भगं (*ā bhagaṃ*)—that is fit for enjoyment, the wealth
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—establish
- ये उक्तिनः (*ye uktinaḥ*)—we who are provided with recitations and hymns
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—always
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you alone
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—the rite
- पुनते (*punate*)—we who accomplish it, such ones, us
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by your auspicious deeds
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- प्रतिर (*pratira*)—cause us to increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, establish among our sons, grandsons and the rest the wealth that brings victory in battles, protects good people, is filled with all people, sons, grandsons and the rest, and is fit for enjoyment. Us, who are provided with recitations and the like and always accomplish the rite addressed to you alone, cause to increase exceedingly by your auspicious deeds.

### Printed p. 622

##### English translation
Quick in battle, nourisher of the righteous, Lord of all, to the worship such Indra amongst the people, may those worshippers who by action bring good fruit, sing hymns and continue without a break to perform the rite.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्ते॒ साधि॒ष्मोऽव॑से॒ ते स्या॑नु॒ भरे॑षु ते ।  
> व॒यं होत्रा॑भिरु॒त दे॒वहू॑तिभिः सस॒वांसो॑ मनामदे । ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । ते । साधिष्ठः । अवसे । ते । स्याम । भरेषु । ते ।  
> वयं । होत्राभिः । उत । देवहूतिभिः । ससनांसः । मनामहे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यः अस्मद्दणः अवसे रक्षणाय ते तव साधिषः अतिशयेन योऽस्ति
> तद्गणगतास्ते वयं भरेषु संग्रामेषु ते तव संबंधिनः स्याम । भवेम । संगते
> त्वत्पालनीया भवेमेत्यर्थः । उतापि च हे इंद्र ससवांस हनिर्लक्षणान्नवंतः ।
> ससमित्यन्ननाम । नेमः ससं इत्यन्ननामसु पाठात् । तादृशा वयं यजमानाः
> देवहूतिभिः । देवानिंद्रादीन् हवंति ता देवहूतयः । ताभी होत्राभिः
> वाग्निस्तुतिलक्षणाभिः त्वां मनामहे स्तुमः । होत्रेति वाङ्माम । ऋक् होत्रा
> गीः—इति वाज्ञामसु पाठात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the group of ours that is the most excellent for protection, belonging to you, we who belong to that group, may we be yours in battles; that is, in battle may we be protected by you. Moreover, O Indra, we sacrificers who have food in the form of oblations, the word for food, as it is read in the list of names of food, नेमः ससं (*nemaḥ sasaṃ*), with the calls to the gods, that is, the speeches that call the gods Indra and the rest, with these hotrās, that is, praises in the form of speech, praise you. The word for these praises is a name of speech, as it is read in the list of names of speech.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—among those who belong to you
- साधिष्ठः (*sādhiṣṭhaḥ*)—the most excellent
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whatever group of sacrificers there is, we who have it

### Printed p. 623

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, among the groups of sacrificers who belong to you, it is we who are the most excellent. Grant that we, such as we are, may be under your shelter in battles for our protection. And we, who possess the oblation, praise you with praise-words fit for calling the gods.

##### English translation
May we have all that are best of you, we shall seek your protection and we shall invoke you. We shall sing hymns in invocation of you we shall worship you and praise you.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हं हि ते॑ हरिवो॒ ब्रह्म॑ वाज॒युरा॒जिं यामि॒ सदो॒तिभिः॑ ।  
> त्वामिदे॒व तममे॒ सम॑श्व॒युर्ग॒व्युरग्रे॑ मथी॒नां ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आहं । हि । ते । हरिऽवः । ब्रह्म । वाजययुः । आजिं । यामि । सदा । ऊतिऽभिः ।  
> त्वां । इत् । एव । तं । अमे । सं । अश्वययुः । गव्युः । अग्रे । मथीनां ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे हरिवः हरिसंज्ञकाश्वोपेतेंद्र ते त्वदीयः योऽहं मेध्य ऋषिः
> पाजयुः अन्नकामः सन् ब्रह्म अन्नमुद्धिश्य सदा सर्वदा ऊतिभिः त्वत्कृताभिः
> रक्षाभिः सह आजिं संग्रामं यामि प्राप्नोमि । हीति प्रसिद्धं । त्वामेव सं अमे
> संगतो भवामि । संग्रामे त्वामेषाश्रयामि । नेतरं कंचनेत्यर्थः । एवेत्यनर्फको निपातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Harivas, Indra, you who have the horses named Hari, I, who belong to you, the seer Medhya, desiring food, always go to battle for the sake of food together with the protections made by you. The word "hi" means "as is well known". I unite myself with you alone; in battle I take refuge in you alone, in no other. That is the meaning. The word "eva" is a meaningless particle.

- गव्युः (*gavyuḥ*)—and desiring cows, I who am such

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who have horses named Hari, I, desiring food, always go to battle together with your protections in order to obtain food. I, desiring horses and desiring cows, face the terrible enemies, taking with me you alone, the renowned, and fighting together with you **NOTE**.

##### English translation
Indra Lord of the horse named Hari, desirous of food, horse and cattle we are invoking you and under your protection go to you; when we are overtaken with fear, place you before the enemies.

## Sūkta 54 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta of eight Ṛks beginning एतत्ते (*etatte*) is the sixth, the vision of Kāṇva Mātariśvān **NOTE**, addressed to Indra. It is listed in the Anukramaṇikā: एतत्ते मातरिश्वा नो विश्व इति वैश्वदेवः (*etatte mātariśvā no viśva iti vaiśvadevaḥ*), a Prāgātha. The third and fourth Ṛks have the Viśve Devāḥ as deity; of the other six the deity is Indra. The metre of the odd-numbered Ṛks is Bṛhatī and that of the even-numbered is Satobṛhatī. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning एतत्ते (*etatte*) is the sixth among the Vālakhilya sūktas **NOTE**. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is one called Mātariśvā Kāṇvaḥ; the third and fourth Ṛks of this sūkta have the Viśve Devāḥ as deity. The remaining six Ṛks have Indra as deity. The odd-numbered Ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre; the even-numbered Ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: एतत्ते मातरिश्वा नो विश्व इति वैश्वदेवः प्रगाथः (*etatte mātariśvā no viśva iti vaiśvadevaḥ pragāthaḥ*). The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

### Printed p. 625

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 54; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 24, 25. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Seer: Mātariśvā Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: 1, 2, 5-8 Indraḥ; 3, 4 Viśve Devāḥ. Metre: Prāgāthaṃ (odd Ṛks Bṛhatī; even Ṛks Satobṛhatī).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒तत्त॑ इंद्र वी॒र्यं॑ गी॒र्भिर्गृ॒णंति॑ का॒रवः॑ ।  
> ते स्तोभं॑त॒ ऊर्ज॑मावन्घृत॒श्चुतं॑ पौ॒रासो॑ नक्षन्थि॒तिभिः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एतत् । ते । इंद्र । वीर्यं । गीःभिः । गृणंति । कारवः ।  
> ते । स्तोभंतः । ऊर्जं । अवन् । घृतश्चुतं । पौरासः । नक्षन् । धीतिभिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ये कारवः स्तोतारः ते तव संबंधि एतत् दृश्यमानं वृष्ट्यादिलक्षणसामर्थ्यं गीर्भिः स्तुतिरूपाभिर्वाग्भिः गृणंति स्तुवंति ते स्तोभंतः स्तोतारः
> ऊर्ज० अन्नं आवन् प्राप्नुवंति । किंच ते पौरासः पुरे भवाः स्तोतारः धीतिभिरंगुलीभिः धृतश्चुतं धृतस्राविणं गवादिगणं नक्षन् व्याप्नुवंति । त्वदनुग्रहात्
> गवादिपशून् अंगुलीभिः सर्वदा दुहंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, those singers, the praisers, praise with songs, that is, with words in the form of praise, this visible power of yours, which has the form of rain and the like. Those praisers, praising you, obtain strength, that is, food. Moreover those praisers who dwell in the city reach with their fingers the herd of cows and other animals that streams ghee. By your favour they always milk cows and other animals with their fingers. That is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- कारवः (*kāravaḥ*)—the praisers
- एतत् ते वीर्यं (*etat te vīryaṃ*)—this your prowess
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with praises
- गृणंति (*gṛṇaṃti*)—they praise
- ते (*te*)—they
- स्तोभंतः (*stobhaṃtaḥ*)—praising you
- ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)—food
- आवन् (*āvan*)—obtain
- पौरासः (*paurāsaḥ*)—the sacrificers who dwell in the city
- धीशिभिः (*dhīśibhiḥ*)—with their fingers
- धृतश्चुतं (*dhṛtaścutaṃ*)—the cows that yield ghee and the like
- नक्षन् (*nakṣan*)—obtain

### Printed p. 626

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the praisers extol your prowess with praises. Praising you, they obtain food. They obtain cows that yield, through their fingers, milk and ghee and the like. (Or: by their rites, the dhīti, they accomplish the sacrifice that is filled with ghee and the like.)

##### English translation
Indra, the worshippers are singing the praise of your heroism, and by praising you attain strength. They have brought you sacrifices dropping ghee.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नक्षं॑त॒ इंद्र॒मव॑से सुकृ॒त्यया॒ येषां॑ सु॒तेषु॒ मंद॑से ।  
> यथा॑ संव॒र्ते अम॑दो॒ यथा॑ कृ॒श ए॒वास्मे इं॑द्र मत्स्व ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नक्षंते । इंद्रं । अवसे । सुकृत्यया । येषां । सुतेषु । मंदसे ।  
> यथा । संवर्ते । आमदः । यथा । कृशे । एव । अस्मे इति । इंद्र । मत्स्य ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र येषां यजमानानां संबंधिषु सुतेष्टभिषुतेषु सोमेषु
> निभातेषु (? निपीतेषु) त्वं मंदसे हृष्यसि ते यजमानाः अवसे अन्नाय रक्षणाय
> वा सुकृत्यया शोभनेन सोमाभिषवकर्मणा इंद्रं परमेश्वरं त्वां नक्षंते
> व्याप्नुवंती । नक्षतिर्वाप्तिकर्मा इन्वति नक्षति इति व्याप्तिकर्मसु पाठात् । अन्नाद्यर्थं
> त्वामाश्रयंत इत्यर्थः । अतो हे इंद्र यथा येन प्रकारेण संवर्ते एतन्नामके
> यषौ यजमाने सति आमदः हृष्टवानसि यथा च कृशे एतन्नाम्यि यजमाने
> आमदः एव एवमनेन प्रकारेण अस्मै अस्मासु काण्वेषु मत्स्य हृष्टो भव
> सोमपानादिनेति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, those sacrificers in whose pressed Somas **NOTE** you rejoice, those sacrificers reach you, the Supreme Lord, for food or for protection, by the good rite of the Soma-pressing. The verb for reaching has the sense of pervading, for it is read among words of pervading: इन्वति नक्षति इति व्याप्तिकर्मसु पाठात् (*invati nakṣati iti vyāptikarmasu pāṭhāt*). The meaning is that they take refuge in you for food and the like. Therefore, O Indra, as you rejoiced when the seer called Saṃvarta was the sacrificer, and as you rejoiced when the sacrificer was the one called Kṛśa, in this way rejoice in us, the Kāṇvas, by the drinking of Soma and the like; that is the supplement.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येषां (*yeṣāṃ*)—of which sacrificers
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—with the pressed Somas
- मंदसे (*maṃdase*)—you attain satisfaction (those same sacrificers)
- सुकृत्यया (*sukṛtyayā*)—by their excellent rites

### Printed p. 627

- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—you, who are the Lord
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- नक्षंते (*nakṣaṃte*)—they approach
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- संवर्ते (*saṃvarte*)—by the Soma-drinking in the seer called Saṃvarta
- आमदः (*āmadaḥ*)—you attained delight
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- कृशे (*kṛśe*)—you delighted by the Soma-drinking in the sacrificer called Kṛśa
- एव (*eva*)—in the same way
- आस्मे (*āsme*)—by the drinking of the Soma that is in us also
- मत्स्य (*matsya*)—attain delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, those sacrificers by whose offered Soma-drinking you attain satisfaction approach you, the Lord, for protection, by their excellent rites. O Indra, in the manner in which you attained delight by the Soma-drinking in the seer called Saṃvarta, and delighted by the Soma-drinking in the sacrificer called Kṛśa, in the same way attain delight by the drinking of the Soma that is in us also.

##### English translation
Indra, whose Soma exhilarates you, their righteous actions are reaching you; as you were favourably disposed to Samvarta and Krisa so be towards us.

> वस॑वो रु॒द्रा अव॑से न॒ आ ग॑मञ्छृ॒ण्वंतु॑ म॒रुतो॒ हवं॑ ॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । विश्वे । सजोषसः । देवासः । गंतन । उप । नः ।  
> वसवः । रुद्राः । अवसे । नः । आ । गमन् । शृण्वंतु । मरुतः । हवं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सजोषसः सह जुषमाणाः विश्वे देवासः सर्वॆ देवाः नोऽस्माकं यज्ञमुद्दिश्येति शेषः । नोऽस्माकमुप समीपे आ गंतन आगच्छंतु । किंच वसवोऽष्टौ
> रुद्रा एकादश च नोऽस्माकमवसे रक्षणाय आ गमन् आगच्छंतु । मरुतः एकोनपंचाशत्संख्याका देवास्तु हवमस्मत्कृतं स्तोत्रं शृण्वंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May all the gods, delighting together, come near to us, to our sacrifice; "to our sacrifice" is the supplement. Moreover, may the eight Vasus and the eleven Rudras come for our protection. May the Maruts, the gods numbering forty-nine, hear the praise made by us.

May all the gods, who show delight together, come to us to take part in our sacrifice. May the Vasus and the Rudras come for our protection. May the Maruts hear our praise.

May all the gods come to us being equally delighted. May Vashus and Rudras come for our protection, may Maruths hear our invocation ;

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पू॒षा विष्णु॒ र्हव॑नं मे॒ सर॑स्व॒त्यवं॑तु स॒प्त सिंध॑वः ।  
> आपो॒ वातः॒ पर्व॑तासो॒ वन॒स्पतिः॑ शृ॒णोतु॑ पृथि॒वी हवं॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पूषा । विष्णुः । हवनं । मे । सरस्वती । अवंतु । सप्त । सिंधवः ।  
> आपः । वातः । पर्वतासः । वनस्पतिः । शृणोतु । पृथिवी । हवं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूषा पोषको देवः विष्णुर्वापको देवः सरस्वती । सर इत्युदकनाम ।
> तद्वती देवी च एते सर्वॆ मे मम मातरिश्वानस्य (मातरिश्वनः) ऋषेः हवनमाह्वानं । स्तोत्रमिति यावत् । अवंतु शृण्वंतु । अवतिरत्र श्रवणकर्मा । अव रक्षणगति
> इत्यस्मिन् सूत्रे (?) तस्य श्रवणाभिधानात् । किंच सप्त सप्तसंख्याकाः सिंधवो
> गंगाद्या नद्य आपः जलाभिमानिन्यो देवताः वातो वायुः पर्वतास॥ पर्ववतां
> मेर्वादीनामभिमानिनो देवाश्च मे हवनं अवंतु शृण्वंतु । अथ च वनस्पतिः
> वनानां पातारः पालको (पालका) देवाः पृथिवी च देवी मे हवं स्तोत्रं
> शृणोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Pūṣan, the nourishing god; Viṣṇu, the pervading god; and the goddess Sarasvatī, for the word for water is सर इत्युदकनाम (*sara ityudakanāma*), so she is the goddess who has it: all these, may they hear my invocation, that is, my praise, mine, the seer Mātariśvān **NOTE**. The verb for protecting is used here in the sense of hearing, since in that Sūtra its meaning of hearing is given **NOTE**. Moreover the seven rivers, the Gaṅgā and the rest, the waters, that is, the deities who preside over water, the wind, and the mountains, that is, the gods who preside over mountains such as Meru, may they hear my invocation. And further the lords of the forests, the protecting gods, and the goddess Earth, may they hear my invocation, my praise.

- हवनं (*havanaṃ*)—invocation
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—let them hear
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the deities of the waters
- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—Vāyu, the wind
- पर्वतासः (*parvatāsaḥ*)—the mountains
- वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*)—the deity Vanaspati
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the goddess who presides over the earth
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—my invocation in the form of praise
- शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—let her hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, the goddess Sarasvatī and the seven rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā hear my invocation. May the deities of the waters, Vāyu, the mountains, the deity Vanaspati and the goddess who presides over the earth hear my invocation in the form of praise.

##### English translation
Pusha, Vishnu and Sarashvati, seven oceans, water, Vayu, Mountain and forests hear my call and protect me. May the earth hear my invocation.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदिं॑द्र॒ राधो॒ अस्ति॑ ते॒ माघो॑नं मघवत्तम ।  
> तेन॑ नो बोधि सध॒माद्यो॑ वृ॒धे भगो॑ दा॒नाय॑ वृत्रहन्॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । इंद्र । राधः । अस्ति । ते । माघोनं । मघवत्कतम ।  
> तेन । नः । बोधि । सध्वमाद्यः । वृधे । भगः । दानाय । वृत्तहन् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृत्रहंतरिंद्र त्वं दानार्थं वृधे वर्धनार्थं च नोऽस्मान् पात्रभूतान् बोधि
> बुध्यस्व । तद्धनदानेन आस्मान् समृद्धान् कर्तुं जानीहीत्यर्थः । कीदृशस्त्वं ।
> सधमाद्यः सहमादनयोग्यः भगो भजनीयश्च ॥

### Printed p. 630

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, most wealthy one, with that well-known wealth of yours, which has the wealthy one, that is, yourself, as its lord, and with that wealth, O slayer of Vṛtra, know us, who are fit recipients, for giving and for increase. That is, understand how to make us prosperous by the gift of that wealth. What kind of one are you? One fit to rejoice together with us, and one to be served.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवत्तम (*maghavattama*)—the most praiseworthy, the wealthy one
- सधमाद्यः (*sadhamādyaḥ*)—one fit to rejoice with us
- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—destroyer of enemies
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- माघोनं (*māghonaṃ*)—abounding in wealth
- यत् राधः (*yat rādhaḥ*)—whatever wealth and prosperity
- अस्ति (*asti*)—there is
- तेन (*tena*)—together with it
- वृधे (*vṛdhe*)—for the increase of our welfare
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—for making gifts to us
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know as belonging to you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, most praiseworthy and wealthy, who like to rejoice together with us, destroyer of enemies, together with whatever wealth and prosperity, abounding in riches, you have, know us as belonging to you, for the increase of our welfare and for making gifts to us.

##### English translation
Indra, Maghavan and killer of enemies grow your wealth, with it and be exhilarated for prosperity and gift ; you are worshipable.

> वी॒ती होत्रा॑भिरु॒त दे॒ववि॑तिभिः सस॒वांसो॒ वि शृ॑ण्वरे ॥ ६ ॥

> वीती । होत्राभिः । उत । देववीतिभिः । ससवांसः । वि । शृण्वरे ॥ ६ ॥

> हे सुक्रतो शोभनकर्मवन्निंद्र त्वमित् त्वमेव नोऽस्मान् वाजे संग्रामे
> आवक्षि अवहसि प्रापयसि । त्वत्साहाय्कॆन वयं धनार्थं संग्रामं गंतुमुत्सहामह इत्यर्थः । कीदैशस्त्वं । होत्राभिः स्तुतिलक्षणाभिः वाग्भिः सह । वीती अकनवान्
> स्तुतिभिः प्रोत्सहमानो हविरत्तेत्यर्थः । उतापि च ससवांसः हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतो

### Printed p. 631

> यजमानाः देवनीतिभिः देवकर्तृकाशनैः वि शृण्वरे । विशेषेण श्रूयंते । यदा
> हि त्वादृता देवास्त्रेषां हविरश्नुवंति तदा ते विख्याता भवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ājipati, protector of battle; O lord of leaders, protector of the leaders, that is, of the soldiers (the bhāṣya gives also the reading in brackets); O Indra of good deeds: you alone lead us into battle. That is, with your help we are eager to go to battle for the sake of wealth. What kind of one are you? One who is together with the Hotṛ-hymns, that is, with words in the form of praise. Of वीती (*vītī*) he says **NOTE**: that you, encouraged by the praises, eat the oblation. Further, the sacrificers who are possessed of food in the form of oblations are widely heard of, that is, become renowned, through the eatings of the gods **NOTE**. When the gods, honoured by you, partake of their oblation, then they become renowned. That is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आजिपते (*ājipate*)—protector of battle
- नृपते (*nṛpate*)—protector of men
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Indra, doer of excellent deeds
- त्वमिद्दि (*tvamiddi*)—you alone
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- वाजे (*vāje*)—to battle
- आ वक्षि (*ā vakṣi*)—lead us
- उत (*uta*)—and
- होत्राभिः (*hotrābhiḥ*)—with words of praise
- वीती (*vītī*)—you are one who eats the oblation
- ससवांसः (*sasavāṃsaḥ*)—the sacrificers who possess oblations
- देवनीतिभिः (*devanītibhiḥ*)—together with food fit for the enjoyment of the gods
- वि शृण्वरे (*vi śṛṇvare*)—are proclaiming your fame

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, protector of battle, protector of the performers of sacrifice, doer of excellent deeds, lead us, you alone, to battle. With our words of praise you are one who eats the oblation. The sacrificers who possess oblations, together with food fit for the enjoyment of the gods, proclaim your fame.

##### English translation
Lord of battle, institutor of righteous actions, king, lead us to battle. It is rumoured that Gods unite at a rite to partake sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> संति॒ ह्य१॒॑ र्य आ॒शिष॒ इंद्र॒ आयु॒र्जना॑नां ।

> आस्मान् । नक्षस्व । मघवन् । उप । अवसे । धुक्षस्व । पिप्युषीं । इषं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे परमेश्वर हि यस्मात् जनानां जायमानानां यजमानानामस्माकं
> स्वभूतमायुः चरुपुरोडाशाद्यन्नं आशिषः गवाश्वाद्यैश्वर्याणि च आर्यॆ
> जगत्सामिनि इंद्रे परमेश्वरे त्वयि संति समर्पितानि भवंति । अतो हे मघवन्
> धनवन्निंद्र अस्मान् यजमानान् उप नक्षस्व समीपे व्याप्नुहि । आत्मीयत्वेन
> स्वसमीपे कुर्वित्यर्थः । किंचास्माकमवसे रक्षणाय पिप्युषीं अतिशयेन पालयित्रिं
> इषमन्नं धुक्षस्व प्रपूरय देहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Supreme Lord, since for the people, that is, for us the sacrificers who are being born, our life, food such as the caru and the purodāśa, and the blessings, that is, wealth such as cattle and horses, are placed with you, the lord of the world, Indra, the Supreme Lord; therefore, O wealthy Indra, draw near to us the sacrificers, reach us in nearness. That is, make us your own and keep us near yourself. Further, for our protection fill us, that is, give us, food that nourishes in the highest degree.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—(O Indra) needed by us, the performers of sacrifice
- आशिषः (*āśiṣaḥ*)—the wealth of cattle and the like
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—the food that is the means of sacrifice
- अर्ये (*arye*)—the lord
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—in you, who are the lord of the world
- संति हि (*saṃti hi*)—are indeed
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- उप नक्षस्व (*upa nakṣasva*)—come near
- अवसे (*avase*)—for our protection
- पिप्युषीं (*pipyuṣīṃ*)—nourishing
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- धुक्षस्व (*dhukṣasva*)—fill into us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the wealth of cattle and the like that we, the performers of sacrifice, desire, and the food that is the means of sacrifice, are in you, the lord of the world. O wealthy Indra, come near to us. For our protection fill us with nourishing food.

##### English translation
Lord Indra is the the disposer of blessing of the longevity of men; Maghavan be kind to us, increase us, give us food.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वयं यजमानाः ते त्वदीयाः स्मः । त्वं चास्माकमसि । त्वमस्माकं
> तवस्मसि (ऋ. सं. ८-९२-३२) इति श्रुतेः । अतः हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मवन्निंद्र
> स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैः विधेम परिचरेम त्वां । यस्मात्त्वदीया वयं तस्मात्त्वं
> प्रस्कण्वाय कण्वपुत्राय मह्यं मातरिश्वानाय (? मातरिश्वने) राधो धनं नि
> तोशय नियमेन देहि । तदेव राधो विशिनष्टि । महि महत् पूज्यं स्फूरं
> स्थूलं प्रौढमित्यर्थः । शशयं देवब्राह्मणादिशरीरे शयानं तैरुपभोग्यमित्यर्थः।
> आद्रयं लज्जारहितं । पापवर्त्मना लब्धं धनं हि लज्ञासहितं भवति । इदं तु न
> तथा । ईश्वरानुग्रहलब्धात्तस्येत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, we the sacrificers are yours, and you are ours, as the śruti says त्वमस्माकं तवस्मसि (*tvamasmākaṃ tavasmasi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-92-32). Therefore, O Śatakratu, Indra of many deeds, we serve you with hymns of praise. Since we are yours, therefore give, bestow firmly, wealth to Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva, to me, Mātariśvān **NOTE**. He then describes that wealth. महि (*mahi*) means great, worthy of honour; स्फूरं (*sphūraṃ*) means large, ample, abundant. शशयं (*śaśayaṃ*) means lying in the bodies of gods, brahmins and others, to be enjoyed by them. आद्रयं (*ādrayaṃ*) means without shame **NOTE**: wealth gained by a sinful way is accompanied by shame, but this is not so, because it is obtained through the favour of the Lord **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we, the sacrificers
- ते (*te*)—we are yours
- त्वं अस्माकं (*tvaṃ asmākaṃ*)—you also are ours, therefore
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O Indra, doer of many valiant deeds
- स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—with hymns of praise
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—we serve you
- प्रस्कण्वाय (*praskaṇvāya*)—to me, called Praskaṇva, the son of the seer Kaṇva
- महि (*mahi*)—worthy of honour
- स्थूरं (*sthūraṃ*)—abundant
- शशयं (*śaśayaṃ*)—fit to be enjoyed
- अह्वयं (*ahvayaṃ*)—shameless, that is, not unjustly gained **NOTE**
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth
- नि तोशय (*ni tośaya*)—give without fail

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we who perform sacrifice are yours, and you too are ours. O Indra, who do many valiant deeds, we serve you with hymns of praise. To me, called Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva, give without fail wealth that is worthy of honour, that is, excellent, abundant and fit to be enjoyed.

##### English translation
Indra, we, the Sacrificers are yours, you too are ours. Indra, we shall worship you with praises. Satakritu, you give substantial, wealth to Praskanwa.

### Printed p. 634

## Sūkta 55 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta of five Ṛks beginning भूरीत् (*bhūrīt*) is the seventh, the vision of Kṛśa Kāṇva, with the praise of Praskaṇva's gift as its deity, in the Gāyatra metre. It is listed in the Anukramaṇikā: भूरीत् पंच कृशः प्रस्कण्वस्य दानस्तुतिर्गायत्रं तु तृतीयांत्ये अनुष्टुभौ (*bhūrīt paṃca kṛśaḥ praskaṇvasya dānastutirgāyatraṃ tu tṛtīyāṃtye anuṣṭubhau*). The metre of the last Ṛk and of the third is Anuṣṭubh; of the others, Gāyatrī. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning भूरीत् (*bhūrīt*) is the seventh among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is one called Kṛśaḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Since the praise of the gift of the seer Praskaṇva is told in this sūkta, the praise of Praskaṇva's gift is the deity of this sūkta. The third and fifth Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: भूरीत् पंच कृशः प्रस्कण्वस्य दानस्तुतिर्गायत्रं तु तृतीयांत्ये अनुष्टुभौ (*bhūrīt paṃca kṛśaḥ praskaṇvasya dānastutirgāyatraṃ tu tṛtīyāṃtye anuṣṭubhau*). The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 55; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 26. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Kṛśaḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: Praskaṇasya dānastutiḥ **NOTE**. Metre: 1, 2, 4 Gāyatrī; 3, 5 Anuṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भूरीदिंद्र॑स्य वी॒र्यं१॒॑ १ व्यख्य॑म॒भ्याय॑ति ।  
> राध॑स्ते दस्यवे वृक ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भूरि । इत् । इंद्रस्य । वीर्यं । वि । अख्यं । अभि । आ । अयति ।  
> राधः । ते । दस्यवे । वृक ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 635

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रस्य समर्थस्य प्रस्कण्वस्य वीर्यं दानल क्षणसामर्थ्यं भूरीत् प्रचुरमेव सत् अभि अभितः आ आयति अभिमुख्येन प्राप्नोतीति व्यख्यं व्यज्ञासिषमहं ।
> ईश्वरेणाल्पमपि कृतं कर्म बहु भवत् प्रसिद्ध्यतीत्यर्थः । इदानीमृषिः प्रत्यक्षीकृत्याह । हे वृक शत्रुविकर्तन प्रस्कण्व ते तव संबंधि राधो धनं दस्युवे दस्युं
> हंतुं समर्थं भवतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The prowess of Indra, that is, of the capable Praskaṇva, his capacity of the nature of giving, being abundant, भूरीत् (*bhūrīt*), reaches me from every side, turned towards me. This I have come to know, व्यख्यं (*vyakhyaṃ*). That is, a deed done even in a small way by the Lord becomes great and is renowned. Now the seer, making it present before him, says: O Vṛka, cutter of enemies, Praskaṇva, your wealth is able to slay the dasyu; "is able" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra (or of Praskaṇva, who is capable of everything)
- वीर्यं (*vīryaṃ*)—the capacity (the power of giving and the like)
- भूरि इत् (*bhūri it*)—being exceedingly abundant
- अभ्यायति (*abhyāyati*)—the matter that it pervades everywhere
- व्यख्यं (*vyakhyaṃ*)—I have fully understood
- वृक (*vṛka*)—O Indra, who cut down the enemy
- ते (*te*)—your
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth
- दस्यवे (*dasyave*)—helps for the destruction of the enemy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have understood that the capacity of Indra is exceedingly strong and pervades everywhere. O Indra, who cut down the enemy, your wealth helps for the destruction of the enemy.

##### English translation
We know the works of Indra as various; he is a bull unto the Dashys, his wealth is coming to us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Take the word Indra to mean the seer. The word इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*) is explained as of Praskaṇva, who is capable in all deeds, and वीर्यं (*vīryaṃ*) as a special capacity for giving and the like.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तं श्वे॒तास॑ उ॒क्षणो॑ दि॒वि तारो॒ न रो॑चंते ।  
> म॒ह्ना दिवं॒ न त॑स्तभुः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतं । श्वेतासः । उक्षणः । दिवि । तारः । न । रोचंते ।  
> मह्ना । दिवं । न । तस्तभुः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 636

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे प्रस्कण्व त्वया दत्ताः शतसंख्याकाः श्वेतासः श्वेताः शुक्लवर्णाः उक्षणः
> उक्षाणः रेतःसेचनसमर्था बलीवर्दा रोचंते दीप्यंते । क इव । दिवि द्युलोके
> तारो न तारा इव । ता यथा दिवि रोचंते तद्वदेते भुवीत्यर्थः । किंच मह्ना
> तेजसो महत्वे (महत्वेन) दिवं न तारा यथा द्युलोकं तस्तभुः व्याप्नुवंति
> तद्वदेते मह्ना यशसो महत्वेन भुवं व्याप्नुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Praskaṇva, the hundred white bulls given by you, श्वेतासः (*śvetāsaḥ*) white, of a bright colour, उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*) bulls capable of shedding seed, shine, that is, glitter. Like what? Like stars in the heaven, the sky. As these shine in the heaven, so do these on the earth. That is the meaning. Further, by the greatness of their brilliance, as the stars pervade the sky, so these pervade the earth by the greatness of their fame.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतं (*śataṃ*)—(O Praskaṇva) a hundred in number (given by you)
- श्वेतासः (*śvetāsaḥ*)—of a bright colour
- उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*)—and vigorous bulls
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- तारा न (*tārā na*)—as the stars shine
- रोचंते (*rocaṃte*)—shine
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by their greatness
- दिवं न (*divaṃ na*)—as the stars pervade the whole sky
- तस्तंभुः (*tastaṃbhuḥ*)—these bulls can pervade the whole earth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Praskaṇva, the hundred bulls given by you, of a bright colour and vigorous, shine as the stars shine in the sky. As the stars pervade the whole sky by their greatness, these bulls too pervade the whole earth.

##### English translation
As the stars shining in the sky so hundreds of bulls are looking beautiful thus beautifying the heaven with their grandeur.

> शतं । मे । बल्बजस्तुकाः । अरुषीणां । चतुःशतं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रस्कण्वः शतमपरिमितान् वेणून् मस्करान् । प्रादादिति सर्वत्र शेषः । शतं
> शतसंख्याकान् शुनः सारमेयान् प्रादात् । तथा शतं बहूनि म्लातानि मृदूकृतानि
> चर्माणि अजिनानि प्रादात् । किंच शतमपरिमिताः बल्बजस्तुताः तृणपूलाः मे
> मह्यं कृशनाम्ने ऋषये प्रादात् । अथ च अरुषीणामारोचमानानां गवां
> चतुःशतं प्रादात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Praskaṇva gave a hundred, that is, countless, bamboo staffs. "He gave" is to be supplied everywhere. He gave a hundred dogs, hounds. Likewise he gave a hundred softened hides, antelope skins. Further, he gave a hundred, that is, countless, bundles of balbaja grass **NOTE** to me, the seer named Kṛśa. And he gave four hundred shining cows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रस्कण्वः (*praskaṇvaḥ*)—Praskaṇva
- मे (*me*)—to me
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—countless
- वेणान् (*veṇān*)—gave staffs of bamboo
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred in number
- शुनः (*śunaḥ*)—gave dogs (hounds)
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred in number
- म्लातानि (*mlātāni*)—made soft
- चर्माणि (*carmāṇi*)—gave black antelope skins and the like
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—many in number
- बल्बजस्तुकाः (*balbajastukāḥ*)—gave bundles of the grass called balbaja
- चुतुः शतं (*cutuḥ śataṃ*)—four hundred
- अरुषीणां (*aruṣīṇāṃ*)—gave herds of attractive cows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praskaṇva gave me countless bamboo staffs, a hundred hounds (dogs of a good breed), many antelope skins and the like made soft, a great number of bundles of the grass called balbaja, and four hundred herds of attractive cows.

##### English translation
Praskanwa gave me one hundred sticks, one hundred dogs, hides, fodder and four hundred cows.
