##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे काण्वायनाः कण्वगोत्राः प्रस्कण्वा वयोवयः अतिशयेन पक्षिण इव ।
> लुप्तोपमेयं । विचरंतः विहायसि चरंतः यूयं सुदेवाः स्थ कल्याणदेवाः
> भवथ । अतोऽस्मदाशिषा अश्वा इव चंक्रमत विहरत यूयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Kāṇvāyanas, Praskaṇvas of the lineage of Kaṇva, you who move exceedingly like birds through the sky are सुदेवाः (*sudevāḥ*), that is, you have good gods. Therefore, by our blessing, you move about, roam, like horses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- काण्वायनाः (*kāṇvāyanāḥ*)—O sages Praskaṇva, born in the lineage of Kaṇva
- वयोवयः (*vayovayaḥ*)—like birds with most excellent wings
- विचरंतः (*vicaraṃtaḥ*)—moving through the whole sky
- सुदेवाः (*sudevāḥ*)—becoming recipients of the grace of excellent gods
- स्थ (*stha*)—you are renowned (and likewise)
- अश्वासः न (*aśvāsaḥ na*)—in the manner in which horses move everywhere
- चंक्रमत (*caṃkramata*)—move about, swift and strong

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sage Praskaṇvas, born in the lineage of Kaṇva, moving through the whole sky like birds with most excellent wings, and becoming recipients of the grace of excellent gods, you are renowned. Likewise, in the manner in which horses move everywhere over the earth, move about swift and possessed of mighty strength in our regions too.

##### English translation
Sons of Kanwas, traversing the sky like birds, you are mightily wandering like horses.

> श्यावीः । अतिध्वसन् । पथः । चक्षुषा । चन । संनशे ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 639

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आदित् दानानंतरमेव अनूनस्य अन्यूनस्य । सर्वोत्कृष्टस्येति यावत् ।
> साप्तस्य एवंनाम्मः कण्वपुत्रस्य संबंधि महि महत् श्रवः यशः न चर्किरन् न
> कर्तुमिच्छंति । तद्यशः संपादयितुं केचित् नेशते इत्यर्थः । किंच पथः धर्ममार्गात् सकाशात् अतिध्वसन् अतिशयेनाधः पतन् कृपणः पुमान् श्यावीः कपिला गाः
> चक्षुषा जन नेत्रेणापि संनशे सम्यक् व्याप्तुं संद्रष्टुं नेष्टे । किमुत वक्तव्यं
> तद्यशःसंपादने नेष्टे इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आदित् (*ādit*), immediately after the gift, of अनूनस्य (*anūnasya*), the unreduced, that is, the most excellent, साप्तस्य (*sāptasya*), of the son of Kaṇva so named, the great fame, महि श्रवः (*mahi śravaḥ*): they did not wish to make it, न चर्किरन् (*na carkiran*). That is, none are able to acquire that fame. Further, a miserly man who falls far down from the path of dharma cannot fully obtain, that is, cannot see, the tawny cows even with the eye **NOTE**. How much less, it need not be said, can he acquire that fame.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित् (*ādit*)—immediately after this gift described above
- अनूनस्य (*anūnasya*)—of the giver who is flawless and most excellent
- साप्तस्य (*sāptasya*)—the descendants of Sāpta, who was the son of Kaṇva
- महि श्रवः (*mahi śravaḥ*)—in this very manner, exceeding fame
- न चर्किरन् (*na carkiran*)—did not wish to acquire
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—from the path of dharma
- अतिध्वसन् (*atidhvasan*)—the miserly, who slip and fall into the lower way
- श्यावीः (*śyāvīḥ*)—attractive cows
- चक्षुषा चन (*cakṣuṣā cana*)—even with the eyes
- संनशे (*saṃnaśe*)—(do not) let them be seen

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Immediately after this gift described above, the descendants of Sāpta, the son of Kaṇva, an unblemished and most excellent giver, did not wish to acquire exceeding fame in this very manner. The miserly, who leave the path of dharma and fall into the lower way, do not let attractive cows be seen even with the eyes. For them there is no earning of fame at all, even before that.

##### English translation
Let the seven yolk team be praised. The young lives are of mighty strength. The deep ground makes go gallopping baffling the idle fellow.

## Sūkta 56 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta of five Ṛks beginning प्रति ते (*prati te*) is the eighth, the vision of Kāṇva Pṛṣadhra, in the Gāyatra metre. It is listed in the Anukramaṇikā: प्रति ते पृषध्रोऽंत्या अग्निसूर्यदेवत्या पंक्तिशृंदस्का । शेषा इंद्रदेवत्या गायत्रीछंदस्काः (*prati te pṛṣadhro 'ṃtyā agnisūryadevatyā paṃktiśṛṃdaskā | śeṣā iṃdradevatyā gāyatrīchaṃdaskāḥ*). The last Ṛk has Agni and Sūrya as deity and is in the Paṅkti metre; the others have Indra as deity and are in the Gāyatrī metre. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

### Printed p. 640

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning प्रति ते (*prati te*) is the eighth among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has five Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: प्रति ते पृषध्रोऽन्त्या अग्निसूर्यदेवत्या पंक्तिश्चंदस्का (*prati te pṛṣadhro 'ntyā agnisūryadevatyā paṃktiścaṃdaskā*). The seer of this sūkta is one called Pṛṣadhraḥ Kāṇvaḥ. The praise of Praskaṇva's gift is the deity of the first four Ṛks of this sūkta; or else Indra is the deity. The fifth Ṛk has Agni and Sūrya as deity; the fifth Ṛk is in the Paṅkti metre. The remaining Ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 56; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 27. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Pṛṣadhraḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: 1-4 Praskaṇvasya dānastutiḥ (Indro vā); 5 Agnisūryau. Metre: 1-4 Gāyatrī; 5 Paṅktiḥ.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रति॑ ते दस्यवे वृक॒ राधो॑ अद॒र्श्यह्र॑यं ।  
> द्यौर्न प्र॑थि॒ना शवः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रति । ते । दस्यवे । वृक । राधः । आदर्शि । अह्रयं ।  
> द्याः । न । प्रथिना । शवः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृक शत्रुविकर्तनेंद्र ते तव स्वभूतं राधो धनं दस्यवे उपक्षपयित्रे
> शक्रवे प्रति प्रतिकूलं आदर्शि दृष्टं । शत्रुनापहृतं सन् (शत्रुणापहृतं सत्) न तस्य
> उपकाराय भवति प्रत्युपकारायैव जायत इत्यर्थः । कीदृशं राधः । अह्वयं
> लज्जारहितं । शत्रुहनने प्रगल्भमिति यावत् । किंच ते शवः बलं प्रथिना पृथुत्वेन
> द्यौर्न द्युलोक इवास्ति । अतः सर्वोत्कृष्टं त्वामहं सौमात्यभिप्रायः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vṛka, cutter of enemies, Indra, your own wealth has been seen hostile to the dasyu, the harasser, the enemy. Taken away by an enemy, it does not serve for his benefit but arises for a return injury. That is the meaning. What kind of wealth? अह्वयं (*ahvayaṃ*), shameless, that is, bold in slaying the enemy. Further, your strength, by its vastness, is like the heaven, the sky. Therefore, you, the most excellent, I **NOTE**.

### Printed p. 641

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृक (*vṛka*)—O Indra, cutter of enemies
- ते (*te*)—your
- अह्रयं (*ahrayaṃ*)—not afraid of the enemy
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth
- दस्यवे (*dasyave*)—to the violent enemy
- प्रत्यदर्शि (*pratyadarśi*)—has appeared hostile
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—your strength also
- प्रथिना (*prathinā*)—by its growth
- द्यौः न (*dyauḥ na*)—spreads as far as the sky and is extended

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, cutter of enemies, your wealth, which is not afraid of the enemy, has appeared hostile to the violent enemy. Your strength also, by its growth, spreads as far as the sky and is extended.

##### English translation
You are a bull to the Dashus, your inexhaustible wealth has been perceived. Your forces spread to the Heaven.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दश॒ मह्यं॑ पौतक्र॒तः स॒हस्रा॒ दस्य॑वे॒ वृकः॑ ।  
> नित्या॑द्रा॒यो अ॑मंहत ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दश । मह्यं । पौतक्रतः । सहस्रा । दस्यवे । वृकः ।  
> नित्यात् । रायः । अमंहत ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पौतक्रतः पवित्रकर्मवन्निंद्र मह्यं मदर्थं दश सहस्रा अयुतसंख्याकान् दस्यून् उपक्षयित्थन् शत्रून् वृकः निवृत्तवान् छिन्नवानसि । अत एव नित्यात्
> शाश्वतात् त्वत्तः भीताः संतस्ते शत्रवः रायः धनानि अमंहत अदुः मह्यं ।
> मंहतिर्दानकर्मा तत्र तस्य पाठात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra of pure deeds, for me, for my sake, you have cut down and destroyed ten thousand, that is, a number of ten thousand, दस्यून् (*dasyūn*), destroyers, enemies. Therefore, being afraid of you, the eternal one, those enemies gave to me रायः (*rāyaḥ*), riches. The verb maṃh has the sense of giving, since it is so read in that place.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पौतक्रतः (*pautakrataḥ*)—O Indra of purified deeds
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—for me
- दश सहस्रा (*daśa sahasrā*)—ten thousand in number
- दस्यवे (*dasyave*)—violent enemies
- वृकः (*vṛkaḥ*)—you have cut down and destroyed
- नित्यात् (*nityāt*)—the enemies who feared you, who are of eternal state
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—all the riches
- अमंहत (*amaṃhata*)—offered to me

### Printed p. 642

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra of purified deeds, for me you have cut down and destroyed ten thousand violent enemies. The enemies who feared you, who are of eternal state, offered all their riches to me.

##### English translation
You are a bull to the Dashus, give me ten thousand from your permanent wealth.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तं मे॑ गर्द॒भानां॑ श॒तमूर्णा॑वतीनां ।  
> श॒तं दा॒सा अति॒ स्रजः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतं । मे । गर्दभानां । शतं । ऊर्णावतीनां ।  
> शतं । दासान् । अति । स्रजः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> किंच हे इंद्र त्वत्तो भीतास्ते मे मह्यमृषये पृषध्रिनाम्ने (पृषध्र)
> गर्दभानां रासभानां शतं । अमंहत अदुः इति पूर्वमंत्रगतेनान्वयः सर्वत्र !
> अथ च ऊर्णावतीनां मेषीनां शतमदुः । तथा शतान् शतसंख्याकान् दासान्
> भृत्यान् अति अतिशयिताः स्रजो मालाश्च अदुः । एवंप्रभावस्त्वां (प्रभावं श्वां)
> सौमात्यर्थः । यद्वा उभयोर्मंत्रयोरयमर्थः । पौतक्रतः । पूते पवित्रॆ
> स्थाने क्रतः पादविक्षेपो यस्याः सा पूतक्रता अदितिः । पवित्रदेशे पादन्यासः
> आदितेरुचित एव । दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत् पादं इति वचनात् । तस्या अपत्यं पौतक्रत
> इंद्रः । दस्यवे । दस्युः कर्मोपक्षयिता तमःसंघः । तं हंतुं वृकश्चंद्रमाः सन
> (सन्) नित्यात् अनुपक्षीणात् स्वकोशात् सकाशात् दश सहस्रा आयुतसंख्याकानि
> रायः धनानि मह्यं पृषध्रनाम्ने अमंहत प्रादात् । किंच गर्दभमेषीदासमालाशतान्यपि मे मह्यं स एव प्रादात् इति । वृकश्चंद्रमा भवति (निरु. ५-२०)
> इति यास्कः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Further, O Indra, those afraid of you gave to me, the seer named Pṛṣadhri **NOTE**, a hundred asses. The connection with "gave" in the previous mantra holds everywhere. And they gave a hundred ewes, sheep with wool, likewise a hundred servants, and excellent garlands. Such is your power; this is the meaning **NOTE**.

Or else the meaning of the two mantras is this. पौतक्रतः (*pautakrataḥ*): Pūtakratā is Aditi, the one whose step, kratu, is set in a pure, holy place. The setting of the foot in a holy place is fitting for Aditi, by the saying दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत् पादं (*dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyaset pādaṃ*) **GLOSS**. Her offspring is Pautakrata, Indra. दस्यवे (*dasyave*): the dasyu is the mass of darkness that harms ritual action. To slay it, Indra, being the Vṛka, the moon, gave to me, the one named Pṛṣadhra, from his eternal, undiminished own treasury ten thousand, that is, a number of ten thousand, riches. Further, he alone gave to me also hundreds of asses, sheep, servants and garlands. So Yāska says: वृकश्चंद्रमा भवति (*vṛkaścaṃdramā bhavati*) (Ni. 5-20) **GLOSS**.

- मे (*me*)—(O Indra, the enemies who feared you) to me
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred in number
- गर्दभानां (*gardabhānāṃ*)—gave asses (mules)
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred in number
- ऊर्णावतीनां (*ūrṇāvatīnāṃ*)—gave sheep full of wool
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—a hundred in number
- दासान् (*dāsān*)—gave servants
- अति स्रजः (*ati srajaḥ*)—gave excellent garlands too

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the enemies who feared you gave me a hundred asses. They gave a hundred sheep with wool. They gave a hundred servants. They offered excellent garlands too.

##### English translation
Give me oue hunbred asses, one hundred worthy sheep and one hundred slaves.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत्रो इति । अपि । प्र । अनीयत । पूतक्रताय्कॆ । विअक्ता ।  
> अश्वानां । इत् । न । यूथ्यां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> किंच व्यक्ता विविधं गंता नानादेशेषु प्रचलन् इंद्रः तत्र स्वर्गे वर्तमानैः
> (? वर्तमानाय्कॆ) पूतक्रताय्कॆ एतन्नाम्ने ( ? न्नाम्नै ) समात्रॆऽपि (स्वमात्रॆऽपि)
> प्रानीयत प्रापितवान् । किमित्युच्यते । अश्वानां वडबानां यूथ्यां संहतिं । न
> केवलं मह्यमेव प्रादादपि तु स्वजनन्या अपि वडवावृंदं प्रापितवान् । इतीयानिंद्रः समर्थ इति भावः । इत् न इति निपातद्वयमनर्थकं ॥

### Printed p. 644

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Further, व्यक्ता (*vyaktā*), one who goes variously, Indra, moving about in different regions, brought, प्रानीयत (*prānīyata*), in heaven, to Pūtakratā, one of this name, and also to his own mother **NOTE**, a herd of mares. He says what it was: the herd, the multitude, of mares. Not only to me did he give; he also brought a herd of mares to his own mother. Thus Indra is capable; this is the sense. The two particles इत् (*it*) and न (*na*) are without meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- व्यक्ता (*vyaktā*)—Indra, who has various wanderings
- तत्र (*tatra*)—who is in heaven
- पूतक्रताय्कॆ (*pūtakratāykè*)—to the one called Pūtakratā
- अपि (*api*)—and also to his own mother
- अश्वानां (*aśvānāṃ*)—of horses
- यूथ्यां (*yūthyāṃ*)—the herd
- प्रानीयत (*prānīyata*)—brought and gave

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who has various wanderings, brought and gave a herd of horses to the one called Pūtakratā who is in heaven, and also to his own mother.

##### English translation
To the Putakrita has been brought mare, well-crested one unlike any in the herd.

> अग्निः । शुक्रेण । शोचिषा । बृहत् । सूरः । आरोचत । दिवि । सूर्यः । आरोचत॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आथानयाग्नि सूर्यौ स्तूयेते । स प्रसिद्धोऽग्निः चिकिशुः चेतनावतो
> यजमानस्य । कर्मणि षष्ठि । चेतनावंतं यजमानं अचेति जानाति । कीद्वतः सः ।
> हव्यवाट् हविषां वोढा सुमद्रथः स्वयमेव रंहणस्वभावः । ७मत् स्वयमित्यर्थः (निरु. ६-२२) इति यास्कः । असहायगमनशील इत्यर्थः । किंच बृहत् महान्
> योऽग्निः शुक्रेण शुक्लेन शोचिषा तेजसा सूरः सुष्टु ईरयिता प्रेरकः सन् रात्रौ
> भुवि अरोचत दीप्यते । आथ च दिवा दिवि (?) द्योतमाने स्वर्लोके सूर्यः
> सुष्टु प्रेरयितादित्यः अरोचत दीप्यते । उभाभ्यामहोरात्रात्मकः सर्वः कालः
> आक्रांत इत्यभिप्रायः ॥

### Printed p. 645

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now by this Ṛk Agni and Sūrya are praised. That well-known Agni चिकिशुः (*cikiśuḥ*), of the sacrificer who is endowed with consciousness (the genitive is in the sense of the accusative), knows, अचेति (*aceti*), the sacrificer who is endowed with consciousness. What kind of one is he? हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*), the carrier of oblations, and सुमद्रथः (*sumadrathaḥ*), of the nature of speeding by himself. Yāska says that the word means "by himself" (Ni. 6-22) **NOTE**. That is, one inclined to go without a helper. Further, the great Agni, with white, bright splendour, सूरः (*sūraḥ*), being the good impeller, shines at night on the earth. And by day, in the shining world of heaven **NOTE**, Sūrya, the good impeller, the Āditya, shines. By the two the whole time, of the nature of day and night, is pervaded. This is the intention.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हव्यवाह् (*havyavāh*)—he who carries the oblation to the gods
- सुमद्रथः (*sumadrathaḥ*)—he who has an auspicious chariot
- स. (*sa.*)—he who is well known
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- चिकितुः (*cikituḥ*)—the sacrificer who has attained knowledge of the rite
- अचेति (*aceti*)—knows
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—of great form
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*)—radiant
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with splendour
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—as the impeller of all
- आरोचित (*ārocita*)—shines (at night on the earth)
- दिवि (*divi*)—by day
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—in the form of Sūrya
- आरोचित (*ārocita*)—shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who carries the oblation to the gods, who has an auspicious chariot and is well known, knows the sacrificer who has attained knowledge of the rite. Agni, of great form, endowed with radiant splendour, as the impeller of all, shines at night on the earth. By day he shines in the form of Sūrya.

##### English translation
Agni has appeared, is wise and has beautiful chariot and carries sacrifices. He is moving with white and brilliant rays, he is looking irate ; he appears in the heaven like Surja.

## Sūkta 57 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta of four Ṛks beginning युवं देवा (*yuvaṃ devā*) is the ninth, the vision of Kāṇva Medhya, addressed to the Aśvins, in the Triṣṭubh metre. It is listed in the Anukramaṇikā: युवं देवा चतुष्कं मेध्य आश्विनं त्रैष्टुभं (*yuvaṃ devā catuṣkaṃ medhya āśvinaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ*). The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning युवं देवा (*yuvaṃ devā*) is the ninth among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has four Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is one called Medhyaḥ Kāṇvaḥ; the deities are the Aśvin deities; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: युवं देवा चतुष्कं मेध्य आश्विनं त्रैष्टुभं (*yuvaṃ devā catuṣkaṃ medhya āśvinaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ*). The ritual application is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

### Printed p. 646

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 57; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 4, Varga 28. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 4. Seer: Medhyaḥ Kāṇṇaḥ **NOTE**. Deity: Āśvinau. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वं दे॑वा॒ क्रतु॑ना पू॒र्वेण॑ यु॒क्ता रथे॑न तवि॒षं य॑जत्रा ।  
> आग॑च्छतं नासत्या॒ शची॑भिरि॒दं तृ॒तीयं॒ सव॑नं पिबाथः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवं । देवा । क्रतुना । पूर्व्येण । युक्ता । रथेन । तविषं । यजत्रा ।  
> आ । अगच्छतं । नासत्या । शचीभिः । इदं । तृतीयं । सवनं । पिबाधः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यजत्रा यजनीयौ पूज्यौ देवौ द्योतमानावश्विनौ पूर्वेण पुरा
> भवेन क्रतुना कर्मणा अनुग्रहबुद्ध्या ना उपेत् युवं युवां प्रति रथेन
> रंहणस्वभावेन स्यंदनेन संयुक्ता अश्वाः तविषं बलं यथा भवति तथा वहंतीति
> शेषः । तस्मात् हे नासत्या सत्यभूतौ युवां शचीभिः अनुग्रहलक्षणैः कर्मभिः
> सह इदं तृतीयं सवनमुद्दिश्य आगच्छतमागच्छतं । आगत्य च पिबाथः पिबतं
> सोममिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O worshipful, यजत्रा (*yajatrā*), shining Aśvins, by an ancient rite, that is, an action of former times, with a thought of favour towards you **NOTE**, horses yoked to a chariot, a speeding car, carry you with force; "carry" is to be supplied. Therefore, O नासत्या (*nāsatyā*), true ones, come together with your deeds of favour to this third libation, and having come drink the Soma; "Soma" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजत्रा (*yajatrā*)—worshipful
- देवा (*devā*)—divine
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—O Aśvin deities
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- पूर्वेण (*pūrveṇa*)—ancient
- क्रतुना (*kratunā*)—being endowed with rites
- शविषं (*śaviṣaṃ*)—powerfully
- रथेन (*rathena*)—with a chariot
- युक्ताः (*yuktāḥ*)—having yoked horses
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—together with your deeds of favour
- इदं तृतीयं सवनं (*idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ savanaṃ*)—with regard to this third libation
- आ गच्छतं (*ā gacchataṃ*)—be pleased to come
- पिबाधः (*pibādhaḥ*)—drink this Soma

### Printed p. 647

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshipful ones, divine in nature, O Aśvin deities, may you two also, being endowed with the rites of old, having horses yoked to the chariot as if giving it strength, and being accompanied by your actions of favour, be pleased to come with regard to this third libation.

##### English translation
O Aswins, come with your protective actions and chariot with horses.
and drink by the right of your action the third libation.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वां दे॒वास्त्रय॑ एकाद॒शासः॑ स॒त्याः स॒त्यस्य॑ ददृशे पु॒रस्ता॑त् ।  
> अ॒स्माकं॑ य॒ज्ञं सव॑नं जुषा॒णा पा॒तं सोम॑मश्विना॒  ॑
> दीद्यग्नी ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवां । देवाः । त्रयः । एकादशासः । सत्याः । सत्यस्य । ददृशे । पुरस्तात् ।  
> अस्माकं । यज्ञं । सवनं । जुषाणा । पातं । सोमं । अश्विना । दीद्यग्नी इति  
> दीद्यग्नी ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विन् युवां द्वौ अपरे च त्रय एकादशासः त्रयस्त्रिंशद्देवाः ।
> ते च अष्टौ वसवः एकादश रुद्रा द्वादशादित्याः प्रजापतिश्च वषट्कारश्च इति श्रुतिप्रसिद्धाः । सर्वे यूयं सत्याः यथार्थभूताः संतः सत्यस्यावितथस्य यज्ञस्य
> पुरस्तात् पुरोदेशे ददृशे दृश्यमाना भवथ । अतोऽस्माकं संबंधिनं सवनं ।
> सूयतेऽभिषूयते सोमो यत्रेति सवनः । तं तादृशं यज्ञं यजनीयमध्वरं
> जुषाणा जुषमाण् सेवमान् युवां सोमं अभिषुतसोमरसं पातं पिबतं ।
> कीदृशौ युवां । दीद्यग्नी ! दीदिः अतिशयेन दीप्यमानः अग्निः जठरानलो
> ययोस्तौ तादृशौ । भिषजोः भवतोर्दिप्ताग्नित्वमप्युचितमिति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, you two, and the other thirty-three gods, "three elevens" (thirty-three), who are the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the twelve Ādityas, Prajāpati and Vaṣaṭkāra, as well known from the Śruti, all of you, being true, that is, real in being, become visible in front of the true, unfailing sacrifice. Therefore, accepting our sacrifice, which is called savana because Soma is pressed in it, that is, the sacrifice that is to be performed and is free from harm, do you two drink the Soma, the pressed Soma juice. What are you two like? दीद्यग्नी (*dīdyagnī*): those of whom the digestive fire blazes exceedingly. For physicians such as you two a blazing fire is also fitting; such is the meaning.

- युवां (*yuvāṃ*)—you two

- सत्याः (*satyāḥ*)—being of the nature of truth

- ददृशे (*dadṛśe*)—appear

- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- सवनं (*savanaṃ*)—called the third libation

- पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, may you two and also the remaining thirty-three gods, being of the nature of truth, appear in front of our sacrifice, which is of the nature of truth. O Aśvin deities, having a blazing digestive fire, enjoying our sacrifice called the third libation, drink the Soma offered by us.

##### English translation
The number of Gods are thirty-three, they are true, they are visible
before the rite. Aswins with brilliant fire come to my this Soma rite
and drink.

it is praiseworthy. Only by your favour does the Sun, your father, rain on the earth. Otherwise the water of the earth has been drawn up by him with the channels of his own rays; how could he rain, being one who draws up? Therefore this is the doing of you two alone; such is the intention. Since it is so, when there is a search for cows, those well-known thousands of praises, that is, sacrifices, which are praised, are begun (this is to be supplied). To all those sacrifices, indeed, you two come near, that is, go to their neighbourhood; the change of number is Vedic. For what purpose? To drink Soma. The word "uta" has no meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—for the abundance of the earth
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the sky
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—the water in the form of rain
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the Sun who pours down
- तत् (*tat*)—that state of his
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- पनाय्कं (*panāykaṃ*)—highly praiseworthy
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—is indeed the action (and therefore)

- तान् सर्वान् इत् (*tān sarvān it*)—with regard to all those sacrifices

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, the Sun who pours down water in the form of rain from the sky for the abundance of the earth, that state of that Sun, which is a benefit to the world, is indeed your highly praiseworthy action. Therefore, with regard to all those sacrifices, praiseworthy and numbering thousands, that there are for the search for cows, come to drink the Soma.

##### English translation
Aswins you are the granter of the desired, by heaven, earth and sky.
I have invoked you, those who praised thousand times, come to them for
drink.

> प्र अवतं प्रकर्षण रक्षतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O worshipful Aśvins, this portion of yours, of the nature of Soma, which is to be partaken of, is placed here with firmness; "to take it, come" is to be supplied. Further, O Nāsatyas, true Aśvins, come near, that is, go close to hear these praises, these words of the nature of praise, which are close at hand. And drink the Soma, which is endowed with sweetness. Further, protect well, that is, protect excellently, our sacrificer, who has given the oblation, with your actions that bestow the desired fruit.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यजत्रा (*yajatrā*)—worthy of worship
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—O Aśvin deities
- वां (*vāṃ*)—in your direction
- आयं भागः (*āyaṃ bhāgaḥ*)—this portion in the form of Soma
- निहितः (*nihitaḥ*)—is placed
- इमा गिरः (*imā giraḥ*)—having regard to these words of praise
- उप यातं (*upa yātaṃ*)—be pleased to come
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—very pleasant
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink
- अस्मे (*asme*)—belonging to us
- दाश्वांसं (*dāśvāṃsaṃ*)—the sacrificer who gives the oblation
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—with your actions of favour
- प्रावतं (*prāvataṃ*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshipful Aśvin deities, this portion in the form of Soma is placed in your direction. Having regard to these words of praise, be pleased to come. Drink the very pleasant Soma juice. Protect the sacrificer who belongs to us and gives the oblation with your actions of favour.

##### English translation
Nasatyas, your portion remains thus set apart this is your praise, do come and proteet us, drink this sweet Soma and protect the sacrificer with your actions.

### Printed p. 651
## Sūkta 58 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, यमृत्विजः (*yamṛtvijaḥ*), is the tenth among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has three Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Medhya Kāṇva; the deities are the Viśvedevas **NOTE** or the priests. The metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: the three Ṛks beginning with यमृत्विजः (*yamṛtvijaḥ*) are addressed to the Viśvedevas, or the first is in praise of the priests. The use in ritual is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Particulars

Sūkta 58 (Vālakhilya sūkta 10). Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 6. Sūkta 58. Aṣṭaka 6. Adhyāya 4. Varga 29. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Seer: Medhyaḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: 1. the Viśvedevas or the priests; 2-3. the Viśvedevas. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यमृ॒त्विजो॑ बहु॒धा क॒ल्पयं॑तः॒ सचे॑तसो य॒ज्ञमि॒मुं  ॑
> वहंति ।  
> यो अ॑नूचा॒नो ब्रा॑ह्म॒णो यु॒क्त आ॑सी॒त्का स्वि॒त्तत्र॒ यज॑मानस्य सं॒वित् ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 652

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । ऋत्विजः । बहुधा । कल्पयंतः । सचेतसः । यज्ञं । इमं । वहंति ।  
> यः । अनूचानः । ब्राह्मणः । युक्तः । आसीत् । का । स्वित् । तत्र । यजमानस्य ।  
> संवित् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सचेतसः समानप्रज्ञाः ऋत्विजः यमिमं यज्ञं यजनीयकर्मविशेषं
> बहुधा अनेकप्रकारेण कल्पयंतः रचयंतः संतः वहंति देवान् प्रापयंति !
> तमिमं यज्ञं कुर्वन् ब्राह्मणः ऋत्विग्लक्षणो विप्रः यज्ञकर्मविशेषे युक्तः
> समाहितः आसीत् । तत्र कर्मणि का स्मित् । स्विदिति वितर्कॆ । का ना यजमानस्य
> संवित् प्रज्ञा । न किंचित्करा इत्यर्थः । यत्र कर्मणि ऋत्विगेव सावधानोऽस्ति तत्र
> यजमानस्य प्रज्ञापाटवेन किं प्रयोजनमस्ति । न किंचिदपीति भाव ॥ कीदृशो
> ब्राह्मणः । अनूचानः गुरोः सकाशादधीतवेदवेदांगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests of like mind, arranging this sacrifice, this particular sacrificial action, in many ways, that is, devising it, carry it, that is, convey the gods to it. In that sacrifice, the Brahmin, a sage of the nature of a priest, who performs this sacrifice, is engaged, that is, attentive, in the particular sacrificial action. In that rite, what then is the sacrificer's understanding? "Svit" denotes conjecture. It is of no use: such is the meaning. In a rite in which the priest alone is attentive, what purpose has the sacrificer's skill of understanding? None at all; such is the sense. What sort of Brahmin? अनूचानः (*anūcānaḥ*): one who has studied the Veda and the Vedāṅgas from a teacher.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सचेतसः (*sacetasaḥ*)—having equal understanding
- ऋत्विजः (*ṛtvijaḥ*)—the priests
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which sacrifice
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—in many ways
- कल्पयंतः (*kalpayaṃtaḥ*)—arranging
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—to this very sacrifice
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—bring the gods (and further)
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—to this sacrifice
- युक्तः (*yuktaḥ*)—being engaged
- अनूचानः (*anūcānaḥ*)—one accomplished in the study of the Veda
- यः ब्राह्मणः आसीत् (*yaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ āsīt*)—the Brahmin who is of the nature of a priest and is present
- तत्र (*tatra*)—in such an excellent sacrifice
- यजमानस्य (*yajamānasya*)—of the sacrificer
- संवित् (*saṃvit*)—the need for complete knowledge
- का स्मित् (*kā smit*)—why indeed is it needed?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the excellent sacrifice that the priests of equal understanding arrange in many ways, and to which they bring the gods, and in which the Brahmin, accomplished in the study of the Veda and of the nature of a priest, is intent on the rite, what indeed is the need of the sacrificer's complete knowledge?

##### English translation
Of him who is variously conceived by the noble minded priests engaged
in this rite who do not atter any word, are engaged as a priest, how little do
the worshippers know of him.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकः केवल एनाग्निः दानादिगुणयुक्तो देवः बहुधा बाडववैद्युताद्यनेकप्रकारेण समिद्धः सम्यक् दीपो भवति । यथा एकः एकाकी सूर्यः प्राणिनां

> सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (ऋ. सं. १-११५-१) इति श्रुतेः । किंच एका एकाकिन्नेव
> उषाः तमो विवासयंती देवी सर्वं समस्तमिदं दृश्यमानं जगत् वि भाति

> देवा अष्टेकाकिनः संतोऽनेकभवनसमर्थास्तदा परं ब्रह्म एकं सदनेकं भवेदिति
> किमु वक्तव्यमित्यभिप्रायः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Only one Agni, a god endowed with qualities such as bounty, is kindled well in many ways, as the submarine fire, as lightning and in other manifold forms. As the one, lone Sun, the god who rouses beings well to action, having entered into the whole world, as the Śruti says तत्सृष्टा तदेवानुप्राविशत् (*tatsṛṣṭā tadevānuprāviśat*) (Tai. U. 2-6) **NOTE** **GLOSS**, has appeared in many forms; for the Śruti says सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1) **GLOSS**. Further, the one Dawn alone, the goddess who drives away the darkness, makes all this visible world shine forth in particular. Therefore it is fitting (this is to be supplied) that the one, non-dual Brahman became this world, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, in particular forms. When gods such as Agni, although single, are able to become many, what need is there to say that the supreme Brahman, being one, should become many: such is the intention.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एक एवाग्निः (*eka evāgniḥ*)—the one Agni, of the nature of truth
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—in many forms, such as lightning
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—is kindled
- एकः सूर्यः (*ekaḥ sūryaḥ*)—the one Sun
- विश्वं अनु (*viśvaṃ anu*)—having entered the whole world
- प्रभूतः (*prabhūtaḥ*)—is produced in different forms
- एक एव उषाः (*eka eva uṣāḥ*)—the one goddess Dawn
- इदं सर्वं (*idaṃ sarvaṃ*)—all this world
- वि भाति (*vi bhāti*)—illumines
- एकं ना इदं (*ekaṃ nā idaṃ*)—this one principle, of the nature of truth
- सर्वं (*sarvaṃ*)—in all the forms of the world
- वि बभूव (*vi babhūva*)—has been transformed

### Printed p. 654

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The one Agni, of the nature of truth, is kindled in many forms such as lightning. The one Sun, having entered the whole world, is produced in different forms. The one goddess of dawn illumines this whole world. This one principle, of the nature of truth, has been transformed into all the forms of the world.

##### English translation
Sage Agni appears kindled in many forms; one Sun lords over the whole world ; one Dawn reveal every thing. One is in various forms.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ज्योति॑ष्मंतं केतु॒मंतं॑ त्रिच॒क्रं सु॒खं रथं॑ सु॒षदं॒ भूरि॑वारं ।  
> चि॒त्राम॑घा॒ यस्य॒ योगे॑ऽधिजज्ञे॒ तं वां॑ हु॒वे अति॑ रिक्तं॒  ॑
> पिबध्यॆ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ज्योतिष्मंतं । केतुमंतं । त्रिचक्रं । सुखं । रथं । सुसदं । भूरिवारं ।  
> चित्रमघा । यस्य । योगे । अधिजज्ञे । तं । वां । हुवे । अति । रिक्तं । पिबध्यै ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विश्वेदेवाः वां । वचनव्यत्ययश्चादसः । वो युष्माकं मध्यॆ अतिरिक्तं
> निरतिशयं तं तच्छब्दवाच्यं परमात्मानं पिबध्यॆ सोमं पातुं हुवे आह्वयामि ।
> तं कं । यस्य परमात्मनः योगे सेव्यसेवकभावसंबंधे सति चित्रमघा । चित्रं
> चायनीयं मघं गवाश्वादिलक्षणं धनं यस्याः सा चित्रमघा । पूजनीयानेकधनोपेता लक्ष्मीः अधि जज्ञे अधिकं प्रादुरभूत् युधिष्ठिरादेस्तं । केदृशं तं ।
> ज्योतिष्मंतं ज्योतींषि सूर्यादीनि प्रकाश्यत्वेन संति यस्य तं । तस्य भासा
> सर्वमिदं विभाति इति श्रुतेः । केतुमंतं । केतवः प्रज्ञाः विषयाः संति यस्य तं ।
> यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित् (मु. उ. १-१-९) इति श्रुतेः । केतुरिति प्रज्ञानाम । केतुः
> केत इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । त्रिचक्रं त्रिषु भूरादिलोकेषु चक्रं चंक्रमणं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Viśvedevas, "among you" (the change of number is Vedic): I call that unsurpassed one, the Supreme Self, indicated by the word "that", to drink Soma. Which one? He in union with whom, that is, in the relation of served and servant, Lakṣmī, endowed with wonderful, desirable wealth in the form of cows, horses and the like, arose in abundance, as to Yudhiṣṭhira and others **NOTE**. What is he like? ज्योतिष्मंतं (*jyotiṣmaṃtaṃ*): he who has lights such as the Sun as things to be illumined; for the Śruti says तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति (*tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti*) **GLOSS**. केतुमंतं (*ketumaṃtaṃ*): he who has cognitions, that is, cognitions, as his objects; for the Śruti says यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित् (*yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit*) (Mu. U. 1-1-9) **NOTE** **GLOSS**; केतुः (*ketuḥ*) is a name for cognition, since केतुः केत (*ketuḥ keta*) are read among its names. त्रिचक्रं (*tricakraṃ*): he who has a striding, that is, a striding, in the three worlds, Bhūḥ and the rest,

### Printed p. 655

> त्रिविक्रमावतारे यस्य तं । इदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे (ऋ. सं. १-१३-१७) इत्यादि श्रुतेः ।
> यद्वा त्रिषु लोकेषु अप्रतिहतं चक्रं सुदर्शनाख्यं यस्य तं । सुखं निरतिशयानंदात्मकं । ओं कं ब्रह्म खं इति श्रुतेः । रथं रंहणस्वभावं । गमनशीलमिति
> यावत् । अपाणिपादो जवनो ग्रहीता (श्वे. उ. ३-१९) इति श्रुतेः । सुषदं ।
> शोभने आत्मस्वरूपे सीदति तिष्ठतीति सुषत् सुप्रतिष्ठः तं । प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठा प्रज्ञानं
> ब्रह्म इति श्रुतेः । भूरिवारं भूरिभिर्बहुभिः प्राणिभिः वारो वरणेयस्तं ।
> सर्वात्मकत्वात् सर्वप्रियत्वमुचितमस्य । आत्मनः कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति
> (बृ उ. २-४-५) इति श्रुतेः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

in the Trivivikrama incarnation, as the Śruti and so on say इदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे (*idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-17) **NOTE** **GLOSS**. Or else, he whose discus, called Sudarśana, is unobstructed in the three worlds. सुखं (*sukhaṃ*): of the nature of unsurpassed bliss; for the Śruti says ओं कं ब्रह्म खं (*oṃ kaṃ brahma khaṃ*) **GLOSS**. रथं (*rathaṃ*): of the nature of swiftness, that is, given to moving; for the Śruti says अपाणिपादो जवनो ग्रहीता (*apāṇipādo javano grahītā*) (Śve. U. 3-19) **NOTE** **GLOSS**. सुषदं (*suṣadaṃ*): he who abides, that is, stands, in his own beautiful nature of the Self, well established; for the Śruti says प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठा प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म (*prajñā pratiṣṭhā prajñānaṃ brahma*) **GLOSS**. भूरिवारं (*bhūrivāraṃ*): he who is to be chosen by many beings. Since he is of the nature of all, being dear to all is fitting for him; for the Śruti says आत्मनः कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति (*ātmanaḥ kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati*) (Bṛ. U. 2-4-5) **GLOSS**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—(O Viśvedevas) of which Supreme Self
- योगे (*yoge*)—there being connection
- चित्रामघा (*citrāmaghā*)—the worshipful goddess of wealth
- अधिजज्ञॆ (*adhijajñè*)—is born, such a one
- वां (*vāṃ*)—among all of you
- अति रिक्तं (*ati riktaṃ*)—one of surpassing glory
- ज्योतिष्मंतं (*jyotiṣmaṃtaṃ*)—one possessed of radiance, who causes light even to the Sun and the rest
- केतुमंतं (*ketumaṃtaṃ*)—one who has cognition as his object
- त्रिचक्रं (*tricakraṃ*)—one whose nature is to move in the three worlds
- सुखं (*sukhaṃ*)—the giver of unsurpassed bliss of the Self
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—one given to moving
- सुषदं (*suṣadaṃ*)—one whose state in the Self is excellent
- भूरिवारं (*bhūrivāraṃ*)—one who is worthy of the search of all
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Supreme Self
- पिबध्यै (*pibadhyai*)—to drink Soma
- हुवे (*huve*)—I pray and call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viśvedevas, I pray and call that Supreme Self, to drink Soma: he in connection with whom the worshipful goddess of wealth is born; one of surpassing glory among all of you; one possessed of radiance, who causes light even to the Sun and the rest; one who has cognition as his object; one whose nature is to move in the three worlds; the giver of unsurpassed bliss of the Self; one given to moving; one whose state in the Self is excellent; and one who is worthy of the search of all.

##### English translation
Dazzling chariot moving quickly on its three wheels, sending out brilliance with easy seat and abundance with his approach the dawn came out with wounderful abundance ; come here and drink in your charit.

### Printed p. 656
## Sūkta 59 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, इमानि वां (*imāni vāṃ*), is the eleventh and last among the Vālakhilya sūktas. It has seven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Suparṇa Kāṇva; the deity is Indra and Varuṇa; the metre is Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: इमानि वां सप्त सुपर्ण ऐंद्रावरुणं जागतं (*imāni vāṃ sapta suparṇa aiṃdrāvaruṇaṃ jāgataṃ*). The use in ritual is to be learnt from the Sūtra.

##### Particulars

Sūkta 59 (Vālakhilya sūkta 11). Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 6. Sūkta 59. Aṣṭaka 6. Adhyāya 4. Varga 30, 31. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: Suparṇaḥ Kāṇvaḥ. Deity: Indrāvaruṇā. Metre: Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मानि॑ वां भाग॒धेया॑नि सिस्रत॒ इंद्रा॑वरुणा॒ प्र म॒हे ॒॑ 
> सुतेषु वां ।  
> य॒ज्ञेय॑ज्ञे ह॒ सव॑ना भुर॒ण्यथो॒ यत्सु॑न्व॒ते यज॑मानाय॒  ॑
> शिक्षथः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमानि । वां । भागधेयानि । सिस्त्रते । इंद्रावरुणा । प्र । महे । सुतेषु । वां ।  
> यज्ञेयज्ञे । ह । सवना । भुरण्यथः । यत् । सुन्वते । यजमानाय । शिक्षथः ॥

### Printed p. 657

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणा इंद्रावरुणौ इमानि इदानीं कृतानि भागधेयानि भवदंशभूतानि चरुपुरोडाशादिहवींषि वां युवां प्रति सिस्रते प्राप्तुमिच्छंति । अतः
> सुतेषु अभिषुतेषु सोमेषु सत्सु महे महते पूजनाय वां युवां प्र
> प्रार्चये । उपसर्गवशाद्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । यत् यस्मात् यज्ञेयज्ञे
> प्रतियज्ञं सवना त्रिष्टपि सवनेषु भुरण्यथो ह गच्छथः खलु । किंच सुन्वते
> सोमाभिषवं कुर्वते यजमानाय शिक्षथः अभिमतं प्रयच्छथः। शिक्षतिर्दानकर्मा।
> पृणाति शिक्षति इति दानकर्मगु पाठात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, these portions that have now been made, your shares, that is, oblations such as caru and puroḍāśa that have become your part, desire to reach you. Therefore, when the Soma has been pressed, I honour you two forth for great worship; the verb that suits the preposition is to be supplied. Because at every sacrifice you two go to the three savanas, and further give what he desires to the sacrificer who presses Soma. The root the verb शिक्षति (*śikṣati*) has the sense of giving, since it is read among the verbs of giving.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa
- यत् (*yat*)—by whose power of yours
- यज्ञॆ यज्ञे ह (*yajñè yajñe ha*)—to each and every sacrifice
- सवना (*savanā*)—at all three times of pressing
- भुरण्यथः (*bhuraṇyathaḥ*)—you go (and)
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—to the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice
- यजमानाय (*yajamānāya*)—to the performer of the sacrifice
- शिक्षथः (*śikṣathaḥ*)—you give what he desires (therefore)
- वां (*vāṃ*)—offered with you in view
- इमानि भागधेयानि (*imāni bhāgadheyāni*)—these caru and puroḍāśa, which belong to your share
- सिस्रते (*sisrate*)—approach, desiring you alone
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—when the Soma juice has been pressed and made ready
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- महे (*mahe*)—for worship
- प्र (*pra*)—I pray

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities Indra and Varuṇa, by your power you go at the three times of pressing to each and every sacrifice, and give to the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice what he desires. Therefore the caru, puroḍāśa and the like, which are offered with you in view and belong to your share, approach you alone, desiring you. When the Soma juice has been pressed and made ready, I pray to you for your worship.

##### English translation
Agni, Indra, Varuna in the chief rite we invoke you to drink Soma. This is your portion; come following it, in every rite, nourish the sacrifices and libations, make gift to the worshipper offering Soma libations.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणा इंद्रावरुण् भवंतो यदा आस्तां ओषध्यादिकर्तृत्वेनाभूतां तदा निःसिद्धरीः नितरां मंगलस्वभावा ओषधीः व्रीह्याद्या ओषधयः आपः

> भवंतौ रजसोऽंतरिक्षलोकस्य संबंधिनः अध्वनो मार्गस्य पारे परतीरे सिस्रतुः

> असुरादिः नकिः ओहते न कोऽपि तर्कगोचरो भवति । स्वेच्छया । विहरतोर्भवतोः
> गतिप्रतिघातकः शत्रुः न कोऽप्यस्तीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, when you two became the makers of herbs and the like, then the highly auspicious herbs, rice and the other plants, and the waters attain your greatness. Further, you two who move at will on the far shore of the path of the rajas, the atmospheric world: of you two no enemy, a destroyer, an the word अदेवः (*adevaḥ*), that is, one opposed to the gods, such as an Asura, is conceivable. The meaning is that there is no enemy at all to obstruct the going of you two as you roam at your own will.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa
- आस्तां (*āstāṃ*)—(when) you are the makers of herbs and the like, then
- निः सिध्वरिः (*niḥ sidhvariḥ*)—of auspicious nature
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the herbs, rice and so on
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—your greatness itself
- आशत (*āśata*)—attain
- या (*yā*)—you who
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- अध्वनः पारे (*adhvanaḥ pāre*)—in all the shore regions of the paths
- सिस्रतुः (*sisratuḥ*)—move, such as you are
- ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—to you two
- शत्रुः (*śatruḥ*)—one who is an enemy
- आदेवः (*ādevaḥ*)—and is opposed to the gods
- नकिः ओहते (*nakiḥ ohate*)—no Asura is able to withstand you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities Indra and Varuṇa, when you are the makers of herbs and the like, the auspicious herbs, rice and so on, and the waters attain your greatness itself. No Asura, an enemy and opponent of the gods, is able to withstand you two, who move in all the shore regions of the paths of the atmosphere.

### Printed p. 659

##### English translation
Indra and Varuna are here, walking by a path leading to beyond the sky ; no god-fearing men can be their enemy. The vegetable and water attain their powers ;

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒त्यं तदिं॑द्रावरुणा कृ॒शस्य॑ वां॒ मध्व॑ ऊ॒र्मिं दु॑हते स॒प्त  ॑
> वाणीः ।  
> ताभि॑र्दा॒श्वांस॑मवतं शुभस्पती॒ यो वा॒मद॑ब्बो अ॒भि पाति॒  ॑
> चित्तिभिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सत्यं । तत् । इंद्रावरुणा । कृशस्य । वां । मध्वः । ऊर्मिं । दुहते । सप्त । वाणीः ।  
> ताभिः । दाश्वांसं । अवतं । शुभः । पती इति । यः । वां । आदब्धः । अभि । पाति ।  
> चित्तिभिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणा इंद्रावरुणौ याः सप्तसंख्याकाः सर्पणस्वभावा वा वाणीः
> वाण्यः सप्तहोत्रकाणां स्तुतिरूपा वाचः कृशस्य एतन्नान्नो यजमानस्य संबंधिनः
> मध्वः मधुरस्य सोमस्य ऊर्मिं तदुपलक्षितं रसं प्रति वां युवां हवते
> प्रपूरयंतीति यत् तत्सत्यमवितथमेव । तस्मात्ताभिर्वाणीभिर्हेतुभूताभिः युवां
> दाश्वांसं हविर्दत्तवंतं यजमानं अवतं रक्षतं । यजमानं विशिनष्टि । हे
> शुभस्पती उदकस्य पालयिताराविंद्रावरुणौ यो यजमानः अदब्धः केनाप्यहिंसितः
> सन् चित्तिभिः प्रज्ञोपलक्षितैः कर्मभिः वां युवामभि पाति सर्वतो रक्षति ।
> तमवतमिति पूर्वणान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, the seven words, which are seven in number or of a flowing nature, the speeches in praise of the seven hotṛs, fill you two, in the direction of the wave of the sweet Soma, that is, the juice that is marked by it, of the sacrificer called Kṛśa: that is true, unfailing. Therefore, by those words as the cause, protect the sacrificer who has given the oblation. He describes the sacrificer: O Śubhaspatī, protectors of water, Indra and Varuṇa, the sacrificer who, unharmed by anyone, guards you two on every side with actions marked by understanding, protect him; the construction is with what precedes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa
- सप्त वाणीः (*sapta vāṇīḥ*)—the speeches in praise of the seven hotṛs
- कृशस्य (*kṛśasya*)—of the sacrificer called Kṛśa
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of the sweet Soma juice

### Printed p. 660
- ऊर्मिं (*ūrmiṃ*)—towards the juice
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two
- दुहते (*duhate*)—bring and fill: that which is said
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—is indeed of the nature of truth
- शुभस्पती (*śubhaspatī*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa, protectors of water
- अदब्धः (*adabdhaḥ*)—unharmed by anyone
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- चित्तिभिः (*cittibhiḥ*)—with his own actions done with understanding
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you two
- अभि पाति (*abhi pāti*)—guards on every side
- दाश्वांसं (*dāśvāṃsaṃ*)—that same sacrificer, the giver of oblation
- शाभिः (*śābhiḥ*)—in return for those same praises
- अवतं (*avataṃ*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities Indra and Varuṇa, that which is said, that the speeches in praise of the seven hotṛs bring you and fill you two towards the juice of the sweet Soma of the sacrificer called Kṛśa, is indeed of the nature of truth. O Indra and Varuṇa, protectors of water, protect that same sacrificer, the giver of oblation, in return for those same praises, who, unharmed by anyone, guards you on every side with his own actions done with understanding.

##### English translation
Indra and Varuna, it is true that for you Saptavani is effusing the Soma of Krisha ; you are the supporter of good works. The men without enemy who worship you wih good works, protect him your worshipper.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> घृ॒त॒पुषः॒ सौम्या॑ जी॒रदा॑नवः स॒प्त स्वसा॑रः॒ सद॑न ऋ॒तस्य॑ ।  
> या ह॑ वामिंद्रावरुणा घृत॒श्चुत॒स्ताभि॑र्धत्तं॒ यज॑मानाय  
> शिक्षतं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> घृतंपुषः । सौम्याः । जीरदानवः । सप्त । स्वसारः । सदने । ऋतस्य ।  
> याः । ह । वां । इंद्रावरुणा । घृतश्चुतः । ताभिः । धत्तं । यजमानाय । शिक्षतं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ताः सत्यवाण्यः क्व संतीत्यपेक्षायामाह । ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य सदने स्थाने सप्त
> सप्तसंख्याकाः स्वसारः स्वयंसारिण्यो वाण्यः संति । कीदृश्यस्ताः । घृतपुरुषः ।
> घृतमित्युदकनाम । तेन सोमरसो लक्ष्यते । तथा च सोमरसस्राविण्य इत्यर्थः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Where are those true words? In answer to this question he says: in the seat, the place, of ṛta, the sacrifice, there are seven words, "sisters", that is, flowing of themselves. What are they like? घृतपुरुषः (*ghṛtapuruṣaḥ*) **NOTE**: घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*) is a name for water, and by it the Soma juice is indicated. Thus the meaning is that they are streaming with the Soma juice.

### Printed p. 661

> सोम्याः सोमार्हाः जीरदानवः क्षिप्रदानाः । किंच हे इंद्रावरुणा इंद्रावरुणौ
> या वाण्यः वां युवामुद्दिश्य धृतश्चुतः सोमरसस्राविण्यो भवंति अथवा
> आज्यस्राविण्यो भवंति । हेति प्रसिद्धं । ताभिर्हेतुभूताभिः धत्तं यजमानं
> पुष्टीतं । तदर्थं च यजमानाय शिक्षतमभिमतं दत्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seven words are worthy of Soma and are quick givers. Further, O Indra and Varuṇa, those words which, addressed to you, drip Soma juice, or else drip ghee: the particle in the verse means that this is well known. By those words as the cause, support the sacrificer; and for that purpose give the sacrificer what he desires.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धृतपुरुषः (*dhṛtapuruṣaḥ*)—those that pour the Soma juice in the form of water
- सौम्याः (*saumyāḥ*)—worthy of Soma
- जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*)—those that give quickly
- सप्त स्वसारः (*sapta svasāraḥ*)—the seven words
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice, which is of the nature of truth
- सदने (*sadane*)—are in the place
- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa
- धृतश्चुतः (*dhṛtaścutaḥ*)—which press the Soma juice
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which words of praise
- वां (*vāṃ*)—praise you
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—with them
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—be a support to the sacrificer
- यजमानाय (*yajamānāya*)—to the sacrificer
- शिक्षतं (*śikṣataṃ*)—give what he desires

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seven words, which pour the Soma juice in the form of water, are worthy of Soma and give quickly, are in the place of the sacrifice, which is of the nature of truth. O deities Indra and Varuṇa, with those words of praise that press the Soma juice and praise you, be a support to the sacrificer. Give the sacrificer what he desires.

##### English translation
The amiable seven sisters in the house of rite, are become giver of abundance. Indra and Varuna those who drop ghee for you, uphold them, give them gifts.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अवो॑चाम मह॒ते सौभ॑गाय स॒त्यं त्वे॒षाभ्यां॑ महि॒मान॑मिंद्रि॒यं ।  
> अ॒स्मान्ति॑न्नंद्रावरुणा धृत॒श्चुत॒स्त्रिभिः॑ सा॒प्तेभि॑रवतं शुभस्पती ॥

### Printed p. 662

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अवोचाम । महते । सौभगाय । सत्यं । त्वेषाभ्यां । महिमानं । इंद्रियं ।  
> अस्मान् । सु । इंद्रावरुणा । धृतश्चुतः । त्रिभिः । साप्तेभिः । अवतं । शुभः । पती  
> इति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणा इंद्रावरुणौ त्वेषाभ्यां दीप्ताभ्यां भवद्भा० संपादितं
> महिमानं कीर्तिविशेषं वयं महते बृहते सौभगाय ऐश्वर्याय अवोचाम
> वर्णयेम । कीदृशं महिमानं । सत्यमवितथं । युष्मत्स्वरूपानुकूलमित्यर्थः ।
> इंद्रियं इंद्रयोः परमेश्वरयोर्भवतोर्ज्ञापकं । तस्मात् हे शुभस्पती
> उदकस्य पालयिताराविंद्रावरुणौ युवां धृतश्चुतः सोमरसस्राविणोऽस्मान्
> यजमानान् त्रिभिः साप्तेभिः । सप्तयोऽश्वाः तेषां समूहः । सप्तयूथैस्तैः
> त्रिसंख्याकैरश्वसमूहैः सोतं (? सु अवतं] सुतरां पालयतं । इंद्रावरुणयोरैश्वर्ययोगात् अश्वैरस्मत्पालनं समंजसमिति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, we would describe, for great good fortune, that is, prosperity, the greatness, the special renown, brought about by you two, the radiant ones. What sort of greatness? True, unfailing, that is, in accord with your nature; and making known you two, the two supreme lords. Therefore, O Śubhaspatī, protectors of water, Indra and Varuṇa, you who stream Soma juice, protect us, the sacrificers, well with three sevens: sapti are horses, and their company; with those three companies of horses protect us exceedingly **NOTE**. Since Indra and Varuṇa are lords, protection of us by horses is fitting: such is the sense. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa
- त्वेषाभ्यां (*tveṣābhyāṃ*)—brought about by you, the shining ones
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—of the nature of truth
- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—and making known your nature
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—the greatness
- महते (*mahate*)—for great
- सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*)—well-being
- अवोचाम (*avocāma*)—we praise
- शुभस्पती (*śubhaspatī*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa, protectors of water
- धृतश्चुतः (*dhṛtaścutaḥ*)—who press and offer the Soma juice
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- त्रिभिः साप्तेभिः (*tribhiḥ sāptebhiḥ*)—with the three horses
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- अवतं (*avataṃ*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities Indra and Varuṇa, we praise, for great well-being, the greatness brought about by you, the shining ones, which is of the nature of truth and makes known your nature. O deities Indra and Varuṇa, protectors of water, protect exceedingly us, who press and offer the Soma juice, together with the three horses.

##### English translation
Desirous of good fortune we are praising the nobleness of brilliant
Indra and Varuna. We are dropping ghee, Indra and Varuna are the lords of
righteous works. May they protect us by thrice seven.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑वरुणा॒ यदृ॒षिभ्यो॑ मनी॒षां वा॒चो म॒तिं श्रु॒तम॑दत्त॒मग्रे॑ ।  
> यानि॒ स्थाना॑न्यसृजंत॒ धीरा॑ य॒ज्ञं त॑न्वा॒नास्तप॑सा॒भ्य॑पश्यं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंद्रावरुणा । यत् । ऋषिभ्यः । मनीषां । वाचः । मतिं । श्रुतं । अदत्तं । अग्रे ।  
> यानि । स्थानानि । असृजंत । धीराः । यज्ञं । तन्वानाः । तपसा । अभि । अपश्यं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणा इंद्रावरुणौ यत् ये ऋषयः यज्ञं तन्वानाः कर्मविशेषं विस्तारयंतः अत एव धीराः शुद्धांतःकरणत्वेन धीमंतः संतः अग्रे
> अंतःकरणशुद्धेः प्राक् यानि स्थानानि गृहक्षेत्रादीनि स्थितानि तानि असृजंत विसृष्टवंतः । तत्यजिरिति (? तत्यजुरिति) यावत् । तेभ्य ऋषिभ्यः मंत्रदृग्भ्यः मनीषादिश्रुशांतं सर्वं युवां आदत्तं दत्तवंतौ इत्यहं तपसा आलोचनात्मकेन ज्ञानेन
> अभ्यपश्यं सर्वतो दृष्टवानस्मि । मनीषा अत्र चिज्जडविवेकवती बुद्धिः । वाचः
> उपनिषल्लक्षणा गिरः । मतिर्मननं तर्कसामर्थ्यं । श्रुतं शास्त्रमीमांसालक्षणं ।
> एतत्सर्वं भवद्भा० तेभ्यो दत्तमिति श्रीमच्चरणप्रसादाल्लब्धज्ञानेन मया
> ज्ञातमित्यर्षेवक्तुरभिप्रायः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, those seers who, extending the sacrifice, that is, spreading out a particular rite, and for that very reason wise through a purified mind, gave up, before the purification of the mind, whatever places, houses, fields and the like, they possessed; that is, they abandoned them **NOTE**. To those seers, the beholders of the mantras, you two gave all this, beginning with manīṣā and ending with śruta; thus I have seen on every side through austerity, that is, knowledge consisting of reflection. Here manīṣā is the intellect that discriminates the conscious from the inert; vācaḥ are words characterised as Upaniṣads; mati is reflection, the power of reasoning; śruta is what is characterised by the śāstras and by Mīmāṃsā. All this was given by you two to them, and this has been known by me through knowledge obtained by the grace of your venerable feet: such is the intention of the seer who speaks.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa
- यज्ञं तन्वानाः (*yajñaṃ tanvānāḥ*)—performing the sacrifice at length
- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—being wise
- आग्रे (*āgre*)—prior to their renunciation
- यानि स्थानानि (*yāni sthānāni*)—whatever places there were, such as houses and fields, all of them
- यत् (*yat*)—which seers
- आसृजंत (*āsṛjaṃta*)—gave up
- ऋषिभ्यः (*ṛṣibhyaḥ*)—to such seers
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—discriminating intellect
- वाचः (*vācaḥ*)—the words of truth, such as the Upaniṣads
- मतिं (*matiṃ*)—the power of reflection and the like
- श्रुतं (*śrutaṃ*)—knowledge of the śāstras and the like
- अदत्तं (*adattaṃ*)—that you graciously gave
- तपसा (*tapasā*)—by the power of my austerity
- अभ्यपश्यं (*abhyapaśyaṃ*)—I have found out

### Printed p. 664

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities Indra and Varuṇa, I have found out by the power of my austerity that you graciously gave discriminating intellect, the words of truth such as the Upaniṣads, the power of reflection and the like, and knowledge of the śāstras and the like to those seers who, performing the sacrifice at length and being wise, gave up, prior to their renunciation, whatever houses, fields and other possessions they had.

##### English translation
Indra and Varuna what you did grant to the Rishis wise-worded hymns,
Sruti and the Lokas : we are being engaged in rite, shall engage them.

> अदृप्तं अनुद्धतं । मोहशून्यमिति यावत् । रायः धनस्य पोषं पुष्टिं च
> यजमानेषु धत्तं धारयतं । किंचास्मासु स्तोतृषु प्रजां पुत्रपौत्रादिरूपा
> पुष्टिं धनादेः समृद्धिं भूतिं गवाश्वादिगजांतसंपदं च धत्तं धारयतं । अथ च
> दीर्घायुत्वाय चिरजीवनाय नोऽस्माकमायुः जीवितकालं प्र तिरतं प्रवर्धयतं । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, grant to the sacrificers cheerfulness of mind, and freedom from arrogance, that is, from delusion, and the increase and nourishment of wealth. Further, grant to us, the praisers, offspring, in the form of sons, grandsons and the like, prosperity in the form of the growth of wealth and the rest, and well-being, that is, riches from cows and horses up to elephants. And increase our span of life, our time of living, for long life; the root तिरति (*tirati*) with the prefix has the sense of increasing.

### Printed p. 665

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Indra and Varuṇa
- यजमानेषु (*yajamāneṣu*)—among the sacrificers
- सौमनसं (*saumanasaṃ*)—a cheerful mind
- अदृप्तं (*adṛptaṃ*)—freedom from pride
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- पोषं (*poṣaṃ*)—and nourishment
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—establish
- अस्मासु (*asmāsu*)—in us (the praisers)
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—the wealth of offspring
- पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*)—the prosperity of wealth
- भूतिं (*bhūtiṃ*)—the riches of cows and the like
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—fill
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life
- दीर्घायुत्वाय (*dīrghāyutvāya*)—to live for a long time
- प्र तिरतं (*pra tirataṃ*)—increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities Indra and Varuṇa, establish among the sacrificers a cheerful mind, freedom from pride, wealth and nourishment. Fill us, the praisers, with the wealth of offspring, the prosperity of wealth and the riches of cows and the like. Increase our life so that we may live for a long time.

##### English translation
Indra and Varuna the wealth which pleases the might, but does not make vain, give the worshippers such wealth ; give us sons, nourishment and cover, preserve our longevity, that we may live long

## Sūkta 60 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सप्तमेऽनुवाके दश सूक्तानि । तत्राग्न आ याहीति विंशत्यृचं प्रथमं
> सूक्तं प्रगाथपुत्रस्य भर्गस्यार्षमाग्नेयं । प्रथमातृतीयाद्ययुजो बृहत्क्यो
> द्वितीयाचतुर्थादियुजः सतोबृहत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अग्न आ विंशतिभर्गः
> प्रागाथ आग्नेयं प्रागाथं त्विति ॥ प्रातरनुवाक आग्नेये क्रत् बार्हते छंदस्याश्विनशस्त्रे चेदं सूक्तं । तथा च सूत्रितं । आयमग्निरग्न आ याहि । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the seventh anuvāka there are ten sūktas. Among them the first sūkta, तत्राग्न आ याहीति (*tatrāgna ā yāhīti*), of twenty Ṛks, has as its seer Bharga, the son of Pragātha; its deity is Agni. The first, third and the other odd Ṛks are Bṛhatī, the second, fourth and the other even ones are Satobṛhatī. So it is stated in the Anukramaṇikā: अग्न आ विंशतिभर्गः प्रागाथ आग्नेयं प्रागाथं त्विति (*agna ā viṃśatibhargaḥ prāgātha āgneyaṃ prāgāthaṃ tviti*) **GLOSS**. At the morning recitation this sūkta serves for the Āgneya kratu, for the Ṛks in the Bṛhatī metre, and for the Āśvina śastra. So it is aphorised: आयमग्निरग्न आ याहि (*āyamagniragna ā yāhi*) (Ā. 4-13) **GLOSS**.

##### Anuvāda

In the seventh anuvāka of the eighth maṇḍala of the Ṛgvedasaṃhitā there are ten sūktas. Among them this sūkta, अग्न आ याहि (*agna ā yāhi*), is the first. It has twenty Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Bharga, the son of Pragātha; the deity is Agni. The odd Ṛks of this sūkta, the first, third and so on, are in the Bṛhatī metre. The even Ṛks

### Printed p. 666
are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अग्न आ विंशतिर्भर्गः प्रागाथ आग्नॆयं प्रागाथं तु (*agna ā viṃśatirbhargaḥ prāgātha āgnèyaṃ prāgāthaṃ tu*) **GLOSS**. At the time of reciting the mantras of the morning recitation, this sūkta is applied for the Ṛks in the Bṛhatī metre connected with the Āgneya kratu and for the mantras of the Āśvina śastra, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra अयमग्निरग्न आ याहि (*ayamagniragna ā yāhi*) (Ā. 4-13).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 60. Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 7. Aṣṭaka 6. Adhyāya 4. Varga 32, 33, 34, 35. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 20. Seer: Bhargaḥ Prāgāthaḥ. Deity: Āgniḥ **NOTE**. Metre: Prāgāthaṃ.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्न॒ आ या॑ह्य॒ग्निभि॒र्होता॑रं त्वा वृणीमहे ।  
> आ त्वाम॑नक्तु॒ प्रय॑ता ह॒विष्म॑ती॒ यजि॑ष्ठं ब॒र्हिरा॒सदे॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । आ । याहि । अग्निभिः । होतारं । त्वा । वृणीमहे ।  
> आ । त्वां । आनक्तु । प्रयता । हविष्मती । यजिष्यं । बर्हिः । आसदे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने अग्निभिर्यष्टवैः सहा याहि । आगच्छ । तदर्थं होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं त्वा त्वां वृणीमहे । त्वा त्वामागतं प्रयताध्वर्युहस्ताभ्यां
> नियता हविष्मती धृतवती यजिष्ठं त्वां बर्हिर्बर्हिष्यासद आसाद्या सर्वतोऽनक्तु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, come with the agnis fit to be worshipped. For that purpose we choose you as hotṛ, the caller of the gods. May the ladle, held in the adhvaryu's hand, filled with the oblation, anoint you on every side, you, the most worthy of worship, as you come, when you are seated on the sacred grass.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अग्निभिः (*agnibhiḥ*)—with your other special glories
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—who are of the nature of the hotṛ
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वृणीमहे (*vṛṇīmahe*)—we choose
- प्रयता (*prayatā*)—offered by the hand of the adhvaryu
- हविष्मती (*haviṣmatī*)—and possessed of the oblation, this ladle (the ghee)
- यजिष्ठं (*yajiṣṭhaṃ*)—the most worshipful
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—on the seat of sacred grass
- आसदे (*āsade*)—to sit
- आ अनस्तु (*ā anastu*)—may it perform the anointing everywhere

### Printed p. 667

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, come with your other special glories; we choose you, who are of the nature of the hotṛ. May the ghee, offered by the ladle in the adhvaryu's hand and having the nature of an oblation, perform the anointing everywhere, so that you may be seated on the seat of sacred grass.

##### English translation
Agni, come hither with the fires, we choose you as our invoking priest ; let the presented offering anoint you, the chief sacrificer, to sit down on the sacred grass.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अच्छा॒ हि त्वा॑ सहसः सूनो अंगिरः॒ स्रुच॒श्चरं॑त्यध्व॒रे ।  
> ऊ॒र्जो नपा॑तं धृ॒तके॑शमीमहे॒ग्निं य॒ज्ञेषु॑ पू॒र्व्यं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अच्छ । हि । त्वा । सहसः । सूनो इति । अंगिरः । स्रुचः । चरंति । अध्वरे ।  
> ऊर्जः । नपातं । घृतकेशं । ईमहे । अग्निं । यज्ञेषु । पूर्व्यं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सहसः सूनो बलस्य पुत्र । बलेन मध्यमानत्वात् । हे अंगिरोऽंगिरसां मध्य एक । अथवांगतिर्गतिकर्मा । सर्वत्र संगत । त्वा त्वामध्वरे यागेऽच्छाभिप्राप्तं स्रुचश्चरंति । गच्छंति । आत ऊर्जोऽन्नस्य नपातं न पातयितारं रक्षकं बलस्य
> नप्तारं ना धृतकेशं प्रदीप्तकलशस्थानीयज्वालं पूर्व्यं पुरातनं पूरकं वाग्निं
> यज्ञेष्वस्मदीयेष्टिमहे । सौमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O son of strength, because Agni is produced by churning with strength; O Aṅgiras, the chief one among the Aṅgirases, or else (the root is of the sense of motion) the one who goes everywhere: the ladles move toward you, who have been brought near at the sacrifice. Therefore we pray, at our sacrifices, to Agni, the protector of food (or the one who does not let it fall), or the grandson of strength, who is butter-haired, whose flame is like a kindled vessel, and who is ancient or the fulfiller. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*)—chief among the Aṅgirases
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- अच्छ (*accha*)—to bring you toward us
- स्रुचः (*srucaḥ*)—the ladles
- चरंति हि (*caraṃti hi*)—are striving
- ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*)—of food
- नपातं (*napātaṃ*)—the protector
- घृतकेशं (*ghṛtakeśaṃ*)—who has blazing flames
- पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*)—the ancient
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we praise

### Printed p. 668

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength, chief among the Aṅgirases, the ladles are striving to bring you before us in the sacrifice. We praise in the sacrifices Agni, the protector of food, the one with blazing flames, the ancient.

##### English translation
Angiras, son of strength, the ladles go to find you in the sacrifice ; we praise the ancient Agni in our offerings, the grandson of food, butter-haired.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ क॒विर्वे॒दा अ॑सि॒ होता॑ पावक॒ यक्ष्यः॑ ।  
> मं॒द्रो यजि॑ष्ठो अध्व॒रेष्वीड्यो॒ विप्रे॑भिः शुक्र॒ मन्म॑भिः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । कविः । वेधाः । असि । होता । पावक । यक्ष्यः ।  
> मंद्रः । यजिष्ठः । अध्वरेषु । ईड्यः । विप्रेभिः । शुक्र । मन्मभिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने कविर्मेधावी त्वं वेधा विधातासि फलानां । हे पावक होता
> देवानामाह्वाता होमनिष्पादको वा यक्ष्यो यष्टव्योऽसि हे शुक्र दीप्त
> मंद्रो मोदनीयो यजिष्ठो यष्टृतमस्त्वमध्वरेषु यज्ञेषु विप्रेभिर्म
> धाविभिर्युत्विग्भिर्मन्मभिर्मननीयैः स्तोत्रैरीड्यः स्तुत्योऽसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you who are wise, you are the ordainer of the fruits. O purifier, you are the hotṛ, the caller of the gods, or the accomplisher of the oblation, and you are the one to be worshipped. O bright one, you are delightful and the best of worshippers; in the sacrifices you are to be praised by the wise priests with hymns worthy of meditation. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—you who are wise
- वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*)—as the creator
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- पावक (*pāvaka*)—O Agni, the purifier
- होता (*hotā*)—the caller of the gods to the sacrifice
- यक्ष्यः (*yakṣyaḥ*)—and the most worshipful, you are
- शुक्र (*śukra*)—O Agni, the radiant
- मंद्रः (*maṃdraḥ*)—the delightful
- यजिष्ठः (*yajiṣṭhaḥ*)—the most worshipful, you
- विप्रेभिः (*viprebhiḥ*)—by the wise priests
- मन्मभिः (*manmabhiḥ*)—by means of hymns of meditation
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)—you are praised

### Printed p. 669

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who are wise are the creator. O purifier, you are the caller of the gods to the sacrifice and the most worshipful. O radiant Agni, you who are delightful and most worshipful are praised in the sacrifices by the wise priests by means of hymns of meditation.

##### English translation
Agni, you, wise, are the creator (of consequences) ; O purifier, you are the invoking priest, worthy of worship ; bright one, you are to be praised in our sacrifices by the priests with hymns, yourself the chief ministrant worthy to be rejoiced in.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अद्रो॑घ॒मा व॑होश॒तो य॑विष्ठ्य दे॒वा अ॑जस्र वी॒तये॑ ।  
> अ॒भि प्रयां॑सि॒ सुधि॒ता व॑सो गहि॒ मंद॑स्व धी॒तिभि॑र्हि॒तः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अद्रोघं । आ । वह । उशतः । यविष्य । देवान् । अजस्र । वीतये ।  
> आभि । प्रयांसि । सुधिता । वसो इति । गहि । मंदस्व । धीतिभिः । हितः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अद्रोघमद्रोग्द्धारं मां प्रति हे यविष्ठ्य युवतमाजस्र नित्य आ वह ।
> आनय । कान् । उशतोऽस्मदर्थं कामयमानान्देवान् । किमर्थं । वीतयेहविर्भक्षणाय । हे वसो वासकाग्ने सुधिता सुनिहितानि प्रयांस्यन्नान्यभि गहि ।
> अभिगच्छ । अगत्य च धीतिभिः स्तुतिभिर्हितो निहितः सन्मंदस्व । यद्वा । धीतिभिर्मंदस्पेति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O ever-youthful, constant Agni, bring to me, who do not injure, the gods who desire (the oblation) on our behalf, so that they may eat the oblation. O Vasu, dweller-giving Agni, go to the well-placed foods; having come, and being set in place with praises, rejoice. Or else the construction is: rejoice with the praises. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यविष्ठ्य (*yaviṣṭhya*)—O Agni, the most youthful
- अजस्र (*ajasra*)—the eternal
- उशतः (*uśataḥ*)—who desire the oblation
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—to eat the oblation
- अद्रोघं (*adroghaṃ*)—to me, who am without blemish
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Agni, giver of dwelling

### Printed p. 670

- सुधिता (*sudhitā*)—well offered
- प्रयांसि अभि (*prayāṃsi abhi*)—toward the foods
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be pleased to come
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—you who are well established
- धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)—with praises
- मंदस्व (*maṃdasva*)—rejoice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, most youthful and eternal, bring the gods who desire the oblation to me, who am without blemish, to eat the oblation. O Agni, giver of dwelling, be pleased to come toward the well-offered foods. You who are well established, rejoice with the praises.

##### English translation
Most youthful, eternal one, bring the longing gods to me guileless, to eat (the oblation) ; giver of dwellings, approach the well-placed food ; rejoice, being set in your place with praises.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमित्स॒प्रथा॑ अ॒स्यग्ने॑ त्रातर्ऋ॒तस्क॒विः ।  
> त्वां विप्रा॑सः समिधान दीदिव॒ आ वि॑वासंति वे॒धसः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वां । विप्रासः । संइधान । दीदिवः । आ । विवासंति । वेधसः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आग्ने त्राता रक्षक ऋतः सत्यभूतः कविः क्रांतप्रज्ञस्त्वमित्त्वमेव सप्रथाः
> सर्वतः पृथुरसि । भवसि । हे समिधान समिध्यमान हे दीदिवो दीप्त त्वां विप्रासो
> विप्रा मेधाविनो वेधसो विधातारः स्तोतारो विवासंति । परिचरंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, protector, truthful, wise: you alone are widely extended on every side. O kindled and shining one, the wise, the ordainers, that is, the praisers, serve you.

- त्वं इत् (*tvaṃ it*)—you alone

- दीदिवः (*dīdivaḥ*)—O radiant Agni

- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—the wise
- वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)—the praisers
- आ विवासंति (*ā vivāsaṃti*)—serve everywhere

### Printed p. 671

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who are the protector, the truthful and the one of surpassing wisdom, are extended and pervade everywhere. O well-kindled and radiant Agni, the wise and the praisers serve you everywhere.

##### English translation
Deliverer Agni, you, the truthful and the seer, are widely spread ; O kindled blazing one, the wise praisers wait on you.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शोचा॑ शोचिष्ठ दीदि॒हि वि॒शे मयो॒ रास्व॑ स्तो॒त्रे म॒हा  ॑
> असि ।  
> दे॒वानां॒ शर्म॒न्मनु॑ संतु सू॒रयः॑ शत्रू॒षाहः॑ स्व॒ग्नयः॑ ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शोचॆ । शोचिष्ठ । दीदिहि । विशे । मयः । रास्वः । स्तोत्रे । महान् । असि ।  
> देवानां । शर्मन् । मम । संतु । सूरयः । शत्रुसहः । सुअग्नयः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शोचिष्ठातिशयेन शोचयितरग्ने शोच । दीप्यस्व । दीदिहि । दीपयास्मान् । विशे प्रजायै स्तोत्रे मयः सुखं रास्व । देहि । त्वं महानसि । देवानां
> संबंधिनि शर्मञ्छर्मणि सुखे मम सूरयः स्तोतारो मेधाविनोऽस्माकंपुत्रादयो वा संतु । भवंतु । शत्रुषाहः शत्रुणामभिभवितारः स्वग्नयः शोभनाग्नयश्च संतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, most radiant, who cause to shine to the utmost: shine, and make us shine. Give happiness to the people and to the praiser; you are great. May my praisers, the wise ones, or my sons and the rest, be in the happiness that belongs to the gods; may they be overcomers of enemies and possessors of good fires. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विशे (*viśe*)—to your people
- स्तोत्रे (*stotre*)—to the praiser
- मयः (*mayaḥ*)—happiness
- रास्व (*rāsva*)—give
- महान् आसि (*mahān āsi*)—you are great
- मम (*mama*)—belonging to me

- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—the praisers (my sons and the rest)
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—given by the gods
- शर्मन् (*śarman*)—in the happiness
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—may they be
- शत्रुषाहः (*śatruṣāhaḥ*)—overcomers of enemies
- स्वग्नयः (*svagnayaḥ*)—and good worshippers of fire, may they be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, most radiant, shine still more brightly. Make us shine too. Give happiness to the praisers, who are your people. You are great. May my sons and the rest, your praisers, enjoy the happiness given by the gods. May they be overcomers of their enemies and good worshippers of fire.

##### English translation
Most resplendent (Agni), shine forth and illuminate (us); give happiness to your people, to your worshipper, for you are great ; may my priests abide in the bliss of the gods, subduing their enemies, possessing bright fires.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॑ चिद्वृ॒द्धम॑त॒समग्ने॑ सं॒जूर्व॑सि॒ क्षमि॑ ।  
> ए॒वा द॑ह मित्रमहो॒ यो अ॑स्म॒ध्रुग्दु॒र्मन्मा॒ कश्च॒ वेन॑ति ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । चित् । वृद्धं । अतसं । अग्ने । संजूर्वसि । क्षमि ।  
> एव । दह । मित्रमहः । यः । अस्मध्रुक् । दुःमन्मा । कः । च । वेनति ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने क्षमि क्षमायां वर्तमानं वृद्धमतसं शुष्कं काष्ठं यथा येन
> प्रकारेण संजूर्वसि । जर्वतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । सम्यग्दहसीत्यर्थः । एवैवं दह हे
> मित्रमहो मित्राणामस्माकं पूजक तेजो ना । कं । योऽस्मध्रुगस्माकं द्रोग्धा
> कश्च कश्चिद्दुर्मन्मा दुर्मतिर्वेनति कामयतेऽस्मान्द्रोग्धुं तं दहेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, just as you burn thoroughly dry wood lying on the earth (the root is of the sense of injury, and the meaning is that you burn it well), so burn, O Mitramahas, whoever among those hostile to us, an evil-minded one, desires to harm us; burn him. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 673

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रमहः (*mitramahaḥ*)—O worshipful one, to us who are your friends
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- क्षमि (*kṣami*)—on the earth
- वृद्धं अतसं (*vṛddhaṃ atasaṃ*)—old, dry wood
- यथा चित् (*yathā cit*)—in the way in which
- संबूर्वसि (*saṃbūrvasi*)—you burn completely **NOTE**
- एव (*eva*)—in the same way
- यः कश्च (*yaḥ kaśca*)—whoever
- दुर्मन्मा (*durmanmā*)—being evil-minded
- अस्मध्रुक् (*asmadhruk*)—wishing us harm
- वेनति (*venati*)—who wishes to deceive us, him too
- दह (*daha*)—burn completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, worshipful to us all who are your friends, as you burn completely old, dry wood lying on the earth, in the same way burn completely whoever, being evil-minded and wishing us harm, desires to deceive us.

##### English translation
As, Agni, you consume old timber on the earth, so cherisher of friends, do you burn our injurer, whoever evil-minded wishes (our ill).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा नो॒ मर्ता॑य रि॒पवे॑ रक्ष॒स्विने॒ माघशं॑साय रीरधः ।  
> अस्रे॑दद्भिस्त॒रणि॑भिर्यविष्ठ्य शि॒वेभिः॑ पाहि पा॒युभिः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । नः । मर्ताय । रिपवे । रक्षस्विने । मा । अघशंसाय । रीरधः ।  
> अस्रेधत्भिः । तरणिभिः । यविष्ठ्य । शिवेभिः । पाहि । पायुभिः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्मान्मर्ताय मरणधर्माय रिपवे शत्रवे हिंसित्रे रक्षस्विने बलवते
> मा रीरधः । वशमानये । तथाघशंसाय पापशंसकाय मा रीरधः । हे यविष्ठ्य
> युवतम अस्रेधद्भिरहिंसकैस्तरणिभिस्तारकैः शिवेभिः सुखकर्वैः पायुभिः पालनैर्नोऽस्मान्पाहि । रक्ष ॥
> XXIV 43

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Do not subject us to a mortal, that is, a creature subject to death, an enemy, a injurer, a strong one (the sense is: do not bring us under his control); likewise not to one who speaks of sin. O most youthful Agni, protect us with protections that do not harm, that carry across, that bring happiness.

- यविष्य (*yaviṣya*)—O Agni, the very youthful

- मर्ताय (*martāya*)—and of human form
- रिपवे (*ripave*)—to the injuring enemy
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा रीरधः (*mā rīradhaḥ*)—do not hand over
- अघशंसाय (*aghaśaṃsāya*)—to one who wishes us harm too

- तरणिभिः (*taraṇibhiḥ*)—that carry across sorrow

- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the very youthful, do not hand us over to an injuring enemy who is strong and of human form. Do not hand us over to one who wishes us harm. Protect us with protections that do not injure, that carry us across sorrow and that are auspicious.

##### English translation
Subject us not to a strong mortal enemy, nor to the malevolent; O most youthful, guard us with your unharming delivering, auspicious protections.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पा॒हि नो॑ अग्न॒ एक॑या पा॒ह्यु१॒॑ १ त द्वि॒तीय॑या ।  
> पा॒हि गी॒र्भिस्ति॒ सृभि॑रूर्जा० पते पा॒हि च॑त॒सृभि॑र्वसो ॥ ९ ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पाहि । नः । अग्ने । एकया । पाहि । उत । द्वितीयया ।  
> पाहि । गीःभिः । तिसृभिः । ऊर्जां । पते । पाहि । चतसृभिः । वसो इति ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने नोऽस्मानेकयर्चा गिरा पाहि । रक्ष । उतापि च द्वितीयॆयर्चा
> पाहि । पालय । पाहि । तिसृभिर्गिर्भिरूर्जामन्नानां बलानां वा पते स्वामिन् ।
> तथा पाहि चतसृभिर्गर्भिर्हे वसो वासकाग्ने ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, protect us with one ṛc, one hymn, and also protect us with a second ṛc. Protect us with three hymns, O lord of foods or of strengths, O master. Likewise protect us with four hymns, O Vasu, dweller-giving Agni.

O Agni, protect us with our utterance of a single ṛc and with a group of utterances of two ṛcs. Further, O protector of food, protect us with a group of three ṛcs. O giver of dwelling, protect us also with a group of four ṛcs. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पा॒हि विश्व॑स्माद्र॒क्षसो॒ अरा॑व्लः॒ प्र स्म॒ वाजे॑षु नोऽव ।  
> त्वामिद्धि नेदि॑ष्ठं दे॒वता॑तय आ॒सिं नक्षा॑महे वृ॒धे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पाहि । विश्वस्मात् । रक्षसः । अराव्नः । प्र । स्म । वाजेषु । नः । अव ।  
> त्वां । इत् । हि । नेदिष्टं । देवतातये । आपिं । नक्षामहे । वृधे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने विश्वस्मात्सर्वस्माद्रक्षसोऽरावोऽदातुः सकाशात्पाहि । रक्षास्मान् ।
> वाजेषु संग्रामेषु नोऽस्यान् प्राव । प्रकर्षेण रक्ष । स्मेति पूरणः । हि यस्मान्नेदिष्टमासन्नमापिं बंधुभूतं त्वामित्तामेव देवतातये यज्ञाय यज्ञसिद्ध्यर्थं वृधे वर्धनाय नक्षामहे व्याप्नुमः । नक्षतिर्वाप्तिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, protect us from every rākṣasa, from the one who does not give. In battles protect us fully; the particle स्म (*sma*) is a filler. Because you are nearest, close, a kinsman, you alone do we approach for the sacrifice, to accomplish the sacrifice, and for increase; the root meaning is that of obtaining.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॑ अग्ने वयो॒वृधं॑ र॒यिं पा॑वक॒ शंस्यं॑ ।  
> रास्वा॑ च न उपमाते पुरु॒स्पृहं॒ सुनी॑ती॒ स्वय॑शस्तरं ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । आग्ने । वयःवृधं । रयिं । पावक । शंस्यं ।  
> रास्व । च । नः । उपमाते । पुरुस्पृहं । सुनीती । स्वयशःतरं ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने पावक शोधक वयोवृधमन्नस्य वर्धकं शंस्यं शंसनीयं
> रयिं धनं नोऽस्मभ्यमा हरेति शेषः । आहृत्य च हे उपमाते । उपास्मत्समीपे
> माति नो धनमित्युपमातिः । हे तादृशाग्ने नोऽस्मभ्यं सुनीती सुनीत्या
> शोभननयनेन पुरुस्पृहं बहुभिः स्पृहणीयं स्वयशस्तरमत्यंतं स्वभूतकीर्ति
> धनं रास्व च । देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, purifier, bring to us wealth that increases food and is praiseworthy (the verb "bring" is to be supplied). And having brought it, O Upamāti, one who measures our wealth close to us, O Agni such as you are, give us, by good guidance, wealth desired by many and bringing exceedingly its own fame.

- रास्व (*rāsva*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, purifier, bring us wealth that increases our food and is praiseworthy. O Agni, who are near us and see the measure of our wealth, give us, by the most excellent way, wealth that is desired by many and is the cause of excellent fame.

##### English translation
Purifying Agni, bestow upon us food-augmenting excellent wealth ; and (bring) us, O meter-out of good, by auspicious guidance, (a treasure) desired by many and bringing its own fame.

#### Ṛk 12

**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> येन॒ वंसा॑म॒ पृत॑नासु॒ शर्ध॑त॒स्तरं॑तो अ॒र्य आ॒दिशः॑ ।  
> स त्वं नो॑ वर्ध॒ प्रय॑सा शचीवसो॒ जिन्वा॒ धियो॑ वसु॒विदः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> येन । वंसाम । पृतनासु । शर्धतः । तरंतः । आर्यः । आदिशः ।  
> सः । त्वं । नः । वर्ध । प्रयसा । शचीवसो इति शचीवसो। जिन्न । धियः । वसुविदः॥

> येन धनेन हृतनासु संग्रामेषु शर्धतो वेगं कुर्वतोऽर्योऽरीञ्छत्रूनादिक अदेष्ट्वाञ्स्त्रप्रक्षेप्तांस्तरंतो वंसाम हिंसाम तद्धनं देहि । हे
> शचीवसो प्रज्ञया वासयितः कर्म धनं वा स प्रसिद्धस्त्वं नोऽस्मान्वर्ध । वर्धय ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By which wealth we may strike down, in battles, the enemies who press on with speed and who hurl weapons, give us that wealth. O Śacīvasu, one who causes to dwell by wisdom, or one whose wealth is rites: you, the famous one, make us grow. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 678

> प्रीणयॆ । प्रयसान्नेन त्वं वा वर्ध । अस्मदीयेन प्रयसा हविषा वसुविदो
> वसूनां लंभकानि धियः कर्माण्यस्मदीयानि जिन्न । प्रीणय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Satisfy us. Or else: you grow with food; with our oblation, satisfy our rites, which are the finders of wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
